declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionAssignment
declarations.doc:
The assignment sending every matter generator to zero and keeping the connection
generators. Its relations hold in the commutative target.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def connectionAssignment :
    T.Assignment (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionRetraction
declarations.doc:
The retraction of the local field algebra onto the complexified gauge-only algebra: it
forgets the matter symbols.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def connectionRetraction :
    T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionRetraction_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma connectionRetraction_ιConnection (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    T.connectionRetraction (T.ιConnection v)
      = (1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionRetraction_comp_includeConnection
declarations.doc: The retraction is a left inverse of the connection inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma connectionRetraction_comp_includeConnection :
    T.connectionRetraction.comp T.includeConnection
      = AlgHom.id ℂ (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionRetraction_includeConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma connectionRetraction_includeConnection (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.connectionRetraction (T.includeConnection y) = y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.includeConnection_injective
declarations.doc: The complexified gauge-only algebra embeds in the local field algebra.
declarations.statement: lemma includeConnection_injective : Function.Injective T.includeConnection

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.range_includeConnection
declarations.doc: The range of the connection inclusion is the gauge sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_includeConnection :
    T.includeConnection.range = T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge}

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.includeConnection_mem_gaugeSector
declarations.statement:
lemma includeConnection_mem_gaugeSector (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.includeConnection y ∈ T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge}

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorEquiv
declarations.doc:
The gauge sector is the complexification of the gauge-only algebra: the connection
inclusion, corestricted to its range. The source is complexified because the gauge-only
algebra is real while the sector is a complex subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeSectorEquiv :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) ≃ₐ[ℂ] ↥(T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge})

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.coe_gaugeSectorEquiv
declarations.doc: In the local field algebra the equivalence is the canonical inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_gaugeSectorEquiv (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorEquiv y : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = T.includeConnection y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorEquiv_symm_includeConnection
declarations.doc: The inverse recovers an element from its inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorEquiv_symm_includeConnection (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤)
    (hy : T.includeConnection y ∈ T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge}) :
    T.gaugeSectorEquiv.symm ⟨T.includeConnection y, hy⟩ = y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_one_tmul_ι
declarations.doc:
A real gauge-only generator, embedded with the scalar `1`, is the corresponding
connection symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_one_tmul_ι (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorEquiv ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) v) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T.ιConnection v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_tmul
declarations.doc: `z ⊗ₜ x` maps to `z` times the image of `1 ⊗ₜ x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_tmul (z : ℂ) (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorEquiv (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = z • (T.gaugeSectorEquiv ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_gaugeField
declarations.doc:
The gauge-field symbol `∂_s A_μ^φ`, for any derivative multiset, spacetime index and
adjoint covector, is the connection symbol with the same labels.
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_gaugeSectorEquiv_gaugeField (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorEquiv (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.gaugeField 𝔤 s μ φ) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T.gaugeRealization.A s μ φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorEquiv_complexRepJet
declarations.doc:
The equivalence intertwines the complexified gauge-only jet action with the restricted
jet action of the gauge sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorEquiv_complexRepJet (U : GJ) (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.gaugeSectorEquiv (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepJet jets U y)
      = SectorAlgebra.repJet T {FieldCategory.gauge} U (T.gaugeSectorEquiv y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorEquiv_complexRepLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The equivalence intertwines the complexified gauge-only Lorentz action with the
restricted Lorentz action of the gauge sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorEquiv_complexRepLorentzGroup (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.gaugeSectorEquiv (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ y)
      = SectorAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T {FieldCategory.gauge} Λ (T.gaugeSectorEquiv y)

modules.title: Realizations of the ordinary gauge sector
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

For a complex algebra `B`, realizations of the ordinary gauge sector
`T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge}` are the real realizations of the gauge-only algebra
`LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤` in `B`, its two actions viewed over `ℝ` by restriction of
scalars. The correspondence is the algebra equivalence `GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorEquiv`
composed with the universal property of base change `AlgHom.liftEquiv`; the gauge symbols
`∂_s A_μ^φ` agree on both sides.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv` : the correspondence, with both round trips.
- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_A`,
  `GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom_gaugeField` : the gauge symbols
  of corresponding realizations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The correspondence
- B. Computation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The correspondence
## B. Computation

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv
declarations.doc:
Realizations of the ordinary gauge sector are the real realizations of the gauge-only
algebra, the target keeping its complex actions restricted to `ℝ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv :
    SectorAlgebra.Realization T {FieldCategory.gauge} B repJet repLorentz
      ≃ LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.Realization jets B (repJet.restrictScalars ℝ)
          (repLorentz.restrictScalars ℝ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_toAlgHom
    (f : SectorAlgebra.Realization T {FieldCategory.gauge} B repJet repLorentz) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv f).toAlgHom
      = ((f.toAlgHom.comp T.gaugeSectorEquiv.toAlgHom).restrictScalars ℝ).comp
          Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_toAlgHom_apply
    (f : SectorAlgebra.Realization T {FieldCategory.gauge} B repJet repLorentz)
    (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv f).toAlgHom x
      = f.toAlgHom (T.gaugeSectorEquiv ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_A
declarations.doc: The gauge symbols of the corresponding real realization are the sector symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_A
    (f : SectorAlgebra.Realization T {FieldCategory.gauge} B repJet repLorentz)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv f).A s μ φ
      = f.toAlgHom (T.gaugeSectorEquiv (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.gaugeField 𝔤 s μ φ))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom
    (h : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.Realization jets B (repJet.restrictScalars ℝ)
      (repLorentz.restrictScalars ℝ)) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv.symm h).toAlgHom
      = (AlgHom.liftEquiv ℝ ℂ (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) B h.toAlgHom).comp
          T.gaugeSectorEquiv.symm.toAlgHom

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom_apply
    (h : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.Realization jets B (repJet.restrictScalars ℝ)
      (repLorentz.restrictScalars ℝ)) (x : T.SectorAlgebra {FieldCategory.gauge}) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv.symm h).toAlgHom x
      = AlgHom.liftEquiv ℝ ℂ (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) B h.toAlgHom
          (T.gaugeSectorEquiv.symm x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom_gaugeField
declarations.doc: The sector symbols of the corresponding sector realization are the gauge symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv_symm_toAlgHom_gaugeField
    (h : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.Realization jets B (repJet.restrictScalars ℝ)
      (repLorentz.restrictScalars ℝ)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    (T.gaugeSectorRealizationEquiv.symm h).toAlgHom
        (T.gaugeSectorEquiv (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.gaugeField 𝔤 s μ φ)) = h.A s μ φ

modules.title: `V`-valued jets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The jets of a field valued in a complex vector space `V` are `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V`. This file
provides the basic toolkit for them, independent of any gauge group:

* `jetOfConstant` — the inclusion of constants, `v ↦ 1 ⊗ v`;
* `jetDeriv`/`jetIteratedDeriv` — the formal derivative, acting on the jet factor;
* `jetEval` — evaluation at the base point, `f ⊗ v ↦ (constant coefficient of f) • v`.

## ii. Key results

- `jetOfConstant` : the inclusion of constants into `V`-valued jets: `v ↦ 1 ⊗ v`
- `jetDeriv` : the formal derivative on `V`-valued jets in the direction `μ`, acting on the jet
  factor
- `jetIteratedDeriv` : the iterated formal derivative on `V`-valued jets, in the (unordered)
  directions given by the multiset `μs`
- `jetEval`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. `V`-valued jets
- B. The jets of a product of value spaces
- C. The jets of an indexed product of value spaces

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. `V`-valued jets

## B. The jets of a product of value spaces

A field valued in `V × W` is a pair of fields, one valued in `V` and one in `W`, and the
identification `jetProdEquiv` of its jets with the pair of their jets intertwines every
piece of the jet toolkit: the inclusion of constants, the formal derivative and the
base-point evaluation all act componentwise.

## C. The jets of an indexed product of value spaces

A field valued in a finite product `∀ i, E i` is a family of fields, one for each index,
and `jetPiEquiv` identifies its jets with the family of their jets. It intertwines the
whole jet toolkit index by index, exactly as `jetProdEquiv` does in the binary case. The
index type has to be finite for the identification to exist at all: a jet of a field
valued in an infinite product need not have all but finitely many of its components
constant, so `TensorProduct.piRightHom` is only an equivalence in the finite case.

declarations.name: jetOfConstant
declarations.doc: The inclusion of constants into `V`-valued jets: `v ↦ 1 ⊗ v`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetOfConstant : V →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: jetOfConstant_apply
declarations.statement: lemma jetOfConstant_apply (v : V) : jetOfConstant v = (1 : SpaceTimeAlgebra) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v

declarations.name: jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal derivative on `V`-valued jets in the direction `μ`, acting on the jet
factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: jetDeriv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_tmul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    jetDeriv μ (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = pderiv μ f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v

declarations.name: jetDeriv_comm
declarations.doc:
Formal derivatives on `V`-valued jets commute, since the partial derivatives of
jets do.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (jetDeriv (V := V) μ).comp (jetDeriv ν) = (jetDeriv ν).comp (jetDeriv μ)

declarations.doc:
Post-composition with `jetDeriv` is right-commutative, which is what allows
iterated derivatives to be indexed by a `Multiset` of directions.
declarations.statement:
instance : RightCommutative (fun (L : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) => L.comp (jetDeriv μ))

declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv
declarations.doc:
The iterated formal derivative on `V`-valued jets, in the (unordered) directions
given by the multiset `μs`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetIteratedDeriv (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma jetIteratedDeriv_zero :
    jetIteratedDeriv (V := V) (0 : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma jetIteratedDeriv_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetIteratedDeriv (V := V) (μ ::ₘ μs) = (jetDeriv μ).comp (jetIteratedDeriv μs)

declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv_add
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative is additive in the multiset of directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetIteratedDeriv_add (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetIteratedDeriv (V := V) (s + t) =
      (jetIteratedDeriv s).comp (jetIteratedDeriv t)

declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma jetIteratedDeriv_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetIteratedDeriv (V := V) ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = jetDeriv μ

declarations.name: jetEval
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of a `V`-valued jet at the base point:
`f ⊗ v ↦ (constant coefficient of f) • v`. This is a retraction of
`jetOfConstant`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetEval : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: jetEval_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_tmul (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    jetEval (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = constantCoeff f • v

declarations.name: jetEval_jetOfConstant
declarations.statement: lemma jetEval_jetOfConstant (v : V) : jetEval (jetOfConstant v) = v

declarations.name: jetEval_smul
declarations.doc:
Evaluation at the base point is semilinear over the jet ring: a scalar jet acts through
its constant coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_smul (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEval (f • z) = constantCoeff f • jetEval z

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The jets of a product are the product of the jets**: `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (V × W)` splits as
`(SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ V) × (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ W)`, the jet-ring factor being shared.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev jetProdEquiv :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V × W) ≃ₗ[ℂ] (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) × (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv_jetOfConstant
declarations.statement:
lemma jetProdEquiv_jetOfConstant (v : V) (w : W) :
    jetProdEquiv (jetOfConstant (v, w)) = (jetOfConstant v, jetOfConstant w)

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv_jetDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma jetProdEquiv_jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V × W)) :
    jetProdEquiv (jetDeriv μ z) =
      (jetDeriv μ (jetProdEquiv z).1, jetDeriv μ (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma jetProdEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V × W)) :
    jetProdEquiv (jetIteratedDeriv s z) =
      (jetIteratedDeriv s (jetProdEquiv z).1, jetIteratedDeriv s (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The identification is `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linear: multiplication by a scalar jet acts on both
components.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetProdEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V × W)) :
    jetProdEquiv (χ • z) = (χ • (jetProdEquiv z).1, χ • (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: jetProdEquiv_symm_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetProdEquiv_symm_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (a : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (b : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W) :
    (jetProdEquiv (V := V) (W := W)).symm (χ • a, χ • b)
      = χ • (jetProdEquiv (V := V) (W := W)).symm (a, b)

declarations.name: jetEval_prod
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_prod (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V × W)) :
    jetEval z = (jetEval (jetProdEquiv z).1, jetEval (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The jets of a finite product are the product of the jets**:
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (∀ i, E i)` splits as `∀ i, SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ E i`, the jet-ring factor being
shared.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev jetPiEquiv :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] E i

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_jetOfConstant
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_jetOfConstant (v : ∀ i, E i) :
    jetPiEquiv E (jetOfConstant v) = fun i => jetOfConstant (v i)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_jetDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    jetPiEquiv E (jetDeriv μ z) i = jetDeriv μ (jetPiEquiv E z i)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    jetPiEquiv E (jetIteratedDeriv s z) i = jetIteratedDeriv s (jetPiEquiv E z i)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The identification is `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linear: multiplication by a scalar jet acts on every
component.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    jetPiEquiv E (χ • z) i = χ • (jetPiEquiv E z i)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_symm_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_symm_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (a : ∀ i, SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] E i) :
    (jetPiEquiv E).symm (fun i => χ • a i) = χ • (jetPiEquiv E).symm a

declarations.name: jetEval_pi
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_pi (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    jetEval z i = jetEval (jetPiEquiv E z i)

declarations.name: jetPiEquiv_eq_lTensor_proj
declarations.doc:
The component of the splitting is the projection on the value factor. Reading off
the summand `i` of a jet of a `(∀ i, E i)`-valued field is applying the projection onto
that summand to the value factor, the jet-ring factor being untouched. This is the form
in which the splitting meets the naturality statements, which are all phrased in terms of
linear maps of value spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPiEquiv_eq_lTensor_proj (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    jetPiEquiv E z i = LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i) z

declarations.name: jetPi_hom_ext
declarations.doc:
Two maps into the jets of a product agree as soon as their species components do.
The splitting is an equivalence, so a jet of a `(∀ i, E i)`-valued field is determined by
its summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetPi_hom_ext {N : Type} [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℂ N]
    {A B : N →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, E i)}
    (h : ∀ i, (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i)).comp A
      = (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i)).comp B) : A = B

modules.title: Fibrewise actions on `V`-valued jets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A gauge transformation acts on the jets `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V` of a `V`-valued field. What makes
that action local is that it is *fibrewise*: it commutes with multiplication by scalar
jets, so it acts on the values of the field over the identity on spacetime. This file
collects what follows from fibrewise-linearity alone, before any component space is built:

* a fibrewise action is determined by its values on constant jets, and for
  finite-dimensional `V` that restriction is a matrix of power series, its *coefficient*
  `jetCoeff` in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V`, which is multiplicative;
* the conjugate action `repConj` on the jets of the conjugate field, again fibrewise;
* the naturality of both in the value space: a linear map of value spaces intertwining two
  fibrewise actions intertwines their coefficients, and their conjugate actions.

These are the ingredients from which the action on the jet component space is assembled in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.JetComponent.GaugeAction`; they
live here, upstream of `MatterField`, because the infinitesimal-action theory that
`MatterField` is stated over already needs `repConj`.


- `JetComponentSpace.jetCoeff` : the coefficient of a fibrewise action, in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End
  V`.
- `JetComponentSpace.coeff_mul_of_smul_comm` : the coefficient is multiplicative.
- `JetComponentSpace.repConj`, `repConj_smul_comm` : the action on the jets of the
  conjugate field.
- `JetComponentSpace.jetCoeff_naturality` : the coefficient is natural in the value space.
- `JetComponentSpace.lTensor_comp_repConj` : so is the conjugate action.

## ii. Key results

- `repConj` : the conjugate jet action
- `repConj_smul_comm` : the conjugate jet action is fibrewise-linear whenever the original is
- `jetCoeff` : the coefficient of a fibrewise gauge action

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Naturality of the coefficient in the value space

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Naturality of the coefficient in the value space

A linear map `f : V →ₗ W` of value spaces intertwining two fibrewise jet actions relates their
coefficients, but not as an equation between elements of two different modules: the comparison takes
place in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (V →ₗ W)`, into which `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` maps by
postcomposition with `f` and `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End W` by precomposition. The two images agree, and
that single identity is what carries the gauge action across a map of value spaces.

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.rep_tmul_of_smul_comm
declarations.doc:
**A fibrewise action is determined by its values on constant jets.** If the gauge
action commutes with multiplication by scalar jets — the statement that it acts on the
values of the field, over the identity on spacetime — then its value on a general jet
`f ⊗ₜ v` is the constant-jet value `rep U (1 ⊗ₜ v)` scaled by `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_tmul_of_smul_comm
    {rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)}
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    rep U (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = f • rep U (jetOfConstant v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lift_mul_tmul
declarations.doc:
**The canonical evaluation is a right module map.** Writing `ev` for the canonical
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V → (V →ₗ SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ V)`, `g ⊗ T ↦ (v ↦ g ⊗ₜ T v)`, multiplying on
the right by `b ⊗ T` applies `T` to the argument and scales the value by `b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_mul_tmul (x : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V)
    (b : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (T : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) (x * (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] T)) v
      = b • TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) x (T v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.rep_lift_of_smul_comm
declarations.doc:
**A fibrewise action is the `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linear extension of its coefficient.** If the
element `x` of `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` records `rep U` on constant jets, then `rep U` agrees
with left multiplication by `x` on every coefficient `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_lift_of_smul_comm
    {rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)}
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G) (x : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V)
    (hx : ∀ v : V, TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
      (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) x v = rep U (jetOfConstant v))
    (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    rep U (TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) y v)
      = TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) (x * y) v

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.coeff_mul_of_smul_comm
declarations.doc:
**The coefficient of a fibrewise action is multiplicative.** Recording `rep` on
constant jets as a family `c` in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V`, group multiplication becomes
multiplication in that algebra. This is the identity that makes the induced action on
the symbols a representation, and it needs no basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_mul_of_smul_comm
    {rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)}
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (c : G → SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V)
    (hc : ∀ (U : G) (v : V),
      TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) (c U) v = rep U (jetOfConstant v))
    (U W : G) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) (c U * c W) v
      = rep (U * W) (jetOfConstant v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.symbolAction_mul
declarations.doc:
**The symbol action of a coefficient is an anti-homomorphism.** Let `Θ` send a
coefficient `g ⊗ T` in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` to the endomorphism `jetRingAction g ⊗ Tᵀ` of
the symbol space `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗ Dual V`. Then `Θ` reverses products: the jet-ring
factor is multiplicative (`jetRingAction_mul`, and `SpaceTimeAlgebra` is commutative) while the
target factor is contravariant (`Module.Dual.transpose_comp`). Composed with `U ↦ U⁻¹`
this is exactly what makes the induced action a representation, with no induction over
the antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_mul
    (Θ : (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) →ₗ[ℂ]
      Module.End ℂ (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V))
    (hΘ : ∀ (g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (T : Module.End ℂ V),
      Θ (g ⊗ₜ[ℂ] T) = TensorProduct.map (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction g)
        (Module.Dual.transpose T))
    (x y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) :
    Θ (x * y) = Θ y ∘ₗ Θ x

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lift_congr_leftComm
declarations.doc:
**The coefficient of a linear map, canonically.** For finite-dimensional `V` the canonical
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (V →ₗ W) → (V →ₗ SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ W)` is inverted by reassociating the
contraction `Dual V ⊗ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ W) ≃ SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (Dual V ⊗ W) ≃ SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗
(V →ₗ W)`. This is the finite-rank input, obtained from `dualTensorHomEquiv` rather than from a
basis. Only the source `V` has to be finite-dimensional; the target is arbitrary, which is what lets
the naturality statements below compare two different value spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_congr_leftComm [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (G : Module.Dual ℂ V ⊗[ℂ] (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V W (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W))
        ((TensorProduct.congr (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra) (dualTensorHomEquiv ℂ V W))
          (TensorProduct.leftComm ℂ (Module.Dual ℂ V) SpaceTimeAlgebra W G)) v
      = dualTensorHom ℂ V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W) G v

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.repConj
declarations.doc:
**The conjugate jet action.** Given a gauge action on the jets of a `V`-valued field,
this is the induced action on the jets of the *conjugate* field.

It is `Representation.conj rep` — the same underlying maps, read on `ConjModule` — carried
across the identification

  `ConjModule (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) ≃ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] ConjModule V`

which is `ConjModule.tensorEquiv` (conjugation is monoidal) followed by
`SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv` on the jet-ring factor (the real structure of the jet ring). On
pure tensors the composite is `f ⊗ₜ v ↦ star f ⊗ₜ v`, so `repConj` carries the conjugate
gauge matrix — the physicists' `ψ̄ ↦ ψ̄ U†`.

Being a representation is free: `LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv` is a ring equivalence of
endomorphism rings, hence multiplicative.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repConj (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) :
    Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] ConjModule V)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.repConj_apply_tmul
declarations.doc:
On pure tensors the conjugate jet action conjugates the jet factor: it is `rep`
evaluated at `star f ⊗ₜ v`, read back through the same identification.
declarations.statement:
lemma repConj_apply_tmul (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : G) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    repConj rep U (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := V) v)
      = ((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
          (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
        (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) (rep U (star f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)))

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.tensorEquiv_congr_conjEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
**The identification conjugates the jet-ring action.** Carrying a `V`-valued jet over
to the conjugate side turns multiplication by `star χ` into multiplication by `χ`: the
`star` on the jet-ring factor is exactly what absorbs the conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorEquiv_congr_conjEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    ((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
        (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
          (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) (star χ • y))
      = χ • ((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
        (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
          (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) y)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.repConj_apply_conjEquiv
declarations.doc:
The conjugate jet action is the original one, read through the identification. On
a jet carried over to the conjugate side, `repConj rep U` is `rep U` applied on the
original side and carried over again. Everything about `repConj` beyond its definition
follows from this.
declarations.statement:
lemma repConj_apply_conjEquiv (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) (U : G)
    (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    repConj rep U (((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
        (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
        (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) y))
      = ((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
          (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
        (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) (rep U y))

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.repConj_smul_comm
declarations.doc:
**The conjugate jet action is fibrewise-linear whenever the original is.** This is
what lets the coefficient machinery of `coeff_mul_of_smul_comm` be instantiated at
`ConjModule V`, giving the conjugate half of the symbol action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repConj_smul_comm
    {rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)}
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] ConjModule V) :
    repConj rep U (χ • z) = χ • repConj rep U z

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lTensor_conjEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
The identification of the conjugate of the jets with the jets of the conjugate is
natural in the value space. A linear map of value spaces acts on either side by the same
underlying map, so carrying a jet over to the conjugate side commutes with it.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_conjEquiv_naturality (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (ConjModule.map (k := ℂ) f))
        (((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := V)).symm.trans
          (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule V))))
          (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) y))
      = ((ConjModule.tensorEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra) (N := W)).symm.trans
          (TensorProduct.congr SpaceTimeAlgebra.starConjEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ (ConjModule W))))
        (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)
            ((LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f) y))

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lTensor_comp_repConj
declarations.doc:
The conjugate jet action is natural in the value space. A linear map of value
spaces intertwining two fibrewise jet actions intertwines the actions on the jets of the
conjugate fields, through the induced map of conjugate modules. This is what supplies the
conjugate half of the naturality of the gauge action on the jet component space, which
does not follow from the unconjugated half.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_comp_repConj (repV : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (repW : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)) (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W)
    (hf : ∀ U : G, (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f).comp (repV U)
      = (repW U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f)) (U : G) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (ConjModule.map (k := ℂ) f)).comp (repConj repV U)
      = (repConj repW U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (ConjModule.map (k := ℂ) f))

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lift_injective
declarations.doc:
**The coefficient is determined by its action on constants.** For finite-dimensional `V` the
canonical evaluation `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (V →ₗ W) → (V →ₗ SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ W)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_injective [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    {x y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V →ₗ[ℂ] W)}
    (h : ∀ v : V, TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V W (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
      (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W)) x v = TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V W
        (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
      (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W)) y v) : x = y

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeff
declarations.doc:
**The coefficient of a fibrewise gauge action.** For finite-dimensional `V`, the
restriction of `rep U` to constant jets is an element of `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` — a matrix of
power series, obtained canonically from `dualTensorHomEquiv` rather than from a basis.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetCoeff [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) (U : G) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeff_spec
declarations.doc: The coefficient reproduces `rep U` on constant jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeff_spec [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) (U : G) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
      (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) (jetCoeff rep U) v = rep U (jetOfConstant v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lift_lTensor_llcomp
declarations.doc: Postcomposing a coefficient with `f` evaluates as applying `f` to the value.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_lTensor_llcomp (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (x : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V W (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W))
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V W f) x) v
      = LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f
        (TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
          (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) x v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.lift_lTensor_lcomp
declarations.doc:
Precomposing a coefficient with `f` evaluates as evaluating at the image of the
argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_lTensor_lcomp (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ W) (v : V) :
    TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V W (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W))
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.lcomp ℂ W f) y) v
      = TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ W W (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra W)) y (f v)

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeff_naturality
declarations.doc:
The coefficient of a fibrewise action is natural in the value space. If `f` maps
the values of one field to the values of another and intertwines their jet actions, then
the coefficient of the first followed by `f` is `f` followed by the coefficient of the
second, as elements of `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (V →ₗ W)`. Both value spaces have to be
finite-dimensional, since both coefficients have to exist; no fibrewise-linearity is used
here, the coefficient being defined for any action.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeff_naturality [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    [Module.Free ℂ W] [Module.Finite ℂ W]
    (repV : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (repW : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W)) (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W)
    (hf : ∀ U : G, (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f).comp (repV U)
      = (repW U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f)) (U : G) :
    LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V W f) (jetCoeff repV U)
      = LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.lcomp ℂ W f) (jetCoeff repW U)

modules.title: The Lorentz action on the local field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Lorentz group `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the local field algebra `J(T)` of a field datum by
algebra endomorphisms: on the generators of a matter species by the action
`JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup` of that species, mixing the derivative label and the
target index, and on the connection generators by the gauge-only action
`LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup`. The construction is that of the jet gauge action
in `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalField.GaugeAction`: the lift of a
compatible assignment, with the representation laws from uniqueness.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom`, `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup` : the action of a
  Lorentz transformation, as an algebra endomorphism and as a representation, with
  `repLorentzGroup_ιFermion`, `repLorentzGroup_ιBoson`, `repLorentzGroup_ιConnection` on the
  generators.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_includeConnection` : on the connection factor the action
  is the complexified gauge-only action.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq` : the law of the connection generators.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz assignment of a transformation
- B. The action of a transformation
- C. The action on the connection factor
- D. The representation

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzConnection
declarations.doc:
The connection generators after a Lorentz transformation: the gauge-only action on the
degree-one element, included into the local field algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzAssignment
declarations.doc:
The assignment of the generators defining the action of a Lorentz transformation: each
matter species acts on its own component functions, the connection generators through
the gauge-only action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzAssignment (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) : T.Assignment T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation on the local field algebra, as an algebra
endomorphism: the lift of its Lorentz assignment.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repLorentzAlgHom (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson j) Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
          LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ v))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_comp_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation restricts to the complexified gauge-only action
on the connection factor, as an equation of algebra maps out of the complexified
gauge-only algebra, compared on the real generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_comp_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ).comp T.includeConnection
      = T.includeConnection.comp (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroupAlgHom 𝔤 Λ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation restricts to the complexified gauge-only action
on the connection factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
On the real gauge-only algebra, included, a Lorentz transformation acts through the
gauge-only action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection_one_tmul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x))
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_one
declarations.doc: The identity transformation acts as the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzAlgHom_one : T.repLorentzAlgHom 1 = AlgHom.id ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_mul
declarations.doc: The action of a product of transformations is the composite of the actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_mul (Λ₁ Λ₂ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom (Λ₁ * Λ₂) = (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ₁).comp (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ₂)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: The action of the Lorentz group on the local field algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (x * y) = T.repLorentzGroup Λ x * T.repLorentzGroup Λ y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_one (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (1 : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = 1

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson j) Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
          LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ v))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action restricts to the complexified gauge-only action on the connection
factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the connection generators: a transformation carries a connection
generator to the generator of the transformed component, with no shift. This is the
generator-level form of `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection`, with no reference
to the connection factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.ιConnection (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ v)

modules.title: The mass-weight filtration and the invariants of a local field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The local field algebra of a field datum is graded by mass weight: a generator `∂_s φ_α`
of a field of mass weight `w` has weight `w + 2 |s|`, a connection generator `∂_s A_μ` has
weight `2 + 2 |s|`. The grading is recorded by the algebra endomorphisms scaling each
generator by `c` to its weight, for real `c`; the weight-`n` piece is the common
eigenspace of eigenvalue `c ^ n`, and the filtration is the join of the pieces of weight
at most `w`.

Together with the actions of the jet gauge group and of the Lorentz group this gives the
submodule of gauge and Lorentz invariants of mass weight at most `w`, which is what a
Lagrangian classification describes. Everything here is generic: a model contributes only
its datum.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale` : the scaling of the local field algebra by `c` to the
  mass weight of each generator.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule`, `massWeightSubmoduleLE` : the graded pieces and
  the filtration.
- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeInvariants`, `lorentzInvariants`, `invariantsLE` : the invariants,
  and the invariants of mass weight at most `w`.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonNormSq` : the contraction `φ† φ` of a bosonic species with its
  conjugate through a basis of its value space, the simplest invariant.
- `GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_map` : an isomorphism of local field algebras respecting the
  actions and the scaling carries the invariants of one datum onto those of the other.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight scaling
- B. The graded pieces and the filtration
- C. The invariants
- D. The contraction of a boson with its conjugate
- E. Transport along an isomorphism

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight scaling
## B. The graded pieces and the filtration
## C. The invariants
## D. The contraction of a boson with its conjugate

## E. Transport along an isomorphism

An isomorphism of local field algebras intertwining the jet gauge action, the Lorentz
action and the mass-weight scaling carries the graded pieces, the filtration and the
invariants of one datum onto those of the other. This is what relates two presentations
of the same field content, such as a model's table and a hand-built datum.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightAssignment
declarations.doc:
The assignment scaling each generator by `c` to its mass weight: a component function
`∂_s φ_α` of a species of mass weight `w` by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, a connection generator
`∂_s A_μ` by `c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)`. The relations hold because the images are generators of
the same kind.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightAssignment (c : ℝ) : T.Assignment T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
**The mass-weight scaling of the local field algebra**: the algebra endomorphism
scaling each generator by `c` to its mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightScale (c : ℝ) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιFermion (c : ℝ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale (T.fermion i).massWeight (c : ℂ) x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιBoson (c : ℝ) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale (T.boson j).massWeight (c : ℂ) y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιConnection (c : ℝ) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.ιConnection (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace.massWeightScale 𝔤 c v)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
**The weight-`n` piece** of the local field algebra: the elements scaled by `c ^ n`
under every mass-weight scaling: the equaliser of the scalings and the scalars.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff {n : ℕ} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.massWeightSubmodule n ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, T.massWeightScale c x = ((c : ℂ) ^ n) • x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: **The mass-weight filtration**: the join of the pieces of weight at most `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (h : k ≤ w) :
    T.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeInvariants
declarations.doc: **The gauge invariants**: the elements fixed by every jet of gauge transformations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeInvariants : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_gaugeInvariants_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_gaugeInvariants_iff {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.gaugeInvariants ↔ ∀ U : GJ, T.repJet U x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzInvariants
declarations.doc: **The Lorentz invariants**: the elements fixed by every Lorentz transformation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzInvariants : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_lorentzInvariants_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_lorentzInvariants_iff {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.lorentzInvariants ↔ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE
declarations.doc:
**The invariants of mass weight at most `w`**: the gauge and Lorentz invariants in the
filtration. A Lagrangian of mass dimension at most `w / 2` is an element of it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def invariantsLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_invariantsLE_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_invariantsLE_iff {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.invariantsLE w ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w
      ∧ (∀ U : GJ, T.repJet U x = x) ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
A description of the invariants of mass weight at most `w`, element by element: an
element of the filtration fixed by both groups is exactly an element of `Q`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariantsLE_eq_iff (w : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.invariantsLE w = Q ↔ ∀ x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra,
      (x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ∧ (∀ U : GJ, T.repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x) ↔ x ∈ Q

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_inf_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
A description of the invariants of mass weight at most `w` lying in a submodule `A`,
element by element.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariantsLE_inf_eq_iff (w : ℕ) (A Q : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.invariantsLE w ⊓ A = Q ↔ ∀ x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra,
      (x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ∧ x ∈ A ∧ (∀ U : GJ, T.repJet U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x) ↔ x ∈ Q

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonNormSq
declarations.doc:
**The contraction `φ† φ`** of a bosonic species with its conjugate, through a basis of
its value space: the sum over the basis of the conjugate coordinate times the coordinate.
For a scalar in a unitary representation it is the mass term.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonNormSq (j : T.BosonSpecies) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule_apply_iff
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling is respected: the weight-`n` piece is carried onto the
weight-`n` piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_apply_iff
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x))
    (n : ℕ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.massWeightSubmodule n ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_map
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_map
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x)) (n : ℕ) :
    (T.massWeightSubmodule n).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmoduleLE_map
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_map
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x)) (w : ℕ) :
    (T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeInvariants_map
declarations.doc: The gauge invariants are carried onto the gauge invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeInvariants_map (hjet : ∀ (U : GJ) x, e (T.repJet U x) = T'.repJet U (e x)) :
    T.gaugeInvariants.map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.gaugeInvariants

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzInvariants_map
declarations.doc: The Lorentz invariants are carried onto the Lorentz invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzInvariants_map
    (hlor : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) x, e (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = T'.repLorentzGroup Λ (e x)) :
    T.lorentzInvariants.map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.lorentzInvariants

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_apply_iff
declarations.doc: The filtration is respected, element by element.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_apply_iff
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x)) (w : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_invariantsLE_apply_iff
declarations.doc: The invariants of mass weight at most `w` are respected, element by element.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_invariantsLE_apply_iff (hjet : ∀ (U : GJ) x, e (T.repJet U x) = T'.repJet U (e x))
    (hlor : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) x, e (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = T'.repLorentzGroup Λ (e x))
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x)) (w : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.invariantsLE w ↔ x ∈ T.invariantsLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_map
declarations.doc:
**The invariants of mass weight at most `w` are carried onto the invariants of mass
weight at most `w`** by an isomorphism respecting the two actions and the scaling.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariantsLE_map (hjet : ∀ (U : GJ) x, e (T.repJet U x) = T'.repJet U (e x))
    (hlor : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) x, e (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = T'.repLorentzGroup Λ (e x))
    (hscale : ∀ (c : ℝ) x, e (T.massWeightScale c x) = T'.massWeightScale c (e x)) (w : ℕ) :
    (T.invariantsLE w).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.invariantsLE w

modules.title: Realizations of the local field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A complex algebra `B` carries the fields of a gauge-field datum when the local field
algebra `J(T)` maps into it by a complex algebra map equivariant for the jet gauge group
and the Lorentz group, both acting on `B` by algebra endomorphisms:
`GaugeFieldData.Realization`. The generator images are not stored: they are read off the
map as `Realization.toAssignment`, the connection factor as `Realization.gaugeRealization`
and the matter symbols as `Realization.fermionSymbol` and companions.

By the universal property of `J(T)` a realization is the same thing as a compatible
assignment of the generators satisfying the six generator-level transformation laws of
`GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant`, the connection law being affine: a jet moves a
connection generator by the transport of its inverse plus the Maurer–Cartan shift.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.Realization` : an algebra carrying the fields of a datum.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.gaugeRealization` : the gauge bosons of a realization, with
  `toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength` identifying the realized field-strength tower.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivFermion` and companions : the realized
  covariant matter towers are the towers of the realized symbols.
- `GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant` : the generator-level equivariance of an
  assignment, with `IsEquivariant.toRealization` and
  `GaugeFieldData.realizationEquivAssignment`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Realizations
- B. The assignment of a realization
- C. The gauge bosons of a realization
- D. The matter symbols and towers of a realization
- E. Equivariant assignments

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization
declarations.doc:
A complex algebra `B` carrying the fields of the datum `T`: a complex algebra map out
of the local field algebra, equivariant for the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group,
both acting on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms. No commutativity, injectivity
or surjectivity is assumed, and no derivative operator on `B` is involved. It is built
from the fields `toAlgHom`, `map_fst`, `map_snd`, `fst_mul`, `snd_mul` of
`Representation.EquivariantAlgHom`, which the lemmas `map_repJet`, `map_repLorentz`,
`repJet_mul` and `repLorentz_mul` name.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Realization (T : GaugeFieldData jets) (B : Type) [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    (repJet : Representation ℂ GJ B) (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.id
declarations.doc: The local field algebra realized in itself, by the identity.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def id : Realization T T.LocalFieldAlgebra T.repJet T.repLorentzGroup

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.id_toAlgHom
declarations.statement: lemma id_toAlgHom : (id T).toAlgHom = AlgHom.id ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.ext_generators
declarations.doc:
Two realizations agreeing on the generators of every species and on the connection
generators are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_generators {h₁ h₂ : Realization T B repJet repLorentz}
    (hf : ∀ i x, h₁.toAlgHom (T.ιFermion i x) = h₂.toAlgHom (T.ιFermion i x))
    (hb : ∀ j y, h₁.toAlgHom (T.ιBoson j y) = h₂.toAlgHom (T.ιBoson j y))
    (ha : ∀ v, h₁.toAlgHom (T.ιConnection v) = h₂.toAlgHom (T.ιConnection v)) : h₁ = h₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.map_repJet
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the jet gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repJet (U : GJ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.repJet U x) = repJet U (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.map_repLorentz
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repLorentz (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = repLorentz Λ (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.repJet_mul
declarations.doc: The jet gauge group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement: lemma repJet_mul (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B) : repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.repLorentz_mul
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment
declarations.doc:
The generator images of a realization, as a compatible assignment: the inverse of the
universal property applied to its algebra map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toAssignment : T.Assignment B

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment_fermion
declarations.statement:
lemma toAssignment_fermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    h.toAssignment.fermion i x = h.toAlgHom (T.ιFermion i x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment_boson
declarations.statement:
lemma toAssignment_boson (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)) :
    h.toAssignment.boson j y = h.toAlgHom (T.ιBoson j y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment_connection
declarations.statement:
lemma toAssignment_connection (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤) :
    h.toAssignment.connection v = h.toAlgHom (T.ιConnection v)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.lift_toAssignment
declarations.statement: lemma lift_toAssignment : h.toAssignment.lift = h.toAlgHom

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.gaugeRealization
declarations.doc:
The gauge bosons of a realization: the connection factor of `J(T)` carried into `B`,
so that the gauge-boson symbol theory applies to the images.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeRealization : GaugeAlgebraRealization jets B repJet repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.gaugeRealization_A
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeRealization_A (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    h.gaugeRealization.A s μ φ = h.toAlgHom (T.gaugeRealization.A s μ φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.id_gaugeRealization_A
declarations.statement: lemma id_gaugeRealization_A : (id T).gaugeRealization.A = T.gaugeRealization.A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The map of a realization carries the included field-strength tower to the covariant
tower of the realized gauge-boson symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivFieldStrength l μ ν φ)
      = GaugeAlgebraRealization.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint h.gaugeRealization.A l
        (GaugeAlgebraRealization.fieldStrength h.gaugeRealization.A μ ν) 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.fermionSymbol
declarations.doc: The realized derivative symbols of a fermionic species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i) →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.conjFermionSymbol
declarations.doc: The realized conjugate derivative symbols of a fermionic species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conjFermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i)) →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.bosonSymbol
declarations.doc: The realized derivative symbols of a bosonic species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j) →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.conjBosonSymbol
declarations.doc: The realized conjugate derivative symbols of a bosonic species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conjBosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j)) →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivFermion
declarations.doc:
The realized covariant tower of a fermionic species is the covariant tower of its
realized symbols, computed against the realized gauge-boson symbols. No derivative
operator on `B` is involved: both sides are the same finite algebraic expression.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivFermion i l φ)
      = GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter h.gaugeRealization.A (T.fermion i).repAlgebra
        (h.fermionSymbol i) n l 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivConjFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivConjFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ}
    (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivConjFermion i l φ)
      = GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter h.gaugeRealization.A
        (LocalGaugeData.actionConj (T.fermion i).repAlgebra) (h.conjFermionSymbol i) n l 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivBoson (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivBoson j l φ)
      = GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter h.gaugeRealization.A (T.boson j).repAlgebra
        (h.bosonSymbol j) n l 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivConjBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivConjBoson (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivConjBoson j l φ)
      = GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter h.gaugeRealization.A
        (LocalGaugeData.actionConj (T.boson j).repAlgebra) (h.conjBosonSymbol j) n l 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant
declarations.doc:
The generator-level transformation laws of an assignment: each matter species
transforms by the jet action of its own component space, and the connection generators
transform affinely, by the transport of the inverse jet plus its Maurer–Cartan shift.
The Lorentz laws are all linear. These are the laws the generators of `J(T)` themselves
satisfy.
declarations.statement:
structure Assignment.IsEquivariant {B : Type} [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B] (d : T.Assignment B)
    (repJet : Representation ℂ GJ B) (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B) : Prop where
  /-- A jet acts on the generators of a fermionic species by the action of its component
    space. -/
  repJet_fermion : ∀ (U : GJ) (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)),
    repJet U (d.fermion i x) = d.fermion i (JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.fermion i) U x)
  /-- A jet acts on the generators of a bosonic species by the action of its component
    space. -/
  repJet_boson : ∀ (U : GJ) (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)),
    repJet U (d.boson j y) = d.boson j (JetComponentSpace.repJet (T.boson j) U y)
  /-- A jet acts affinely on the connection generators. -/
  repJet_connection : ∀ (U : GJ) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤),
    repJet U (d.connection v) = d.connection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.transport jets U⁻¹ v)
      + (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.mcShift jets U⁻¹ v : ℂ) • (1 : B)
  /-- A Lorentz transformation acts on the generators of a fermionic species by the action
    of its component space. -/
  repLorentz_fermion : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : JetComponentSpace (T.fermion i)), repLorentz Λ (d.fermion i x)
      = d.fermion i (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)
  /-- A Lorentz transformation acts on the generators of a bosonic species by the action of
    its component space. -/
  repLorentz_boson : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : JetComponentSpace (T.boson j)), repLorentz Λ (d.boson j y)
      = d.boson j (JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson j) Λ y)
  /-- A Lorentz transformation acts linearly on the connection generators. -/
  repLorentz_connection : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤),
    repLorentz Λ (d.connection v)
      = d.connection (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace.repLorentzGroup 𝔤 Λ v)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment_isEquivariant
declarations.doc:
The assignment of a realization is equivariant: the laws are those of the generators of
`J(T)`, transported along the map.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAssignment_isEquivariant
    (h : Realization T B repJet repLorentz) :
    h.toAssignment.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant.lift_comp_repJetAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The lift of an equivariant assignment intertwines the jet gauge actions, as an equality
of algebra maps: both sides agree on the generators of every species and on the
connection generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.lift_comp_repJetAlgHom {d : T.Assignment B}
    (hd : d.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz)
    (hJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B), repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂) (U : GJ) :
    d.lift.comp (T.repJetAlgHom U) = (repJet.toAlgHom hJ U).comp d.lift

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant.lift_comp_repLorentzAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The lift of an equivariant assignment intertwines the Lorentz actions, as an equality of
algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.lift_comp_repLorentzAlgHom {d : T.Assignment B}
    (hd : d.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz)
    (hL : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    d.lift.comp (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ) = (repLorentz.toAlgHom hL Λ).comp d.lift

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant.toRealization
declarations.doc:
An equivariant assignment lifts to a realization: each equivariance law is an equality
of two algebra maps agreeing on the generators, so it follows from the generator laws by
the universal property.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsEquivariant.toRealization {d : T.Assignment B}
    (hd : d.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz)
    (hJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B), repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂)
    (hL : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂) :
    Realization T B repJet repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Assignment.IsEquivariant.toRealization_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma IsEquivariant.toRealization_toAlgHom {d : T.Assignment B}
    (hd : d.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz)
    (hJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B), repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂)
    (hL : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂) :
    (hd.toRealization hJ hL).toAlgHom = d.lift

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.realizationEquivAssignment
declarations.doc:
The mapping-out universal property of `J(T)` in equivariant form: for target actions by
algebra endomorphisms, realizations of `T` in `B` are exactly the equivariant compatible
assignments of its generators.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def realizationEquivAssignment {B : Type} [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    {repJet : Representation ℂ GJ B} {repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B}
    (hJ : ∀ (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B), repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂)
    (hL : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B),
      repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂) :
    {d : T.Assignment B // d.IsEquivariant repJet repLorentz}
      ≃ Realization T B repJet repLorentz

modules.title: The ordinary sector algebras of the local field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A sector is a finite set of `GaugeFieldData.FieldCategory`, chosen among `fermion`, `gauge`
and `scalar`. It selects ordinary generator families of the local field algebra `J(T)` of a
field datum: the derivative symbols `∂_s ψ` of every fermionic species and their conjugates
for `fermion`, those of every bosonic species and their conjugates for `scalar`, and the
connection symbols `∂_s A_μ` for `gauge`. The ordinary sector algebra `T.SectorAlgebra S`
is the complex unital subalgebra of `J(T)` generated by the selected families.

The category `scalar` names the bosonic species `T.BosonSpecies` of the datum; a bosonic
`MatterField` need not be a Lorentz scalar, and the selection does not assert that it is.
A sector selects generator families only: no multiplicity of fields, mass dimension, gauge
invariance or Lagrangian term is encoded.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.FieldCategory` : the three categories of fields.
- `GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra` : the ordinary sector algebra of a sector, with
  `SectorAlgebra.induction` and `SectorAlgebra.algHom_ext`.
- `SectorAlgebra.mono`, `SectorAlgebra.empty`, `SectorAlgebra.univ`,
  `SectorAlgebra.union` : the lattice laws of the selection.
- `SectorAlgebra.repJet`, `SectorAlgebra.repLorentzGroup` : the restricted actions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Field categories and their ordinary generators
- B. The ordinary sector algebra
  - B.1. Membership of the selected families
  - B.2. Generation
  - B.3. The lattice laws of the selection
- C. Stability under the actions
- D. The restricted actions

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Field categories and their ordinary generators
## B. The ordinary sector algebra
### B.1. Membership of the selected families
### B.2. Generation
### B.3. The lattice laws of the selection

## C. Stability under the actions

Each generator law of `J(T)` stays inside the family of the generator it acts on, the
connection law up to a scalar shift, so both actions preserve every sector algebra.

## D. The restricted actions

The restricted actions of two nested sectors agree along `Subalgebra.inclusion`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.FieldCategory
declarations.doc: The categories of fields a sector may select.
declarations.statement:
inductive FieldCategory where
  /-- The fermionic species. -/
  | fermion : FieldCategory
  /-- The gauge bosons. -/
  | gauge : FieldCategory
  /-- The bosonic species. -/
  | scalar : FieldCategory
deriving DecidableEq

lemma sectorGenerators_cases {P : T.LocalFieldAlgebra → Prop} {b : T.LocalFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.sectorGenerators S)
    (hf : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S → ∀ v, P (T.ιFermionTotal v))

    (hg : FieldCategory.gauge ∈ S → ∀ v, P (T.ιConnection v)) : P b

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.induction
declarations.doc:
A property holding on the selected generators and the scalars and closed under sums
and products holds on the sector algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma induction {P : T.LocalFieldAlgebra → Prop} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.SectorAlgebra S)
    (hf : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S → ∀ v, P (T.ιFermionTotal v))
    (hs : FieldCategory.scalar ∈ S → ∀ v, P (T.ιBosonTotal v))
    (hg : FieldCategory.gauge ∈ S → ∀ v, P (T.ιConnection v))
    (halg : ∀ z : ℂ, P (z • (1 : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)))
    (hadd : ∀ x y, P x → P y → P (x + y))
    (hmul : ∀ x y, P x → P y → P (x * y)) : P x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.algHom_ext
declarations.doc:
Two algebra maps out of a sector algebra agreeing on the selected generators are
equal. This is uniqueness only: a sector algebra is not free on its generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma algHom_ext {B : Type} [Semiring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    {f g : ↥(T.SectorAlgebra S) →ₐ[ℂ] B}
    (hf : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S) (v : T.FermionGenerators),
      f ⟨T.ιFermionTotal v, ιFermionTotal_mem hS v⟩ = g ⟨T.ιFermionTotal v, ιFermionTotal_mem hS v⟩)
    (hs : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.scalar ∈ S) (v : T.BosonGenerators),
      f ⟨T.ιBosonTotal v, ιBosonTotal_mem hS v⟩ = g ⟨T.ιBosonTotal v, ιBosonTotal_mem hS v⟩)
    (hg : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.gauge ∈ S) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤),
      f ⟨T.ιConnection v, ιConnection_mem hS v⟩ = g ⟨T.ιConnection v, ιConnection_mem hS v⟩) :
    f = g

declarations.statement: lemma univ : T.SectorAlgebra Finset.univ = ⊤

    T.repLorentzGroup Λ x ∈ T.SectorAlgebra S
