declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acting on a sector algebra, by restriction.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) (T.SectorAlgebra S)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.coe_repJet
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_repJet (U : GJ) (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    (repJet T S U x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = T.repJet U x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.repJet_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_apply_mul (U : GJ) (x y : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    repJet T S U (x * y) = repJet T S U x * repJet T S U y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.coe_repLorentzGroup
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_repLorentzGroup (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    (repLorentzGroup T S Λ x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = T.repLorentzGroup Λ x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    repLorentzGroup T S Λ (x * y) = repLorentzGroup T S Λ x * repLorentzGroup T S Λ y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.inclusion_repJet
declarations.statement:
lemma inclusion_repJet {S' : Finset FieldCategory} (h : S ⊆ S') (U : GJ) (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T h) (repJet T S U x)
      = repJet T S' U (Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T h) x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.inclusion_repLorentzGroup
declarations.statement:
lemma inclusion_repLorentzGroup {S' : Finset FieldCategory} (h : S ⊆ S') (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T h) (repLorentzGroup T S Λ x)
      = repLorentzGroup T S' Λ (Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T h) x)

modules.title: Realizations of the ordinary sector algebras
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A complex algebra `B` carries the ordinary sector `S` of a field datum when the sector
algebra `T.SectorAlgebra S` maps into it by a complex algebra map equivariant for the jet
gauge group and the Lorentz group, both acting on `B` by algebra endomorphisms:
`GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization`. No species condition is involved.

A sector realization is determined by its images of the selected generators
(`Realization.ext_generators`); nothing asserts that an arbitrary assignment of those images
extends to a realization. Realizations restrict along `Subalgebra.inclusion` from the local
field algebra to every sector and from a sector to every smaller one, and successive
restrictions agree with the direct one.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization` : an algebra carrying an ordinary sector.
- `GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict` : restriction to a smaller sector,
  with `restrict_restrict`.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector` : restriction of a realization of the local
  field algebra to a sector, with `restrict_restrictSector`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Sector realizations
- B. Restriction to a smaller sector
- C. Restriction from the local field algebra

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Restriction to a smaller sector
## C. Restriction from the local field algebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization
declarations.doc:
A complex algebra `B` carrying the ordinary sector `S` of the datum `T`: a complex
algebra map out of the sector algebra, equivariant for the jet gauge group and the Lorentz
group, both acting on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms. The lemmas `map_repJet`,
`map_repLorentz`, `repJet_mul` and `repLorentz_mul` name its fields.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Realization (T : GaugeFieldData jets) (S : Finset FieldCategory) (B : Type)
    [Semiring B] [Algebra ℂ B] (repJet : Representation ℂ GJ B)
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.id
declarations.doc: A sector algebra realized in itself, by the identity.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def id :
    Realization T S (T.SectorAlgebra S) (SectorAlgebra.repJet T S)
      (SectorAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T S)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.id_toAlgHom
declarations.statement: lemma id_toAlgHom : (id T S).toAlgHom = AlgHom.id ℂ (T.SectorAlgebra S)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.map_repJet
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repJet (U : GJ) (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    h.toAlgHom (SectorAlgebra.repJet T S U x) = repJet U (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.map_repLorentz
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repLorentz (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    h.toAlgHom (SectorAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T S Λ x) = repLorentz Λ (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.repJet_mul
declarations.statement: lemma repJet_mul (U : GJ) (b₁ b₂ : B) : repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.repLorentz_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.ext_generators
declarations.doc:
A sector realization is determined by its images of the selected generators. Only
uniqueness is asserted, not the extension of an arbitrary assignment.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_generators {h₁ h₂ : Realization T S B repJet repLorentz}
    (hf : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S) (v : T.FermionGenerators),
      h₁.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιFermionTotal v, ιFermionTotal_mem hS v⟩
        = h₂.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιFermionTotal v, ιFermionTotal_mem hS v⟩)
    (hs : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.scalar ∈ S) (v : T.BosonGenerators),
      h₁.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιBosonTotal v, ιBosonTotal_mem hS v⟩
        = h₂.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιBosonTotal v, ιBosonTotal_mem hS v⟩)
    (hg : ∀ (hS : FieldCategory.gauge ∈ S) (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace 𝔤),
      h₁.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιConnection v, ιConnection_mem hS v⟩
        = h₂.toAlgHom ⟨T.ιConnection v, ιConnection_mem hS v⟩) : h₁ = h₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict
declarations.doc: The restriction of a sector realization to a smaller sector.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrict (h : Realization T S' B repJet repLorentz) (hS : S ⊆ S') :
    Realization T S B repJet repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_toAlgHom (h : Realization T S' B repJet repLorentz) (hS : S ⊆ S') :
    (h.restrict hS).toAlgHom = h.toAlgHom.comp (Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T hS))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_toAlgHom_apply (h : Realization T S' B repJet repLorentz) (hS : S ⊆ S')
    (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    (h.restrict hS).toAlgHom x = h.toAlgHom (Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T hS) x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict_toAlgHom_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_toAlgHom_mk (h : Realization T S' B repJet repLorentz) (hS : S ⊆ S')
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) (hx : x ∈ T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    (h.restrict hS).toAlgHom ⟨x, hx⟩ = h.toAlgHom ⟨x, mono T hS hx⟩

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict_id_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_id_toAlgHom (hS : S ⊆ S') :
    ((id T S').restrict hS).toAlgHom = Subalgebra.inclusion (mono T hS)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.SectorAlgebra.Realization.restrict_restrict
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_restrict {S'' : Finset FieldCategory} (h : Realization T S'' B repJet repLorentz)
    (hS' : S' ⊆ S'') (hS : S ⊆ S') :
    (h.restrict hS').restrict hS = h.restrict (hS.trans hS')

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector
declarations.doc: The restriction of a realization of the local field algebra to a sector.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def restrictSector : SectorAlgebra.Realization T S B repJet repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_toAlgHom :
    (h.restrictSector S).toAlgHom = h.toAlgHom.comp (T.SectorAlgebra S).val

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_toAlgHom_apply (x : T.SectorAlgebra S) :
    (h.restrictSector S).toAlgHom x = h.toAlgHom x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_id_toAlgHom
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_id_toAlgHom :
    ((id T).restrictSector S).toAlgHom = (T.SectorAlgebra S).val

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_fermionSymbol
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_fermionSymbol (hS : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    (h.restrictSector S).toAlgHom ⟨T.fermionSymbol i s φ, SectorAlgebra.fermionSymbol_mem hS i s φ⟩
      = h.fermionSymbol i s φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_conjFermionSymbol
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_conjFermionSymbol (hS : FieldCategory.fermion ∈ S)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    (h.restrictSector S).toAlgHom
      ⟨T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ, SectorAlgebra.conjFermionSymbol_mem hS i s φ⟩
      = h.conjFermionSymbol i s φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_bosonSymbol
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_bosonSymbol (hS : FieldCategory.scalar ∈ S) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    (h.restrictSector S).toAlgHom ⟨T.bosonSymbol j s φ, SectorAlgebra.bosonSymbol_mem hS j s φ⟩
      = h.bosonSymbol j s φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrictSector_conjBosonSymbol
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictSector_conjBosonSymbol (hS : FieldCategory.scalar ∈ S) (j : T.BosonSpecies)

modules.title: The field symbols of the local field algebra and their transformation laws
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The generators of the local field algebra `J(T)` of a field datum are the derivative
symbols of its species: `∂_s ψ^φ`, indexed by a derivative multiset `s` and a covector `φ`
of the value space, the conjugate symbols `∂_s ψ̄^φ`, indexed by a covector of the
conjugate value space, and the gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` of the connection factor.
This file packages the matter symbols of each species as families over `s` and proves
their two transformation laws, `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn` for the jet gauge action and
`IsLorentzDerivTransforms` for the Lorentz action, and packages the connection factor as
a realization of the gauge bosons in `J(T)`, so that the covariant derivative theory of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.CovariantDeriv` applies inside `J(T)`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeRealization` : the connection factor as a realization of the gauge
  bosons in `J(T)`.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionSymbol`, `GaugeFieldData.conjFermionSymbol`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonSymbol`, `GaugeFieldData.conjBosonSymbol` : the matter symbols.
- `GaugeFieldData.transformsIn_fermionSymbol`,
  `GaugeFieldData.isLorentzDerivTransforms_fermionSymbol` and companions : their gauge
  and Lorentz laws.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The connection factor as a realization of the gauge bosons
- B. The matter symbol families
- C. The jet gauge transformation of the matter symbols
- D. The Lorentz transformation of the matter symbols

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The connection factor as a realization of the gauge bosons
## B. The matter symbol families

## C. The jet gauge transformation of the matter symbols

Each symbol map intertwines the jet gauge action on `J(T)` with `JetComponentSpace.repDual`
on its half of the component space, and the law of the symbols is
`JetComponentSpace.repDual_basis_tmul` pushed through the symbol map.

## D. The Lorentz transformation of the matter symbols

Each symbol map intertwines the Lorentz action on `J(T)` with the tensor product of the
action on derivative labels and the contragredient action on the value index, and the law
of the symbols is that of the derivative monomials,
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.repLorentzGroup_basis_ofFn`.

modules.title: The Taylor coefficients of the adjoint action
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A gauge jet `U` acts on the gauge algebra of jets by the adjoint action `Ad_U`. What the
transformation law of a gauge field `A_μ ↦ Ad_U A_μ + ω_μ(U)` sees of `Ad_U`, after
differentiating `x` times and evaluating at the base point, is the physicists'
`∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀`: a linear map `adjointCoeff U x : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤` on the constant gauge
algebra, and its transpose `adjointDualCoeff U x` on the dual index carried by the field
symbols. This file develops these coefficients for any package `jets`.

The central result is the Taylor–Leibniz theorem `evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjointJ`: the
base-point Taylor coefficients of `Ad_U Y` for an arbitrary jet `Y` are the antidiagonal
convolution of the coefficients of `Ad_U` with those of `Y`. For a matrix group it is the
Leibniz rule for products of matrices of power series; here it is derived from the Leibniz
rule `deriv_adjoint` for a single derivative, by induction on the number of derivatives.
Its corollaries are the multiplicativity `adjointCoeff_mul` of the coefficients up to
convolution, and the recursion `adjointCoeff_cons` expressing one more derivative of a
coefficient through the Maurer–Cartan form.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff` : the coefficient `∂_x (Ad_U)|₀`, with its values
  `adjointCoeff_zero` at the base point and `adjointCoeff_one` on the identity jet.
- `LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_cons` : one more derivative of a coefficient is minus the
  antidiagonal convolution of `ad` of the derived Maurer–Cartan form against lower
  coefficients.
- `LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjointJ` : the Taylor–Leibniz theorem.
- `LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_mul` : the coefficients of a product are the convolution
  of the coefficients of the factors.
- `LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff` : the transposed coefficients, with
  `adjointDualCoeff_singleton`, `adjointDualCoeff_pair` and `adjointDualCoeff_cons`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint Taylor coefficients
- B. The recursion through the Maurer–Cartan form
- C. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem
- D. The dual coefficients

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The adjoint Taylor coefficients
## B. The recursion through the Maurer–Cartan form
## C. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem
## D. The dual coefficients

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀`: include a constant gauge algebra element into
jets, act by the adjoint of `U`, differentiate `x` times, and evaluate at the base
point. For `x = 0` this is the adjoint action of the value of `U`; for `x ≠ 0` it sees
the derivatives of the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjointCoeff (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_apply (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤) :
    jets.adjointCoeff U x a =
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv x (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie a)))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_zero
declarations.doc: The zeroth coefficient is the adjoint action of the value of the jet.
declarations.statement: lemma adjointCoeff_zero (U : GJ) : jets.adjointCoeff U 0 = jets.adjoint (jets.eval U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc: A jet with trivial value has trivial zeroth coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : GJ} (hU : jets.eval U = 1) :
    jets.adjointCoeff U 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_one
declarations.doc: The coefficients of the identity jet: only the base point survives.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_one (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.adjointCoeff (1 : GJ) p = if p = 0 then LinearMap.id else 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_lie
declarations.doc:
The coefficients are derivations of the bracket up to convolution, by the iterated
Leibniz rule for the jet bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_lie (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a b : 𝔤) :
    jets.adjointCoeff U x ⁅a, b⁆ =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => ⁅jets.adjointCoeff U p.1 a, jets.adjointCoeff U p.2 b⁆).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.deriv_adjoint_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc:
One derivative of the adjoint action on a constant is minus the bracket with the
Maurer–Cartan form: the Leibniz rule `deriv_adjoint` with the constant's derivative
killed.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_adjoint_ofConstantLie (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤) :
    jets.deriv μ (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie a)) =
      -⁅jets.maurerCartan U μ, jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie a)⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
One more derivative of a coefficient: differentiating the adjoint once produces minus
`ad` of the Maurer–Cartan form, and the remaining derivatives distribute over the bracket
by the Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_cons (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.adjointCoeff U (μ ::ₘ x) =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤 (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.1 (jets.maurerCartan U μ))) ∘ₗ
          jets.adjointCoeff U p.2).sum)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjoint_cons
declarations.doc:
The inductive step of the Taylor–Leibniz theorem: the rule for `μ ::ₘ s` derivatives
follows from the rule for every sub-multiset of `s`. Peeling off `∂_μ` by the Leibniz
rule `deriv_adjoint` leaves `Ad_U (∂_μ Y)`, handled by the rule for `s`, and a bracket
with the Maurer–Cartan form, handled by the rule for the parts of `s`; on the other side
the coefficients at `μ ::ₘ p` unfold by `adjointCoeff_cons`, and the two triple sums
agree by coassociativity of the antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjoint_cons (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (Y : 𝔤J)
    (ih : ∀ t ≤ s, ∀ Z : 𝔤J, jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv t (jets.adjointJ U Z)) =
      (t.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        jets.adjointCoeff U p.1 (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.2 Z))).sum) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv (μ ::ₘ s) (jets.adjointJ U Y)) =
      ((μ ::ₘ s).antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        jets.adjointCoeff U p.1 (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.2 Y))).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjointJ
declarations.doc:
The Taylor–Leibniz theorem for the adjoint action: the base-point Taylor coefficients
of `Ad_U Y` are the antidiagonal convolution of the coefficients `adjointCoeff U` of
`Ad_U` with those of `Y`. For a matrix group this is the Leibniz rule for products of
matrices of power series; here it follows from the single-derivative Leibniz rule
`deriv_adjoint` by strong induction on the number of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjointJ (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (Y : 𝔤J) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv x (jets.adjointJ U Y)) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        jets.adjointCoeff U p.1 (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.2 Y))).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjoint_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor data of `Ad_U Y` vanish up to a given order whenever those of
`Y` do.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_mul
declarations.doc:
The coefficients are multiplicative up to convolution: the coefficient of a product of
jets is the antidiagonal convolution of the coefficients of the factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_mul (U V : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jets.adjointCoeff (U * V) x =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => jets.adjointCoeff U p.1 ∘ₗ jets.adjointCoeff V p.2).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀` acting on the dual adjoint index of a gauge-field
symbol: the transpose of `adjointCoeff U x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointDualCoeff (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_apply (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤)
    (a : 𝔤) : jets.adjointDualCoeff U x φ a = φ (jets.adjointCoeff U x a)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_zero
declarations.doc:
The zeroth dual coefficient is the dual of the adjoint action of the value of the
jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_zero (U : GJ) :
    jets.adjointDualCoeff U 0 = (jets.adjoint (jets.eval U)).dualMap

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc: A jet with trivial value has trivial zeroth dual coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : GJ} (hU : jets.eval U = 1) :
    jets.adjointDualCoeff U 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
The dual form of `adjointCoeff_cons`: one more derivative of a dual coefficient is
minus the antidiagonal convolution of lower dual coefficients against `ad` of the derived
Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_cons (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    jets.adjointDualCoeff U (μ ::ₘ x) φ =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        jets.adjointDualCoeff U p.2 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤
          (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.1 (jets.maurerCartan U μ))))).sum)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_singleton
declarations.doc:
The dual coefficient at a single derivative is minus the underived coefficient
precomposed with `ad` of the base-point Maurer–Cartan form. This is what cancels the
Leibniz cross terms of the gauge law against the commutator cross terms in the field
strength.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_singleton (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    jets.adjointDualCoeff U {μ} φ =
      -jets.adjointDualCoeff U 0 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤
        (jets.evalLie (jets.maurerCartan U μ)))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_pair
declarations.doc:
The dual coefficient at two derivatives: the underived coefficient against `ad` of the
derived Maurer–Cartan form, and the once-derived coefficient against `ad` of the
Maurer–Cartan form itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_pair (U : GJ) (ρ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    jets.adjointDualCoeff U (ρ ::ₘ {μ}) φ =
      -jets.adjointDualCoeff U 0 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤
        (jets.evalLie (jets.deriv ρ (jets.maurerCartan U μ))))
      - jets.adjointDualCoeff U {ρ} (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ 𝔤
        (jets.evalLie (jets.maurerCartan U μ)))

modules.title: Local gauge data: further consequences of the laws
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The structure `LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J`, its iterated derivative and its morphisms are
defined in `Physlib.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Basic`. This file adds the
consequences of its laws used by the rest of the gauge theory in `PhyslibAlpha`:

* the values of the Maurer–Cartan form on the identity and on inverses, from the cocycle law;
* the fact that the Maurer–Cartan form is determined by the Leibniz rule `deriv_adjointJ` up
  to the centre of `𝔤J`, which is why it is a field of the structure;
* the base-point Taylor data of a bracket, as a function of that of its arguments;
* the mixin `Faithful`. The transformation laws never ask that the jets be *honest* jets, and
  `Faithful` records two properties which are true of any honest jet group but are not
  consequences of the laws: an element of `𝔤J` is determined by its base-point Taylor data,
  and a jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form is constant. The stronger mixin `Free`, in
  `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Truncation`, adds that every
  Taylor family is realised.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_one`, `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_inv` : the values of the
  Maurer–Cartan form on the identity and on inverses.
- `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_eq_of_deriv_adjointJ` : the Maurer–Cartan form is determined
  by the Leibniz rule `deriv_adjointJ` up to the centre of `𝔤J`.
- `LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_bracket_congr` : the base-point Taylor data of a bracket
  is determined by that of its arguments.
- `LocalGaugeData.Faithful` : the jets are determined by their base-point Taylor data.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. First consequences of the laws
- B. The Taylor data of a bracket
- C. Faithful packages

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. First consequences of the laws
## B. The Taylor data of a bracket

## C. Faithful packages

The two laws below make a pure jet (`eval U = 1`) recoverable from its Maurer–Cartan form;
see `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero`. They hold for the full jet group of
any matrix group and for its truncations, but are recorded separately from the structure
because the covariance theory does not need them.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_one
declarations.doc: The Maurer–Cartan form of the identity vanishes: the cocycle law at `1 * 1 = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma maurerCartan_one (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : jets.maurerCartan 1 μ = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_inv
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form of an inverse: `ω_μ(U⁻¹) = − Ad_{U⁻¹} ω_μ(U)`, the cocycle
law applied to `U⁻¹ U = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_inv (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.maurerCartan U⁻¹ μ = - jets.adjointJ U⁻¹ (jets.maurerCartan U μ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_adjointJ_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc:
At the base point, the adjoint action of a jet on a constant is the adjoint action of
its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_adjointJ_ofConstantLie (U : GJ) (a : 𝔤) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie a)) = jets.adjoint (jets.eval U) a

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_eq_of_deriv_adjointJ
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form is determined by the Leibniz rule, up to the centre. Since
`adjointJ U` is invertible, `deriv_adjointJ` says exactly that the inner derivation
`⁅maurerCartan U μ, ·⁆` is `adjointJ U ∘ deriv μ ∘ adjointJ U⁻¹ − deriv μ`; so any other
form obeying the same rule differs from it by something acting trivially in the adjoint
representation of `𝔤J`. It follows that the Maurer–Cartan form is redundant data exactly
when that representation is faithful — which it is not for the Standard Model, whose jet
gauge algebra has a central `u(1)` factor. That is why `maurerCartan` is a field of the
structure rather than a construction from the rest of it.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_eq_of_deriv_adjointJ
    (hfaithful : ∀ x y : 𝔤J, (∀ z : 𝔤J, ⁅x, z⁆ = ⁅y, z⁆) → x = y)
    (ω : GJ → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J)
    (hω : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : 𝔤J),
      jets.deriv μ (jets.adjointJ U x)
        = jets.adjointJ U (jets.deriv μ x) - ⁅ω U μ, jets.adjointJ U x⁆) :
    ω = jets.maurerCartan

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_bracket_congr
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor data of a bracket is determined by that of its arguments.
If the base-point values of the iterated derivatives of `a` and `b` along sub-multisets
of `w` agree with those of `a'` and `b'`, then so do those of the brackets: the iterated
Leibniz rule expands the bracket over the antidiagonal of `w`, whose parts are all
sub-multisets of `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_bracket_congr (w : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a b a' b' : 𝔤J)
    (ha : ∀ p ≤ w, jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p a)
      = jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p a'))
    (hb : ∀ p ≤ w, jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p b)
      = jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p b')) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv w ⁅a, b⁆)
      = jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv w ⁅a', b'⁆)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Faithful
declarations.doc:
A package is faithful when an element of `𝔤J` is determined by the base-point values
of its iterated derivatives (Taylor determinacy) and a jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan
form is the constant jet of its value.
declarations.statement:
class Faithful (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) : Prop where
  ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDeriv : ∀ {x y : 𝔤J},
    (∀ s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s x) = jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s y)) → x = y
  eq_ofConstant_of_maurerCartan_eq_zero : ∀ {U : GJ},
    jets.maurerCartan U = 0 → U = jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: Taylor determinacy of a faithful package, in the form of an extensionality lemma.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDeriv [jets.Faithful] {x y : 𝔤J}
    (h : ∀ s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s x) = jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s y)) :
    x = y

modules.title: The factors of a gauge group
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A gauge group is presented, as in a model-building table, by its factors: `U(1)` factors
and `SU(n)` factors. This file says what a factor of a local gauge data package is, without
reference to matter:

* `LocalGaugeData.U1Factor` : a unitary jet `u U` attached to each gauge jet, with the
  matching components `φ`, `φJ` of the gauge algebra and its jets, related by the
  Maurer–Cartan form `φJ (ω_μ U) = i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹` and invariant under the adjoint action;
* `LocalGaugeData.SUFactor` : a unitary matrix of jets `u U` attached to each gauge jet,
  with the matching matrix components `φ`, `φJ`, related by the Maurer–Cartan form
  `φJ (ω_μ U) = i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹` and transforming by conjugation under the adjoint action;
* `LocalGaugeData.Factor`, `Factors` : a factor of either kind, and a gauge group as a
  list of factors.

Factors pull back along a morphism of local gauge data, `LocalGaugeData.Hom`
(`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Basic`). The projections of a
product are such morphisms
(`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Prod`), which is how a factor of
one side becomes a factor of the product.

The canonical factors of the concrete packages are `LocalGaugeData.u1Factor` and
`LocalGaugeData.suFactor`, and the representations
a factor names (the charge twist, the fundamental) are built in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.MatrixRep.Factors`.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.U1Factor` : a `U(1)` factor of the local gauge data.
- `LocalGaugeData.SUFactor` : an `SU(n)` factor of the local gauge data.
- `LocalGaugeData.Factor`, `LocalGaugeData.Factors` : a gauge group presented by its factors.
- `LocalGaugeData.Factors.comap` : pulling factors back along a morphism.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. `U(1)` factors
- B. `SU(n)` factors
- C. A gauge group as a list of factors
- D. Pulling factors back along a morphism

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. `U(1)` factors
## B. `SU(n)` factors
## C. A gauge group as a list of factors
## D. Pulling factors back along a morphism

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.U1Factor
declarations.doc:
**A `U(1)` factor** of the local gauge data: a unitary jet `u U` attached to each gauge
jet, with the corresponding components `φ c` of the gauge algebra and `φJ a` of its jets,
related by the Maurer–Cartan form `φJ (ω_μ U) = i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹` and invariant under the
adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
structure U1Factor (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) where
  /-- The unitary jet of a gauge jet. -/
  u : GJ →* unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra
  /-- The `u(1)` component of a gauge algebra element. -/
  φ : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] ℂ
  /-- The `u(1)` component of a jet of gauge algebra elements. -/
  φJ : 𝔤J → SpaceTimeAlgebra
  φJ_ofConstantLie : ∀ c, φJ (jets.ofConstantLie c) = C (φ c)
  φJ_cc_foldl : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J),
    constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p (φJ a))
      = φ (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p a))
  φJ_maurerCartan : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    φJ (jets.maurerCartan U μ)
      = Complex.I • (pderiv μ (u U : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * star (u U : SpaceTimeAlgebra))
  φJ_adjoint : ∀ (U : GJ) (c : 𝔤),
    φJ (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie c)) = φJ (jets.ofConstantLie c)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SUFactor
declarations.doc:
**An `SU(n)` factor** of the local gauge data: a unitary matrix of jets `u U` attached
to each gauge jet, with the corresponding matrix components `φ c` of the gauge algebra
and `φJ a` of its jets, related by the Maurer–Cartan form `φJ (ω_μ U) = i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹`
and transforming by conjugation under the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
structure SUFactor (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) (n : Type) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    where
  /-- The unitary matrix of jets of a gauge jet. -/
  u : GJ →* Matrix n n SpaceTimeAlgebra
  u_unitary : ∀ U, star (u U) * u U = 1
  /-- The matrix component of a gauge algebra element. -/
  φ : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix n n ℂ
  /-- The matrix component of a jet of gauge algebra elements. -/
  φJ : 𝔤J → Matrix n n SpaceTimeAlgebra
  φJ_ofConstantLie : ∀ c, φJ (jets.ofConstantLie c) = (φ c).map (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra)
  φJ_cc_foldl : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J),
    ((φJ a).map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p f))
      = φ (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p a))
  φJ_maurerCartan : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    φJ (jets.maurerCartan U μ)
      = Complex.I • (((u U).map fun f => pderiv μ f) * star (u U))
  φJ_adjoint : ∀ (U : GJ) (c : 𝔤),
    φJ (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie c)) = u U * φJ (jets.ofConstantLie c) * star (u U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Factor
declarations.doc:
**A factor of the gauge group**, presented in the local gauge data: a `U(1)` factor or
an `SU(n)` factor.
declarations.statement:
inductive Factor (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J)
  /-- A `U(1)` factor. -/
  | U1 (F : U1Factor jets)
  /-- An `SU(n)` factor. -/
  | SU {n : ℕ} (F : SUFactor jets (Fin n))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Factors
declarations.doc: **A gauge group presented by its factors.**
declarations.statement: abbrev Factors (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) : Type

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.U1Factor.comap
declarations.doc: A `U(1)` factor pulled back along a morphism.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def U1Factor.comap (F : U1Factor jets') (h : Hom jets jets') : U1Factor jets

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SUFactor.comap
declarations.doc: An `SU(n)` factor pulled back along a morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def SUFactor.comap {n : Type} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (F : SUFactor jets' n)
    (h : Hom jets jets') : SUFactor jets n

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Factor.comap
declarations.doc: A factor pulled back along a morphism.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev Factor.comap (h : Hom jets jets') : Factor jets' → Factor jets

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Factors.comap
declarations.doc:
A list of factors pulled back along a morphism. Written by recursion rather than as
`List.map`, so that it unfolds at reducible transparency, as the charge tuples of a table
over `Factors.factors` require.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev Factors.comap (h : Hom jets jets') : Factors jets' → Factors jets

modules.title: Matrix jet groups
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`U(1)` and `SU(n)` present their local gauge data in the same way: the gauge jets are
unitary matrices of jets, the Lie algebra jets are hermitian matrices of jets, evaluation is
the entrywise constant coefficient, constants embed entrywise, the derivative and the
coordinates act entrywise, the adjoint action is conjugation `U a U†` and the Maurer–Cartan
form is `i (∂_μ U) U†`. Every law of `LocalGaugeData` then follows from matrix identities
over the jet ring.

`MatrixJets` records such a presentation: injective maps of the four carriers into matrices,
and what each structure map is in matrices. From it, `MatrixJets.toLocalGaugeData` proves
the laws once, `MatrixJets.faithful` shows the package is faithful, `MatrixJets.free`
reduces its freeness to three conditions on the carriers, and `MatrixJets.suFactor` is its
canonical `SU`-type factor. The concrete packages `u1` and
`su n` are instances.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets` : a presentation of gauge jets by matrices of jets.
- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.toLocalGaugeData` : the local gauge data it presents.
- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.faithful` : that local gauge data is faithful.
- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.suFactor` : its canonical `SU`-type factor.
- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.free` : a criterion for that local gauge data to be free.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The presentation
- B. The local gauge data
- C. The iterated derivative and faithfulness
- D. The canonical factor
- E. Freeness

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The presentation

## B. The local gauge data

Every law is an identity of matrices, read through the injective maps `lieJ` and `toMat₀`.
## C. The iterated derivative and faithfulness
## D. The canonical factor

## E. Freeness

A presentation by matrices is free when its carriers are large enough: the Lie algebra
jets contain every matrix of jets with Taylor data in the Lie algebra, and the gauge jets
contain the unitary fundamental solution `V` of the radial system `E V = −i P V` for every
Lie algebra jet `P`. Taylor completeness and radial integrability then hold because they
hold for matrices of jets.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets
declarations.doc:
**A presentation of gauge jets by matrices**: the value group, its Lie algebra, the jet
group and its Lie algebra of jets embed into `κ × κ` matrices, and every structure map of
the local gauge data is what it is for matrices: the entrywise constant coefficient,
inclusion of constants, derivative and coordinate multiplication, conjugation for the
adjoint actions and `i (∂_μ U) U†` for the Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
structure MatrixJets (κ : Type) [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (G₀ : Type) [Group G₀]
    (𝔤 : Type) [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤] (GJ : Type) [Group GJ]
    (𝔤J : Type) [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J] where
  /-- The matrix of a value. -/
  toMat₀ : G₀ →* Matrix κ κ ℂ
  toMat₀_injective : Function.Injective toMat₀
  /-- The matrix of jets of a gauge jet. -/
  toMatJ : GJ →* Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra
  toMatJ_injective : Function.Injective toMatJ
  toMatJ_mul_star : ∀ U, toMatJ U * star (toMatJ U) = 1
  star_toMatJ_mul : ∀ U, star (toMatJ U) * toMatJ U = 1
  /-- The matrix of a Lie algebra element. -/
  lie₀ : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix κ κ ℂ
  lie₀_injective : Function.Injective lie₀
  lie₀_bracket : ∀ a b, lie₀ ⁅a, b⁆ = Complex.I • (lie₀ a * lie₀ b - lie₀ b * lie₀ a)
  /-- The matrix of jets of a Lie algebra jet. -/
  lieJ : 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra
  lieJ_injective : Function.Injective lieJ
  lieJ_bracket : ∀ a b, lieJ ⁅a, b⁆ = Complex.I • (lieJ a * lieJ b - lieJ b * lieJ a)
  /-- Evaluation of a gauge jet at the base point. -/
  eval : GJ →* G₀
  toMat₀_eval : ∀ U, toMat₀ (eval U) = (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix (toMatJ U)
  /-- A constant gauge transformation as a jet. -/
  ofConstant : G₀ →* GJ
  toMatJ_ofConstant : ∀ g, toMatJ (ofConstant g) = (C : ℂ →+* SpaceTimeAlgebra).mapMatrix (toMat₀ g)
  /-- Evaluation of a Lie algebra jet at the base point. -/
  evalLie : 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤
  lie₀_evalLie : ∀ a, lie₀ (evalLie a) = (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix (lieJ a)
  /-- A constant Lie algebra element as a jet. -/
  ofConstantLie : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J
  lieJ_ofConstantLie : ∀ a, lieJ (ofConstantLie a) = (C : ℂ →+* SpaceTimeAlgebra).mapMatrix (lie₀ a)
  /-- The formal derivative in the direction `μ`. -/
  deriv : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J
  lieJ_deriv : ∀ μ a, lieJ (deriv μ a) = (lieJ a).map (pderiv μ)
  /-- Multiplication of a jet by the spacetime coordinate `x_μ`. -/
  coord : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤J
  lieJ_coord : ∀ μ a, lieJ (coord μ a) = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • lieJ a
  /-- The adjoint action of the jet group on the jet Lie algebra. -/
  adjoint : Representation ℝ GJ 𝔤J
  lieJ_adjoint : ∀ U a, lieJ (adjoint U a) = toMatJ U * lieJ a * star (toMatJ U)
  /-- The adjoint representation of the value group on its Lie algebra. -/
  adjointValue : Representation ℝ G₀ 𝔤
  lie₀_adjointValue : ∀ g a, lie₀ (adjointValue g a) = toMat₀ g * lie₀ a * star (toMat₀ g)
  /-- The Maurer–Cartan form `i (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of a gauge jet. -/
  maurerCartan : GJ → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤J
  lieJ_maurerCartan : ∀ U μ, lieJ (maurerCartan U μ)
    = Complex.I • ((toMatJ U).map (pderiv μ) * star (toMatJ U))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.eval_ofConstant
declarations.statement: lemma eval_ofConstant (g : G₀) : M.eval (M.ofConstant g) = g

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.evalLie_lie
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_lie (a b : 𝔤J) : M.evalLie ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅M.evalLie a, M.evalLie b⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.ofConstantLie_lie
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstantLie_lie (a b : 𝔤) :
    M.ofConstantLie ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅M.ofConstantLie a, M.ofConstantLie b⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.evalLie_ofConstantLie
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_ofConstantLie (a : 𝔤) : M.evalLie (M.ofConstantLie a) = a

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.deriv_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J) :
    M.deriv μ (M.deriv ν a) = M.deriv ν (M.deriv μ a)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.deriv_bracket
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_bracket (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : 𝔤J) :
    M.deriv μ ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅M.deriv μ x, y⁆ + ⁅x, M.deriv μ y⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.deriv_ofConstantLie
declarations.statement: lemma deriv_ofConstantLie (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤) : M.deriv μ (M.ofConstantLie a) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.deriv_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J) :
    M.deriv μ (M.coord ν a) = M.coord ν (M.deriv μ a) + if μ = ν then a else 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.evalLie_coord
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_coord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : 𝔤J) : M.evalLie (M.coord μ a) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.coord_lie
declarations.statement: lemma coord_lie (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a b : 𝔤J) : ⁅M.coord μ a, b⁆ = M.coord μ ⁅a, b⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.conj_mul_conj
declarations.doc: Conjugation by a unitary matrix respects products.
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_mul_conj (U : GJ) (A B : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    (M.toMatJ U * A * star (M.toMatJ U)) * (M.toMatJ U * B * star (M.toMatJ U))
      = M.toMatJ U * (A * B) * star (M.toMatJ U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.adjoint_lie
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_lie (U : GJ) (x y : 𝔤J) :
    M.adjoint U ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅M.adjoint U x, M.adjoint U y⁆

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.evalLie_adjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_adjoint (U : GJ) (x : 𝔤J) :
    M.evalLie (M.adjoint U x) = M.adjointValue (M.eval U) (M.evalLie x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.maurerCartan_ofConstant
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_ofConstant (g : G₀) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    M.maurerCartan (M.ofConstant g) μ = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.maurerCartan_cocycle
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_cocycle (U V : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    M.maurerCartan (U * V) μ = M.maurerCartan U μ + M.adjoint U (M.maurerCartan V μ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.maurerCartan_structure
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_structure (U : GJ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    M.deriv μ (M.maurerCartan U ν) - M.deriv ν (M.maurerCartan U μ)
      + ⁅M.maurerCartan U μ, M.maurerCartan U ν⁆ = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.deriv_adjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_adjoint (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : 𝔤J) :
    M.deriv μ (M.adjoint U x) = M.adjoint U (M.deriv μ x)
      - ⁅M.maurerCartan U μ, M.adjoint U x⁆

declarations.statement: lemma evalLieHom_apply (a : 𝔤J) : M.evalLieHom a = M.evalLie a

    M.toLocalGaugeData.ofConstantLie = M.ofConstantLie

declarations.statement:
lemma toLocalGaugeData_deriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    M.toLocalGaugeData.deriv μ = M.deriv μ

declarations.statement:
lemma toLocalGaugeData_mulCoord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.toLocalGaugeData_adjoint
declarations.statement:

declarations.statement:
lemma toLocalGaugeData_maurerCartan :
    M.toLocalGaugeData.maurerCartan = M.maurerCartan

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.lieJ_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative is the entrywise iterated formal derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieJ_iteratedDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J) :
    M.lieJ (M.toLocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv s a)
      = (M.lieJ a).map fun f => SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv s f

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.lie₀_evalLie_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: The base-point value of the iterated derivative, entrywise.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie₀_evalLie_iteratedDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J) :
    M.lie₀ (M.toLocalGaugeData.evalLie (M.toLocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv s a))
      = (M.lieJ a).map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv s f)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.faithful
declarations.doc:
**A package presented by matrices is faithful**: a jet is determined entrywise by the
constant coefficients of its derivatives, and a jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form has
constant entries.
declarations.statement: lemma faithful : M.toLocalGaugeData.Faithful

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.suFactor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical `SU`-type factor** of a package presented by matrices: the matrices of
jets themselves.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def suFactor : SUFactor M.toLocalGaugeData κ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.lieJ_radial
declarations.doc:
The radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form, in matrices:
`∑_μ x_μ · i (∂_μ U) U†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieJ_radial (U : GJ) :
    M.lieJ (M.toLocalGaugeData.radial U) =
      ∑ μ, (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) •
          (Complex.I • ((M.toMatJ U).map (pderiv μ) * star (M.toMatJ U)))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.mem_truncationKer_zero_iff
declarations.doc: A gauge jet is pure exactly when its matrix is the identity at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_zero_iff (U : GJ) :
    U ∈ M.toLocalGaugeData.truncationKer 0 ↔
      (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix (M.toMatJ U) = 1

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets.free
declarations.doc:
**A criterion for freeness.** A presentation by matrices is free when every matrix of
jets built entrywise from Taylor data in `𝔤` is a Lie algebra jet, the Lie algebra jets
are hermitian, and every unitary solution `V` of `E V = −i P V`, `V(0) = 1`, for a Lie
algebra jet `P`, is a gauge jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma free
    (hTaylor : ∀ c : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤,
      ∃ Y, M.lieJ Y = SpaceTimeAlgebra.taylorMatrix fun s => M.lie₀ (c s))
    (hherm : ∀ a, star (M.lieJ a) = M.lieJ a)
    (hlift : ∀ (ρ : 𝔤J) (V : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra),
      (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix V = 1 → V * star V = 1 →
      ∑ μ, (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • V.map (pderiv μ) = ((-Complex.I) • M.lieJ ρ) * V →
      ∃ U, M.toMatJ U = V) :
    M.toLocalGaugeData.Free

modules.title: The Maurer–Cartan form of a local gauge data package
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Maurer–Cartan form `ω_μ(U) = i (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of a package
`jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J` is the field `jets.maurerCartan`, subject to the cocycle
law `maurerCartan_cocycle`, its value `maurerCartan_ofConstant` on constants, and the
flatness (structural) equation `maurerCartan_structure`. This file develops what follows
from those laws alone, for any package: nothing here mentions a particular gauge group.

The main construction is the *symmetrized* Maurer–Cartan form

  `ω̄_r(U) = (1 / |r|) ∑_{μ ∈ r} ∂_{r − {μ}} ω_μ(U)`,

the average over which direction of the multiset `r` is carried by the form itself rather
than by a derivative. Its point is `iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add`: an
iterated derivative `∂_s ω_μ(U)` is the symmetrized form at `μ ::ₘ s` plus an average of
iterated derivatives of *brackets* of Maurer–Cartan forms in strictly fewer directions —
the structural equation used to trade an antisymmetric part for lower-order data. This gives
the inductive step `evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq`, and iterating
it, `evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all`: the base-point Taylor
data of `ω` is determined by the base-point symmetrized data. How this determines a pure
jet, and the truncation filtration it defines, is the subject of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Truncation`.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_structure` : the structural equation
  at the base point, to all orders.
- `LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm` : the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form, with
  `symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton` and the recursion
  `symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons`.
- `LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add` : the symmetrization
  defect is an average of brackets in fewer directions.
- `LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all` : the
  base-point symmetrized data determine the base-point Taylor data of `ω`, with the
  inductive step `evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq`.
- `LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero` : the
  base-point half of Maurer–Cartan triangularity.
- `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff` : in a faithful package, the Maurer–Cartan form
  vanishes exactly on the constant jets.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The structural equation at the base point
- B. The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form
- C. Determination of the Maurer–Cartan form by its symmetrized coefficients
- D. Faithful packages and the Maurer–Cartan form

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The structural equation at the base point
## B. The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form
## C. Determination of the Maurer–Cartan form by its symmetrized coefficients
## D. Faithful packages and the Maurer–Cartan form

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_structure
declarations.doc:
The all-orders structural equation of the Maurer–Cartan form, at the base point:
the `s`-th derivative of `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ + ⁅ω_μ, ω_ν⁆ = 0`, with the bracket
expanded by the iterated Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_structure
    (U : GJ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv (μ ::ₘ s) (jets.maurerCartan U ν)) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv (ν ::ₘ s) (jets.maurerCartan U μ))
      - (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          ⁅jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.1 (jets.maurerCartan U μ)),
            jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p.2 (jets.maurerCartan U ν))⁆).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form `ω̄_r(U) = (1/|r|) ∑_{μ ∈ r} ∂_{r − {μ}} ω_μ(U)`:
the average, over the directions of `r`, of the Maurer–Cartan form in one direction
differentiated along the remaining ones.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm (U : GJ) (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : 𝔤J

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_apply_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_apply_zero (U : GJ) :
    jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U 0 = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_one
declarations.statement: lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_one : jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm 1 = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_ofConstant
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_ofConstant (g : G₀) :
    jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm (jets.ofConstant g) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U {μ} = jets.maurerCartan U μ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons
declarations.doc:
The recursion for the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form: peeling one direction off the
multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U (μ ::ₘ r) =
    (1/(r.card + 1 : ℝ) : ℝ) • (jets.iteratedDeriv r (jets.maurerCartan U μ))
    + ((r.card : ℝ)/(r.card + 1 : ℝ)) •
      jets.deriv μ (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add
declarations.doc:
The symmetrization defect of the Maurer–Cartan form: an iterated derivative of
`ω` is the corresponding symmetrized form plus an average of iterated derivatives
of brackets of `ω` in strictly fewer directions. This is the structural equation
`maurerCartan_structure` used to trade the antisymmetric part for lower-order data.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add (U : GJ)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan U μ) =
      jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U (μ ::ₘ s) +
      (1/(s.card + 1 : ℝ)) • (s.map fun ν =>
        jets.iteratedDeriv (s.erase ν)
          ⁅jets.maurerCartan U μ, jets.maurerCartan U ν⁆).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Maurer–Cartan triangularity, base-point half: if the base-point symmetrized
Maurer–Cartan data of `U` vanish in every nonempty multiset of at most `n` directions,
then so do all its base-point Maurer–Cartan Taylor coefficients below order `n`. The
induction is on the order: the symmetrization defect
`iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add` expresses `∂_s ω_μ` through the
symmetrized form, which vanishes by hypothesis, and brackets of `ω`s differentiated
strictly fewer times, which vanish by the inductive hypothesis through
`evalLie_iteratedDeriv_bracket_congr`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero (U : GJ) {n : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), r ≠ 0 → r.card ≤ n →
      jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) = 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (hs : s.card < n) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan U μ)) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq
declarations.doc:
Determination step: if the base-point symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of `U` and
`V` agree, and their Maurer–Cartan Taylor data agree in fewer than `n` directions,
then they agree in `n` directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq (U V : GJ) (n : ℕ)
    (hsym : ∀ r, jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm V r))
    (ih : ∀ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), s.card < n →
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan U μ)) =
        jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan V μ)))
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (hs : s.card = n) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan U μ)) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan V μ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all
declarations.doc:
**The symmetrized data determine the Maurer–Cartan Taylor data**: if the base-point
symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of `U` and `V` agree, so do all base-point Taylor
coefficients of their Maurer–Cartan forms. Strong induction on the order, with
`evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq` as the step.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all (U V : GJ)
    (hsym : ∀ r, jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm V r))
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan U μ)) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.maurerCartan V μ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: In a faithful package, the Maurer–Cartan form vanishes exactly on the constant jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff [jets.Faithful] (U : GJ) :
    jets.maurerCartan U = 0 ↔ U = jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)

modules.title: Local gauge data from a list of factors
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A gauge group is named, as in a model-building table, by a list of symbols `U1` and
`SU n`. This file builds the local gauge data of such a list: the product, in the order of
the list, of the local gauge data `LocalGaugeData.u1` and `LocalGaugeData.su n` of the
factors. The carriers are the corresponding products of `JetU1` and `JetSU n`, and of
their Lie algebras, so that a model's gauge group is a concrete product of matrix groups.
The list of factors of the product, in the sense of the table layer, is assembled from
the canonical factors of the pieces (`Factors.factors`), and the gauge data is faithful
and free because each factor is and both properties pass to products.

With this, a model on any gauge group built from `U(1)` and `SU(n)` factors is a table
alone: `LocalGaugeData.ofFactors Γ` is its gauge data and `Factors.factors Γ` is what its
rows are charged under.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.FactorSpec` : the symbols `U1` and `SU n`.
- `LocalGaugeData.ofFactors` : the local gauge data of a list of factors.
- `LocalGaugeData.Factors.factors` : the canonical factors of that gauge data.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFreeOfFactors` : that gauge data is free.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Factor symbols and their gauge data
- B. The carriers of a list of factors
- C. The gauge data of a list of factors
- D. The canonical factors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Factor symbols and their gauge data

## B. The carriers of a list of factors

The carriers of a list of factors are the products, in the order of the list, of the
carriers of the factors; a one-element list has the carriers of its factor. The carriers
are definitions rather than abbreviations, so that instance search on them goes through
the instances below rather than through the unfolded products: this keeps the instances
found at every use site identical to those inside the gauge data.

The carriers are written by recursion on the list rather than as a fold, so that a single
factor has its own carrier rather than `f.G × Unit`, and so that the carrier of a list
unfolds to the literal product of the carriers of its factors, `JetSU 3 × JetSU 2 × JetU1`
for the Standard Model. The same recursion gives the instances and the gauge data below.
## C. The gauge data of a list of factors
## D. The canonical factors

modules.title: The product of local gauge data
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The local gauge data of a product of gauge groups: every structure map acts
componentwise, and every law holds componentwise. The projections are morphisms of local
gauge data, so a factor of either side pulls back to the product, and the product of two
faithful (free) packages
is faithful (free).

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.prod` : the product of two local gauge data.
- `LocalGaugeData.Hom.fst`, `LocalGaugeData.Hom.snd` : the projections, as morphisms.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFaithfulProd` : the product of faithful packages is faithful.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFreeProd` : the product of free packages is free.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The product
- B. The projections
- C. Faithfulness
- D. Freeness

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The adjoint representation of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The adjoint representation of `SU(N)` acts on the complexified Lie algebra
`SUAlgebraComplexified N = ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)` as the complexification of the conjugation action
`X ↦ g X g⁻¹` on `su(N)` (A). The generalized Gell-Mann matrices, a real basis of `su(N)`, give the
basis `adjBasis N` of the complexified Lie algebra. Sending `z ⊗ X` to the matrix `z X` identifies
the complexified Lie algebra with the traceless complex matrices (`adjMat`), injectively
(`adjMat_injective`) and onto (`adjMat_ofTraceless`), and on matrices the adjoint action is
conjugation (`adjMat_adjRep`). The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are the trace pairings
`tr (λ_a A) / 2`.

In the Gell-Mann basis the adjoint action of `g` has the matrix `adjMatrix g`, with entries
`tr (λ_a g λ_b g⁻¹) / 2`: real, the Gell-Mann matrices being hermitian, and orthogonal, the matrix
of `g⁻¹` being the transpose (B).

The trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)` is symmetric and nondegenerate, the trace pairing with a Gell-Mann
matrix being twice the coordinate, and it is invariant under the adjoint action, so it is the
contraction `adjContr` of two adjoint indices (C).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.adjRep` : the adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra.
- `suTensor.adjMat` : the complexified Lie algebra as traceless complex matrices.
- `suTensor.adjMatrix` : the matrix of the adjoint action in the Gell-Mann basis.
- `suTensor.adjMatrix_inv` : the matrix of `g⁻¹` is the transpose of that of `g`.
- `suTensor.traceForm_nondegenerate` : the trace form is nondegenerate.
- `suTensor.adjContr` : the contraction of two adjoint indices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra
- B. The matrix of the adjoint action
- C. The trace form and the contraction

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis `1 ⊗ λ_a` of the complexified Lie algebra `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjBasis : Basis (GellMann.Index N) ℂ (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma adjBasis_apply (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    adjBasis N a = (1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] GellMann.realBasis a

declarations.name: suTensor.val_inv_mul_val
declarations.statement: lemma val_inv_mul_val (g : SU N) : (g⁻¹).1 * g.1 = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.val_inv
declarations.statement: lemma val_inv (g : SU N) : (g⁻¹).1 = star g.1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjRep
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra: the complexification of the
adjoint action `X ↦ g X g⁻¹` on `su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjRep : Representation ℂ (SU N) (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat
declarations.doc:
The matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra, `z ⊗ X ↦ z X`: a traceless complex
matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjMat : SUAlgebraComplexified N →ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_tmul (z : ℂ) (X : SUAlgebra N) : adjMat N (z ⊗ₜ X) = z • X.1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjBasis
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_adjBasis (a : GellMann.Index N) : adjMat N (adjBasis N a) = GellMann.matrix a

declarations.name: suTensor.trace_adjMat
declarations.doc: The matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_adjMat (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) : (adjMat N A).trace = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjRep
declarations.doc: The adjoint representation moves the matrix by conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_adjRep (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjMat N (adjRep N g A) = g.1 * adjMat N A * (g⁻¹).1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis_repr_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are read off by the trace form,
`A = ∑ (tr (λ_a A) / 2) λ_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjBasis_repr_apply (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    (adjBasis N).repr A a = (GellMann.matrix a * adjMat N A).trace / 2

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_injective
declarations.doc: An element of the complexified Lie algebra is determined by its matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_injective : Function.Injective (adjMat N)

declarations.name: suTensor.ofTraceless
declarations.doc: The element of the complexified Lie algebra with a given traceless matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofTraceless (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) : SUAlgebraComplexified N

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_ofTraceless
declarations.doc: Every traceless matrix is the matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_ofTraceless {M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    adjMat N (ofTraceless M) = M

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action of `g` in the Gell-Mann basis.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev adjMatrix (g : SU N) : Matrix (GellMann.Index N) (GellMann.Index N) ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of the matrix of the adjoint action, `tr (λ_a g λ_b g⁻¹) / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMatrix_apply (g : SU N) (a b : GellMann.Index N) :
    adjMatrix g a b = (GellMann.matrix a * (g.1 * GellMann.matrix b * (g⁻¹).1)).trace / 2

declarations.name: suTensor.star_adjMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action is real, the Gell-Mann matrices being hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_adjMatrix_apply (g : SU N) (a b : GellMann.Index N) :
    star (adjMatrix g a b) = adjMatrix g a b

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_inv
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `g⁻¹` is the transpose of that of `g`, by the cyclicity
of the trace.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMatrix_inv (g : SU N) : adjMatrix g⁻¹ = (adjMatrix g)ᵀ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_inv_mul
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action of `g⁻¹` times that of `g` is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMatrix_inv_mul (g : SU N) : adjMatrix g⁻¹ * adjMatrix g = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm
declarations.doc: The trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)` on the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_apply (A B : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    traceForm N A B = (adjMat N A * adjMat N B).trace

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_isSymm
declarations.doc: The trace form is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma traceForm_isSymm : (traceForm N).IsSymm

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_adjBasis
declarations.doc: The trace form against a Gell-Mann basis vector is twice the coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_adjBasis (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    traceForm N A (adjBasis N a) = 2 * (adjBasis N).repr A a

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_separatingLeft
declarations.doc:
An element orthogonal to every element under the trace form vanishes: its coordinates are its
trace pairings with the Gell-Mann basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_separatingLeft (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (hA : ∀ B, traceForm N A B = 0) :
    A = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: The trace form is nondegenerate on the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: lemma traceForm_nondegenerate : (traceForm N).Nondegenerate

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContr
declarations.doc: The contraction of two adjoint indices, the trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjContr : ((adjRep N).tprod (adjRep N)).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContr_flip_injective
declarations.doc: The trace form separates the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContr_flip_injective :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjContr N).toLinearMap).flip

modules.title: The Lie algebra `su(n)` over a `*`-algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Lie algebra of `SU(n)` is the real Lie algebra of traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices,
with bracket `⁅a, b⁆ = i (a b − b a)` — the factor of `i` keeps the bracket of two hermitian
matrices hermitian. Nothing in this description depends on the entries being complex
numbers: it makes sense over any commutative `*`-algebra `R` over `ℂ`, and the two cases the
theory of jets needs are `R = ℂ` (the Lie algebra itself) and `R` the ring of formal power
series in the spacetime coordinates (its jets). `SUAlgebraOver R n` is this Lie algebra,
together with the conjugation action `a ↦ U a U†` of the unitary group of `R`.

Over `R = ℂ` the Lie algebra is real, since `i` times a hermitian matrix is anti-hermitian. Its
complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` is `SUAlgebraComplexified n`, the complex vector space on which
the adjoint representation of `SU(n)` acts in the complex tensors of `SU(n)`.

## ii. Key results

- `SUAlgebraOver` : the traceless hermitian matrices as a real Lie algebra.
- `SUAlgebraOver.conj` : the conjugation representation of the unitary group.
- `SUAlgebraComplexified` : the complexification of `su(n)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Traceless hermitian matrices
- B. The conjugation representation
- C. The bracket
- D. The complexification

## iv. References

* None.

lemma mem_iff (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    A ∈ submodule R n ↔ star A = A ∧ A.trace = 0

declarations.doc: An element from a traceless hermitian matrix.

declarations.statement:
lemma ofMatrix_val (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hA : star A = A) (hT : A.trace = 0) :
    (ofMatrix A hA hT).1 = A

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.star_val
declarations.statement: lemma star_val (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) : star a.1 = a.1

declarations.statement: lemma trace_val (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) : a.1.trace = 0

declarations.statement: lemma ext {a b : SUAlgebraOver R n} (h : a.1 = b.1) : a = b

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.conj
declarations.doc: **The conjugation representation** of the unitary group on `su(n)`: `a ↦ U a U†`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conj : Representation ℝ (unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (SUAlgebraOver R n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.conj_apply_val
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_apply_val (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) :
    (conj U a).1 = U.1 * a.1 * star U.1

declarations.doc: The bracket `i (a b − b a)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket (SUAlgebraOver R n) (SUAlgebraOver R n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.bracket_val
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_val (a b : SUAlgebraOver R n) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.1 = Complex.I • (a.1 * b.1 - b.1 * a.1)
noncomputable instance : LieRing (SUAlgebraOver R n)
noncomputable instance : LieAlgebra ℝ (SUAlgebraOver R n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebraComplexified
declarations.doc: **The complexified Lie algebra `su(n)_ℂ = ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`**, a complex vector space.
declarations.statement: abbrev SUAlgebraComplexified (n : ℕ) : Type

modules.title: The local gauge data of `SU(n)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The gauge group `SU(n)`, with its jets, its Lie algebra and the jets of its Lie algebra,
packaged as local gauge data `LocalGaugeData.su n`. The jets of gauge transformations are
the special unitary matrices of formal power series, the Lie algebra `su(n)` is the
traceless hermitian matrices (`SUAlgebraOver ℂ n`) and its jets the traceless hermitian
matrices of power series. Evaluation and the constant inclusion act entrywise, the adjoint
action is conjugation, and the Maurer–Cartan form is `i (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`, hermitian by the
differentiated unitarity relation and traceless by Jacobi's formula.

This is a presentation by matrices of jets, `LocalGaugeData.suMatrixJets n`, so the laws of
the local gauge data, its canonical `SUFactor` and its faithfulness come from
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets`. What this file
supplies is the carriers and the structure maps on them.

## ii. Key results

- `SU`, `JetSU`, `SUAlgebra`, `JetSUAlgebra` : the carriers.
- `JetSUAlgebra.mc` : the Maurer–Cartan form.
- `LocalGaugeData.suMatrixJets` : the presentation of `SU(n)` by matrices of jets.
- `LocalGaugeData.su` : the local gauge data of `SU(n)`.
- `LocalGaugeData.suFactor` : its canonical `SU(n)` factor.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFaithfulSU` : the package is faithful.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFreeSU` : the package is free.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The carriers
- B. The structure maps on the group
- C. The structure maps on the Lie algebra
- D. The Maurer–Cartan form
- E. The presentation and the local gauge data

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: JetSU.eval

Evaluation of a jet of an `SU(n)` gauge transformation at the base point: the entrywise

declarations.name: JetSU.eval_val
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_val (U : JetSU n) : (eval U).1 =
    (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix U.1

declarations.doc:
The jet of a constant `SU(n)` gauge transformation: the entrywise inclusion of
constants.

declarations.name: JetSU.ofConstant_val
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: JetSU.trace_mcMatrix
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan matrix `i (∂_μ U) U†` is traceless, by Jacobi's formula and
`det U = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_mcMatrix (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (U : JetSU n) :

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.trace_mapMatrix_constantCoeff
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_mapMatrix_constantCoeff (a : JetSUAlgebra n) :
    ((constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix a.1).trace = 0

    ((C : ℂ →+* SpaceTimeAlgebra).mapMatrix a.1).trace = 0

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.ofConstantLie

declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofConstantLie : SUAlgebra n →ₗ[ℝ] JetSUAlgebra n

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.ofConstantLie_val
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstantLie_val (a : SUAlgebra n) :

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.adjoint
declarations.doc: The adjoint action `a ↦ U a U†` of the jets of `SU(n)` on the jets of `su(n)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjoint : Representation ℝ (JetSU n) (JetSUAlgebra n)

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.mc
declarations.doc: The Maurer–Cartan form `i (∂_μ U) U†` of an `SU(n)` gauge jet.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def mc (U : JetSU n) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetSUAlgebra n

declarations.name: JetSUAlgebra.mc_val

lemma mc_val (U : JetSU n) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :

modules.title: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the standard basis of the traceless complex `N × N`
matrices, the complexified Lie algebra of `SU(N)`, generalizing the Pauli matrices (`N = 2`) and
the Gell-Mann matrices (`N = 3`). There are `N² - 1` of them, of three kinds:

- for `j < k` the symmetric matrix `E_jk + E_kj`,
- for `j < k` the antisymmetric matrix `-i E_jk + i E_kj`,
- for `1 ≤ n ≤ N - 1` the diagonal matrix `√(2 / (n (n + 1))) (E_00 + ⋯ + E_(n-1)(n-1) - n E_nn)`.

They are hermitian and traceless, and orthogonal under the trace form, `tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
Orthogonality makes them linearly independent, and there are as many as the dimension of the
traceless matrices, so they form a basis, `GellMann.basis`, whose coordinates are read off by the
trace form, `GellMann.basis_repr_apply`. Being hermitian they lie in the real Lie algebra `su(N)`
of traceless hermitian matrices, and there they form a real basis, `GellMann.realBasis`: the
coordinates `tr (λ_a H) / 2` of a traceless hermitian matrix `H` are real (E).

## ii. Key results

- `GellMann.Index` : the labels of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `GellMann.matrix` : the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `GellMann.trace_matrix_mul_matrix` : `tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
- `GellMann.basis` : the basis of the traceless matrices they form.
- `GellMann.realBasis` : the basis of the real Lie algebra `su(N)` they form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrices
- B. The diagonal profiles
- C. Orthogonality
- D. The basis
- E. The real basis of `su(N)`

## iv. References

* None.
