declarations.name: suTensor.toMatrix_fundRep
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_fundRep (g : SU N) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (fundRep N g) = g.1

declarations.name: suTensor.toMatrix_antiFundRep
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_antiFundRep (g : SU N) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (antiFundRep N g)
      = (g⁻¹).1ᵀ

declarations.name: suTensor.toMatrix_rep_inv
declarations.doc: On every color, the matrix of `g⁻¹` is the conjugate transpose of the matrix of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_rep_inv (k : Color) (g : SU N) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix (basis N k) (basis N k) (rep N k g⁻¹)
      = (LinearMap.toMatrix (basis N k) (basis N k) (rep N k g))ᴴ

declarations.name: suTensor.isAdjointClosed
declarations.doc: Every list of colors of the `SU(N)` tensors is closed under adjoints, with `g' = g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: lemma isAdjointClosed {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Color) : (suTensor N).IsAdjointClosed c

modules.title: The truncation filtration of the jet gauge group
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A jet of gauge transformations is *trivial to order `n`* when it agrees with the identity
up to and including its `n`-th derivatives. For a matrix group this is a statement about
Taylor coefficients of matrix entries; for an abstract package `jets` it is phrased through
the two things the package provides at the base point, the value `eval U` and the
Maurer–Cartan form: `U` is trivial to order `n` when `eval U = 1` and the base-point Taylor
coefficients of `ω_μ(U)` vanish below order `n`. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem makes these
jets a subgroup `truncationKer n`, normal in `GJ`, and the subgroups decrease with `n`.

The zeroth member, the *pure jets* with `eval U = 1`, is the complement of the constant
jets: every jet factors uniquely as a pure jet times the constant jet of its value,
`truncationProjZero`. When the package is `Faithful`, a pure jet is determined by its
Maurer–Cartan form, and hence by the base-point values of the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan
form, `symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff`; and membership in `truncationKer n` is exactly the
vanishing of those symmetrized data up to order `n`.

What a jet trivial to order `n` does to the fields is the point of the filtration: all its
adjoint Taylor coefficients of order between `1` and `n` vanish,
`adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer`, so it acts on the gauge-field symbols with at
most `n` derivatives by a pure translation.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.truncationKer` : the jets trivial to order `n`, as a subgroup.
- `LocalGaugeData.mem_truncationKer_zero_iff` : the pure jets.
- `LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer` : deep jets kill the positive
  adjoint coefficients.
- `LocalGaugeData.truncationKer_normal` : the filtration is by normal subgroups.
- `LocalGaugeData.truncationProjZero` : the projection of a jet onto the pure jets.
- `LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero` : a pure jet of a faithful package
  is determined by its Maurer–Cartan form.
- `LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective` : and by its symmetrized
  Maurer–Cartan data.
- `LocalGaugeData.mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero` : the
  filtration through the symmetrized data.
- `LocalGaugeData.radial` : the radial component `∑_μ x_μ ω_μ` of the Maurer–Cartan form,
  whose Taylor data are the symmetrized data.
- `LocalGaugeData.Free` : Taylor completeness and radial integrability, which make the
  symmetrized data free coordinates on the pure jets,
  `LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_surjective`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The truncation filtration
- B. The adjoint coefficients of a deep jet
- C. Normality
- D. The projection onto the pure jets
- E. Pure jets and their Maurer–Cartan data
- F. The radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form
- G. Free packages

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The truncation filtration
## B. The adjoint coefficients of a deep jet
## C. Normality
## D. The projection onto the pure jets
## E. Pure jets and their Maurer–Cartan data

## F. The radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form

The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a pure jet are, up to the normalization by the
order, the base-point Taylor data of a single element of `𝔤J`: the radial component
`ρ(U) = ∑_μ x_μ ω_μ(U)` of the Maurer–Cartan form. This is the Euler identity applied
to each summand.
## G. Free packages

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.truncationKer
declarations.doc:
The jets trivial to order `n`: value the identity, and base-point Taylor coefficients
of the Maurer–Cartan form vanishing below order `n`. Closure under products and inverses
is the cocycle law together with the Taylor–Leibniz theorem for the adjoint action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def truncationKer (n : ℕ) : Subgroup GJ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.mem_truncationKer_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The zeroth truncation kernel is the group of pure jets, those with identity value.
declarations.statement: lemma mem_truncationKer_zero_iff {U : GJ} : U ∈ jets.truncationKer 0 ↔ jets.eval U = 1

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Deep jets kill the positive adjoint coefficients: for a jet trivial to order `n`, the
adjoint coefficients of order between `1` and `n` vanish. One derivative of the adjoint
is `ad` of the Maurer–Cartan form, whose base-point data vanish below order `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer {n : ℕ} {U : GJ} (hU : U ∈ jets.truncationKer n)
    {x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxn : x.card ≤ n) :
    jets.adjointCoeff U x = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointDualCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc: The dual form of `adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer`.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_mul_of_mem_truncationKer_right
declarations.doc: Up to order `n`, a jet trivial to order `n` is invisible on the right of a product.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.adjointCoeff_conj_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Up to order `n`, a conjugate of a jet trivial to order `n` has the adjoint
coefficients of the identity.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjoint_conj_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Up to order `n`, a conjugate of a jet trivial to order `n` acts trivially on the
base-point Taylor data of the jet Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDeriv_adjoint_conj_of_mem_truncationKer (g : GJ) {n : ℕ} {U : GJ}
    (hU : U ∈ jets.truncationKer n) {s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hs : s.card ≤ n)
    (Y : 𝔤J) : jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s (jets.adjointJ (g * U * g⁻¹) Y)) =
      jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s Y)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_conj
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form of a conjugate, by the cocycle law: the conjugating jet
contributes its own form and its transport by the conjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_conj (g U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.maurerCartan (g * U * g⁻¹) μ =
      jets.maurerCartan g μ + jets.adjointJ g (jets.maurerCartan U μ)
        - jets.adjointJ (g * U * g⁻¹) (jets.maurerCartan g μ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.truncationKer_normal
declarations.doc:
The truncation kernels are normal subgroups: conjugating a jet trivial to order `n`
gives a jet trivial to order `n`.
declarations.statement: instance truncationKer_normal (n : ℕ) : (jets.truncationKer n).Normal

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.truncationProjZero
declarations.doc:
The projection of a jet onto the pure jets, stripping its value: `U ↦ U · (U₀)⁻¹`.
This is not a group homomorphism; it is the cocycle of the splitting of `GJ` by the
constant jets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def truncationProjZero (U : GJ) : jets.truncationKer 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.coe_truncationProjZero
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_truncationProjZero (U : GJ) :
    (jets.truncationProjZero U : GJ) = U * (jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U))⁻¹

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.eq_truncationProjZero_mul_ofConstant
declarations.doc: Every jet is its pure part times the constant jet of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_truncationProjZero_mul_ofConstant (U : GJ) :
    U = jets.truncationProjZero U * jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.truncationProjZero_eq_one_iff
declarations.doc: The pure part of a jet is trivial exactly when the jet is constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma truncationProjZero_eq_one_iff {U : GJ} :
    jets.truncationProjZero U = 1 ↔ U = jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.truncationProjZero_ofConstant
declarations.statement:
lemma truncationProjZero_ofConstant (g : G₀) :
    jets.truncationProjZero (jets.ofConstant g) = 1

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_truncationProjZero
declarations.doc:
Stripping the value of a jet does not change its Maurer–Cartan form: by the cocycle
law, right multiplication by a constant jet drops out.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_truncationProjZero (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jets.maurerCartan (jets.truncationProjZero U) μ = jets.maurerCartan U μ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a pure jet: the base-point values of its
symmetrized Maurer–Cartan forms, indexed by nonempty multisets of directions. Total
symmetry is automatic from the multiset indexing.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff (U : jets.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) : 𝔤

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_apply (U : jets.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) :
    jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U r =
      jets.evalLie (jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U.1 r.1)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.mem_truncationKer_of_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Maurer–Cartan triangularity: a pure jet whose symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data vanish
up to order `n` is trivial to order `n`. The symmetrized data control the Taylor data of
the Maurer–Cartan form through the symmetrization defect.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_of_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero (U : jets.truncationKer 0)
    (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (hr : r ≠ 0), r.card ≤ n →
      jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U ⟨r, hr⟩ = 0) :
    U.1 ∈ jets.truncationKer n

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Conversely, the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a jet trivial to order `n` vanish
up to order `n`: each term of the symmetrized form carries fewer than `n` derivatives.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The truncation filtration through the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data: a pure jet is
trivial to order `n` exactly when its symmetrized data vanish up to order `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero (U : jets.truncationKer 0)
    (n : ℕ) : U.1 ∈ jets.truncationKer n ↔
      ∀ (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (hr : r ≠ 0), r.card ≤ n →
        jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U ⟨r, hr⟩ = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero
declarations.doc:
A pure jet of a faithful package is determined by its Maurer–Cartan form. By the
cocycle and inverse laws `ω(V⁻¹ U) = Ad_{V⁻¹}(ω(U) − ω(V)) = 0`, so `V⁻¹ U` is the
constant jet of its value, which is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero {U V : GJ} (hU : U ∈ jets.truncationKer 0)
    (hV : V ∈ jets.truncationKer 0) (h : jets.maurerCartan U = jets.maurerCartan V) :
    U = V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective
declarations.doc:
A pure jet of a faithful package is determined by its symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data.
The symmetrized data determine all base-point Taylor data of the Maurer–Cartan form
(`evalLie_iteratedDeriv_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all`), hence the form itself by
Taylor determinacy, hence the jet by `maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective :
    Function.Injective jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.radial
declarations.doc: The radial component `∑_μ x_μ ω_μ(U)` of the Maurer–Cartan form of a jet.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def radial (U : GJ) : 𝔤J

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_radial
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data are the Taylor data of the radial component:
`sym(ω(U))_r|₀ = (1/|r|) (∂_r ρ(U))|₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_radial (U : jets.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) :
    jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U r =
      (1 / (r.1.card : ℝ)) • jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv r.1 (jets.radial U.1))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Free
declarations.doc:
A package is free when it is faithful and its jets are honest formal power series in
the coordinates: every family of base-point Taylor data is realized by an element of
`𝔤J` (Taylor completeness), and every element vanishing at the base point is the radial
component of the Maurer–Cartan form of a pure jet (radial integrability, the solution of
the Euler equation `∑_μ x_μ ∂_μ U = −i ρ U` with `U(0) = 1`). Both hold for the full jet
group of any matrix group. Freeness makes the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data free
coordinates on the pure jets, `symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective`; like `Faithful`
it is recorded separately from the structure because the covariance theory does not
need it, only the classification of invariants does.
declarations.statement:
class Free (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) : Prop extends Faithful jets where
  exists_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_eq : ∀ c : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤,
    ∃ Y : 𝔤J, ∀ s, jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s Y) = c s
  exists_radial_eq : ∀ ρ : 𝔤J, jets.evalLie ρ = 0 → ∃ U : jets.truncationKer 0, jets.radial U.1 = ρ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.exists_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_eq
declarations.doc: Taylor completeness of a free package.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_eq (c : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤) :
    ∃ Y : 𝔤J, ∀ s, jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv s Y) = c s

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.exists_radial_eq
declarations.doc: Radial integrability of a free package.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_radial_eq {ρ : 𝔤J} (hρ : jets.evalLie ρ = 0) :
    ∃ U : jets.truncationKer 0, jets.radial U.1 = ρ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_surjective
declarations.doc:
Every family of symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data is realized by a pure jet: realize the
data, rescaled by the order, as the Taylor data of an element `ρ` vanishing at the base
point, and integrate `ρ` to a pure jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_surjective :
    Function.Surjective jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data are free coordinates on the pure jets of a free
package.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective :
    Function.Bijective jets.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

modules.title: The local gauge data of `U(1)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The abelian gauge group `U(1)`, with its jets, its Lie algebra and the jets of its Lie
algebra, packaged as local gauge data `LocalGaugeData.u1`. The jets of gauge
transformations are the unitary formal power series, the Lie algebra is the self-adjoint
(real) scalars and its jets the self-adjoint power series, with vanishing bracket and
trivial adjoint action. The Maurer–Cartan form is `i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹`.

Read as `1 × 1` matrices, this is a presentation by matrices of jets,
`LocalGaugeData.u1MatrixJets`, so the laws of the local gauge data and its faithfulness come
from `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.MatrixJets`. What this file
supplies is the carriers, the structure maps on them, and the canonical `U1Factor`.

## ii. Key results

- `U1`, `JetU1`, `U1Algebra`, `JetU1Algebra` : the carriers.
- `LocalGaugeData.u1MatrixJets` : the presentation of `U(1)` by `1 × 1` matrices of jets.
- `LocalGaugeData.u1` : the local gauge data of `U(1)`.
- `LocalGaugeData.u1Factor` : its canonical `U(1)` factor.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFaithfulU1` : the package is faithful.
- `LocalGaugeData.instFreeU1` : the package is free.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The carriers
- B. The structure maps
- C. The Maurer–Cartan form
- D. The presentation and the local gauge data
- E. The canonical factor

## iv. References

* None.

The Lie algebra `u(1)` over a `*`-ring: the self-adjoint elements, with vanishing
bracket.
declarations.statement: abbrev U1AlgebraOver (R : Type) [Ring R] [StarRing R] : Type

declarations.name: U1Algebra

declarations.name: U1AlgebraOver.bracket_eq_zero

declarations.name: JetU1.eval
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a jet of a `U(1)` gauge transformation at the base point.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eval : JetU1 →* U1

declarations.name: JetU1.eval_val
declarations.statement: lemma eval_val (u : JetU1) : (eval u : ℂ) = constantCoeff (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: JetU1.ofConstant
declarations.doc: The jet of a constant `U(1)` gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofConstant : U1 →* JetU1

declarations.name: JetU1.ofConstant_val
declarations.statement: lemma ofConstant_val (u : U1) : (ofConstant u : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = C (u : ℂ)

declarations.name: JetU1.deriv
declarations.doc: The formal derivative of a `u(1)` jet.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def deriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetU1Algebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetU1Algebra

declarations.name: JetU1.deriv_val
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_val (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetU1Algebra) :
    (deriv μ a : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = pderiv μ a

declarations.name: JetU1.coord
declarations.doc: Multiplication of a `u(1)` jet by the coordinate `x_μ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def coord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetU1Algebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetU1Algebra

declarations.name: JetU1.coord_val
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_val (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetU1Algebra) :
    (coord μ a : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * a

declarations.name: JetU1.evalLie
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a `u(1)` jet at the base point.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evalLie : JetU1Algebra →ₗ[ℝ] U1Algebra

declarations.name: JetU1.evalLie_val
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_val (a : JetU1Algebra) : (evalLie a : ℂ) = constantCoeff (a : SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: JetU1.ofConstantLie
declarations.doc: A constant as a `u(1)` jet.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofConstantLie : U1Algebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetU1Algebra

declarations.name: JetU1.ofConstantLie_val
declarations.statement: lemma ofConstantLie_val (a : U1Algebra) : (ofConstantLie a : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = C (a : ℂ)

declarations.name: JetU1.star_mcVal
declarations.doc: The Maurer–Cartan scalar `i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹` of a unitary jet is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_mcVal (u : JetU1) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    star (Complex.I • (pderiv μ (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * star (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra)))
      = Complex.I • (pderiv μ (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * star (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra))

declarations.name: JetU1.mc
declarations.doc: The Maurer–Cartan form `i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹` of a `U(1)` jet.

declarations.statement:
lemma mc_val (u : JetU1) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (mc u μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = Complex.I •
        (pderiv μ (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * star (u : SpaceTimeAlgebra))

declarations.doc: **The presentation of `U(1)` by `1 × 1` matrices of jets.**
declarations.statement: noncomputable def u1MatrixJets : MatrixJets (Fin 1) U1 U1Algebra JetU1 JetU1Algebra

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1
declarations.doc:
**The local gauge data of `U(1)`**: unitary jets, self-adjoint scalar jets with
vanishing bracket and trivial adjoint action, and the Maurer–Cartan form
`i (∂_μ u) u⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def u1 : LocalGaugeData U1 U1Algebra JetU1 JetU1Algebra

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1_eval

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1_ofConstant

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1_evalLie_apply

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1_ofConstantLie

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.instFreeU1

The local gauge data of `U(1)` is free. Real Taylor data give a self-adjoint jet, and
the unitary Euler transport of a `1 × 1` matrix is a unitary jet.
declarations.statement: instance instFreeU1 : u1.Free

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.u1Factor
declarations.doc: The canonical `U(1)` factor of the local gauge data of `U(1)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def u1Factor : U1Factor u1

modules.title: Matter fields of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A matter field of a gauge theory is specified by the data a physicist writes down: a
finite-dimensional complex vector space `V` in which the field takes its values, the
representation of the Lorentz group on `V`, the action of the jets of gauge
transformations on the jets of the field — which must be *fibrewise*, that is act on the
values of the field over the identity of spacetime — the mass weight of the field, and the
statistics, bosonic or fermionic, that the field is declared to obey. All of this is
relative to a gauge context `jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J`: the jet gauge group
`GJ` the field's jet action is a representation of, and the global group `G₀`, Lie
algebras `𝔤`, `𝔤J` and structure maps that make `GJ` the jets of `G₀` rather than an
unrelated group. Fixing `jets` rather than `GJ` alone is what lets the global gauge action
`repConstant` below be taken along the *canonical* inclusion `jets.ofConstant`, instead of
an arbitrary homomorphism supplied by hand.

`MatterField jets` bundles this data. The statistics is declared once, where the field is
defined, and separately from the Lorentz representation. `GaugeFieldData` requires the
declaration of each matter field it includes to agree with the collection, fermionic or
bosonic, to which that field is assigned. From the other data the general theory produces,
on the bosonic and fermionic algebras of the field, the jet gauge action, the global gauge
action, the Lorentz action and the mass-weight scaling, in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.StandardModel.Matter.Bosonic.Basic`,
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.StandardModel.Matter.Fermionic.Basic` and the files beside them.

## ii. Key results

- `MatterField` : the data of a matter field.
- `MatterField.PureJetsActTrivially`, `MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible` : two conditions
  on a matter field used by the covariant derivative theory.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The data of a matter field
- B. Conditions on a matter field

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The data of a matter field

## B. Conditions on a matter field

Two properties the data of a matter field does not in general imply: the transformation
laws constrain the base-point coefficient of a pure jet only to commute with the
infinitesimal action (a scalar twist by a character of the jet group nontrivial on pure
jets preserves every field of the structure), and they do not relate the gauge and Lorentz
actions at all. Both hold for the matter fields of the physical theories, and they are
recorded as conditions rather than as fields, to be assumed where the covariant derivative
theory needs them: the first for the factorization of the jet action through evaluation,
the second for the Lorentz law of the covariant derivatives.

declarations.name: MatterField
declarations.doc:
**A matter field** of a gauge theory over the gauge context `jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J`:
a finite-dimensional complex target space `V`, the Lorentz representation on `V`, a
fibrewise action of `GJ` on the jets `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V` of the field, the infinitesimal
action of the gauge algebra generating it, the mass weight of the field (in the units
in which a derivative has weight `2`), and its declared statistics.
declarations.statement:
structure MatterField {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {GJ : Type} [Group GJ] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) where
  /-- The target space of the field. -/
  V : Type
  [instAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup V]
  [instModule : Module ℂ V]
  [instFree : Module.Free ℂ V]
  [instFinite : Module.Finite ℂ V]
  /-- The representation of the Lorentz group on the target space. -/
  repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V
  /-- The action of the jets of gauge transformations on the jets of the field. -/
  repJet : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)
  /-- The action of the gauge algebra. -/
  repAlgebra : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V
  /-- The gauge action is fibrewise: it commutes with multiplication by scalar jets. -/
  repJet_smul : ∀ (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), repJet U (χ • z) =
      χ • repJet U z
  /-- The action of the gauge algebra generates the action of the jets of gauge
    transformations: it is the infinitesimal action underlying `repJet`, the physicists'
    `i dρ(T^a)`. This is what makes the covariant derivative of the field transform
    covariantly. -/
  repAlgebra_isInfinitesimalAction : jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf repAlgebra repJet
  /-- The mass weight of the field. -/
  massWeight : ℕ
  /-- The statistics the field is declared to obey, bosonic or fermionic. `GaugeFieldData`
    requires it to agree with the collection the field is assigned to; the single-field
    algebras `StandardModel.FermionicAlgebra M` and `StandardModel.BosonicAlgebra M` are
    defined for every `M`, whatever its declared statistics. -/
  statistic : FieldStatistic

declarations.name: MatterField.PureJetsActTrivially
declarations.doc:
Pure gauge jets act trivially at the base point: a jet with trivial value has identity
zeroth Taylor coefficient on the value space. With the fibrewise law, the base-point
value of the jet action is then a function of the value of the jet.
declarations.statement: def PureJetsActTrivially : Prop

declarations.name: MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal gauge action commutes with the Lorentz representation on the value
space.
declarations.statement: def GaugeLorentzCompatible : Prop

modules.title: Charged matter fields under `U(1)` jets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A field valued in a complex vector space `V` with integer charge `n` transforms under a
`U(1)` gauge transformation `U = e^{iχ}` by `ψ ↦ U^n ψ`. On jets this is multiplication of the
jet-ring factor of `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V` by the unitary power series `U^n`; the action is
manifestly fibrewise. `MatterField.charged` packages a Lorentz representation, a charge,
a mass weight and a declared statistic into a matter field for the jet gauge group
`unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra` of `U(1)`.

## ii. Key results

- `MatterField.chargeRep` : the charge-`n` action of `U(1)` jets on the jets of a field.
- `MatterField.chargeRep_smul` : the action is fibrewise.
- `MatterField.charged` : the matter field of charge `n`, over a supplied
  infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Powers of a unitary jet
- B. The charge action on jets
- C. Charged matter fields

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Powers of a unitary jet
## B. The charge action on jets
## C. Charged matter fields

declarations.name: MatterField.chargePow
declarations.doc: The unitary power series `U ^ n` of a `U(1)` jet, for an integer charge `n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def chargePow (n : ℤ) (U : unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) : SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: MatterField.chargePow_one
declarations.statement: lemma chargePow_one (n : ℤ) : chargePow n 1 = 1

declarations.name: MatterField.chargePow_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma chargePow_mul (n : ℤ) (U W : unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    chargePow n (U * W) = chargePow n U * chargePow n W

declarations.name: MatterField.chargeRep
declarations.doc:
**The charge-`n` action of `U(1)` jets on the jets of a `V`-valued field**:
multiplication of the jet-ring factor by `U ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chargeRep (n : ℤ) (V : Type) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] :
    Representation ℂ (unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)

declarations.name: MatterField.chargeRep_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeRep_tmul (n : ℤ) (U : unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    chargeRep n V U (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = (chargePow n U * f) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v

declarations.name: MatterField.chargeRep_smul
declarations.doc: **The charge action is fibrewise**: it commutes with multiplication by scalar jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeRep_smul (n : ℤ) (U : unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    chargeRep n V U (χ • z) = χ • chargeRep n V U z

declarations.name: MatterField.charged
declarations.doc:
**The charged matter field**: a field with values in `V`, Lorentz representation
`repLorentz`, electric charge `n`, mass weight `w` and declared statistic `σ`, as a matter
field for the jets of `U(1)`, in any gauge context `jets` whose jet group is
`unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra`.

The infinitesimal action `act` of the gauge algebra is supplied, not constructed. For a
charge-`n` field it is `c ↦ (i n φ(c)) • id` for the functional `φ` reading off the
`u(1)` component of `c`, and no such functional is available: `jets` relates the gauge
algebra `𝔤` to the jets only through `evalLie` and `maurerCartan`, neither of which
identifies a `u(1)` direction in an arbitrary `𝔤`. The rest of the data does not depend
on `jets` beyond its jet group, so it is supplied polymorphically.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def charged {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 (unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) 𝔤J) [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V) (n : ℤ) (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hact : jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf act (chargeRep n V)) (w : ℕ) (σ : FieldStatistic) :
    MatterField jets

declarations.name: MatterField.charged_V
declarations.statement:
lemma charged_V {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 (unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) 𝔤J) [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V) (n : ℤ) (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hact : jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf act (chargeRep n V)) (w : ℕ) (σ : FieldStatistic) :
    (charged jets repLorentz n act hact w σ).V = V

modules.title: Gauge tensors in a general representation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The adjoint story of `TransformsInAdjoint` generalizes to an arbitrary representation
of the jet gauge group: a matter field valued in a representation space `V` has
symbols `[∂_s ψ^i]` contracted against duals of `V`, and its transformation law is
the Leibniz convolution of the base-point Taylor coefficients of the representation.

Since the gauge transformations are jets, the representation must act on `V`-valued
jets `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V` — the value of `rep U` at a constant vector is spacetime
dependent, and the derivative symbols see its Taylor coefficients. This file provides
the toolkit for `V`-valued jets:

* `jetOfConstant` — the inclusion of constants, `v ↦ 1 ⊗ v`;
* `jetDeriv`/`jetIteratedDeriv` — the formal derivative, acting on the jet factor;
* `jetEval` — evaluation at the base point, `f ⊗ v ↦ (constant coefficient of f) • v`;

and with them

* `repDualCoeff rep U x` — the physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` transposed to the dual
  of `V`, the analogue of `adjointDualCoeff` for a general representation;
The gauge tensors of a representation themselves — `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn`, the
generalization of `TransformsInAdjoint` — are defined on top of `repDualCoeff` in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.TransformsIn`.


The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = D_ρ F + (A_ρ acting on the value index)` requires
the *infinitesimal* action of the gauge algebra on the value space — physicists'
`i dρ(T^a)` — which cannot be extracted from the abstract group representation `rep`
(there is no differentiable structure to differentiate it). It is therefore taken as
data: an `ℝ`-bilinear action `act : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] W →ₗ[ℝ] W`. The layer is
built for an arbitrary finite-dimensional real value space `W`, so that the adjoint
case `act = adAction` (the bracket as a bilinear map) literally specializes:
`covDerivAction A adAction F D ρ = covDerivAdjoint A F D ρ` holds definitionally
(`covDerivAction_adAction`).

The compatibility between `rep` and `act` — the structure `IsInfinitesimalActionOf` —
and the theorem that under it the covariant derivative preserves the gauge tensors live
in `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.InfinitesimalAction`.

## ii. Key results

- `repDualCoeff` : the physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` acting on the complex dual index of a
  matter-field symbol: the transpose of `repCoeff`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The dual representation coefficients and gauge tensors in a representation
- B. The covariant derivative through an infinitesimal action
- C. The span lemma
- D. Naturality in the algebra

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The dual representation coefficients and gauge tensors in a representation

## B. The covariant derivative through an infinitesimal action

The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` requires the *infinitesimal*
action of the gauge algebra on the value space — physicists' `i dρ(T^a)` — which
cannot be extracted from the abstract group representation `rep` (there is no
differentiable structure to differentiate it). It is therefore taken as data: an
action `act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V`, real-linear in the algebra slot (the
gauge algebra is a real Lie algebra) and complex-linear in the value slot, matching
the complex duals indexing the matter families.

## C. The span lemma

Replacing derivatives of a matter family by covariant derivatives does not change
the generated algebra of symbols: the correction terms are products of gauge-field
components with matter components. Note the statement is about generated
*subalgebras*, not linear spans — `∇_ρ F − ∂_ρ F` is a sum of products `A · F`,
which lies in the algebra generated by the symbols but not in their linear span.

## D. Naturality in the algebra

The matter analogue of `bracketFam_map` and `iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_map`: a
multiplicative linear map into another algebra carries the derived action, and hence
the whole covariant matter tower, to the tower of the image families. The derived
action is a finite sum of products of components, so only multiplicativity is needed;
no derivative operator on the target is involved.

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficient of the representation: include the constant
vector into `V`-valued jets, act by `rep U`, differentiate `x` times, evaluate at
the base point. The composite is complex-linear: the physicists'
`∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` as a ℂ-linear map on the value space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repCoeff (rep : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` acting on the complex dual index of a
matter-field symbol: the transpose of `repCoeff`. This is the analogue of
`adjointDualCoeff` for a general representation of the jet gauge group; for `x = 0`
it is the dual (contragredient) action of the value of `U`, and for `x ≠ 0` it sees
the derivatives of the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repDualCoeff (rep : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.jetEval_rep_of_smul
declarations.doc:
For a fibrewise representation, evaluating the transform of a jet at the base point
is the zeroth Taylor coefficient of the transform of its base-point value: the jet ring
factor passes through the action and is then evaluated.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_rep_of_smul (rep : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : GJ) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEval (rep U z) = repCoeff rep U 0 (jetEval z)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff_zero_mul
declarations.doc:
The zeroth Taylor coefficients of a fibrewise representation are multiplicative: they
form a representation of the jet gauge group on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_mul (rep : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U W : GJ) : repCoeff rep (U * W) 0 = repCoeff rep U 0 ∘ₗ repCoeff rep W 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.tensorAction
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-valued field on a matter field at the tensor level:
multiplication in `B` on the first factors, the ℂ-linear infinitesimal action `act`
of the gauge algebra on `V` on the second, so that on pure tensors
`(b₁ ⊗ c) · (b₂ ⊗ v) = (b₁ b₂) ⊗ act c v`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorAction (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) :
    (B ⊗[ℝ] 𝔤) →ₗ[ℝ] (B ⊗[ℂ] V) →ₗ[ℂ] B ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.tensorAction_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_tmul (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (b₁ b₂ : B)
    (c : 𝔤) (v : V) :
    tensorAction act (b₁ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) (b₂ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = (b₁ * b₂) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] act c v

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.tensorAction_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_map_left (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂) (s : B ⊗[ℝ] 𝔤)
    (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    tensorAction act ((TensorProduct.map (Φ.restrictScalars ℝ) LinearMap.id) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (tensorAction act s t)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.tensorAction_one_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_one_left (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (c : 𝔤)
    (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    tensorAction act ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) t =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (act c)) t

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.tensorAction_map_right_antidiagonal
declarations.doc:
`tensorAction` under an antidiagonal pair of transport families: if the
`V`-transports intertwine `act` with the `𝔤`-transports as an
antidiagonal convolution, so do `id ⊗ ·` over `tensorAction`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_map_right_antidiagonal (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (Tg : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] 𝔤)
    (Tv : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (hT : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (w : V), Tv x (act c w) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => act (Tg p.1 c) (Tv p.2 w)).sum)
    (s : B ⊗[ℝ] 𝔤) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      tensorAction act ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tg p.1)) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tv p.2)) t)).sum =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tv x)) (tensorAction act s t)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquivC
declarations.doc:
The canonical equivalence between matter fields `B ⊗[ℂ] V` and their component
families `φ ↦ F^φ` over the complex dual — `dualPairEquiv` for a general
finite-dimensional complex value space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualPairEquivC : (B ⊗[ℂ] V) ≃ₗ[ℂ] (Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquivC_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_tmul (b : B) (v : V) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) φ = φ v • b

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquivC_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_map_left (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) φ =
      Φ (dualPairEquivC t φ)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquivC_map_right
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_map_right (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) t) φ =
      dualPairEquivC t (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.symm_comp_left_C
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_left_C (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm (Φ ∘ₗ g) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (dualPairEquivC.symm g)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.symm_comp_right_C
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_right_C (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm (g ∘ₗ T.dualMap) =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) (dualPairEquivC.symm g)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-indexed component family on a matter one, through the
infinitesimal action `act`: assemble both into fields, act by `tensorAction`, read
back out as components. This is the physicists' `f^a (T_a)^i_j g^j` with `T = act`,
basis-free.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionFam (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_add_left (f₁ f₂ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act (f₁ + f₂) g = actionFam act f₁ g + actionFam act f₂ g

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_add_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g₁ g₂ : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act f (g₁ + g₂) = actionFam act f g₁ + actionFam act f g₂

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_zero_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_zero_left (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act 0 g = 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_zero_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_zero_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    actionFam act f 0 = 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_sum_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_sum_left (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B))
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act S.sum g = (S.map fun f => actionFam act f g).sum

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_sum_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_sum_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)) :
    actionFam act f S.sum = (S.map fun g => actionFam act f g).sum

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repGauge_actionFam
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of the action of an affinely-transforming
adjoint-indexed family on a linearly-transforming matter family: the action of the
transformed families plus one `act`-type cross term. This is `repGauge_bracketFam`
with a homogeneous second slot and the bracket replaced by a general action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_actionFam
    (U : GJ) {f f' : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    {g g' : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B} {cf : 𝔤}
    (hf : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤,
      repGauge U (f ψ) = f' ψ + algebraMap ℂ B (ψ cf))
    (hg : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℂ V, repGauge U (g ψ) = g' ψ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (actionFam act f g φ) =
      actionFam act f' g' φ + g' (φ ∘ₗ act cf)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFamConv
declarations.doc:
The derived action family `A_ρ · F`: the `s`-derivative of the action of the
gauge field on a matter family, given by the Leibniz convolution of the derivative
symbols over the multiset antidiagonal — the matter analogue of `bracketFamConv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionFamConv
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivAction
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` of a matter family of
derivative symbols, in the single direction `ρ`: the extra derivative on the symbol
plus the derived action of the gauge field on the value index. With the physicists'
factor of `i` absorbed into `act` (as it is in the gauge-algebra bracket), this is
`∂_ρ F + i A_ρ^a T_a F` in the `D = ∂ + i A` convention.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covDerivAction
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivAction_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAction_apply
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivAction A act F ρ s φ = F (ρ ::ₘ s) φ + actionFamConv A act ρ F s φ

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
**The iterated covariant derivative** `∇_{l 0} ⋯ ∇_{l (n-1)} F` of a matter family
along an ordered tuple of directions: covariant derivatives do not commute (their
commutator is the action of the field strength), so the iteration is order-dependent
and indexed by `(n : ℕ)` and `l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)` — the same ordered-tuple
indexing as the derivative labels of `IsHiggsAlgebraValued`. The result is again a
family of derivative symbols; the physical iterated covariant derivative is its
value at the empty multiset.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covDerivIter
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) →
      Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_zero (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (l : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter A act F 0 l = F

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_succ (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter A act F (n + 1) l =
      covDerivAction A act (covDerivIter A act F n fun i => l i.succ) (l 0)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquiv_symm_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
Decomposition of an assembled adjoint-indexed family along a basis of the gauge
algebra: the components against the dual basis, tensored with the basis vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_symm_eq_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (bW : Module.Basis ι ℝ 𝔤)
    (g : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    dualPairEquiv.symm g = ∑ i, g (bW.coord i) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] bW i

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dualPairEquivC_symm_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Decomposition of an assembled matter family along a basis of the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_symm_eq_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (bW : Module.Basis ι ℂ V)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm g = ∑ i, g (bW.coord i) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] bW i

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_apply_mem
declarations.doc:
The value of an action of families lies in any subalgebra containing the values
of both families: the action is a finite sum of products of components.

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter_sub_mem
declarations.doc:
**Unitriangularity of the covariant matter tower**: the covariant and plain
derivative symbols of a matter family differ by an element of the subalgebra
generated by the gauge-field symbols and the strictly lower-order matter symbols.
Stated at every derivative multiset `s`, as needed for the induction.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_sub_mem (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F n l s φ - F (List.ofFn l + s) φ ∈
      Algebra.adjoin ℂ
        ({b : B | ∃ (u : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
            (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤), b = A u μ ψ} ∪
          {b : B | ∃ (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
            t.card < n + s.card ∧ b = F t χ})

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter_mem_adjoin_symbols
declarations.doc:
Every derivative symbol of the covariant tower is a polynomial in the gauge-field
symbols and the matter symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_mem_adjoin_symbols (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F n l s φ ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = F s φ})

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
**The span lemma**: the algebra of symbols generated by the gauge field together
with a matter family's *derivative* symbols equals the one generated by the gauge
field together with the matter family's *covariant* derivative tower. The
correction `∇_ρ − ∂_ρ` is the derived action of the gauge field — a sum of products
of symbols, absorbed by the algebra structure.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = F s φ}) =
    Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = covDerivIter A act F n l 0 φ})

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_map
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-indexed family on a matter family is natural in the
algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_map (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act (Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ f) (Φ ∘ₗ g) = Φ ∘ₗ actionFam act f g

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFamConv_map
declarations.doc: The derived action family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    actionFamConv (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act ρ (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) s
      = Φ ∘ₗ actionFamConv A act ρ F s

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivAction_map
declarations.doc: The covariant derivative of a matter family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAction_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivAction (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) ρ s
      = Φ ∘ₗ covDerivAction A act F ρ s

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter_map
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative of a matter family is natural in the algebra: the
image of the tower is the tower of the image families, at every ordered tuple of
directions and every derivative multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) n l
      = fun s => Φ ∘ₗ covDerivIter A act F n l s

modules.title: The infinitesimal action underlying a matter representation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` of a matter family is built from
an action `act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V` of the gauge algebra on the value space. For the
covariant derivative to transform covariantly, `act` must be the *infinitesimal action*
underlying the representation `rep` of the jet gauge group in which the family
transforms — the physicists' statement that the matrices `i dρ(T^a)` generate `rep`.
This file packages that compatibility as the structure `IsInfinitesimalActionOf`, and
proves the theorem it exists for: the covariant derivative preserves the gauge tensors,
`TransformsIn.covDerivAction`.

Everything is stated over a supplied local-gauge-data package
`jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J`; nothing depends on the Standard Model choice of it.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf` : `act` is the infinitesimal action underlying
  `rep`.
- `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.covDerivAction` : the covariant derivative preserves
  `TransformsIn`.
- `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.covDerivIter` : so does every iterated covariant
  derivative.
- `LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.conj` : the conjugate action underlies the
  conjugate representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The infinitesimal action underlying a representation
- B. The covariant derivative preserves `TransformsIn`
- C. The conjugate action and the conjugate representation

## iv. References

* None.
