declarations.name: jetIteratedDeriv_tmul
declarations.doc:
The iterated formal derivative of a `V`-valued jet acts on the jet-ring factor of a
pure tensor: the value factor carries no spacetime dependence.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetIteratedDeriv_tmul (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (v : V) :
    jetIteratedDeriv x (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeffAt
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficient at `x` derivatives of a jet of endomorphisms of `V`:
differentiate `x` times and evaluate at the base point. It is the `V`-valued jet toolkit
applied to the value space `Module.End ℂ V`, and it is what a coefficient in
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` contributes to the derivative symbol `∂_x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetCoeffAt (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeffAt_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure coefficient `f ⊗ T` the Taylor coefficient is the base-point Taylor
coefficient of `f` times `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_tmul (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (T : Module.End ℂ V) :
    jetCoeffAt x (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] T)
      = constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f) • T

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeffAt_apply
declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficient of a jet of endomorphisms, evaluated at a vector, is the Taylor
coefficient of the `V`-valued jet obtained by feeding that vector to the coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_apply (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (c : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    jetCoeffAt x c v = jetEval (jetIteratedDeriv x (TensorProduct.lift
      ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) c v))

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.jetCoeffAt_jetCoeff
declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficients of the gauge coefficient are the Taylor coefficients of the
representation: `jetCoeff rep U` reproduces `rep U` on constant jets, and both sides of
this identity read off the same derivative of that.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_jetCoeff [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) (U : G)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetCoeffAt x (jetCoeff rep U) = GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff rep U x

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.symbolAction_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
A coefficient acts on the derivative symbol `∂_s ψ_φ` by the all-orders Leibniz
convolution of its base-point Taylor coefficients: each splitting `s = s₁ + s₂` of the
derivative multiset contributes the Taylor coefficient at `s₁` acting on the target index
of the lower symbol `∂_{s₂} ψ_φ`.

This is `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction_basis_multiset` in the derivative label,
together with the identification of the scalars it produces as `jetCoeffAt`; both sides
are additive in the coefficient, so it suffices to check it on a pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_basis_tmul (c : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    symbolAction c (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis p.2 ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (jetCoeffAt p.1 c).dualMap φ).sum

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.repDual_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
The transformation law of the derivative symbol `∂_s ψ_φ` under the jet gauge group:
the all-orders Leibniz convolution of the dual representation coefficients
`GaugeAlgebraRealization.repDualCoeff` against lower symbols, with no inhomogeneous term. This is
the identity the `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn` obligations of a matter field rest on.

Nothing here is special to the unconjugated half of the component space: the conjugate
half is this lemma at `repConj rep`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repDual_basis_tmul [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repDual rep hlin U (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis p.2 ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
            GaugeAlgebraRealization.repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ).sum

modules.title: The Lorentz law of the covariant derivatives of a matter family
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The covariant derivative of a matter family adds one ordered derivative slot and the
correction `A_ρ · F`, the derived action `actionFamConv` of the gauge field on the value
index. Expanded in bases, the correction is a scalar combination of Leibniz convolutions of
gauge-field symbols against matter symbols, which gives its Lorentz law and its linearity
in the matter family; the contragredient twist `rep.dual Λ` of the value index passes
through it when the infinitesimal gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action on the
value space (`hcomm`), the one hypothesis on the species. These are the inputs of the
abstract induction `Lorentz.repLorentz_tower`, for any realization of the gauge bosons in
a complex algebra `B`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_covDerivIter` : the Lorentz law of the iterated
  covariant derivative at every derivative multiset.
- `GaugeAlgebraRealization.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter`, `..._conj` : the
  covariant tower of a matter family, and of a conjugate family, transforms as the
  covariant derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Families in the multiset form of the Lorentz law
- B. The derived action family in bases
- C. The Lorentz law of the covariant tower

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Families in the multiset form of the Lorentz law
## B. The derived action family in bases
## C. The Lorentz law of the covariant tower

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.sum_derivConv_sum_fam
declarations.doc:
A scalar combination of convolutions against the gauge field is linear in the
right-hand families.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_derivConv_sum_fam {ι κ ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype ι']
    (f : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (coef : ι → κ → ℂ) (c : ι' → ℂ)
    (g : ι' → κ → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (f j) (fun y => ∑ i, c i • g i k y) s =
      ∑ i, c i • ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (f j) (g i k) s

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_eq_lorentzMix
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz law in the tuple form, read on the underlying multisets: the transformed
family mixes by `lorentzMix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_eq_lorentzMix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hfg : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)), repLorentz Λ (f (List.ofFn l)) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • g (List.ofFn p))
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : repLorentz Λ (f x) = lorentzMix Λ g x 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_apply_mix
declarations.doc: The Lorentz law of the gauge-field symbols, in the multiset form.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_apply_mix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (χ : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤) :
    repLorentz Λ (h.A x μ χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => ∑ a, L[Λ] a μ • h.A t a χ) x 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.isLorentzDerivTransforms_mix
declarations.doc: The Lorentz law of a family of derivative symbols, in the multiset form.

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_sum_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a scalar combination of convolutions against the gauge field: the
direction of the gauge field mixes by its own column, the derivative slots by
`lorentzMix`, and the right-hand families are replaced by their transforms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_sum_derivConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ 𝔤) (coef : ι → κ → ℂ)
    (g g' : κ → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hg : ∀ k y, repLorentz Λ (g k y) = lorentzMix Λ (g' k) y 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repLorentz Λ (∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (fun x => h.A x ρ (bg.coord j)) (g k) s) =
      ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ
        (fun t => ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (fun x => h.A x a (bg.coord j)) (g' k) t)
        s 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_apply_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The action of families expanded in bases of the gauge algebra and the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_apply_eq_sum {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ 𝔤) (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFam act f g φ =
      ∑ j, ∑ k, φ (act (bg j) (bv k)) • (f (bg.coord j) * g (bv.coord k))

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFamConv_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The derived action family expanded in bases.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_eq_sum {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ 𝔤) (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (G : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ G s φ = ∑ j, ∑ k, φ (act (bg j) (bv k)) •
      derivConv (fun x => A x ρ (bg.coord j)) (fun y => G y (bv.coord k)) s

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFamConv_sum_fam
declarations.doc: The derived action family is linear in the matter family.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_sum_fam {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : ι → ℂ)
    (H : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ (fun t => ∑ i, c i • H i t) s φ =
      ∑ i, c i • actionFamConv A act ρ (H i) s φ

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_actionFamConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the derived action family: the derivative slots mix, the direction
of the gauge field mixes by its own column, and the value index is carried by the
transformed matter family.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_actionFamConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (G G' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hG : ∀ y χ, repLorentz Λ (G y χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => G' t χ) y 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (actionFamConv h.A act ρ G s φ) =
      ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => actionFamConv h.A act a G' t φ) s 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.dual_twist
declarations.doc:
The twist of the value index past the gauge action: an endomorphism commuting with
the gauge action may be moved from the dual basis onto the dual vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_twist {κ : Type} [Fintype κ] (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V) (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v))
    (ψ : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (c : 𝔤) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    ∑ k, φ (act c (bv k)) • ψ (T.dualMap (bv.coord k)) =
      ∑ k, (T.dualMap φ) (act c (bv k)) • ψ (bv.coord k)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFam_comp_dual
declarations.doc:
The contragredient action may be pulled out of an action of families, provided the
gauge action commutes with it on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_comp_dual (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v))
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFam act f (g ∘ₗ T.dualMap) φ = actionFam act f g (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionFamConv_comp_dual
declarations.doc: The contragredient action may be pulled out of a derived action family.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_comp_dual (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (K : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ (fun t => K t ∘ₗ T.dualMap) s φ =
      actionFamConv A act ρ K s (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the iterated covariant derivative of a matter family: the ordered
covariant slots mix by their own columns and the multiset of plain derivative slots
mixes by `lorentzMix`, while the value index transforms contragrediently.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_covDerivIter {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep F) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (covDerivIter h.A act F n l s φ) = ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) •
        lorentzMix Λ (fun t => covDerivIter h.A act F n p t (rep.dual Λ φ)) s 0

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative of a matter family transforms as the covariant
derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field, given the Lorentz law of the bare symbols,
the Lorentz law of the gauge field, and the commutation of the infinitesimal gauge
action with the Lorentz action on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep F) :
    IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep (fun {n} l => covDerivIter h.A act F n l 0)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.actionConj_comm_repConj
declarations.doc:
Conjugation preserves the commutation of the gauge action with the Lorentz action:
both are read on the conjugate module through the same underlying maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionConj_comm_repConj (rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ConjModule V) :
    LocalGaugeData.actionConj act c (rep.conj Λ v) =
      rep.conj Λ (LocalGaugeData.actionConj act c v)

declarations.name: GaugeAlgebraRealization.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter_conj
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the covariant tower of a conjugate family, from the commutation of
the gauge action with the Lorentz action of the unconjugated species.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter_conj {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule V) →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep.conj F) :
    IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep.conj
      (fun {n} l => covDerivIter h.A (LocalGaugeData.actionConj act) F n l 0)

modules.title: Matrix representations of a jet gauge group
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A model-building table describes how a field transforms by a *matrix*: the jets of
gauge transformations act on the internal index `ι` of the field through a matrix of
jets `mat U`, the gauge algebra through a matrix of numbers `act c`, and the jets of the
gauge algebra through a matrix of jets `jetAct a`. This file packages such a matrix
representation as `LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep`, together with the two identities that make
`act` the infinitesimal action underlying `mat`: the *derivative identity*
`∂_μ (mat U) = -(jetAct (ω_μ U)) · mat U` in terms of the Maurer–Cartan form, and the
*equivariance identity* `mat U · jetAct c = jetAct (Ad_U c) · mat U`.

The internal index is tensored with a Lorentz representation `S`: the target space of
the field is `S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, and the jets of the field are identified with
`S ⊗ (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)`, on which `mat U` acts by matrix–vector multiplication. The main
theorem, `MatrixRep.isInfinitesimalActionOf`, shows that this action of the gauge algebra
is the infinitesimal action underlying the jet gauge action in the sense of
`LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`, once and for all matrix representations; the
compilation `MatrixRep.matterField` then produces a `MatterField`.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep` : a matrix representation of the jet gauge group with its
  infinitesimal action.
- `MatrixRep.jetEquiv` : the identification `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)) ≃ S ⊗ (ι →
  SpaceTimeAlgebra)`.
- `MatrixRep.repJet`, `MatrixRep.repJet_smul` : the fibrewise jet gauge action.
- `MatrixRep.repCoeff_eq` : the base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet gauge action.
- `MatrixRep.isInfinitesimalActionOf` : the gauge-algebra action is the infinitesimal
  action underlying the jet gauge action.
- `MatrixRep.matterField` : the matter field of a matrix representation.
- `MatrixRep.matterField_gaugeLorentzCompatible` : its gauge and Lorentz actions commute,
  acting on different tensor factors.
- `MatrixRep.matterField_pureJetsActTrivially` : pure jets act trivially on it at the base
  point, when their matrices have identity constant term.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Matrix representations
- B. The target space and its jets
  - B.1. The target space
- C. Endomorphisms from matrices
- D. The jet gauge action
- E. The base-point Taylor coefficients
- F. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action
- G. The matter field
  - G.1. The global action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Matrix representations

## B. The target space and its jets

The target space of the field is `S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` for a Lorentz representation `S`; its jets
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ (S ⊗ (ι → ℂ))` are identified with `S ⊗ (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)` by absorbing the
jet ring into the internal index.

### B.1. The target space

The target space `V` of the field is any complex vector space identified, through `e`,
with `S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` for a Lorentz representation `S`. Keeping `V` abstract (rather than
taking `V = S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` itself) keeps the real-scalar structure on `V` the canonical
`Module.complexToReal`, and lets the concrete target spaces of a model serve as `V`.
## C. Endomorphisms from matrices
## D. The jet gauge action
## E. The base-point Taylor coefficients
## F. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action
## G. The matter field

### G.1. The global action

A matrix representation of jets restricts to the jets of constant gauge transformations;
the constant terms of their matrices are the matrices of a representation of the global
gauge group on the target space. When the matrices of constant jets are constant, the jet
action on a constant jet is this global action on the value factor.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep
declarations.doc:
**A matrix representation** of the jets of gauge transformations on an internal index
`ι`: the jets act by the matrix of jets `mat U`, the gauge algebra by the matrix `act c`,
and the jets of the gauge algebra by the matrix of jets `jetAct a`, subject to the
derivative identity and the equivariance identity that make `act` the infinitesimal
action underlying `mat`.
declarations.statement:
structure MatrixRep (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    where
  /-- The matrix of jets by which a jet of gauge transformations acts. -/
  mat : GJ → Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra
  mat_one : mat 1 = 1
  mat_mul : ∀ U V, mat (U * V) = mat U * mat V
  /-- The matrix by which an element of the gauge algebra acts. -/
  act : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix ι ι ℂ
  /-- The matrix of jets by which a jet of gauge algebra elements acts. -/
  jetAct : 𝔤J → Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra
  jetAct_ofConstantLie : ∀ c, jetAct (jets.ofConstantLie c) = (act c).map (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra)
  /-- The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action matrix are the action matrices
    of the base-point Taylor coefficients. -/
  jetAct_map_cc_foldl : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : 𝔤J),
    ((jetAct a).map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p f))
      = act (jets.evalLie (jets.iteratedDeriv p a))
  /-- The derivative identity: the formal derivative of the matrix of a gauge jet is minus
    the jet action of its Maurer–Cartan form times the matrix. -/
  mat_map_pderiv : ∀ (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    (mat U).map (fun f => pderiv μ f) = -(jetAct (jets.maurerCartan U μ) * mat U)
  /-- The equivariance identity: the matrix of a gauge jet intertwines the constant jet
    action with its adjoint transform. -/
  mat_mul_jetAct : ∀ (U : GJ) (c : 𝔤),
    mat U * jetAct (jets.ofConstantLie c)
      = jetAct (jets.adjointJ U (jets.ofConstantLie c)) * mat U

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.pderivPi
declarations.doc: The entrywise formal derivative on `ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra`, as a `ℂ`-linear map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pderivPi (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) →ₗ[ℂ]
    (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.pderivPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma pderivPi_apply (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (w : ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) (i : ι) :
    pderivPi μ w i = pderiv μ (w i)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.foldPi
declarations.doc: The entrywise iterated formal derivative on `ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra`, as a `ℂ`-linear map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def foldPi (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) →ₗ[ℂ] (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.foldPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma foldPi_apply (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (w : ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) (i : ι) :
    foldPi x w i = SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x (w i)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.foldPi_zero
declarations.statement: lemma foldPi_zero : foldPi (ι := ι) 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.pderivPi_comp_foldPi
declarations.statement:
lemma pderivPi_comp_foldPi (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    pderivPi (ι := ι) μ ∘ₗ foldPi x = foldPi (μ ::ₘ x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.ccPi
declarations.doc: The entrywise base-point evaluation on `ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra`, as a `ℂ`-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ccPi : (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) →ₗ[ℂ] (ι → ℂ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.ccPi_apply
declarations.statement: lemma ccPi_apply (w : ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) (i : ι) : ccPi w i = constantCoeff (w i)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.C_mul_eq_smul
declarations.doc: A constant jet times a jet is the scalar multiple.
declarations.statement: lemma C_mul_eq_smul (z : ℂ) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) : (C z : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * f = z • f

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.ccPi_foldPi_mulVec
declarations.doc:
The base-point evaluation of the iterated derivative of a matrix–vector product with
constant entries is the matrix–vector product of the base-point coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma ccPi_foldPi_mulVec (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (v : ι → ℂ) :
    ccPi (foldPi x (A.mulVec fun k => (C (v k) : SpaceTimeAlgebra)))
      = (A.map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f)).mulVec v

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv
declarations.doc:
The jets of a `V`-valued field as `S ⊗ (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)`, through the identification
`e : V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`: the jet ring is absorbed into the internal index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetEquiv (e : V ≃ₗ[ℂ] S ⊗[ℂ] (ι → ℂ)) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V ≃ₗ[ℂ] S ⊗[ℂ] (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEquiv_tmul (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    jetEquiv e (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) = s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (fun i => v i • f)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.induction_on
declarations.doc: Induction on the jets of a `V`-valued field through the identification `e`.
declarations.statement:
lemma induction_on {P : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V → Prop} (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (tmul : ∀ (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ), P (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)))
    (add : ∀ a b, P a → P b → P (a + b)) : P z

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The identification of jets intertwines the formal derivative with the entrywise
derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEquiv_jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEquiv e (jetDeriv μ z) = LinearMap.lTensor S (pderivPi μ) (jetEquiv e z)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv
declarations.doc:
The identification of jets intertwines the iterated formal derivative with the
entrywise iterated derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEquiv_jetIteratedDeriv (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEquiv e (jetIteratedDeriv x z) = LinearMap.lTensor S (foldPi x) (jetEquiv e z)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEval_eq
declarations.doc: The base-point evaluation of a jet through the identification.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_eq (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEval z = e.symm (LinearMap.lTensor S ccPi (jetEquiv e z))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv_smul
declarations.doc: Multiplication by a scalar jet through the identification.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEquiv e (χ • z)
      = LinearMap.lTensor S
          ((LinearMap.lsmul SpaceTimeAlgebra (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) χ).restrictScalars ℂ)
          (jetEquiv e z)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEquiv_jetOfConstant
declarations.doc: A jet of a constant through the identification.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEquiv_jetOfConstant (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    jetEquiv e (jetOfConstant (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v))) = s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (fun i => C (v i))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEndAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` defined by a complex matrix on
the internal index, as an algebra map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEndAlgHom : Matrix ι ι ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` defined by a complex matrix on
the internal index, with the Lorentz factor untouched.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEnd (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_apply (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (d : V) :
    valEnd e B d = e.symm (LinearMap.lTensor S (Matrix.toLin' B) (e d))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_apply_symm_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_apply_symm_tmul (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    valEnd e B (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) = e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (B.mulVec v))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_add
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_add (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (A + B) = valEnd e A + valEnd e B

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_smul
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (z • A) = z • valEnd e A

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_zero
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_zero : valEnd e (0 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_neg
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_neg (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (-A) = -valEnd e A

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_multiset_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_multiset_sum (m : Multiset (Matrix ι ι ℂ)) :
    valEnd e m.sum = (m.map (valEnd e)).sum

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_mul
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_mul (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (A * B) = valEnd e A ∘ₗ valEnd e B

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.valEnd_one
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_one : valEnd e (1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of `S ⊗ (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)` defined by a matrix of jets on the internal
index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetEnd (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    S ⊗[ℂ] (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) →ₗ[ℂ] S ⊗[ℂ] (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEnd_eq_lTensor
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEnd_eq_lTensor (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    jetEnd S A = LinearMap.lTensor S
      ((Matrix.toLinAlgEquiv' A : Module.End SpaceTimeAlgebra
          (ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra)).restrictScalars ℂ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEnd_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEnd_tmul (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) (s : S) (w : ι → SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    jetEnd S A (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] w) = s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (A.mulVec w)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEnd_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetEnd_one : jetEnd S (1 : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.jetEnd_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEnd_mul (A B : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) : jetEnd S (A * B) =
    jetEnd S A ∘ₗ jetEnd S B

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the jets `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ V` of the field defined by a matrix of jets
on the internal index, through `jetEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matEnd
    (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matEnd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma matEnd_apply (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    matEnd e A z = (jetEquiv e).symm (jetEnd S A (jetEquiv e z))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matEnd_one
declarations.statement: lemma matEnd_one : matEnd e (1 : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matEnd_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma matEnd_mul (A B : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    matEnd e (A * B) = matEnd e A ∘ₗ matEnd e B

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matEnd_smul
declarations.doc:
The matrix endomorphisms are fibrewise: they commute with multiplication by scalar
jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma matEnd_smul (A : Matrix ι ι SpaceTimeAlgebra) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    matEnd e A (χ • z) = χ • matEnd e A z

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repJet
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action** of a matrix representation on the jets of a `V`-valued
field: the matrix of jets acts on the internal index by matrix–vector multiplication,
with the Lorentz factor untouched.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repJet : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repJet_apply
declarations.statement: lemma repJet_apply (U : GJ) : R.repJet e U = matEnd e (R.mat U)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repJet_smul
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action is fibrewise**: it commutes with multiplication by scalar
jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_smul (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    R.repJet e U (χ • z) = χ • R.repJet e U z

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The action of the gauge algebra** of a matrix representation on the target space
`V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`: the action matrix acts on the internal index, real-linearly in the
algebra slot and complex-linearly in the value slot.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repAlgebra : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repAlgebra_apply
declarations.statement: lemma repAlgebra_apply (c : 𝔤) : R.repAlgebra e c = valEnd e (R.act c)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repCoeff_eq
declarations.doc:
**The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet gauge action** are the endomorphisms
of the base-point Taylor coefficients of the matrix of jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_eq (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (R.repJet e) U x
      = valEnd e ((R.mat U).map fun f =>
          constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.isInfinitesimalActionOf
declarations.doc:
**The action of the gauge algebra of a matrix representation is the infinitesimal
action underlying its jet gauge action**: the base-point Taylor coefficients obey the
Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and intertwine the action with the adjoint transports.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf :
    jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf (R.repAlgebra e) (R.repJet e)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repLorentz
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`: the given action on the
Lorentz factor `S`, transported through `e`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repLorentz (ρ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) :
    Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repGlobal
declarations.doc:
**The global gauge action** of a matrix representation of jets: a global gauge
transformation acts by the constant term of the matrix of its constant jet.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repGlobal : Representation ℂ G₀ V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repGlobal_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repGlobal_apply (g : G₀) :
    R.repGlobal e g = valEnd e
        ((R.mat (jets.ofConstant g)).map (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra → ℂ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repGlobal_apply_symm_tmul
declarations.doc:
The global action on a pure tensor: the constant term of the matrix acts on the
internal index.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGlobal_apply_symm_tmul (g : G₀) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    R.repGlobal e g (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v))
      = e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
          ((R.mat (jets.ofConstant g)).map (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra → ℂ)).mulVec v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.map_C_mulVec_smul
declarations.doc:
A matrix of constant jets acts on a scalar jet times a constant vector through its
constant matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_C_mulVec_smul (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (v : ι → ℂ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    (B.map (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra)).mulVec (fun i => v i • χ) = fun i => (B.mulVec v) i • χ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repJet_ofConstant
declarations.doc:
**On jets of constant gauge transformations the jet action is the global action** on
the value factor, provided the matrices of constant jets are constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_ofConstant
    (hconst : ∀ g, R.mat (jets.ofConstant g)
      = ((R.mat (jets.ofConstant g)).map (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra → ℂ)).map
          (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra))
    (g : G₀) :
    R.repJet e (jets.ofConstant g) = TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (R.repGlobal e g)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField
declarations.doc:
**The matter field of a matrix representation**: the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`
with the Lorentz action on `S`, the jet gauge action of the matrix representation, and
the given mass weight and declared statistics.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matterField (ρ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) (w : ℕ) (σ : FieldStatistic) :
    MatterField jets

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_V
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_V : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).V = V

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_repLorentz
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_repLorentz : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).repLorentz = repLorentz e ρ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_repJet
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_repJet : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).repJet = R.repJet e

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_repAlgebra
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_repAlgebra : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).repAlgebra = R.repAlgebra e

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_massWeight
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_massWeight : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).massWeight = w

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_statistic
declarations.statement: lemma matterField_statistic : (R.matterField e ρ w σ).statistic = σ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repLorentz_apply_symm_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_apply_symm_tmul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    repLorentz e ρ Λ (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) = e.symm (ρ Λ s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.repAlgebra_comm_repLorentz
declarations.doc:
The gauge algebra acts on the internal index and the Lorentz group on the Lorentz
factor, so the two actions commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebra_comm_repLorentz (c : 𝔤) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V) :
    R.repAlgebra e c (repLorentz e ρ Λ v) = repLorentz e ρ Λ (R.repAlgebra e c v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_gaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
The matter field of a matrix representation satisfies `MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible`,
for every matrix representation and Lorentz factor: the two actions live on different
tensor factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_gaugeLorentzCompatible :
    (R.matterField e ρ w σ).GaugeLorentzCompatible

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.matterField_pureJetsActTrivially
declarations.doc:
The matter field of a matrix representation satisfies `MatterField.PureJetsActTrivially`
as soon as the matrix of every jet with trivial value has identity constant term. This
hypothesis is not a consequence of the axioms of `MatrixRep`, which fix the constant term
of `mat` on pure jets only up to a scalar character.
declarations.statement:
lemma matterField_pureJetsActTrivially
    (hmat : ∀ {W : GJ}, jets.eval W = 1 → (R.mat W).map
        (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra → ℂ) = 1) :
    (R.matterField e ρ w σ).PureJetsActTrivially

modules.title: Constructions of matrix representations
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The matrix representations of a jet gauge group are closed under the operations by which
a model-building table combines the representations of the factors of the gauge group:
the trivial (singlet) representation, the Kronecker (tensor) product of two
representations, and the conjugate of a representation. This file provides these three
constructions; the representations of the individual factors are built in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.MatrixRep.Factors`.

## ii. Key results

- `MatrixRep.trivial` : the singlet representation on `Fin 1`.
- `MatrixRep.kron` : the Kronecker product of two matrix representations.
- `MatrixRep.conj` : the conjugate of a matrix representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Matrices with an identity factor
- B. The trivial representation
- C. The Kronecker product
- D. The conjugate representation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Matrices with an identity factor

Entrywise maps that send `0` to `0` pass through a Kronecker product with an identity
factor, whether or not they are multiplicative.
## B. The trivial representation
## C. The Kronecker product
## D. The conjugate representation

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.kronecker_one_map
declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_one_map [MulZeroOneClass α] [MulZeroOneClass β] (φ : α → β) (h0 : φ 0 = 0)
    (A : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ α) :
    (A ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ α)).map φ = (A.map φ) ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ β)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.one_kronecker_map
declarations.statement:
lemma one_kronecker_map [MulZeroOneClass α] [MulZeroOneClass β] (φ : α → β) (h0 : φ 0 = 0)
    (B : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ α) :
    ((1 : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ α) ⊗ₖ B).map φ = (1 : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ β) ⊗ₖ (B.map φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.kronecker_map_of_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_map_of_mul [Mul α] [Mul β] (φ : α → β) (hφ : ∀ a b, φ (a * b) = φ a * φ b)
    (A : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ α) (B : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ α) :
    (A ⊗ₖ B).map φ = (A.map φ) ⊗ₖ (B.map φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.neg_kronecker
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_kronecker [Mul α] [HasDistribNeg α] (A : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ α) (B : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ α) :
    (-A) ⊗ₖ B = -(A ⊗ₖ B)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.kronecker_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_neg [Mul α] [HasDistribNeg α] (A : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ α) (B : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ α) :
    A ⊗ₖ (-B) = -(A ⊗ₖ B)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.trivial
declarations.doc:
**The trivial representation**: the one-dimensional singlet, on which every gauge jet
acts as the identity and the gauge algebra by zero.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def trivial : MatrixRep jets (Fin 1)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.kron
declarations.doc:
**The Kronecker product** of two matrix representations: the gauge jets act by the
Kronecker product of the two matrices of jets, the gauge algebra by the Kronecker sum
of the two action matrices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kron (R₁ : MatrixRep jets ι₁) (R₂ : MatrixRep jets ι₂) :
    MatrixRep jets (ι₁ × ι₂)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.foldl_pderiv_star
declarations.doc: The iterated formal derivative commutes with conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma foldl_pderiv_star (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    x.foldl (fun h ρ => pderiv ρ h) (star f) = star (x.foldl (fun h ρ => pderiv ρ h) f)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.conj
declarations.doc:
**The conjugate representation**: the gauge jets act by the entrywise conjugate matrix
of jets, the gauge algebra by the entrywise conjugate action matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conj (R : MatrixRep jets ι) : MatrixRep jets ι

modules.title: The factors of a gauge group as matrix representations
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A model-building table assigns to each field one charge per factor of the gauge group: a
rational charge under a `U(1)` factor, a representation label under an `SU(n)` factor.
The factors themselves, `LocalGaugeData.U1Factor` and `LocalGaugeData.SUFactor`, are part
of the gauge data (`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Factor`). This
file builds the representations they name: `U1Factor.charge n R` twists a matrix
representation `R` by the charge-`n` power of the unitary jet, and `SUFactor.fund` is the
fundamental representation. Together with `MatrixRep.trivial`, `MatrixRep.kron` and
`MatrixRep.conj`, every representation named in a table is assembled from these.

## ii. Key results

- `U1Factor.charge` : the charge twist of a matrix representation by a `U(1)` factor.
- `MatterField.pderiv_chargePow` : the derivative of a power of a unitary jet.
- `SUFactor.fund` : the fundamental representation of an `SU(n)` factor.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Powers of a unitary jet
- B. The charge twist of a `U(1)` factor
- C. The fundamental representation of an `SU(n)` factor

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Powers of a unitary jet
## B. The charge twist of a `U(1)` factor
## C. The fundamental representation of an `SU(n)` factor

declarations.name: MatterField.pderiv_chargePow
declarations.doc:
**The derivative of a power of a unitary jet**: `∂_μ (u ^ n) = n · u ^ n · (u⁻¹ ∂_μ u)`,
for every integer `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pderiv_chargePow (n : ℤ) (w : unitary SpaceTimeAlgebra) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    pderiv μ (chargePow n w)
      = (n : ℂ) •
          (chargePow n w * (star (w : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * pderiv μ (w : SpaceTimeAlgebra)))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.U1Factor.pderiv_chargePow_u
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the charge-`n` power of the unitary jet of a gauge jet, in terms of
the Maurer–Cartan form: `∂_μ (u ^ n) = -(i n) φJ (ω_μ U) · u ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pderiv_chargePow_u (n : ℤ) (U : GJ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    pderiv μ (chargePow n (F.u U))
      = -(((Complex.I * n) • F.φJ (jets.maurerCartan U μ)) * chargePow n (F.u U))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.U1Factor.charge
declarations.doc:
**The charge twist**: a matrix representation twisted by the charge-`n` power of the
unitary jet of the `U(1)` factor. The gauge algebra acts by the original action plus
`i n` times the `u(1)` component.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def charge (n : ℤ) (R : MatrixRep jets ι) : MatrixRep jets ι

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SUFactor.fund
declarations.doc:
**The fundamental representation** of an `SU(n)` factor: the gauge jets act by their
unitary matrices of jets, the gauge algebra by `i` times its matrix component.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fund : MatrixRep jets n

modules.title: Model tables
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A gauge-theory model is written down, as in a model-building tool, as a *table*: the gauge
group as a list of factors, and for each field its number of generations, its Lorentz
label and one charge per factor — an integer charge under a `U(1)` factor, a
representation label under an `SU(n)` factor.

This file defines the tables over any local gauge data and compiles them into the general
theory. A gauge group is a list of `Factor`s of the local gauge data
(`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalGaugeData.Factor`); the charges of a field
form the tuple `Charges Γ` over the list; the charges name a matrix representation
`Charges.rep`, assembled from the factors by the hypercharge twist and the Kronecker
product; a field is its Lorentz label and its charges,
`MatterFieldData Γ`, so that it reads `(.L, .singlet, .fund, -3)`, and compiles to a
`MatterField`; the field data of a model, `FieldData Γ Fields`, assigns each field its
number of generations and its data, and compiles to a `GaugeFieldData`.

## ii. Key results

- `SURep`, `Charges` : the charge labels of a row and the charge tuple.
- `Charges.rep` : the matrix representation named by a charge tuple.
- `LorentzLabel`, `MatterFieldData` : the Lorentz label and the data of a field.
- `LorentzLabel.statistic` : the statistics a table row declares for a label, by convention
  fermionic for a Weyl spinor and bosonic for a scalar.
- `MatterFieldData.toMatterField`, `toMatterFieldOn` : the matter field of a datum, on the
  tensor-product target space or on any target space presented as one.
- `FieldData`, `FieldData.toGaugeFieldData` : the field data of a model and its compilation.
- `FieldData.toGaugeFieldData_gaugeLorentzCompatible` : the field content of a model
  satisfies `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Charge labels
- B. Charge tuples and their internal index
- C. The representation named by a charge tuple
- D. Matter field data and its matter field
- E. The field data of a model and its field content

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Charge labels
## B. Charge tuples and their internal index

## C. The representation named by a charge tuple

The representation is assembled in two steps. The `SU(n)` labels give a Kronecker product
of fundamental and antifundamental representations over the nontrivial dimensions,
`Charges.suRep`, in which a singlet contributes no factor and the trivial representation is
dropped rather than tensored in; the `U(1)` charges then twist the result, `Charges.twist`.

## D. Matter field data and its matter field

A field of a model is written down as its Lorentz label and its charge tuple, so that
`(.L, .singlet, .fund, -3)` is a left-handed doublet of hypercharge `-3`. The datum
compiles to a `MatterField` on the target space `S ⊗ (Idx → ℂ)` of the label's Lorentz
factor and the internal index of the charges, or, through an identification `e`, on any
target space presented as such a tensor product. The label also gives the field its mass
weight and its declared statistics.
## E. The field data of a model and its field content

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SURep
declarations.doc: **A representation label under `SU(n)`.**
declarations.statement:
inductive SURep
  /-- The singlet `1`. -/
  | singlet
  /-- The fundamental `n`. -/
  | fund
  /-- The antifundamental `n̄`. -/
  | antifund
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SURep.dim
declarations.doc: The dimension of the representation of `SU(n)` a label names.
declarations.statement: abbrev SURep.dim (n : ℕ) : SURep → ℕ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SURep.rep
declarations.doc: The matrix representation of an `SU(n)` factor named by a label.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def SURep.rep {n : ℕ} (F : SUFactor jets (Fin n)) :
    (r : SURep) → MatrixRep jets (Fin (r.dim n))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Factor.Charge
declarations.doc:
The charge a field carries under a factor: an integer under `U(1)`, a representation
label under `SU(n)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Factor.Charge : Factor jets → Type

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Charges
declarations.doc:
**The charge tuple** of a row: one charge per factor, as a nested pair so that a row
reads `(1, .fund, .fund)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Charges : Factors jets → Type

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.IdxOfDims
declarations.doc:
**The internal index of a list of dimensions**: the product of the `Fin n` over the
list, with `Fin 1` for the empty list and no trailing factor for a one-element list.
declarations.statement: abbrev IdxOfDims : List ℕ → Type

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.IdxOfDims.fintype
declarations.doc: The index of a list of dimensions is finite.
declarations.statement: def IdxOfDims.fintype : (ds : List ℕ) → Fintype (IdxOfDims ds)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.IdxOfDims.decidableEq
declarations.doc: The index of a list of dimensions has decidable equality.
declarations.statement: def IdxOfDims.decidableEq : (ds : List ℕ) → DecidableEq (IdxOfDims ds)
instance (ds : List ℕ) : Fintype (IdxOfDims ds)
instance (ds : List ℕ) : DecidableEq (IdxOfDims ds)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.SURep.dims
declarations.doc:
The dimensions an `SU(n)` label contributes to the internal index: none for the
singlet, `n` for the fundamental and the antifundamental.
declarations.statement: abbrev SURep.dims (n : ℕ) : SURep → List ℕ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Charges.dims
declarations.doc:
**The dimensions of the internal index** of a charge tuple: the sizes of the
nontrivial `SU(n)` representations it names, in the order of the factors. `U(1)` factors
and singlets contribute nothing, so that a field charged under a single `SU(n)` factor is
indexed by `Fin n` alone.
declarations.statement: abbrev Charges.dims : (Γ : Factors jets) → Charges Γ → List ℕ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.Idx
declarations.doc:
**The internal index** of a field with the given charges: the product of the
nontrivial `SU(n)`-representation indices.
declarations.statement: abbrev Idx (Γ : Factors jets) (c : Charges Γ) : Type

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.MatrixRep.kronDims
declarations.doc:
The Kronecker product with the representation on the remaining dimensions, with the
trivial representation dropped when there are none.

modules.title: The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`MatterField.prod` sums two matter fields of the same mass weight and statistics. This file
does the same for a finite family `M : ι → MatterField jets`, producing a single matter
field valued in `∀ i, (M i).V`. It is the operation that turns the several species of a
theory into one field: the fifteen fermionic multiplets of the Standard Model become one
fermion field, carried by `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField`.

The binary and indexed versions are the same construction with `LinearMap.prodMap`
replaced by `LinearMap.piMap` and `jetProdEquiv` by `jetPiEquiv`, so the proofs run in
parallel; only the diagonal-map algebra used along the way differs. As in the binary case,
the direct sum is represented by one `MatterField`, which has one mass weight and one
statistic, so the summands must share both. The caller supplies the common values `w` and
`σ`, together with proofs that every summand has them, so the direct sum of an empty family
also has a definite weight and statistics.

Finiteness of `ι` is essential and not merely convenient. `jetPiEquiv` — the
identification of the jets of the product with the product of the jets, through which the
jet gauge action is defined — exists only for a finite index type, and finiteness of the
value space, a field of `MatterField`, would fail for an infinite family in any case.

## ii. Key results

- `MatterField.repJetPi` : the jet gauge action of an indexed direct sum.
- `MatterField.repJetPi_smul` : it is fibrewise, as each summand is.
- `MatterField.lTensor_proj_repJetPi` : the projection onto a summand intertwines it with
  that summand's own action.
- `MatterField.repAlgebraPi` : the infinitesimal gauge action of an indexed direct sum.
- `MatterField.repCoeff_repJetPi` : its base-point Taylor coefficients are the family of
  those of the summands.
- `MatterField.pi` : the direct sum of a finite family of matter fields of one mass
  weight and one statistic.
- `MatterField.jetComponentSpacePiEquiv` : the component space of the direct sum is the
  family of the component spaces of the summands.
- `MatterField.jetComponentSpacePiEquiv_symm_single` : a summand sits inside it as the
  pullback along the projection onto that summand.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Diagonal maps of an indexed product
- B. The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields
- C. The component space of the direct sum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Diagonal maps of an indexed product

Every piece of data of the direct sum acts index by index, that is through
`LinearMap.piMap`. The four facts about that construction used below — that it is
additive, negative-preserving and multiset-sum-preserving in the family, and that it
composes index by index — all hold because `piMap` is evaluated pointwise, so each is a
single `LinearMap.ext`.
## B. The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields

## C. The component space of the direct sum

The direct sum was built so that the several species of a theory can be treated as one
field. Nothing is lost in doing so at the level of component functions either: the
symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and `∂_s ψ̄_α` of the summed field are exactly the families, over the
index, of the symbols of the summands. This is the component-space image of the
identification `jetPiEquiv` that defines the summed jet action, and it is the finite
direct sum case of `JetComponentSpace.piEquiv`.

declarations.name: MatterField.repPi
declarations.doc:
The product of a family of representations, acting index by index. This is the
indexed analogue of `Representation.prod`, which Mathlib provides only in the binary
case.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repPi {W : ι → Type} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (W i)]
    [∀ i, Module ℂ (W i)] (ρ : ∀ i, Representation ℂ GJ (W i)) :
    Representation ℂ GJ (∀ i, W i)

declarations.name: MatterField.repJetPi
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action of an indexed direct sum**: the family of actions, read
through the identification of the jets of `∀ i, (M i).V` with the family of jets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repJetPi : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V))

declarations.name: MatterField.repJetPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetPi_apply (U : GJ) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)) :
    repJetPi M U z = (jetPiEquiv fun i => (M i).V).symm
      (fun i => (M i).repJet U (jetPiEquiv (fun i => (M i).V) z i))

declarations.name: MatterField.repJetPi_smul
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge action of an indexed direct sum is fibrewise. It acts index by
index, and each summand is fibrewise, so multiplication by a scalar jet passes through
the splitting untouched. This is the field `repJet_smul` of `MatterField.pi`, stated
separately so that it can be used without fixing a common mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetPi_smul (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)) :
    repJetPi M U (χ • z) = χ • repJetPi M U z

declarations.name: MatterField.lTensor_proj_repJetPi
declarations.doc:
A summand is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action of the direct sum. The
projection onto the value space of one summand, applied to the jets, intertwines the
summed action with that summand's own: the summed action is the family of the actions,
and reading off a summand of the jets is the projection on the value factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_proj_repJetPi (i : ι) (U : GJ) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i)).comp (repJetPi M U)
      = ((M i).repJet U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i))

declarations.name: MatterField.repAlgebraPi
declarations.doc:
**The infinitesimal action of an indexed direct sum**: the family of actions, one on
each summand.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repAlgebraPi : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] (∀ i, (M i).V) →ₗ[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)

declarations.name: MatterField.repAlgebraPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebraPi_apply (c : 𝔤) :
    repAlgebraPi M c = LinearMap.piMap fun i => (M i).repAlgebra c

declarations.name: MatterField.repCoeff_repJetPi
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the summed jet action are the family of the
coefficients of the summands: `jetOfConstant`, `jetIteratedDeriv` and `jetEval` all act
index by index through `jetPiEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repJetPi (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (repJetPi M) U x =
      LinearMap.piMap fun i => GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (M i).repJet U x

declarations.name: MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraPi
declarations.doc:
**The index-by-index algebra action generates the index-by-index jet action**: both
laws of `IsInfinitesimalActionOf` are the corresponding laws of the summands, read
through `repCoeff_repJetPi`, since `piMap` is additive in the family and composes index
by index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraPi :
    jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf (repAlgebraPi M) (repJetPi M)

declarations.name: MatterField.pi
declarations.doc:
**The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields** with common mass weight `w` and
common statistics `σ`, given with proofs that every summand has them. It is one field
valued in `∀ i, (M i).V`, of weight `w` and statistics `σ`, with every action acting index
by index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pi (w : ℕ) (_h : ∀ i, (M i).massWeight = w) (σ : FieldStatistic)
    (_hσ : ∀ i, (M i).statistic = σ) : MatterField jets

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_V
declarations.statement: lemma pi_V : (pi M w h σ hσ).V = ∀ i, (M i).V

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_repJet
declarations.statement: lemma pi_repJet : (pi M w h σ hσ).repJet = repJetPi M

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_repAlgebra
declarations.statement: lemma pi_repAlgebra : (pi M w h σ hσ).repAlgebra = repAlgebraPi M

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_massWeight
declarations.statement: lemma pi_massWeight : (pi M w h σ hσ).massWeight = w

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_statistic
declarations.statement: lemma pi_statistic : (pi M w h σ hσ).statistic = σ

declarations.name: MatterField.pi_repLorentz_apply
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action of the direct sum is the family of Lorentz actions, acting index by
index.
declarations.statement:
lemma pi_repLorentz_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ∀ i, (M i).V) (i : ι) :
    (pi M w h σ hσ).repLorentz Λ v i = (M i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

declarations.name: MatterField.jetComponentSpacePiEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The component space of a direct sum of matter fields splits.** A component function
of `MatterField.pi M w h σ hσ` is exactly a family, one component function per summand. Both
halves split by `JetComponentSpace.fstPiEquiv` and `JetComponentSpace.sndPiEquiv`, and
the pair of families is reassembled into a family of pairs index by index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetComponentSpacePiEquiv :
    JetComponentSpace (pi M w h σ hσ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, JetComponentSpace (M i)

declarations.name: MatterField.jetComponentSpacePiEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma jetComponentSpacePiEquiv_apply (x : JetComponentSpace (pi M w h σ hσ)) (i : ι) :
    jetComponentSpacePiEquiv M w h σ hσ x i =
      (JetComponentSpace.fstPiEquiv (fun i => (M i).V) x.1 i,
        JetComponentSpace.sndPiEquiv (fun i => (M i).V) x.2 i)

declarations.name: MatterField.jetComponentSpacePiEquiv_symm_single
declarations.doc:
**The summand of one species is the pullback along the projection onto it.** A
component function of the summand `i`, placed in the family and read back as a component
function of the direct sum, is that function precomposed with the projection onto the
summand. This is what identifies the splitting with the species inclusions of a direct
sum of component spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetComponentSpacePiEquiv_symm_single (i : ι) (x : JetComponentSpace (M i)) :
    (jetComponentSpacePiEquiv M w h σ hσ).symm (Pi.single i x)
      = JetComponentSpace.comap
        (LinearMap.proj (φ := fun i => (M i).V) i : (pi M w h σ hσ).V →ₗ[ℂ] (M i).V) x

modules.title: The direct sum of two matter fields
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Two matter fields of a gauge theory with the same mass weight and the same declared
statistics combine into one, valued in the product of their value spaces. This is the
operation that lets a multiplet be described either as one field or as its summands: three
generations of a fermion type, or the two chiralities of a Dirac field, are the direct sum
of their pieces.

Every piece of data acts componentwise. The Lorentz representation and the infinitesimal
gauge action are `LinearMap.prodMap` of the two; the jet gauge action is the pair of the
two, read through the identification `jetProdEquiv` of the jets of a product with the
product of the jets. The direct sum is one `MatterField`, with one mass weight and one
statistic, so it takes as hypotheses that the two fields have the same mass weight and the
same statistics.

What has to be proved is the last field of the structure — that the componentwise
infinitesimal action still generates the componentwise jet action.

## ii. Key results

- `MatterField.repJetProd` : the jet gauge action of a direct sum.
- `MatterField.repAlgebraProd` : the infinitesimal gauge action of a direct sum.
- `MatterField.repCoeff_repJetProd` : its base-point Taylor coefficients are the pair of
  those of the summands.
- `MatterField.prod` : the direct sum of two matter fields of the same mass weight and
  statistics.
- `JetComponentSpace.prodEquiv` : the component space of a direct sum splits.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The direct sum of two matter fields
- B. The component space of a direct sum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The direct sum of two matter fields

Two matter fields of the same mass weight combine into one, valued in the product of their
value spaces. Every piece of data acts componentwise: the Lorentz and gauge algebra
actions by `LinearMap.prodMap`, and the jet gauge action through the identification
`jetProdEquiv` of the jets of a product with the product of the jets. What has to be
checked is the last field — that the componentwise algebra action still generates the
componentwise jet action.
## B. The component space of a direct sum

declarations.name: MatterField.repJetProd
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action of a direct sum**: the two actions, read through the
identification of the jets of `M.V × N.V` with the pair of jets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetProd :
    Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (M.V × N.V))

declarations.name: MatterField.repJetProd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetProd_apply (U : GJ) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)) :
    repJetProd M N U z =
      jetProdEquiv.symm (M.repJet U (jetProdEquiv z).1, N.repJet U (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: MatterField.repAlgebraProd
declarations.doc: **The infinitesimal action of a direct sum**: the two actions on the two summands.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repAlgebraProd : 𝔤 →ₗ[ℝ] (M.V × N.V) →ₗ[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)

declarations.name: MatterField.repAlgebraProd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebraProd_apply (c : 𝔤) :
    repAlgebraProd M N c = (M.repAlgebra c).prodMap (N.repAlgebra c)

declarations.name: MatterField.repCoeff_repJetProd
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the summed jet action are the pair of the
coefficients of the summands: `jetOfConstant`, `jetIteratedDeriv` and `jetEval` all act
componentwise through `jetProdEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repJetProd (U : GJ) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff (repJetProd M N) U x =
      (GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff M.repJet U x).prodMap
        (GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff N.repJet U x)

declarations.name: MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraProd
declarations.doc:
**The componentwise algebra action generates the componentwise jet action**: both laws
of `IsInfinitesimalActionOf` are the corresponding laws of the summands, read through
`repCoeff_repJetProd`, since `prodMap` is additive in both slots at once and composes
componentwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraProd :
    jets.IsInfinitesimalActionOf (repAlgebraProd M N) (repJetProd M N)

declarations.name: MatterField.prod
declarations.doc:
**The direct sum of two matter fields** of the same mass weight and statistics, one field
valued in `M.V × N.V` with every action acting componentwise and with the weight and
statistics of `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prod (_h : M.massWeight = N.massWeight) (_hσ : M.statistic = N.statistic) :
    MatterField jets

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_V
declarations.statement: lemma prod_V : (prod M N h hσ).V = (M.V × N.V)

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_repJet
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repJet : (prod M N h hσ).repJet = repJetProd M N

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_repAlgebra
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repAlgebra : (prod M N h hσ).repAlgebra = repAlgebraProd M N

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_repLorentz
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repLorentz : (prod M N h hσ).repLorentz = M.repLorentz.prod N.repLorentz

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_massWeight
declarations.statement: lemma prod_massWeight : (prod M N h hσ).massWeight = M.massWeight

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_massWeight_right
declarations.doc:
The shared weight, read off the second summand: this is what the hypothesis of `prod`
buys — the direct sum has one weight, and it is the weight of either summand.
declarations.statement: lemma prod_massWeight_right : (prod M N h hσ).massWeight = N.massWeight

declarations.name: MatterField.prod_statistic
declarations.statement: lemma prod_statistic : (prod M N h hσ).statistic = M.statistic

declarations.name: JetComponentSpace.prodEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The component space of a direct sum splits.** The component functions of the direct
sum `M.prod N h hσ` are those of `M` together with those of `N`: the dual and the conjugate
both distribute over the finite product, and the derivative label is untouched. Only the
value spaces enter, so the hypotheses `h` and `hσ` are carried along and not used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.JetComponentSpace.prodEquiv (M N : MatterField jets)
    (h : M.massWeight = N.massWeight) (hσ : M.statistic = N.statistic) :
    JetComponentSpace (M.prod N h hσ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace M × JetComponentSpace N

modules.title: Gauge tensors in a representation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A matter field valued in a representation space `V` has symbols `[∂_s ψ^i]` contracted
against duals of `V`. It is a *gauge tensor* — it *transforms in* the representation
`rep` of the jet gauge group — when each derivative symbol transforms by the Leibniz
convolution of the base-point Taylor coefficients `repDualCoeff` of `rep` against the
lower symbols, with no inhomogeneous term. This is the generalization of
`TransformsInAdjoint` from the adjoint representation to an arbitrary one, and the
property preserved by the covariant derivative in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.InfinitesimalAction`.

Nothing here depends on the local gauge data beyond the group `GJ` acting; the definition
lives in the `LocalGaugeData` namespace with the transformation laws that consume it.


- `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn` : the gauge tensors of a representation.
- `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_zero` : the underived symbol transforms through
  the base-point value of the gauge jet alone.
- `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_eval_eq_one`,
  `LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_mem_truncationKer_zero` : a pure jet fixes the
  underived symbol, when the representation is trivial on such jets.

## ii. Key results

- `TransformsIn` : a component family `F`, valued in `B` and indexed by the complex dual of the
  representation space `V`, *transforms in* the representation `rep` of the jet gauge group — with
  the ambient action `repGauge` on `B` — when each derivative symbol `[∂_s F^φ]` transforms by the
  Leibniz convolution of the dual representation coefficients against lower symbols, with no
  inhomogeneous term — the generalization of `TransformsInAdjoint` from the adjoint representation
  to an arbitrary one, and the form consumed by `AlgebraRealization`
- `TransformsIn.repGauge_zero` : a matter gauge tensor transforms at the base point through the dual
  coefficient of the base-point value of the gauge jet alone: the antidiagonal of the empty multiset
  has a single term
- `TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_eval_eq_one` : matter gauge tensors whose zeroth representation
  coefficient is trivial on pure jets are fixed by pure jets: for a family transforming in `rep`, a
  gauge jet with trivial base-point value acts trivially on the underived symbol, provided the
  representation's zeroth Taylor coefficient is the identity on such jets
- `repCoeff_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval` : if pure jets act trivially at the base point, the zeroth
  Taylor coefficient of a jet is that of the constant jet of its value: every jet is a pure jet
  times the constant jet of its value, and the zeroth coefficients are multiplicative for a
  fibrewise representation

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Gauge tensors in a representation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Gauge tensors in a representation

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn
declarations.doc:
A component family `F`, valued in `B` and indexed by the complex dual of the
representation space `V`, *transforms in* the representation `rep` of the jet gauge
group — with the ambient action `repGauge` on `B` — when each derivative symbol
`[∂_s F^φ]` transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the dual representation
coefficients against lower symbols, with no inhomogeneous term — the generalization
of `TransformsInAdjoint` from the adjoint representation to an arbitrary one, and
the form consumed by `AlgebraRealization`.

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_zero
declarations.doc:
A matter gauge tensor transforms at the base point through the dual coefficient of the
base-point value of the gauge jet alone: the antidiagonal of the empty multiset has a
single term.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsIn.repGauge_zero (hF : TransformsIn repGauge rep F) (U : GJ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (F 0 φ) = F 0 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ 0 φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc:
Matter gauge tensors whose zeroth representation coefficient is trivial on pure
jets are fixed by pure jets: for a family transforming in `rep`, a gauge jet with
trivial base-point value acts trivially on the underived symbol, provided the
representation's zeroth Taylor coefficient is the identity on such jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_eval_eq_one {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    {jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J} (hF : TransformsIn repGauge rep F)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : GJ}, jets.eval W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id)
    {U : GJ} (hU : jets.eval U = 1) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (F 0 φ) = F 0 φ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.repCoeff_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
declarations.doc:
If pure jets act trivially at the base point, the zeroth Taylor coefficient of a jet
is that of the constant jet of its value: every jet is a pure jet times the constant jet
of its value, and the zeroth coefficients are multiplicative for a fibrewise
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    (jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J) (rep : Representation ℂ GJ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : GJ}, jets.eval W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id) (U : GJ) :
    repCoeff rep U 0 = repCoeff rep (jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)) 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
declarations.doc:
If pure jets act trivially at the base point, a matter gauge tensor transforms at the
base point as under the constant jet of the value of the gauge jet: the jet action on
underived symbols factors through evaluation.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsIn.repGauge_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    {jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J} (hF : TransformsIn repGauge rep F)
    (hlin : ∀ (U : GJ) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : GJ}, jets.eval W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id) (U : GJ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (F 0 φ) = repGauge (jets.ofConstant (jets.eval U)) (F 0 φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeData.TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_mem_truncationKer_zero
declarations.doc:
Matter gauge tensors are fixed by pure jets: the members of the zeroth truncation kernel
are the jets with trivial base-point value, so `repGauge_eq_of_eval_eq_one` applies.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsIn.repGauge_eq_of_mem_truncationKer_zero {𝔤 : Type} [LieRing 𝔤] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤]
    {G₀ : Type} [Group G₀] {𝔤J : Type} [LieRing 𝔤J] [LieAlgebra ℝ 𝔤J]
    {jets : LocalGaugeData G₀ 𝔤 GJ 𝔤J} (hF : TransformsIn repGauge rep F)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : GJ}, jets.eval W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id)
    (U : jets.truncationKer 0) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U.1 (F 0 φ) = F 0 φ

modules.title: Green operators and causally supported fields
modules.doc:
Retarded and advanced Green operators of a local operator.

## i. Overview

Retarded and advanced Green operators of a local operator. Fields with spacelike compact, future or
past compact support.

## ii. Key results

- `spacelikeCompactFields` : Admissible fields with support contained in the causal hull of a
  compact set.
- `futureSupportedFields` : Fields supported in the future of a compact set.
- `futureSupportedOperator` : Restrict the field equation to fields supported to the future of
  compact sets.
- `spacelikeCompactSolution` : Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `spacelikeCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to spacelike-compact admissible fields.
- `RetardedGreenOperator` : A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal
  support.
- `AdvancedGreenOperator` : An advanced two-sided inverse on compact sources with past causal
  support.
- `GreenOperators` : A pair of causal Green inverses for the same field equation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linear field equations and compact sources
- B. Retarded and advanced Green operators
- C. Past-compact and future-compact support

## iv. References

None.

## A. Linear field equations and compact sources

- `spacelikeCompactFields` : Admissible fields with support contained in the causal hull of a
  compact set.
- `futureSupportedFields` : Fields supported in the future of a compact set.
- `futureSupportedOperator` : Restrict the field equation to fields supported to the future of
  compact sets.
- `spacelikeCompactSolution` : Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `spacelikeCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to spacelike-compact admissible fields.

Lemmas: `operator_mem_futureSupportedFields`, `operator_mem_spacelikeCompactFields`,
`futureSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields`, `pastSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields`.

## B. Retarded and advanced Green operators

- `RetardedGreenOperator` : A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal
  support.
- `AdvancedGreenOperator` : An advanced two-sided inverse on compact sources with past causal
  support.
- `GreenOperators` : A pair of causal Green inverses for the same field equation.
- `reverse` : Reverse time orientation and exchange the Green operators.

## C. Past-compact and future-compact support

- `pastCompactFields` : The full past-compact admissible source and field space.
- `pastCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to the full past-compact support class.

Lemmas: `operator_mem_pastCompactFields`, `futureSupportedFields_le_pastCompactFields`.

declarations.name: LocalOperator.spacelikeCompactFields
declarations.doc: Admissible fields with support contained in the causal hull of a compact set.
declarations.statement: def spacelikeCompactFields (_P : LocalOperator S) (C : CausalRelation M) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.futureSupportedFields
declarations.doc:
Fields supported in the future of a compact set. This is a strictly specified support class;
it is not identified with all past-compact fields without additional geometry.
declarations.statement: def futureSupportedFields (_P : LocalOperator S) (C : CausalRelation M) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_mem_futureSupportedFields
declarations.doc: Locality preserves support in the causal future of a compact set.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_mem_futureSupportedFields (C : CausalRelation M)
    {u : S} (hu : u ∈ P.futureSupportedFields C) :
    P.operator u ∈ P.futureSupportedFields C
