declarations.doc: Restrict the field equation to fields supported to the future of compact sets.
declarations.statement:
def futureSupportedOperator (C : CausalRelation M) :
    P.futureSupportedFields C →ₗ[𝕜] P.futureSupportedFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.spacelikeCompactSolution
declarations.doc: Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
declarations.statement: def spacelikeCompactSolution (C : CausalRelation M) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_mem_spacelikeCompactFields
declarations.doc: Locality preserves spacelike-compact support.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_mem_spacelikeCompactFields (C : CausalRelation M)
    {u : S} (hu : u ∈ P.spacelikeCompactFields C) :
    P.operator u ∈ P.spacelikeCompactFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.futureSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields
declarations.doc: One-sided compactly generated support is spacelike compact.
declarations.statement:
lemma futureSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields (C : CausalRelation M) :
    P.futureSupportedFields C ≤ P.spacelikeCompactFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.pastSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields
declarations.doc: Past-supported compactly generated support is spacelike compact.
declarations.statement:
lemma pastSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields (C : CausalRelation M) :
    P.futureSupportedFields C.reverse ≤ P.spacelikeCompactFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.spacelikeCompactOperator
declarations.doc: The field equation restricted to spacelike-compact admissible fields.
declarations.statement:
def spacelikeCompactOperator (C : CausalRelation M) :
    P.spacelikeCompactFields C →ₗ[𝕜] P.spacelikeCompactFields C

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator
declarations.doc: A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal support.
declarations.statement:
structure RetardedGreenOperator (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- Compact sources produce admissible fields without a compact support requirement. -/
  toLinearMap : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] S
  /-- The response solves the prescribed sourced equation. -/
  solves : ∀ f, P.operator (toLinearMap f) = f.val
  /-- Compact fields are recovered from their equation of motion. -/
  comp_operator : ∀ f, toLinearMap (P.compactOperator f) = f.val
  /-- Retarded propagation is supported in the source's causal future. -/
  support : ∀ f, tsupport (toLinearMap f : M → V) ⊆
    C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.AdvancedGreenOperator
declarations.doc: An advanced two-sided inverse on compact sources with past causal support.
declarations.statement:
structure AdvancedGreenOperator (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- Compact sources produce unrestricted admissible fields. -/
  toLinearMap : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] S
  /-- The response solves the prescribed sourced equation. -/
  solves : ∀ f, P.operator (toLinearMap f) = f.val
  /-- Compact fields are recovered from their equation of motion. -/
  comp_operator : ∀ f, toLinearMap (P.compactOperator f) = f.val
  /-- Advanced propagation is supported in the source's causal past. -/
  support : ∀ f, tsupport (toLinearMap f : M → V) ⊆
    C.causalPast (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators
declarations.doc:
A pair of causal Green inverses for the same field equation.
Formal-adjoint hypotheses and support extensions are not implicit in this bundle.
declarations.statement:
structure GreenOperators (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- The retarded Green inverse. -/
  retarded : RetardedGreenOperator C P
  /-- The advanced Green inverse. -/
  advanced : AdvancedGreenOperator C P

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.reverse
declarations.doc: Reverse time orientation and exchange the Green operators.
declarations.statement: def reverse : GreenOperators C.reverse P

declarations.name: LocalOperator.pastCompactFields
declarations.doc: The full past-compact admissible source and field space.
declarations.statement: def pastCompactFields (_P : LocalOperator S) (C : CausalRelation M) : Submodule 𝕜 S

declarations.name: LocalOperator.operator_mem_pastCompactFields
declarations.doc: Local field equations preserve past-compact support.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_mem_pastCompactFields {u : S} (hu : u ∈ P.pastCompactFields C) :
    P.operator u ∈ P.pastCompactFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.pastCompactOperator
declarations.doc: The field equation restricted to the full past-compact support class.
declarations.statement: def pastCompactOperator : P.pastCompactFields C →ₗ[𝕜] P.pastCompactFields C

declarations.name: LocalOperator.futureSupportedFields_le_pastCompactFields
declarations.doc: Support in the future of one compact set is included in the full past-compact class.
declarations.statement:
lemma futureSupportedFields_le_pastCompactFields (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :
    P.futureSupportedFields C ≤ P.pastCompactFields C

modules.title: The causal propagator and causal uniqueness
modules.doc:
The difference of the retarded and advanced response solves the homogeneous equation.

## i. Overview

The difference of the retarded and advanced response solves the homogeneous equation. Uniqueness of
one-sided solutions follows from the support of the response.

## ii. Key results

- `causalPropagator` : The causal propagator uses the sign convention retarded minus advanced.
- `toSolutionSpace` : The causal propagator with its proven solution-space codomain.
- `HasCausalCutoffs` : Temporal cutoff splitting of spacelike-compact admissible fields.
- `eq_of_local_truncations` : Compact truncations agreeing with the same field in the observation's
  causal past give identical retarded responses.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The causal propagator and compact source kernel
- B. Causal splitting and one-sided uniqueness
- C. Local field equations and causal agreement

## iv. References

None.

## A. The causal propagator and compact source kernel

- `causalPropagator` : The causal propagator uses the sign convention retarded minus advanced.
- `toSolutionSpace` : The causal propagator with its proven solution-space codomain.

Lemmas: `causalPropagator_solves`, `causalPropagator_comp_operator`, `causalPropagator_support`,
`causalPropagator_mem_solution`, `range_compactOperator_le_ker`, `compactOperator_injective`,
`retarded_compact_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero`, `mem_range_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero`,
`causalPropagator_ker`, `toSolutionSpace_ker`.

## B. Causal splitting and one-sided uniqueness

- `HasCausalCutoffs` : Temporal cutoff splitting of spacelike-compact admissible fields.

Lemmas: `futureSupported_unique`, `retarded_mem_futureSupportedFields`,
`advanced_mem_futureSupportedFields_reverse`, `retarded_eq_of_futureSupported`,
`advanced_eq_of_pastSupported`.

## C. Local field equations and causal agreement

Lemmas: `eq_zero_of_no_causal_source`, `eq_of_no_causal_difference`, `eq_of_local_truncations`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalPropagator

declarations.doc: The causal propagator produces homogeneous fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPropagator_solves (f : P.compactSources) :
    P.operator (G.causalPropagator f) = 0

    G.causalPropagator (P.compactOperator f) = 0

declarations.doc: Causal propagation is supported in the union of the future and past of its source.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPropagator_support (f : P.compactSources) :
    tsupport (G.causalPropagator f : M → V) ⊆ C.causalHull (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.statement:

    G.causalPropagator f ∈ P.spacelikeCompactSolution C

declarations.doc: The causal propagator with its proven solution-space codomain.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.range_compactOperator_le_ker
declarations.doc:
Equations of motion are in the kernel of the causal propagator.
The reverse inclusion requires causal compactness and additional arguments.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_compactOperator_le_ker :
    LinearMap.range P.compactOperator ≤ LinearMap.ker G.causalPropagator

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.compactOperator_injective
declarations.doc: A compact homogeneous field vanishes because either Green operator is a left inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma compactOperator_injective : Function.Injective P.compactOperator

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.retarded_compact_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A source in the causal-propagator kernel has a compact retarded response.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_compact_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (f : P.compactSources) (hf : G.causalPropagator f = 0) :
    HasCompactSupport (G.retarded.toLinearMap f : M → V)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.mem_range_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Every zero causal response is an equation-of-motion source of a compact field.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_range_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (f : P.compactSources) (hf : G.causalPropagator f = 0) :
    f ∈ LinearMap.range P.compactOperator

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalPropagator_ker
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the causal propagator consists precisely of equation-of-motion sources.
The proof uses compact causal diamonds rather than an assumed exactness hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPropagator_ker (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :

modules.title: Localization and extension of retarded responses
modules.doc:
A past compact source is cut off to compact pieces.

## i. Overview

A past compact source is cut off to compact pieces. The retarded responses to the pieces define a
response to the whole source.

## ii. Key results

- `PastLocalization` : The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact
  test sections.
- `sourceAt` : Each source has a compact truncation adapted to the observation event.
- `retardedValue` : The pointwise retarded response obtained from observation-adapted compact
  truncations.
- `retardedSection` : The glued retarded field as an admissible section.
- `retardedExtension` : The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.
- `truncationRadius` : A positive ball radius enclosing the relevant compact part of the source.
- `truncationBump` : A smooth compact bump equal to one near the relevant source intersection.
- `bumpTruncate` : A bump truncation is a compact admissible source, not an assumed larger-support
  solution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compact localization of past-compact sources
- B. Constructing Green extensions by local compact truncation
- C. Compact source localization by smooth bump functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Compact localization of past-compact sources

- `PastLocalization` : The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact
  test sections.
- `sourceAt` : Each source has a compact truncation adapted to the observation event.
- `retardedValue` : The pointwise retarded response obtained from observation-adapted compact
  truncations.

Lemmas: `mem_past_bound`, `sourceAt_agrees`, `predecessor_mem_past_bound`,
`retardedValue_eq_on_past_bound`, `retardedValue_eventuallyEq`, `retardedValue_mem`,
`homogeneous_eq_zero`, `pastCompactOperator_injective`.

## B. Constructing Green extensions by local compact truncation

- `retardedSection` : The glued retarded field as an admissible section.
- `retardedExtension` : The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.

Lemmas: `retardedSection_solves`, `retardedValue_support`, `retardedSection_support`,
`retardedSection_mem_pastCompactFields`, `pastCompactOperator_surjective`,
`retardedExtension_solves`, `retardedExtension_eq_section`, `retardedExtension_support`,
`pastCompact_unique`, `futureSupportedOperator_injective` and more.

## C. Compact source localization by smooth bump functions

- `truncationRadius` : A positive ball radius enclosing the relevant compact part of the source.
- `truncationBump` : A smooth compact bump equal to one near the relevant source intersection.
- `bumpTruncate` : A bump truncation is a compact admissible source, not an assumed larger-support
  solution.
- `ofBumpFunctions` : Construct all local compact-source truncation data from bump stability and
  causal topology.

Lemmas: `truncationRadius_pos`, `mem_truncation_ball`, `bumpTruncate_support`,
`bumpTruncate_agrees`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization
declarations.doc: The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact test sections.
declarations.statement:
structure PastLocalization (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- Compact observation bounds whose causal pasts are neighborhoods. -/
  bound : M → Set M
  /-- Every observation bound is compact. -/
  bound_compact : ∀ x, IsCompact (bound x)
  /-- The causal past of an observation bound contains a neighborhood of the event. -/
  bound_neighborhood : ∀ x, C.causalPast (bound x) ∈ 𝓝 x
  /-- Admissible fields glue from local representatives. -/
  local_fields : IsLocalFieldSpace S
  /-- The causal future of a compact set is closed. -/
  closed_compact_future : ∀ K : Set M, IsCompact K → IsClosed (C.causalFuture K)
  /-- Compact source truncation near the causal past of a compact observation set. -/
  truncate : P.pastCompactFields C → (K : Set M) → IsCompact K → P.compactSources
  /-- Truncation agrees as germs with the source throughout that causal past. -/
  truncate_agrees : ∀ f K hK x, x ∈ C.causalPast K →
    ((truncate f K hK).val : M → V) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (f.val : M → V)
  /-- Compact truncation introduces no support outside the original source. -/
  truncate_support : ∀ f K hK,
    tsupport ((truncate f K hK).val : M → V) ⊆ tsupport (f.val : M → V)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedValue_eq_on_past_bound

Retarded responses of different admissible truncations agree locally.
No limit or convergence of the truncation family is required.

declarations.doc: The pointwise construction is admissible by local gluing.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedValue_mem (G : RetardedGreenOperator C P) (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    L.retardedValue G f ∈ S

declarations.doc:
One-sided uniqueness is a consequence of local compact truncation and the compact Green
inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma pastCompactOperator_injective (G : RetardedGreenOperator C P) :

declarations.statement: def retardedSection (f : P.pastCompactFields C) : S

declarations.doc: The topological support bound follows from the closed future of a past-compact source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedSection_support (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    tsupport (L.retardedSection G f : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension
declarations.doc: The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.

noncomputable def retardedExtension (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :

declarations.doc: The constructed extension solves the source equation.

lemma retardedExtension_solves (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_eq_section

lemma retardedExtension_eq_section (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)

    (L.retardedExtension G hC f).val = L.retardedSection G f

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_support
declarations.doc: The full past-compact extension retains the sharp causal support bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedExtension_support (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    tsupport ((L.retardedExtension G hC f).val : M → V) ⊆
      C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.pastCompact_unique
declarations.doc: Uniqueness for admissible fields in the full past-compact class.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.futureSupportedOperator_injective

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_mem_futureSupportedFields

Solvability on compactly generated future support is proved by restricting the constructed

declarations.statement:
lemma futureSupportedOperator_surjective (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :

modules.title: Smooth spacetime fields as Green operator input
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Smooth fields on spacetime admit past and future localization and temporal cutoffs.

## ii. Key results

- `pastLocalization` : Retarded localization for every admissible field space with local gluing and
  bump stability.
- `futureLocalization` : Advanced localization uses the same field hypotheses and the reversed
  verified causal geometry.
- `smoothPastLocalization` : All past-compact smooth fields admit the compact truncations required
  by the general theory.
- `smoothFutureLocalization` : The same analytic field class supplies advanced localization after
  causal reversal.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Localization of admissible fields in Minkowski spacetime
- B. Localization of smooth spacetime fields
- C. Temporal cutoffs of spacelike-compact smooth fields

## iv. References

None.

## A. Localization of admissible fields in Minkowski spacetime

- `pastLocalization` : Retarded localization for every admissible field space with local gluing and
  bump stability.
- `futureLocalization` : Advanced localization uses the same field hypotheses and the reversed
  verified causal geometry.

## B. Localization of smooth spacetime fields

- `smoothPastLocalization` : All past-compact smooth fields admit the compact truncations required
  by the general theory.
- `smoothFutureLocalization` : The same analytic field class supplies advanced localization after
  causal reversal.

Lemmas: `smoothFields_bumpStable`.

## C. Temporal cutoffs of spacelike-compact smooth fields

Lemmas: `isCompact_causalPast_inter`, `isCompact_causalFuture_inter`, `tsupport_cutoff_subset`,
`tsupport_cutoff_sub_subset`, `smoothHasCausalCutoffs`.

modules.title: Uniqueness and the causal exact sequence
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Existence and uniqueness of retarded solutions and the exact sequence of compact sources and
spacelike compact fields.

## ii. Key results

- `sourceOfCausalSplit` : The compact source obtained from a causal splitting of a homogeneous
  field.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient` : Compact test fields modulo the equation of motion are equivalent to
  spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotientOfLocalization` : Homogeneous spacelike-compact solutions are source
  classes, with one-sided inverse and uniqueness hypotheses discharged by local compact
  constructions.
- `toSpacelikeCompact` : The causal propagator with the support codomain required in the exact
  sequence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. One-sided uniqueness for weak solutions
- B. Homogeneous solutions as source classes
- C. The causal Green exact sequence
- D. General sourced field equations

## iv. References

None.

## A. One-sided uniqueness for weak solutions

Lemmas: `distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded`.

## B. Homogeneous solutions as source classes

- `sourceOfCausalSplit` : The compact source obtained from a causal splitting of a homogeneous
  field.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient` : Compact test fields modulo the equation of motion are equivalent to
  spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotientOfLocalization` : Homogeneous spacelike-compact solutions are source
  classes, with one-sided inverse and uniqueness hypotheses discharged by local compact
  constructions.

Lemmas: `compact_equation_of_causal_split`, `causalPropagator_sourceOfCausalSplit`,
`toSolutionSpace_surjective`, `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient_symm_mk`,
`solutionSpaceEquivQuotient_toSolutionSpace`, `spacelikeCompactOperator_surjective_of_localization`.

## C. The causal Green exact sequence

- `toSpacelikeCompact` : The causal propagator with the support codomain required in the exact
  sequence.

Lemmas: `toSpacelikeCompact_ker`, `exact_compactSources`, `exact_spacelikeCompactFields`,
`causalGreen_exactSequence`.

## D. General sourced field equations

Lemmas: `existsUnique_retardedSolution`, `existsUnique_retardedSolution_of_localization`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded
declarations.doc:
Compact advanced Green data and causal localization force a retarded weak homogeneous
solution to vanish. The native test model preserves the underlying scalar test fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded
    (e : P.compactSources ≃ₗ[ℝ] _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : Opens E) ℝ ⊤)
    (he : ∀ f : P.compactSources, (e f : E → ℝ) = f.val.val)
    (G : AdvancedGreenOperator C P) (L : PastLocalization C.reverse P)
    (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (K : Set E) (hK : IsCompact K)
    (T : Distribution (⊤ : Opens E) V ⊤)
    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T (C.causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hzero : ∀ f : P.compactSources, T (e (P.compactOperator f)) = 0) : T = 0

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalPropagator_sourceOfCausalSplit
declarations.doc: The causal propagator reconstructs the difference of a causal split from its common source.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPropagator_sourceOfCausalSplit (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (hret : Function.Injective (P.futureSupportedOperator C))
    (hadv : Function.Injective (P.futureSupportedOperator C.reverse))
    (uPlus : P.futureSupportedFields C) (uMinus : P.futureSupportedFields C.reverse)
    (heq : P.operator uPlus.val = P.operator uMinus.val) :
    G.causalPropagator (sourceOfCausalSplit hC uPlus uMinus heq) = uPlus.val - uMinus.val

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.toSolutionSpace_surjective

Every spacelike-compact homogeneous field is produced by a compact source.
The source is constructed from a causal cutoff rather than postulated as a preimage.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.solutionSpaceEquivQuotient
declarations.doc:
Compact test fields modulo the equation of motion are equivalent to spacelike-compact
homogeneous solutions. All support, cutoff and one-sided supported hypotheses are explicit.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def solutionSpaceEquivQuotient (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (hret : Function.Injective (P.futureSupportedOperator C)) (hadv : Function.Injective
      (P.futureSupportedOperator C.reverse))
    (hcut : P.HasCausalCutoffs C) :
    P.spacelikeCompactSolution C ≃ₗ[𝕜]
      (P.compactSources ⧸ LinearMap.range P.compactOperator)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.solutionSpaceEquivQuotient_symm_mk
declarations.doc: The quotient-to-solution map is exactly the causal propagator on each source class.

The final equation map is onto by solving the two cutoff pieces with the constructed
extensions.

Homogeneous spacelike-compact solutions are source classes, with one-sided inverse and
uniqueness hypotheses discharged by local compact constructions.

declarations.doc: Exactness at spacelike-compact fields follows from causal splitting and one-sided uniqueness.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalGreen_exactSequence
declarations.doc:
The full causal Green sequence, including injectivity and terminal surjectivity.
The larger-support inverses and uniqueness are derived from compact Green data and localization.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalGreen_exactSequence
    (Lret : PastLocalization C P) (Ladv : PastLocalization C.reverse P)
    (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (hcut : P.HasCausalCutoffs C) :
    Function.Injective P.compactOperator ∧
      Function.Exact P.compactOperator G.toSpacelikeCompact ∧

      Function.Surjective (P.spacelikeCompactOperator C)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator.existsUnique_retardedSolution
declarations.doc:
A source has exactly one sharply retarded solution when the future-supported homogeneous
kernel vanishes. Existence follows from the supplied Green operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_retardedSolution
    (huniq : Function.Injective (P.futureSupportedOperator C)) (f : P.compactSources) :
    ∃! u : S, P.operator u = f.val ∧
      tsupport (u : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator.existsUnique_retardedSolution_of_localization
declarations.doc: Local compact-cutoff geometry proves the uniqueness hypothesis of the compact-source theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_retardedSolution_of_localization (L : PastLocalization C P)
    (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (f : P.compactSources) :
    ∃! u : S, P.operator u = f.val ∧
      tsupport (u : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

modules.title: The Klein–Gordon equation
modules.doc:
This file sets up the Klein–Gordon equation on spacetime for smooth fields and for distributions.

## i. Overview

Spacetime is `SpaceTime d` with the speed of light equal to one. The operator `operator m` is the
wave operator plus `m ^ 2` on smooth fields. The mass parameter `m` is any real number. The
operator does not enlarge support, so `equation m` packages it as a local operator. The operator
extends to distributions as `distributionOperator m`. The file `Solution` states the solution.

## ii. Key results

- `operator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on smooth fields.
- `equation` : the Klein–Gordon operator as a local operator.
- `distributionOperator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on distributions.
- `testOperator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on compactly supported smooth test functions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The operator on smooth fields
- B. The operator on distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The operator on smooth fields

`operator m` is `smoothWaveOperator + m ^ 2 • id`. The mass enters as a zeroth order term. The
field type and the dimension are unchanged. `equation m` records that the operator does not
enlarge support.

## B. The operator on distributions

`distributionOperator m` is the wave operator plus `m ^ 2` on `DistributionField d V`. On a test
function it is given by the same operator `testOperator m`, and `distributionOperator_apply`
states this.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.operator
declarations.doc: The massive wave operator, with mass measured in inverse spacetime-length units.
declarations.statement: def operator (m : ℝ) : smoothFields d V →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.equation
declarations.doc: Klein–Gordon is a local equation on the existing smooth spacetime field class.
declarations.statement: def equation (m : ℝ) : LocalOperator (smoothFields d V)

declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator on native distributions.
declarations.statement: def distributionOperator (m : ℝ) : DistributionField d V →L[ℝ] DistributionField d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.testOperator
declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator on native compact smooth test functions.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.distributionOperator_apply
declarations.doc: The positive second-order operator has the same transpose on test functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma distributionOperator_apply (m : ℝ) (T : DistributionField d V)
    (φ : _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)) ℝ ⊤) :
    distributionOperator m T φ = T (testOperator m φ)

modules.title: The massive sine evolution through the massless one
modules.doc:
The massive sine evolution is the massless sine evolution plus a Bessel average of the massless
sine evolutions at smaller radii. This holds in every space dimension.

## i. Overview

The massive multiplier is a Bessel average of the massless cosine multipliers
(`Real.integral_besselSq_cos`). So the massive sine evolution is the Bessel average of the massless
cosine evolution. The massless cosine evolution is the derivative of the massless sine evolution.
Integration by parts moves the derivative to the Bessel weight.

## ii. Key results

- `cosineFourier` : the massless cosine evolution as a Fourier integral.
- `sineEvolution_mass_cos` : the massive sine evolution as a Bessel average of it.
- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero` : the cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.
- `sineEvolution_mass_zero` : the massive sine evolution through the massless one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Bessel average of the cosine evolution
- B. The derivative of the sine evolution
- C. Integration by parts

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Bessel average of the cosine evolution

- `cosineFourier` : the massless cosine evolution as a Fourier integral.
- `sineEvolution_mass_cos` : the massive sine evolution as a Bessel average of it.

## B. The derivative of the sine evolution

- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero` : the cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.

## C. Integration by parts

- `sineEvolution_mass_zero` : the massive sine evolution through the massless one.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cosineFourier
declarations.doc: The cosine evolution of the massless wave equation, as a Fourier integral.
declarations.statement: def cosineFourier (u : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_cos
declarations.doc: **The massive sine evolution is a Bessel average of the massless cosine evolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_cos {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x =
      ∫ u in (-r)..r, ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero
declarations.doc: **The cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) (u₀ : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => sineEvolution ℂ u 0 g x) (cosineFourier u₀ g x) u₀

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cosineFourier_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma cosineFourier_neg (u : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    cosineFourier (-u) g x = cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_cosineFourier
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_cosineFourier (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) : Continuous fun u => cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_zero
declarations.doc:
**The massive sine evolution in terms of the massless one.** The massive sine evolution is the
massless one at the radius plus a Bessel average of the massless sine evolution over smaller
radii.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_zero {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x = sineEvolution ℂ r 0 g x +
      ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..r, ((2 * m ^ 2 * u * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        sineEvolution ℂ u 0 g x

modules.title: The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation on the line
modules.doc:
The retarded Green function in one space dimension is `½ Θ(t - |x|) J₀(m √(t² - x²))`.

## i. Overview

A multiplier that is the cosine transform of an even continuous kernel on `[-r, r]` is the
convolution with that kernel. The Bessel identity says that the multiplier of the massive sine
evolution is the cosine transform of `½ J₀(m √(r² - u²))`. So the sine evolution on the line is the
average of the data against the Bessel kernel over `[x - r, x + r]`. The Duhamel integral then gives
the retarded solution as the integral of the source against the retarded Green function over the
backward light cone. For `m = 0` this is the d'Alembert formula.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_of_kernel` : a cosine-transform multiplier is a convolution.
- `sineEvolution_mass_line` : the sine evolution with mass on the line.
- `solution_mass_line` : the retarded solution with mass on the line.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Convolution kernels
- B. The Bessel kernel

## iv. References

None.

## A. Convolution kernels

- `sineEvolution_of_kernel` : a cosine-transform multiplier is a convolution.

## B. The Bessel kernel

- `sineEvolution_mass_line` : the sine evolution with mass on the line.
- `solution_mass_line` : the retarded solution with mass on the line.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_of_kernel
declarations.doc: **A multiplier that is a cosine transform is a convolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_of_kernel {μ r : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (w : ℝ → ℝ) (W : ℝ)
    (hw : Continuous w) (hwb : ∀ u, |w u| ≤ W) (hwe : ∀ u, w (-u) = w u)
    (hm : ∀ ξ : ℝ, multiplier r μ ξ =
      ((∫ u in (-r)..r, w u * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ξ * u) : ℝ) : ℂ))
    (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r μ g x = ∫ u in (-r)..r, (w u : ℂ) * g (x + u)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_line
declarations.doc:
**The massive sine evolution on the line.** The sine evolution of the mass `m` is the average
of the data against the Bessel kernel `½ J₀ (m √(r² - u²))` over the interval of radius `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_line {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x =
      ∫ u in (-r)..r, ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * g (x + u)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_mass_line
declarations.doc:
**The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation on the line.** The retarded solution at
`(t, x)` is the integral of the source against the retarded Green function
`½ Θ(t - s - |u|) J₀ (m √((t - s)² - u²))` over the backward light cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_mass_line (m : ℝ) (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × ℝ)) ℂ ⊤) (t x : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ ψ (m ^ 2) t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ∫ u in (-(t - s))..(t - s),
      ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * ψ (s, x + u)

modules.title: The retarded Green function with mass in three space dimensions
modules.doc:
The retarded Green function in three space dimensions is
`δ(t - r) / (4π r) - m J₁(m √(t² - r²)) / (4π √(t² - r²)) Θ(t - r)`.

## i. Overview

Dimension raising turns the one-dimensional Green function `½ Θ J₀(m √(t² - x²))` into the
three-dimensional one by `-(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ`. The derivative of the step gives the shell
`δ(t - r) / (4π r)`. The derivative of `J₀` gives the tail with `J₁`.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_origin_radialSource` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at
  the origin.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_space` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution on
  `Space 3`.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The formula at the origin

## iv. References

None.

## A. The formula at the origin

- `sineEvolution_origin_radialSource` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at
  the origin.
- `solution_origin_radialSource` : the formula for the retarded solution on Euclidean three-space.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_space` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution on
  `Space 3`.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_origin_radialSource
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at the origin.** For a radial source with
the profile `Φ` the massive sine evolution at the origin is
`τ Φ(τ) + 2 m² ∫₀^τ u² κ(m² (τ² - u²)) Φ(u) du`, where `κ = -J₁(z) / (2z)` at `y = z²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_origin_radialSource (m : ℝ) {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 0 ≤ τ)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ τ (m ^ 2) (slice ℂ (radialSource Eucl3 (liftProfile P)) s) 0 =
      (τ : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, τ ^ 2) + ((2 * m ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..τ, ((u ^ 2 * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (τ ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          liftProfile P (s, u ^ 2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_origin_radialSource
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution at the origin.** For a radial source
`ψ'(s, x) = Q(s, ‖x‖²)` in three space dimensions the massive retarded solution at `(t, 0)` is
`∫_{s ≤ t} [τ Φ(τ) + 2 m² ∫₀^τ u² κ(m² (τ² - u²)) Φ(u) du] ds` with `τ = t - s`,
`Φ(u) = Q(s, u²)` and `κ(z²) = -J₁(z) / (2 z)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_origin_radialSource (m : ℝ)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ (radialSource Eucl3 (liftProfile P)) (m ^ 2) t 0 =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ((((t - s : ℝ)) : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, (t - s) ^ 2) +
        ((2 * m ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(t - s),
          ((u ^ 2 * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
            liftProfile P (s, u ^ 2))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_origin_radialSource_space
declarations.doc: **The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula on `Space 3`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_origin_radialSource_space (m : ℝ)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ (radialSource (Space 3) (liftProfile P)) (m ^ 2) t 0 =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ((((t - s : ℝ)) : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, (t - s) ^ 2) +
        ((2 * m ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(t - s),
          ((u ^ 2 * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
            liftProfile P (s, u ^ 2))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula with `J₁`.** For `m ≠ 0` the retarded solution at the origin of
a radial source is `∫_{s ≤ t} [τ Φ(τ) - m ∫₀^τ u² J₁(m √(τ² - u²)) / √(τ² - u²) Φ(u) du] ds`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1 {m : ℝ} (hm : m ≠ 0)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ (radialSource (Space 3) (liftProfile P)) (m ^ 2) t 0 =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ((((t - s : ℝ)) : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, (t - s) ^ 2) -
        (m : ℂ) * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(t - s),
          ((u ^ 2 * (Real.besselJ1 (m * Real.sqrt ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) /
            Real.sqrt ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, u ^ 2))

modules.title: The massive Kirchhoff formula for every test source
modules.doc:
In three space dimensions the massive retarded solution of any test source is the massless
Kirchhoff solution plus a Bessel average of the Kirchhoff propagators.

## i. Overview

In three space dimensions the massless sine evolution is Kirchhoff's spherical mean. Inserting it
into the Bessel average of `ClosedForm.MassDeformation` gives the retarded Green function
`δ(t - r) / (4π r) - m J₁ (m √(t² - r²)) / (4π √(t² - r²)) Θ (t - r)` as an identity for the
retarded solution of any test source at any point.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_mass_three` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution.
- `solution_mass_three` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution.
- `solution_mass_three_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Three space dimensions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Three space dimensions

- `sineEvolution_mass_three` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution.
- `solution_mass_three` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution.
- `solution_mass_three_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_three
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution on `Space 3`.** For every Schwartz
source the massive sine evolution is the Kirchhoff propagator at the radius plus a Bessel
average of the Kirchhoff propagators at smaller radii.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_three {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (x : Space 3) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x = wavePropagator 1 r g x +
      ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..r, ((2 * m ^ 2 * u * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        wavePropagator 1 u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_mass_three
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution of a test source.** In three space
dimensions the massive retarded solution at `(t, x)` is the massless Kirchhoff solution plus a
Bessel average of the Kirchhoff propagators of the slices.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_mass_three (m : ℝ) (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space 3)) ℂ ⊤) (t : ℝ)
    (x : Space 3) :
    solution ℂ ψ (m ^ 2) t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, (wavePropagator 1 (t - s) (slice ℂ ψ s) x +
      ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(t - s),
        ((2 * m ^ 2 * u * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          wavePropagator 1 u (slice ℂ ψ s) x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_mass_three_besselJ1
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula with `J₁`.** For `m ≠ 0` the retarded solution of a test source
in three space dimensions is the Duhamel integral of
`wavePropagator 1 τ g x - m ∫₀^τ u J₁ (m √(τ² - u²)) / √(τ² - u²) wavePropagator 1 u g x du`.
The first term is the Green function `δ(t - r) / (4π r)`. The second is
`- m J₁ (m √(t² - r²)) / (4π √(t² - r²)) Θ (t - r)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_mass_three_besselJ1 {m : ℝ} (hm : m ≠ 0)
    (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space 3)) ℂ ⊤) (t : ℝ) (x : Space 3) :
    solution ℂ ψ (m ^ 2) t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, (wavePropagator 1 (t - s) (slice ℂ ψ s) x -
      (m : ℂ) * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(t - s),
        ((u * (Real.besselJ1 (m * Real.sqrt ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) /
          Real.sqrt ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * wavePropagator 1 u (slice ℂ ψ s) x)

modules.title: The retarded solution of the wave equation in one space dimension
modules.doc:
The massless retarded solution in one space dimension is one half of the integral of the source
over the backward light cone.

## i. Overview

The multiplier `sin (2π |ξ| r) / (2π |ξ|)` of the massless sine evolution is the average of
`cos (2π ξ u)` over `u ∈ [-r, r]`. Fourier inversion turns it into the average of the data over the
interval `[x - r, x + r]`. The Duhamel integral over the earlier times is then the integral of the
source over the backward light cone. This is the retarded Green function `½ Θ(t - |x|)` of the wave
equation on the line. It is the case `d = 1` and `m = 0` of the explicit kernels.

## ii. Key results

- `multiplier_zero_eq` : the multiplier as an average of cosines.
- `sineEvolution_zero_mass_apply` : the massless sine evolution on the line is the average of the
  data over an interval.
- `solution_zero_mass_line` : the massless retarded solution on the line is one half of the
  integral of the source over the backward light cone.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The multiplier
- B. The sine evolution
- C. The retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. The multiplier

- `multiplier_zero_eq` : the multiplier as an average of cosines.

## B. The sine evolution

- `sineEvolution_zero_mass_apply` : the massless sine evolution on the line is the average of the
  data over an interval.

## C. The retarded solution

- `solution_zero_mass_line` : the massless retarded solution on the line is one half of the
  integral of the source over the backward light cone.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.multiplier_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The massless multiplier on the line is the average of cosines over `[-r, r]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma multiplier_zero_eq (r : ℝ) (ξ : ℝ) :
    multiplier r 0 ξ = ((1 / 2 * ∫ u in (-r)..r, Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ξ * u) : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_zero_mass_apply
declarations.doc:
**The massless sine evolution on the line.** The sine evolution at the origin of the
mass is the average of the data over the interval of radius `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_zero_mass_apply {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r 0 g x = 1 / 2 * ∫ y in (x - r)..(x + r), g y

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_zero_mass_line
declarations.doc:
**The retarded solution of the wave equation on the line.** The massless retarded solution
at `(t, x)` is one half of the integral of the source over the backward light cone. This is the
retarded Green function `½ Θ(t - |x|)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_zero_mass_line (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × ℝ)) ℂ ⊤) (t x : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ ψ 0 t x =
      1 / 2 * ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ∫ y in (x - (t - s))..(x + (t - s)), ψ (s, y)

modules.title: Kirchhoff's formula for the massless retarded solution in three dimensions
modules.doc:
The massless sine evolution in three space dimensions is Kirchhoff's spherical mean.

## i. Overview

The Fourier multiplier of the sphere mean is `sin (2π |ξ| t) / (2π |ξ|)`. This is the multiplier
of the massless sine evolution. Fourier inversion identifies the two operators on Schwartz
functions. The Duhamel integral of the sphere means is the retarded solution. This is the kernel
`δ(t - r) / (4π r)`.

The sphere integrals and their Fourier transform are taken from the worktree
`causal-green-operators` (`FieldTheory/Wave/Kirchhoff` and `FieldTheory/Wave/Proofs/Fourier`).

## ii. Key results

- `fourier_wavePropagator` : the transform of the Kirchhoff propagator.
- `sineEvolution_zero_mass_three` : the massless sine evolution is the Kirchhoff propagator.
- `solution_zero_mass_three` : the massless retarded solution is the Duhamel integral of the
  spherical means.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sine evolution
- B. The retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. The sine evolution

- `continuous_wavePropagator` : the Kirchhoff propagator of a Schwartz function is continuous.
- `fourier_wavePropagator` : the transform of the Kirchhoff propagator.
- `sineEvolution_zero_mass_three` : the massless sine evolution is the Kirchhoff propagator.

## B. The retarded solution

- `solution_zero_mass_three` : the massless retarded solution is the Duhamel integral of the
  spherical means.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_wavePropagator
declarations.doc: The wave propagator of a Schwartz function is continuous.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_wavePropagator (g : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    Continuous (wavePropagator 1 t g)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourier_wavePropagator
declarations.doc:
**Kirchhoff's formula in Fourier space.** The Fourier transform of the wave propagator is
the multiplier of the massless sine evolution times the transform of the data.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_wavePropagator (g : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (t : ℝ) {ξ : Space 3} (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
    𝓕 (wavePropagator 1 t g) ξ = multiplier t 0 ξ * 𝓕 g ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_zero_mass_three
declarations.doc:
**The massless sine evolution is Kirchhoff's propagator.** In three space dimensions the
massless sine evolution of a Schwartz function is the spherical mean `t M_t g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_zero_mass_three (t : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (x : Space 3) :
    sineEvolution ℂ t 0 g x = wavePropagator 1 t g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_zero_mass_three
declarations.doc:
**Kirchhoff's formula for the retarded solution.** The massless retarded solution in three
space dimensions is the Duhamel integral of the spherical means of the source over the earlier
times. This is the retarded Green function `δ(t - r) / (4π r)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_zero_mass_three (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space 3)) ℂ ⊤) (t : ℝ)
    (x : Space 3) :
    solution ℂ ψ 0 t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, wavePropagator 1 (t - s) (slice ℂ ψ s) x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.wavePropagator_radial
declarations.doc: The Kirchhoff propagator at the origin of a radial function is the radius times its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_radial {Φ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : Space 3 → ℂ} (hg : ∀ x, g x = Φ ‖x‖) {τ : ℝ}
    (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) : wavePropagator 1 τ g 0 = τ * Φ τ

modules.title: Coordinates of spacetime
modules.doc:
Spacetime is identified with time and space.

## i. Overview

Spacetime is identified with time and space. The causal relation and the second derivatives are
transported along the identification.

## ii. Key results

- `coordinates` : Time and space coordinates in units with speed of light equal to one.
- `sourceEquiv` : Compact smooth sources transported to time-space coordinates.
- `sourceOperator` : The transported compact Klein–Gordon operator on Minkowski test sources.
- `operator_of_coordinates` : The neighbour's Klein–Gordon operator has the Fourier coordinate
  differential expression.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The spatial Fourier Green construction on Minkowski spacetime
- B. Coordinate form of the Minkowski Klein–Gordon operator

## iv. References

None.

## A. The spatial Fourier Green construction on Minkowski spacetime

- `coordinates` : Time and space coordinates in units with speed of light equal to one.
- `sourceEquiv` : Compact smooth sources transported to time-space coordinates.
- `sourceOperator` : The transported compact Klein–Gordon operator on Minkowski test sources.

Lemmas: `tsupport_sourceEquiv`.

## B. Coordinate form of the Minkowski Klein–Gordon operator

Lemmas: `coordinates_time`, `coordinates_space`, `precedes_iff_coordinates`,
`causalFuture_coordinates`, `causalPast_coordinates`, `coordinates_basis_time`,
`coordinates_basis_space`, `second_spacetime_deriv`, `second_spacetime_deriv_coordinates`,
`second_time_slice` and more.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.coordinates
declarations.doc: Time and space coordinates in units with speed of light equal to one.
declarations.statement: def coordinates (d : ℕ) : SpaceTime d ≃L[ℝ] ℝ × Space d

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.sourceEquiv
declarations.doc: Compact smooth sources transported to time-space coordinates.
declarations.statement:
def sourceEquiv : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F) ≃ₗ[ℝ]
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space d)), F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.tsupport_sourceEquiv
declarations.doc: Coordinate transport carries the source support to its coordinate image.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_sourceEquiv (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) :
    tsupport (sourceEquiv F f) = coordinates d '' tsupport f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.sourceOperator
declarations.doc: The transported compact Klein–Gordon operator on Minkowski test sources.
declarations.statement:
def sourceOperator (μ : ℝ) (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.coordinates_time
declarations.statement: lemma coordinates_time (p : SpaceTime d) : (coordinates d p).1 = (p.time 1).val

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.coordinates_space
declarations.statement: lemma coordinates_space (p : SpaceTime d) : (coordinates d p).2 = p.space

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.precedes_iff_coordinates
declarations.doc: Minkowski causal precedence is exactly the coordinate light-cone inequality.
declarations.statement:
lemma precedes_iff_coordinates (p q : SpaceTime d) :
    (causalRelation d).Precedes p q ↔
      ‖(coordinates d q).2 - (coordinates d p).2‖ ≤ (coordinates d q).1 - (coordinates d p).1

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.causalFuture_coordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma causalFuture_coordinates (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) :
    (coordinates d) ⁻¹' causalFuture (coordinates d '' K) = (causalRelation d).causalFuture K

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.causalPast_coordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma causalPast_coordinates (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) :
    (coordinates d) ⁻¹' causalPast (coordinates d '' K) = (causalRelation d).causalPast K

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.coordinates_basis_time
declarations.statement:
lemma coordinates_basis_time :
    coordinates d (Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0)) = (1, (0 : Space d))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.coordinates_basis_space
declarations.statement:
lemma coordinates_basis_space (i : Fin d) :
    coordinates d (Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inr i)) = (0, Space.basis i)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.second_spacetime_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma second_spacetime_deriv (h : SpaceTime d → F) (hh : ContDiff ℝ ∞ h)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    SpaceTime.deriv μ (SpaceTime.deriv μ h) p =
      iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h p ![Lorentz.Vector.basis μ, Lorentz.Vector.basis μ]

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.second_spacetime_deriv_coordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma second_spacetime_deriv_coordinates (g : ℝ × Space d → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    SpaceTime.deriv μ (SpaceTime.deriv μ (g ∘ coordinates d)) p =
      iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 g (coordinates d p)
        ![coordinates d (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ), coordinates d (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)]

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.second_time_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma second_time_slice (g : ℝ × Space d → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g)
    (t : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    deriv (deriv (fun s => g (s, x))) t =
      iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 g (t, x) ![(1, 0), (1, 0)]

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.second_space_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma second_space_slice (g : ℝ × Space d → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g)
    (t : ℝ) (x b : Space d) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun y => g (t, y)) x ![b, b] =
      iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 g (t, x) ![(0, b), (0, b)]

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.waveTrace_coordinates
declarations.doc: The Minkowski metric trace is the time second derivative minus the spatial Laplacian.
declarations.statement:
lemma waveTrace_coordinates (g : ℝ × Space d → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    (∑ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, (minkowskiMatrix μ μ : ℝ) •
      SpaceTime.deriv μ (SpaceTime.deriv μ (g ∘ coordinates d)) p) =
      deriv (deriv (fun s => g (s, (coordinates d p).2))) (coordinates d p).1 -
        (Δ (fun y => g ((coordinates d p).1, y))) (coordinates d p).2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.operator_of_coordinates
declarations.doc: The neighbour's Klein–Gordon operator has the Fourier coordinate differential expression.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_of_coordinates (m : ℝ) (g : ℝ × Space d → F) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g)
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    (operator m
      ⟨g ∘ coordinates d, hg.comp (coordinates d).contDiff⟩ : SpaceTime d → F) p =
      deriv (deriv (fun s => g (s, (coordinates d p).2))) (coordinates d p).1 -
        (Δ (fun y => g ((coordinates d p).1, y))) (coordinates d p).2 +
          m ^ 2 • g (coordinates d p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.sourceOperator_eq_operator
declarations.doc: The transported compact source operator is the existing Minkowski Klein–Gordon operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma sourceOperator_eq_operator (m : ℝ)
    (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), F)) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    sourceOperator F (m ^ 2) f p =
      (operator m ⟨f, f.contDiff⟩ : SpaceTime d → F) p

modules.title: The causal propagator kernel
modules.doc:
The causal propagator kernel is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and odd under time
reversal.

## i. Overview

The causal propagator kernel is the retarded kernel minus the advanced kernel, both centred at the
spacetime origin. It solves the homogeneous equation. The covariance of the retarded and advanced
point sources (`retardedPointSource_actDist`) transfers to it. A Lorentz transformation fixes the
origin. An orthochronous one fixes the kernel. A time-reversing one swaps the retarded and the
advanced kernel, so it changes the sign of the causal kernel.

The covariance is proved on the distribution itself. The Fourier transform of the kernel inherits
it with the induced action on the frequencies.

## ii. Key results

- `causalKernel` : the retarded kernel minus the advanced kernel at the origin.
- `causalKernel_actDist` : the kernel is invariant under orthochronous Lorentz transformations.
- `causalKernel_actDist_of_not` : the kernel changes sign under time reversing ones.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The kernel

## iv. References

None.

## A. The kernel

- `causalKernel` : the retarded kernel minus the advanced kernel at the origin.
- `causalKernel_actDist` : the kernel is invariant under orthochronous Lorentz transformations.
- `causalKernel_actDist_of_not` : the kernel changes sign under time reversing ones.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.causalKernel
declarations.doc: The causal propagator kernel: the retarded kernel minus the advanced kernel at the origin.
declarations.statement: def causalKernel (m : ℝ) : DistributionField d ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.smul_zero_of_translation_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A Poincaré transformation without translation fixes the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_zero_of_translation_eq_zero {g : PoincareGroup d} (h : g.translation = 0) :
    g • (0 : SpaceTime d) = 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.causalKernel_actDist
declarations.doc:
**Lorentz invariance of the causal kernel.** An orthochronous Lorentz transformation leaves
the causal propagator kernel invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalKernel_actDist (m : ℝ) {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (h : g.translation = 0) : actDist g (causalKernel m) = causalKernel m

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.causalKernel_actDist_of_not
declarations.doc: A time-reversing Lorentz transformation changes the sign of the causal propagator kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalKernel_actDist_of_not (m : ℝ) {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (h : g.translation = 0) : actDist g (causalKernel m) = -causalKernel m

modules.title: Poincaré covariance for distributional sources
modules.doc:
The retarded and advanced solutions of compactly supported distributions are covariant.

## i. Overview

The Poincaré group acts on distributions by transposition. The Klein–Gordon operator on
distributions commutes with this action because the operator on test functions does. A
transformed compactly supported distribution is compactly supported. The transformed retarded
solution solves the equation for the transformed source and vanishes outside the transformed
causal future. Uniqueness of the retarded solution then gives covariance. The point source is a
retarded solution of a delta distribution. So it is covariant too.

## ii. Key results

- `testOperator_actTestFunction` : the operator on test functions is covariant.
- `distributionOperator_actDist` : the operator on distributions is covariant.
- `retardedDistribution_actCompact` : the retarded solution of a distribution is covariant.
- `retardedPointSource_actDist` : the retarded point source is covariant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The operator on test functions and distributions
- B. Compactly supported distributions
- C. Covariance of the solutions
- D. The point source

## iv. References

None.

## A. The operator on test functions and distributions

- `testOperator_actTestFunction` : the operator on test functions is covariant.
- `distributionOperator_actDist` : the operator on distributions is covariant.

## B. Compactly supported distributions

- `actCompact` : the action on compactly supported distributions.

## C. Covariance of the solutions

- `retardedDistribution_actCompact` : the retarded solution of a distribution is covariant.

## D. The point source

- `retardedPointSource_actDist` : the retarded point source is covariant.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actTestFunction_testFieldEquiv
declarations.doc: The action on test functions agrees with the action on test fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma actTestFunction_testFieldEquiv (g : PoincareGroup d) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    actTestFunction g (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) = testFieldEquiv ℝ (actTest g f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.testOperator_actTestFunction
declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator on test functions commutes with the Poincaré action.
declarations.statement:
lemma testOperator_actTestFunction (m : ℝ) (g : PoincareGroup d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    Spacetime.testOperator m (actTestFunction g φ) =
      actTestFunction g (Spacetime.testOperator m φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.distributionOperator_actDist
declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator on distributions commutes with the Poincaré action.
declarations.statement:
lemma distributionOperator_actDist {V : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V]
    (m : ℝ) (g : PoincareGroup d) (T : DistributionField d V) :
    distributionOperator m (actDist g T) = actDist g (distributionOperator m T)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actCompact
declarations.doc: The action of the Poincaré group on compactly supported distributions.
declarations.statement:
def actCompact (g : PoincareGroup d) (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actCompact_val
declarations.doc: The value of a transformed compactly supported distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma actCompact_val (g : PoincareGroup d) (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    (actCompact g T : DistributionField d V) = actDist g T

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_actCompact
declarations.doc: The retarded solution of a distribution is covariant under orthochronous transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_actCompact {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    retardedDistribution m (actCompact g T) = actDist g (retardedDistribution m T)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedDistribution_actCompact
declarations.doc: The advanced solution of a distribution is covariant under orthochronous transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedDistribution_actCompact {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    advancedDistribution m (actCompact g T) = actDist g (advancedDistribution m T)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_actCompact_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the retarded solution of the transformed source into the transformed
advanced solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_actCompact_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    retardedDistribution m (actCompact g T) = actDist g (advancedDistribution m T)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedDistribution_actCompact_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the advanced solution of the transformed source into the transformed
retarded solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedDistribution_actCompact_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    advancedDistribution m (actCompact g T) = actDist g (retardedDistribution m T)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.deltaCompact
declarations.doc: The delta distribution at `p` as a compactly supported distribution.
declarations.statement: def deltaCompact (p : SpaceTime d) : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actCompact_deltaCompact
declarations.doc: The action sends the delta distribution at `p` to the delta distribution at `g p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma actCompact_deltaCompact (g : PoincareGroup d) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actCompact g (deltaCompact p) = deltaCompact (g • p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedPointSource_eq
declarations.doc: The retarded point source is the retarded solution of the delta distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_eq (p : SpaceTime d) :
    retardedPointSource m p = retardedDistribution m (deltaCompact p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedPointSource_eq
declarations.doc: The advanced point source is the advanced solution of the delta distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedPointSource_eq (p : SpaceTime d) :
    advancedPointSource m p = advancedDistribution m (deltaCompact p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedPointSource_actDist
declarations.doc: The retarded point source is covariant under orthochronous transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_actDist {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actDist g (retardedPointSource m p) = retardedPointSource m (g • p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedPointSource_actDist
declarations.doc: The advanced point source is covariant under orthochronous transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedPointSource_actDist {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actDist g (advancedPointSource m p) = advancedPointSource m (g • p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedPointSource_actDist_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the transformed retarded point source into the advanced point
source at the transformed point.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_actDist_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actDist g (retardedPointSource m p) = advancedPointSource m (g • p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedPointSource_actDist_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the transformed advanced point source into the retarded point source
at the transformed point.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedPointSource_actDist_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    actDist g (advancedPointSource m p) = retardedPointSource m (g • p)

modules.title: Lorentz covariance of the causal kernel on the Fourier side
modules.doc:
The Fourier transform of the causal propagator kernel is invariant under orthochronous Lorentz
transformations acting on the frequencies by the inverse transpose. It is odd under the others.

## i. Overview

The covariance of the causal kernel is proved on test functions (`causalKernel_actDist`). Density
carries it to the tempered extension. The Fourier transform of a tempered functional `T` is
`g ↦ T (𝓕 g)`. For a Lorentz transformation `Λ` the transform of `g ∘ (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ` is `𝓕 g ∘ Λ`
because `|det Λ| = 1`. So a functional with `T (φ ∘ Λ) = c * T φ` has a transform with
`T̂ (g ∘ (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ) = c * T̂ g`. No second Fourier theory enters. The transport is one lemma about
any tempered functional.

## ii. Key results

- `lorentzSplit` : a Lorentz transformation on the split space.
- `freqAct` : the induced action on Schwartz functions of the frequency by `(Λ⁻¹)ᵀ`.
- `fourierDist` : the Fourier transform of a tempered functional.
- `fourierDist_freqAct` : covariance of a functional transports to its transform.
- `temperedCausal` : the tempered causal propagator kernel.
- `fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct` : the transform of the causal kernel is invariant under
  orthochronous transformations.
- `fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct_of_not` : it changes sign under the others.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action on frequencies
- B. Transport of covariance
- C. The tempered causal kernel
- D. The causal kernel on the Fourier side

## iv. References

None.

## A. The action on frequencies

- `lorentzSplit` : a Lorentz transformation on the split space.
- `abs_det_lorentzSplit` : its determinant has absolute value one.
- `freqAct` : the induced action on Schwartz functions of the frequency.
- `fourier_freqAct` : the transform of the transformed function.

## B. Transport of covariance

- `fourierDist` : the Fourier transform of a tempered functional.
- `fourierDist_freqAct` : covariance of a functional transports to its transform.

## C. The tempered causal kernel

- `temperedCausal` : the tempered causal propagator kernel.
- `temperedCausal_comp` : its covariance on Schwartz functions.

## D. The causal kernel on the Fourier side

- `fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct` : invariance under orthochronous transformations.
- `fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct_of_not` : sign change under the others.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.lorentzSplit
declarations.doc: A Lorentz transformation as a linear equivalence of the split space.
declarations.statement: def lorentzSplit (Λ : LorentzGroup d) : SplitSpace d ≃L[ℝ] SplitSpace d

declarations.name: KleinGordon.lorentzSplit_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzSplit_apply (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (ξ : SplitSpace d) :
    lorentzSplit Λ ξ = (splitEquiv d).symm (lorentzCLE Λ (splitEquiv d ξ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.abs_det_lorentzSplit
declarations.doc: The determinant of a Lorentz transformation of the split space has absolute value one.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_det_lorentzSplit (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    |LinearMap.det (lorentzSplit Λ : SplitSpace d →ₗ[ℝ] SplitSpace d)| = 1

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqAct
declarations.doc:
**The action on frequencies.** A Lorentz transformation acts on Schwartz functions of the
frequency by the inverse transpose.
declarations.statement: def freqAct (Λ : LorentzGroup d) : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqAct_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma freqAct_apply (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (g : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) (ξ : SplitSpace d) :
    freqAct Λ g ξ = g (Fourier.invTranspose (lorentzSplit Λ) ξ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourier_freqAct
declarations.doc: **The transform of the transformed function.**
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_freqAct (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (g : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) (ξ : SplitSpace d) :
    𝓕 (freqAct Λ g) ξ = 𝓕 g (lorentzSplit Λ ξ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.partSource
declarations.doc:
The real or imaginary part of a complex Schwartz function of the split space as a real
Schwartz function of spacetime.
declarations.statement: def partSource (part : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ) : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.partSource_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma partSource_apply (part : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (h : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    partSource part h x = part (h ((splitEquiv d).symm x))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierDist
declarations.doc:
**The Fourier transform of a tempered functional.** It sends `g` to the functional applied to
the real and the imaginary part of `𝓕 g`.
declarations.statement: def fourierDist (T : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (g : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.partSource_lorentz
declarations.statement:
lemma partSource_lorentz (part : ℂ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (h : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) :
    partSource part (SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ (lorentzSplit Λ) h) =
      SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (lorentzCLE Λ) (partSource part h)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierDist_freqAct
declarations.doc:
**Covariance of a functional transports to its transform.** If `T (φ ∘ Λ) = c * T φ` then
the transform of `T` at `g ∘ (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ` is `c` times its value at `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierDist_freqAct (T : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (c : ℝ)
    (hT : ∀ φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ),
      T (SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (lorentzCLE Λ) φ) = c * T φ)
    (g : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) : fourierDist T (freqAct Λ g) = c * fourierDist T g

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedAdvanced
declarations.doc: The advanced kernel as a tempered functional: the retarded one reflected through the origin.
declarations.statement: def temperedAdvanced (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedCausal
declarations.doc: **The tempered causal propagator kernel.**
declarations.statement: def temperedCausal (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.compCLM_neg_ofTestFunction
declarations.statement:
lemma compCLM_neg_ofTestFunction (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (ContinuousLinearEquiv.neg ℝ)
      (ofTestFunction φ) = ofTestFunction (actTestFunction (pointReflection 0)⁻¹ φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedAdvanced_ofTestFunction
declarations.statement:
lemma temperedAdvanced_ofTestFunction (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    temperedAdvanced d m (ofTestFunction φ) = advancedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedCausal_ofTestFunction
declarations.statement:
lemma temperedCausal_ofTestFunction (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    temperedCausal d m (ofTestFunction φ) = causalKernel m φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.compCLM_lorentz_ofTestFunction
declarations.statement:
lemma compCLM_lorentz_ofTestFunction (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (lorentzCLE Λ) (ofTestFunction φ) =
      ofTestFunction (actTestFunction (⟨0, Λ⟩ : PoincareGroup d)⁻¹ φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedCausal_comp
declarations.doc:
**Covariance of the tempered causal kernel.** If the causal kernel on test functions picks up
the factor `c` under `Λ` then so does its tempered extension on Schwartz functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma temperedCausal_comp (m : ℝ) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (c : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ),
      causalKernel m (actTestFunction (⟨0, Λ⟩ : PoincareGroup d)⁻¹ φ) = c * causalKernel m φ)
    (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    temperedCausal d m (SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (lorentzCLE Λ) φ) =
      c * temperedCausal d m φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct
declarations.doc:
**The causal kernel on the Fourier side is Lorentz invariant.** Its transform is unchanged
when an orthochronous Lorentz transformation acts on the frequencies by the inverse transpose.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierDist_temperedCausal_freqAct_of_not
declarations.doc:
**The causal kernel on the Fourier side is odd under time reversal.** Its transform changes
sign when a non-orthochronous Lorentz transformation acts on the frequencies.

modules.title: Poincaré covariance of the Klein–Gordon Green operators
modules.doc:
The retarded and advanced solutions commute with the Poincaré group.

## i. Overview

The Klein–Gordon equation is invariant under the Poincaré group. If `u` solves the equation with
source `f` then `g • u` solves it with source `g • f`. An orthochronous element maps the causal
future of the support of `f` to the causal future of the support of `g • f`. So `g • R f` is a
solution with the support condition of the retarded solution for `g • f`. Uniqueness gives
`R (g • f) = g • R f`. The same holds for the advanced solution. An element that reverses time
exchanges the two. So the causal propagator `E` is covariant up to a sign.

## ii. Key results

- `operator_actSmooth` : the Klein–Gordon operator commutes with the Poincaré action.
- `retarded_actTest` : the retarded solution is covariant under orthochronous elements.
- `advanced_actTest` : the advanced solution is covariant under orthochronous elements.
- `retarded_actTest_of_not` : a time reversal exchanges retarded and advanced solutions.
- `propagator_actTest` : the causal propagator is covariant under orthochronous elements.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The operator
- B. Uniqueness of advanced solutions
- C. Covariance of the Green operators
- D. Covariance of the causal propagator

## iv. References

None.

## A. The operator

- `operator_actSmooth` : the Klein–Gordon operator commutes with the Poincaré action.

## B. Uniqueness of advanced solutions

- `existsUnique_advanced` : a compact source has exactly one solution supported in the causal
  past of the source.

## C. Covariance of the Green operators

- `retarded_actTest` : the retarded solution is covariant under orthochronous elements.
- `advanced_actTest` : the advanced solution is covariant under orthochronous elements.
- `retarded_actTest_of_not` : a time reversal exchanges retarded and advanced solutions.
- `advanced_actTest_of_not` : the same for the advanced solution.

## D. Covariance of the causal propagator

- `propagator_actTest` : the causal propagator is covariant under orthochronous elements.
- `propagator_actTest_of_not` : a time reversal changes the sign of the causal propagator.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.operator_actSmooth
declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator commutes with the action of the Poincaré group.
declarations.statement:
lemma operator_actSmooth (m : ℝ) (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : smoothFields d V) :
    Spacetime.operator m (actSmooth g u) = actSmooth g (Spacetime.operator m u)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.compactOperator_actTest
declarations.doc: The compact operator commutes with the action on test fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma compactOperator_actTest (m : ℝ) (g : PoincareGroup d) (f : TestField d V) :
    (equation m).compactOperator (actTest g f) = actTest g ((equation m).compactOperator f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.existsUnique_advanced
declarations.doc: A compact source has exactly one solution supported in the causal past of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_advanced (f : TestField d F) :
    ∃! u : smoothFields d F, Spacetime.operator m u = f ∧
      tsupport (u : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
        (causalRelation d).causalPast (tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.tsupport_actTest
declarations.doc: The support of a transformed test field is the image of the support.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_actTest (g : PoincareGroup d) (f : TestField d F) :
    tsupport ((actTest g f : TestField d F) : SpaceTime d → F) =
      g • tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_actTest
declarations.doc: The retarded solution is covariant under orthochronous Poincaré transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_actTest {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous) (f : TestField d F) :
    retarded F m (actTest g f) = actSmooth g (retarded F m f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced_actTest
declarations.doc: The advanced solution is covariant under orthochronous Poincaré transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma advanced_actTest {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous) (f : TestField d F) :
    advanced F m (actTest g f) = actSmooth g (advanced F m f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_actTest_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the retarded solution of the transformed source into the transformed
advanced solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_actTest_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (f : TestField d F) : retarded F m (actTest g f) = actSmooth g (advanced F m f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced_actTest_of_not
declarations.doc:
A time reversal turns the advanced solution of the transformed source into the transformed
retarded solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma advanced_actTest_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (f : TestField d F) : advanced F m (actTest g f) = actSmooth g (retarded F m f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_actTest
declarations.doc: The causal propagator is covariant under orthochronous Poincaré transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagator_actTest {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous) (f : TestField d F) :
    propagator F m (actTest g f) = actSmooth g (propagator F m f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_actTest_of_not
declarations.doc: A time reversal changes the sign of the causal propagator.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagator_actTest_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (f : TestField d F) :
