    propagator F m (actTest g f) = -actSmooth g (propagator F m f)

modules.title: The solution space as a Poincaré representation
modules.doc:
The space of homogeneous solutions with spacelike compact support carries an action of the
Poincaré group. The causal propagator is an equivariant isomorphism from the compact sources
modulo the equation of motion to this space.

## i. Overview

A homogeneous solution with spacelike compact support is mapped to another one by every Poincaré
transformation. The causal hull of a set is mapped to the causal hull of the image by every
transformation including time reversals. The action on compact sources descends to the quotient by
the image of the equation of motion because the equation of motion is covariant. The isomorphism
of the quotient with the solution space sends the class of a source `f` to the causal propagator
`E f`. It is covariant for orthochronous transformations and changes sign for time reversals.

## ii. Key results

- `actSol` : the action on spacelike compact homogeneous solutions.
- `actQuot` : the action on compact sources modulo the equation of motion.
- `propagatorClass_actQuot` : the isomorphism is covariant for orthochronous transformations.
- `propagatorClass_actQuot_of_not` : the isomorphism changes sign under time reversals.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action on solutions
- B. The action on the quotient
- C. Covariance of the isomorphism

## iv. References

None.

## A. The action on solutions

- `actSol` : the action on spacelike compact homogeneous solutions.

## B. The action on the quotient

- `actQuot` : the action on compact sources modulo the equation of motion.

## C. Covariance of the isomorphism

- `propagatorClass_actQuot` : the isomorphism is covariant for orthochronous transformations.

declarations.doc: Smooth fields form an additive group, needed to form the quotient.
declarations.statement: local instance : AddCommGroup (smoothFields d F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actSmooth_mem_spacelikeCompactSolution
declarations.doc: The action preserves homogeneous solutions with spacelike compact support.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actSol
declarations.doc: The action of the Poincaré group on homogeneous solutions with spacelike compact support.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actSol_coe
declarations.doc: The value of a transformed solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma actSol_coe (g : PoincareGroup d)
    (u : (equation (d := d) (V := F) m).spacelikeCompactSolution (causalRelation d)) :
    ((actSol g u : (equation (d := d) (V := F) m).spacelikeCompactSolution (causalRelation d)) :
      smoothFields d F) = actSmooth g u

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.SourceClasses
declarations.doc: Compact sources modulo the equation of motion.
declarations.statement: abbrev SourceClasses (d : ℕ) (F : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] (m : ℝ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actQuot
declarations.doc: The action on compact sources modulo the equation of motion.
declarations.statement: def actQuot (g : PoincareGroup d) : SourceClasses d F m →ₗ[ℝ] SourceClasses d F m

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actQuot_mk
declarations.doc: The action on the class of a source is the class of the transformed source.
declarations.statement:
lemma actQuot_mk (g : PoincareGroup d) (f : (equation (d := d) (V := F) m).compactSources) :
    actQuot (F := F) (m := m) g (Submodule.Quotient.mk f : SourceClasses d F m) =
      Submodule.Quotient.mk (actTest g f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.solutionsEquivQuotient_symm_mk
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism from the quotient of compact sources onto the solutions sends the class of a
source to its causal propagator.
declarations.statement:
lemma solutionsEquivQuotient_symm_mk (f : (equation (d := d) (V := F) m).compactSources) :
    ((solutionsEquivQuotient (d := d) (F := F) (m := m)).symm (Submodule.Quotient.mk f) :
        smoothFields d F) = propagator F m f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagatorClass_actQuot
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism of compact sources modulo the equation of motion with the solutions is
covariant under orthochronous Poincaré transformations.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagatorClass_actQuot {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : g.IsOrthochronous)
    (x : SourceClasses d F m) :
    (solutionsEquivQuotient (d := d) (F := F) (m := m)).symm (actQuot (F := F) (m := m) g x) =
      actSol g ((solutionsEquivQuotient (d := d) (F := F) (m := m)).symm x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagatorClass_actQuot_of_not
declarations.doc: The isomorphism changes sign under Poincaré transformations that reverse time.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagatorClass_actQuot_of_not {g : PoincareGroup d} (hg : ¬ g.IsOrthochronous)
    (x : SourceClasses d F m) :
    (solutionsEquivQuotient (d := d) (F := F) (m := m)).symm (actQuot (F := F) (m := m) g x) =
      -actSol g ((solutionsEquivQuotient (d := d) (F := F) (m := m)).symm x)

modules.title: Cutoff responses of compact sources
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Cutting the response off by a test function is continuous in the source.

## ii. Key results

- `solutionEvaluation` : Evaluation of the retarded response at a fixed event is continuous in the
  native LF topology.
- `advancedSolutionEvaluation` : Evaluation of the advanced response is continuous in the native LF
  source topology.
- `cutoffSolutionSupported` : A compactly cut off retarded response is continuous between
  fixed-support source and target spaces in every derivative seminorm.
- `cutoffSolution` : Multiplying the retarded Fourier response by a compact smooth cutoff is
  continuous on the native LF test-function space.
- `cutoffAdvancedSolution` : A compactly cut off advanced response is continuous on native smooth
  tests.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources
- B. Continuous source bounds for parameter derivatives
- C. Continuous compactly cut off Green responses
- D. Continuous compactly cut off advanced response

## iv. References

None.

## A. Continuous seminorm bounds for Fourier sources

- `solutionEvaluation` : Evaluation of the retarded response at a fixed event is continuous in the
  native LF topology.
- `advancedSolutionEvaluation` : Evaluation of the advanced response is continuous in the native LF
  source topology.

Lemmas: `exists_solution_supported_seminorm`, `solutionEvaluation_apply`,
`advancedSolutionEvaluation_apply`.

## B. Continuous source bounds for parameter derivatives

Lemmas: `exists_integrand_derivative_supported_seminorm`,
`exists_integral_derivative_supported_seminorm`, `exists_solution_derivative_supported_seminorm`.

## C. Continuous compactly cut off Green responses

- `cutoffSolutionSupported` : A compactly cut off retarded response is continuous between
  fixed-support source and target spaces in every derivative seminorm.
- `cutoffSolution` : Multiplying the retarded Fourier response by a compact smooth cutoff is
  continuous on the native LF test-function space.

Lemmas: `cutoffSolution_apply`.

## D. Continuous compactly cut off advanced response

- `cutoffAdvancedSolution` : A compactly cut off advanced response is continuous on native smooth
  tests.

Lemmas: `cutoffAdvancedSolution_apply`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_solution_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc:
On bounded time intervals the response is controlled by a continuous source seminorm,
uniformly over every spatial observation point.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_solution_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E)) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ)
    (T : ℝ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (p : ℝ × E), |p.1| ≤ T →
        ‖solution F (supportedSource F K f) μ p.1 p.2‖ ≤ q f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionEvaluation
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the retarded response at a fixed event is continuous in the native LF topology.
declarations.statement:
def solutionEvaluation {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (p : ℝ × E) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F) →L[ℝ] F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionEvaluation_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma solutionEvaluation_apply {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (p : ℝ × E)
    (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) :
    solutionEvaluation F hμ p f = solution F f μ p.1 p.2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolutionEvaluation
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the advanced response is continuous in the native LF source topology.
declarations.statement:
def advancedSolutionEvaluation {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (p : ℝ × E) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F) →L[ℝ] F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolutionEvaluation_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedSolutionEvaluation_apply {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (p : ℝ × E)
    (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) :
    advancedSolutionEvaluation F hμ p f = advancedSolution F f μ p.1 p.2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_integrand_derivative_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc: Every parameter derivative of the Fourier integrand has a continuous source bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_integrand_derivative_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E))
    (μ : ℝ) (k N : ℕ) (R : ℝ≥0) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (p z : ℝ × E), |z.1| ≤ R →
        ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun w => solutionIntegrand F (supportedSource F K f) μ w z) p‖ ≤
          q f * (1 + ‖z.2‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_integral_derivative_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc: Every derivative of a fixed-interval Fourier response is controlled continuously by the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_integral_derivative_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E))
    {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (k : ℕ) (R : ℝ≥0) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (p : ℝ × E),
        ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun w => ∫ z : ℝ × E, solutionIntegrand F (supportedSource F K f) μ w z
          ∂((volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 (R : ℝ))).prod volume)) p‖ ≤ q f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_solution_derivative_supported_seminorm
declarations.doc:
Every spacetime derivative of the retarded field is controlled by a continuous source seminorm
on bounded time intervals, uniformly in the spatial observation point.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_solution_derivative_supported_seminorm (K : Compacts (ℝ × E))
    {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (k : ℕ) (T : ℝ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ (ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ (f : ContDiffMapSupportedIn (ℝ × E) F ⊤ K) (p : ℝ × E), |p.1| ≤ T →
        ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun w => solution F (supportedSource F K f) μ w.1 w.2) p‖ ≤ q f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cutoffSolutionSupported
declarations.doc:
A compactly cut off retarded response is continuous between fixed-support source and target
spaces in every derivative seminorm.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cutoffSolution
declarations.doc:
Multiplying the retarded Fourier response by a compact smooth cutoff is continuous on the
native LF test-function space.
declarations.statement:
def cutoffSolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℝ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cutoffSolution_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma cutoffSolution_apply {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℝ))
    (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) (p : ℝ × E) :
    cutoffSolution F hμ χ f p = χ p • solution F f μ p.1 p.2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cutoffAdvancedSolution
declarations.doc: A compactly cut off advanced response is continuous on native smooth tests.
declarations.statement:
def cutoffAdvancedSolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℝ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cutoffAdvancedSolution_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma cutoffAdvancedSolution_apply {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℝ))
    (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) (p : ℝ × E) :
    cutoffAdvancedSolution F hμ χ f p = χ p • advancedSolution F f μ p.1 p.2

modules.title: Descent from `d + k` to `d` space dimensions
modules.doc:
Integrating the sine evolution in `d + k` space dimensions over the extra variables gives the sine
evolution in `d` space dimensions of the integrated data.

## i. Overview

Let `E'` be the Euclidean product of `E` and `F`. The Fourier transform of the integral over `F`
of a function on `E'` is the restriction of its transform to the frequencies `(ξ, 0)`. The
multiplier of the sine evolution depends on the norm of the frequency, so the restriction to
`(ξ, 0)` is the multiplier of `E`. This is Hadamard's method of descent. It holds for every mass.

## ii. Key results

- `integral_sineEvolution_marginal` : descent for the sine evolution, for every mass.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Descent

## iv. References

None.

## A. Descent

- `integral_sineEvolution_marginal` : descent for the sine evolution, for every mass.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integral_sineEvolution_marginal
declarations.doc:
**Descent.** Integrating the sine evolution in `E × F` over `F` gives the sine evolution in
`E` of the integrated data.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_sineEvolution_marginal {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r : ℝ)
    (g' : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × F), ℂ)) (gb : 𝓢(E, ℂ))
    (hgb : ∀ x, gb x = ∫ y : F, g' (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))) (x : E) :
    ∫ y : F, sineEvolution ℂ r μ g' (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)) = sineEvolution ℂ r μ gb x

modules.title: Smooth radial lifts
modules.doc:
A smooth radial source in `d` space dimensions and its lift to `d + 2` dimensions.

## i. Overview

A radial test function is a smooth function `P` of the squared norm. Its lift to two more space
dimensions is `-(1/π) P'` of the squared norm. This is `-(1/(2π ρ)) ∂ρ` of the profile `P(ρ²)`,
written without the singular factor `1/ρ`. The integral of the lift over the plane is the original
function.

## ii. Key results

- `integral_tail_sq` : the tail integral of `u P'(u²)`.
- `integral_plane_lift` : the integral of the lifted profile over the plane.
- `radialSource` : the radial source `P(s, ‖x‖²)` as a test function.
- `liftProfile` : the lift `-(1/π) ∂_q P` of a profile to two more space dimensions.
- `radialSource_marginal` : the lifted radial source integrates to the original one.
- `hasDerivAt_solution_radialSource` : dimension raising for a smooth radial source.
- `transportSource_spaceThree` : a radial source on the Euclidean three-space is radial on
  `Space 3`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The tail integral
- B. The plane integral of the lift
- C. Radial sources
- D. Dimension raising

## iv. References

None.

## A. The tail integral

- `integral_tail_sq` : the tail integral of `u P'(u²)`.

## B. The plane integral of the lift

- `integral_plane_lift` : the integral of the lifted profile over the plane.

## C. Radial sources

- `radialSource` : the radial source `P(s, ‖x‖²)` as a test function.
- `liftProfile` : the lift `-(1/π) ∂_q P` of a profile to two more space dimensions.
- `radialSource_marginal` : the lifted radial source integrates to the original one.

## D. Dimension raising

- `hasDerivAt_solution_radialSource` : dimension raising for a smooth radial source.
- `transportSource_spaceThree` : a radial source on the Euclidean three-space is radial on
  `Space 3`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.radialSource
declarations.doc:
The radial source `(s, x) ↦ P (s, ‖x‖²)` built from a test function `P` of time and the squared
radius.
declarations.statement:
def radialSource (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × V)), ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.radialSource_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma radialSource_apply (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) (x : V) :
    radialSource V P (s, x) = P (s, ‖x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integral_tail_sq
declarations.doc: The tail integral of `u P'(u²)` is `-P(ρ²) / 2` for a smooth compactly supported profile.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_tail_sq {P : ℝ → ℂ} (hP : ContDiff ℝ ∞ P) (hc : HasCompactSupport P) (ρ : ℝ) :
    ∫ u in Ioi ρ, u • deriv P (u ^ 2) = -(P (ρ ^ 2) / 2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integral_plane_lift
declarations.doc:
The plane integral of the lift at a given radius: the lifted profile integrates to the
original profile.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_plane_lift {g : ℝ → ℂ} (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) (hc : HasCompactSupport g) {ρ : ℝ}
    (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) :
    ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), (-(1 / Real.pi : ℝ) : ℝ) • deriv g (ρ ^ 2 + ‖y‖ ^ 2) =
      g (ρ ^ 2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.liftProfile
declarations.doc: The lift of a profile to two more space dimensions: `-(1/π) ∂_q P`.
declarations.statement:
def liftProfile (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.deriv_slice_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_slice_eq (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s q : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun q' : ℝ => P (s, q')) q = lineDeriv ℝ P (s, q) ((0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.liftProfile_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma liftProfile_apply (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s q : ℝ) :
    liftProfile P (s, q) = (-(1 / Real.pi : ℝ) : ℝ) • deriv (fun q' : ℝ => P (s, q')) q

declarations.name: KleinGordon.radialSource_marginal
declarations.doc:
**The lifted radial source integrates to the original one.** The integral over the plane of the
lift `-(1/π) ∂_q P` is `P`.
declarations.statement:
lemma radialSource_marginal (A : WithLp 2 (E × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E')
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) (x : E) :
    radialSource E P (s, x) = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      radialSource E' (liftProfile P) (s, A (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_solution_radialSource
declarations.doc:
**Dimension raising for a smooth radial source.** The retarded solution in `d + 2` space
dimensions of the lift `-(1/π) ∂_q P` of the radial source `P(s, ‖x‖²)` is `-(1 / (2π ρ)) ∂ρ` of the
retarded solution in `d` space dimensions of `P(s, ‖x‖²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_solution_radialSource {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (d : ℕ)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) {e : Space d} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) (t : ℝ)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => solution ℂ (radialSource (Space d) P) μ t (τ • e))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) • solution ℂ (radialSource (Space (d + 2)) (liftProfile P)) μ t
        ((spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0)))) ρ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.transportSource_spaceThree
declarations.statement:
lemma transportSource_spaceThree (Q : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) :
    transportSource spaceThree (radialSource Eucl3 Q) = radialSource (Space 3) Q

modules.title: Dimension raising for the retarded solution
modules.doc:
The retarded solution in `d + 2` space dimensions is `-(1 / (2π ρ)) ∂ρ` of the one in `d` dimensions
for sources that are radial in the extra variables.

## i. Overview

The identity on the slices (`hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial`) passes through the Duhamel integral.
The integrand is bounded uniformly in the time. It vanishes outside the compact time support of the
source. So the derivative in the radius commutes with the time integral.

## ii. Key results

- `norm_sineEvolution_slice_le` : the sine evolution of the slices is bounded uniformly in time.
- `continuous_sineEvolution_slice` : the sine evolution of the slices is continuous in time.
- `hasDerivAt_solution_radial` : dimension raising for the retarded solution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bounds in time
- B. The retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. Bounds in time

- `exists_bound_integrand` : the Fourier integrand is bounded uniformly in the time.
- `norm_sineEvolution_slice_le` : the sine evolution of the slices is bounded uniformly in time.
- `continuous_sineEvolution_slice` : the sine evolution of the slices is continuous in time.

## B. The retarded solution

- `hasDerivAt_solution_radial` : dimension raising for the retarded solution.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_bound_integrand
declarations.doc: The Fourier integrand of the sine evolution of the slice at time `s` is bounded uniformly.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_bound_integrand {μ : ℝ} (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (z ξ : E), ‖(𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ z) : ℂ) •
      (multiplier (t - s) μ ξ • 𝓕 (slice ℂ ψ s) ξ)‖ ≤
        A * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-((Module.finrank ℝ E + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_sineEvolution_slice_le
declarations.doc: The sine evolution of the slices is bounded, and vanishes outside the time support.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sineEvolution_slice_le {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (z : E), ‖sineEvolution ℂ (t - s) μ (slice ℂ ψ s) z‖ ≤
      (Prod.fst '' tsupport ψ).indicator (fun _ => B) s

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_sineEvolution_slice
declarations.doc: The sine evolution of the slices is continuous in the time.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_sineEvolution_slice {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ)
    (z : E) : Continuous fun s : ℝ => sineEvolution ℂ (t - s) μ (slice ℂ ψ s) z

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_solution_radial
declarations.doc:
**Dimension raising for the retarded solution.** Let `ψ'` be a source on `E × ℝ²` that is
radial in the space variables at each time and let `ψb` be its integral over the plane. The
retarded solution of `ψb` along a ray has the derivative `-(2π ρ)` times the retarded solution of
`ψ'` at distance `ρ`. This is `G_{d+2} = -(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ G_d` for every `d` and every mass.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_solution_radial {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ)
    (ψ' : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × WithLp 2 (E × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))), ℂ))
    (ψb : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (hrad : ∀ s, Function.IsRadial (slice ℂ ψ' s))
    (hψb : ∀ s x, ψb (s, x) = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), ψ' (s, WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)))
    {e : E} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) (t : ℝ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => solution ℂ ψb μ t (τ • e))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) • solution ℂ ψ' μ t (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0))) ρ

modules.title: Rotation invariance of the sine evolution
modules.doc:
The sine evolution commutes with linear isometries. It therefore maps radial functions to radial
functions.

## i. Overview

The multiplier of the sine evolution depends on the norm of the frequency. The Fourier transform
commutes with linear isometries. So the sine evolution of a rotated function is the rotation of the
sine evolution. A radial function is invariant under all rotations. So is its evolution.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_comp_isometry` : the sine evolution commutes with linear isometries.
- `isRadial_sineEvolution` : the sine evolution of a radial function is radial.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Isometries

## iv. References

None.

## A. Isometries

- `sineEvolution_comp_isometry` : the sine evolution commutes with linear isometries.
- `isRadial_sineEvolution` : the sine evolution of a radial function is radial.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.multiplier_comp_isometry
declarations.statement:
lemma multiplier_comp_isometry (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) (r μ : ℝ) (ξ : V) :
    multiplier r μ (A ξ) = multiplier r μ ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_comp_isometry
declarations.doc: **The sine evolution commutes with rotations.**
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_comp_isometry {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) (r : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(W, ℂ))
    (x : V) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r μ (SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ A.toContinuousLinearEquiv g)
        x = sineEvolution ℂ r μ g (A x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.isRadial_sineEvolution
declarations.doc: **The sine evolution of a radial function is radial.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isRadial_sineEvolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r : ℝ) {g : 𝓢(V, ℂ)} (hg : Function.IsRadial g) :
    Function.IsRadial (sineEvolution ℂ r μ g)

modules.title: Dimension raising for the sine evolution
modules.doc:
The sine evolution in `d + 2` space dimensions is `-(1 / (2π ρ)) ∂ρ` of the one in `d` dimensions.

## i. Overview

In one space dimension the massless retarded Green function is `½ Θ(t - |x|)`. In three space
dimensions it is `δ(t - r) / (4π r)`. The second is `-(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ` of the first. This holds in
general: `G_{d+2} = -(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ G_d` for every `d` and every mass.

The proof has three steps. Descent (`Descent`) shows that the integral over the two extra
variables of the sine evolution in `d + 2` dimensions is the sine evolution in `d` dimensions of
the integrated data. The sine evolution of a radial function is radial (`Rotation`). The integral
of a radial function over the plane is the tail integral of its profile, whose derivative is
`-ρ Φ(ρ)` (`RadialPlane`). Together they give the identity on the sine evolutions of radial data.

## ii. Key results

- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial` : dimension raising on the slices for every `d` and every mass.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Radial slices in every dimension

## iv. References

None.

## A. Radial slices in every dimension

- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial` : dimension raising on the slices for every `d` and every mass.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial
declarations.doc:
**Dimension raising on the slices.** Let `g'` be a radial Schwartz function on `E × ℝ²` and let
`gb` be its integral over the plane. The sine evolution of `gb` along a ray has the derivative
`-(2π ρ)` times the sine evolution of `g'` at distance `ρ`. This is `S_{d+2} g' = -(1 / (2π ρ))
∂ρ S_d gb` for every dimension `d` and every mass.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r : ℝ)
    (g' : 𝓢(WithLp 2 (E × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), ℂ)) (hrad : Function.IsRadial g')
    (gb : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (hgb : ∀ x, gb x = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      g' (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))) {e : E} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => sineEvolution ℂ r μ gb (t • e))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) • sineEvolution ℂ r μ g' (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0))) ρ

modules.title: Splitting off two space dimensions
modules.doc:
`Space (d + 2)` is isometric to the Euclidean product of `Space d` and the plane.

## i. Overview

Dimension raising compares the sine evolution in `d + 2` space dimensions with the one in `d`
dimensions. The statements `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial` and `hasDerivAt_solution_radial` live
on the Euclidean product `WithLp 2 (E × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))`. This file transports them to
`Space (d + 2)` along a linear isometry.

## ii. Key results

- `spaceSplit` : the isometry `Space (d + 2) ≃ₗᵢ WithLp 2 (Space d × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))`.
- `solution_transportSource` : the retarded solution commutes with isometries of space.
- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial_space` : dimension raising on the slices of `Space (d + 2)`.
- `hasDerivAt_solution_radial_space` : dimension raising on `Space (d + 2)`.
- `hasDerivAt_retardedResponse_radial` : dimension raising for the retarded response on spacetime.
- `spaceThree` : `Space 3` is isometric to the Euclidean three-space.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The isometry
- B. Dimension raising
- C. Three space dimensions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The isometry

- `spaceSplit` : the isometry `Space (d + 2) ≃ₗᵢ WithLp 2 (Space d × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))`.
- `transportSource` : a source pulled back along an isometry of space.
- `solution_transportSource` : the retarded solution commutes with isometries of space.

## B. Dimension raising

- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial_space` : dimension raising on the slices of `Space (d + 2)`.
- `hasDerivAt_solution_radial_space` : dimension raising on `Space (d + 2)`.
- `hasDerivAt_retardedResponse_radial` : dimension raising for the retarded response on spacetime.

## C. Three space dimensions

- `Eucl3` : the Euclidean three-space as a product of the line and the plane.
- `spaceThree` : `Space 3` is isometric to the Euclidean three-space.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.transportSource
declarations.doc: A source on time and `W` pulled back along an isometry `V ≃ W` of space.
declarations.statement:
def transportSource (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × W)), ℂ) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × V)), ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.transportSource_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma transportSource_apply (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × W)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) (x : V) :
    transportSource A ψ (s, x) = ψ (s, A x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.slice_transportSource
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_transportSource (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × W)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) :
    slice ℂ (transportSource A ψ) s =
      SchwartzMap.compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ A.toContinuousLinearEquiv (slice ℂ ψ s)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_transportSource
declarations.doc: **The retarded solution commutes with isometries of space.**
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_transportSource {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (A : V ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] W)
    (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × W)), ℂ)) (t : ℝ) (x : V) :
    solution ℂ (transportSource A ψ) μ t x = solution ℂ ψ μ t (A x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.spaceSplit
declarations.doc: `Space (d + 2)` is isometric to the Euclidean product of `Space d` and the plane.
declarations.statement:
def spaceSplit (d : ℕ) :
    Space (d + 2) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (Space d × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_solution_radial_space
declarations.doc:
**Dimension raising on `Space (d + 2)`.** Let `ψ'` be a source on time and `Space (d + 2)` that
is radial in space at each time and let `ψb` be its integral over the plane. The massive retarded
solution of `ψb` along a ray in `Space d` has the derivative `-(2π ρ)` times the retarded
solution of `ψ'` at distance `ρ`. This is `G_{d+2} = -(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ G_d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_solution_radial_space {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (d : ℕ)
    (ψ' : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space (d + 2))), ℂ)) (ψb : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × Space d)), ℂ))
    (hrad : ∀ s, Function.IsRadial (slice ℂ ψ' s))
    (hψb : ∀ s x, ψb (s, x) = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      ψ' (s, (spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))))
    {e : Space d} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) (t : ℝ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => solution ℂ ψb μ t (τ • e))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) •
        solution ℂ ψ' μ t ((spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0)))) ρ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial_space
declarations.doc: **Dimension raising on the slices of `Space (d + 2)`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_radial_space {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (d : ℕ) (r : ℝ)
    (g' : 𝓢(Space (d + 2), ℂ)) (hrad : Function.IsRadial g') (gb : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    (hgb : ∀ x, gb x = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      g' ((spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))))
    {e : Space d} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => sineEvolution ℂ r μ gb (t • e))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) •
        sineEvolution ℂ r μ g' ((spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0)))) ρ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_retardedResponse_radial
declarations.doc:
**Dimension raising for the retarded response on spacetime.** The sources are transported to
time and space by `sourceEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_retardedResponse_radial {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (d : ℕ)
    (f' : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime (d + 2))), ℂ)) (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℂ))
    (hrad : ∀ s, Function.IsRadial (slice ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ f') s))
    (hmarg : ∀ s x, sourceEquiv ℂ f (s, x) = ∫ y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      sourceEquiv ℂ f' (s, (spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y))))
    {e : Space d} (he : ‖e‖ = 1) (t : ℝ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => retardedResponse ℂ μ f ((coordinates d).symm (t, τ • e)))
      (-(2 * Real.pi * ρ : ℝ) • retardedResponse ℂ μ f'
        ((coordinates (d + 2)).symm (t, (spaceSplit d).symm (WithLp.toLp 2 (ρ • e, 0))))) ρ

modules.title: Distributional sources
modules.doc:
Compactly supported distributions have retarded and advanced responses.

## i. Overview

Compactly supported distributions have retarded and advanced responses. The point source is a
corollary.

## ii. Key results

- `retardedPointSource` : The retarded native point-source distribution obtained by transposing
  advanced evaluation.
- `advancedPointSource` : The advanced native point-source distribution obtained by transposing
  retarded evaluation.
- `realRetardedCutoff` : The continuous cut off real retarded response on native smooth tests.
- `realAdvancedCutoff` : The continuous cut off real advanced response on native smooth tests.
- `retardedLocalizedResponse` : Transposing the cut off advanced test map gives a retarded response
  on all distributions.
- `advancedLocalizedResponse` : Transposing the cut off retarded test map gives an advanced response
  on all distributions.
- `retardedCompactResponse` : The retarded response of a compactly supported distribution.
- `advancedCompactResponse` : The advanced response of a compactly supported distribution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Causal Klein–Gordon responses to a Dirac source
- B. The retarded point source through the spatial Fourier multiplier
- C. Distributional Klein–Gordon Green operators in every dimension

## iv. References

None.

## A. Causal Klein–Gordon responses to a Dirac source

- `retardedPointSource` : The retarded native point-source distribution obtained by transposing
  advanced evaluation.
- `advancedPointSource` : The advanced native point-source distribution obtained by transposing
  retarded evaluation.

Lemmas: `nativeTestDerivative_coe`, `nativeTestOperator_equiv`,
`distributionOperator_retardedPointSource`, `distributionOperator_advancedPointSource`,
`retardedPointSource_vanishes`, `advancedPointSource_vanishes`,
`dsupport_retardedPointSource_subset`, `dsupport_advancedPointSource_subset`.

## B. The retarded point source through the spatial Fourier multiplier

Lemmas: `retardedPointSource_apply`.

## C. Distributional Klein–Gordon Green operators in every dimension

- `realRetardedCutoff` : The continuous cut off real retarded response on native smooth tests.
- `realAdvancedCutoff` : The continuous cut off real advanced response on native smooth tests.
- `retardedLocalizedResponse` : Transposing the cut off advanced test map gives a retarded response
  on all distributions.
- `advancedLocalizedResponse` : Transposing the cut off retarded test map gives an advanced response
  on all distributions.
- `retardedCompactResponse` : The retarded response of a compactly supported distribution.
- `advancedCompactResponse` : The advanced response of a compactly supported distribution.
- `compactDistributionOperator` : The field operator restricts to an endomorphism of compactly
  supported distributions.

Lemmas: `realRetardedCutoff_apply`, `realAdvancedCutoff_apply`, `retardedLocalizedResponse_solves`,
`advancedLocalizedResponse_solves`, `retardedLocalizedResponse_vanishes`,
`advancedLocalizedResponse_vanishes`, `retardedDistribution_eq_zero`,
`advancedDistribution_eq_zero`, `retardedDistribution_unique`, `advancedDistribution_unique` and
more.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.nativeTestDerivative_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma nativeTestDerivative_coe (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    (TestFunction.lineDerivCLM (n := ⊤) (k := ⊤) ℝ (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ) φ : SpaceTime d → ℝ) =
      SpaceTime.deriv μ φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.nativeTestOperator_equiv

lemma nativeTestOperator_equiv (m : ℝ) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    testOperator m (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) =
      testFieldEquiv ℝ ((equation m).compactOperator f)

declarations.statement: def retardedPointSource (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) : Distribution (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)) ℝ ⊤

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.distributionOperator_retardedPointSource

declarations.statement:
lemma distributionOperator_retardedPointSource (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedPointSource_vanishes
declarations.doc: The retarded point-source response annihilates all tests outside the source event's future.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_vanishes (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    Distribution.IsVanishingOn (retardedPointSource m p)
      ((causalRelation d).causalFuture {p})ᶜ

      ((causalRelation d).causalPast {p})ᶜ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.dsupport_retardedPointSource_subset
declarations.doc: Native distributional support of the retarded fundamental solution is causal.
declarations.statement:
lemma dsupport_retardedPointSource_subset (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    Distribution.dsupport (retardedPointSource m p) ⊆ (causalRelation d).causalFuture {p}

declarations.doc: Native distributional support of the advanced fundamental solution is causal.
declarations.statement:
lemma dsupport_advancedPointSource_subset (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    Distribution.dsupport (advancedPointSource m p) ⊆ (causalRelation d).causalPast {p}

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedPointSource_apply
declarations.doc:
**The retarded fundamental solution as propagated Dirac distributions.** Tested against a
real test function `φ` the retarded point source at the event `p` is the real part of the time
integral of the Fourier multiplier `sincPropagator (s - t₀)` applied to the Dirac distribution at
the position `y₀` of `p`, paired with the spatial slice of `φ` at the time `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_apply (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    retardedPointSource m p φ =
      (∫ s in Set.Ioi (coordinates d p).1,
        sineEvolutionTempered ℂ (s - (coordinates d p).1) (m ^ 2)
          (TemperedDistribution.delta (coordinates d p).2)
          (slice ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) s)).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.realRetardedCutoff
declarations.doc: The continuous cut off real retarded response on native smooth tests.
declarations.statement:
def realRetardedCutoff (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.realAdvancedCutoff
declarations.doc: The continuous cut off real advanced response on native smooth tests.
declarations.statement:
def realAdvancedCutoff (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.realRetardedCutoff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma realRetardedCutoff_apply (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (f : TestField d ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    realRetardedCutoff m χ (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) p =
      χ p * ((realRetardedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.realAdvancedCutoff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma realAdvancedCutoff_apply (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (f : TestField d ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    realAdvancedCutoff m χ (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) p =
      χ p * ((realAdvancedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val p

declarations.statement:
lemma retardedLocalizedResponse_vanishes (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (T : DistributionField d V) (K : Set (SpaceTime d))
    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T Kᶜ) :

    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T Kᶜ) :
    Distribution.IsVanishingOn (advancedLocalizedResponse m χ T)
      ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)ᶜ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedDistribution_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A weak homogeneous field with future support in a compact causal future vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_eq_zero (m : ℝ) (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) (hK : IsCompact K)
    (T : DistributionField d V)
    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T ((causalRelation d).causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hzero : distributionOperator m T = 0) : T = 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.advancedDistribution_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A weak homogeneous field with past support in a compact causal past vanishes.
declarations.statement:

    (T : DistributionField d V)
    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)ᶜ)
    (hzero : distributionOperator m T = 0) : T = 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedDistribution_unique
declarations.doc: The same source and retarded support determine a unique distributional solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_unique (m : ℝ) (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) (hK : IsCompact K)
    (u v : DistributionField d V)
    (hu : Distribution.IsVanishingOn u ((causalRelation d).causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hv : Distribution.IsVanishingOn v ((causalRelation d).causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hsource : distributionOperator m u =
      distributionOperator m v) : u = v

    (u v : DistributionField d V)
    (hu : Distribution.IsVanishingOn u ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)ᶜ)
    (hv : Distribution.IsVanishingOn v ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)ᶜ)
    (hsource : distributionOperator m u =
      distributionOperator m v) : u = v

    distributionOperator m (advancedCompactResponse m T) = T.val

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedCompactResponse_vanishes
declarations.doc: The retarded response is supported in the causal future of the source's compact bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedCompactResponse_vanishes (m : ℝ) (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    Distribution.IsVanishingOn (retardedCompactResponse m T)
      ((causalRelation d).causalFuture (compactDistributionBound T))ᶜ

declarations.doc: The advanced response is supported in the causal past of the source's compact bound.

      ((causalRelation d).causalPast (compactDistributionBound T))ᶜ

declarations.doc: Any distributional solution with future support is the retarded response.

    (u : DistributionField d V) (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) (hK : IsCompact K)

    (u : DistributionField d V) (K : Set (SpaceTime d)) (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hu : Distribution.IsVanishingOn u ((causalRelation d).causalPast K)ᶜ)

modules.title: Finite propagation speed
modules.doc:
The weighted local energy decreases.

## i. Overview

The weighted local energy decreases. The retarded solution vanishes outside the causal future of the
source.

## ii. Key results

- `energyDensity` : The energy density `‖v‖² + ∑ᵢ ‖pᵢ‖² + μ ‖u‖²`.
- `EnergyFields` : Fields with the pointwise derivatives needed for the energy identity of the
  Klein–Gordon equation, in the basis vectors `b i`.
- `e` : The energy density of the fields.
- `e'` : The time derivative of the energy density.
- `WeightFields` : A weight for the energy: smooth, compactly supported in space uniformly in time,
  decreasing in time, with a spatial gradient bounded by its time derivative.
- `flux` : The Lie derivative of the energy flux `⟪v, pᵢ⟫` along `b i`.
- `energyDeriv` : The time derivative of the weighted energy density.
- `coneWeight` : The cone weight `N (c - τ - ψ x)` as a weight for the energy estimate.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The weighted local energy
- B. The cone weight
- C. Finite propagation speed for the homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution
- D. Causal support of the retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. The weighted local energy

- `energyDensity` : The energy density `‖v‖² + ∑ᵢ ‖pᵢ‖² + μ ‖u‖²`.
- `EnergyFields` : Fields with the pointwise derivatives needed for the energy identity of the
  Klein–Gordon equation, in the basis vectors `b i`.
- `e` : The energy density of the fields.
- `e'` : The time derivative of the energy density.
- `WeightFields` : A weight for the energy: smooth, compactly supported in space uniformly in time,
  decreasing in time, with a spatial gradient bounded by its time derivative.
- `flux` : The Lie derivative of the energy flux `⟪v, pᵢ⟫` along `b i`.
- `energyDeriv` : The time derivative of the weighted energy density.

Lemmas: `hasDerivAt_e`, `energy_integrand_nonneg`, `continuous_e`, `continuous_e'`,
`hasLineDerivAt_flux`, `e'_eq`, `continuous_energyDeriv`, `hasCompactSupport_of_vanishing`,
`hasDerivAt_energy`, `integral_energyDeriv` and more.

## B. The cone weight

- `coneWeight` : The cone weight `N (c - τ - ψ x)` as a weight for the energy estimate.

Lemmas: `continuous_coneArg`.

## C. Finite propagation speed for the homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution

- `evolveFields` : The evolved field of the Cauchy data `(f0, f1)` as fields for the energy
  estimate, in the orthonormal basis `stdOrthonormalBasis`.

Lemmas: `evolveU_zero_time`, `evolveV_zero_time`, `sineEvolution_apply_eq_zero`,
`functional_sineEvolution`, `sineEvolution_apply_eq_zero'`.

## D. Causal support of the retarded solution

Lemmas: `sineEvolution_slice_eq_zero`, `solution_eq_zero_of_not_mem_causalFuture`,
`tsupport_solution_subset`, `advancedSolution_eq_zero_of_not_mem_causalPast`,
`tsupport_advancedSolution_subset`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.energyDensity
declarations.doc: The energy density `‖v‖² + ∑ᵢ ‖pᵢ‖² + μ ‖u‖²`.
declarations.statement: def energyDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (μ : ℝ) (u v : ℂ) (p : ι → ℂ) : ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.EnergyFields
declarations.doc:
Fields with the pointwise derivatives needed for the energy identity of the Klein–Gordon
equation, in the basis vectors `b i`. The field is `u` with velocity `v`, the spatial derivatives
are `p i`, the time derivatives of those are `q i`, and the second spatial derivatives are `s i`.
declarations.statement:
structure EnergyFields {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (μ : ℝ) (b : ι → E) where
  /-- The field. -/
  u : ℝ → E → ℂ
  /-- The velocity. -/
  v : ℝ → E → ℂ
  /-- The derivative of the field along `b i`. -/
  p : ι → ℝ → E → ℂ
  /-- The derivative of the velocity along `b i`. -/
  q : ι → ℝ → E → ℂ
  /-- The second derivative of the field along `b i`. -/
  s : ι → ℝ → E → ℂ
  hu : ∀ τ x, HasDerivAt (fun r => u r x) (v τ x) τ
  hv : ∀ τ x, HasDerivAt (fun r => v r x) (∑ i, s i τ x - μ • u τ x) τ
  hp : ∀ i τ x, HasDerivAt (fun r => p i r x) (q i τ x) τ
  hpx : ∀ i τ x, HasLineDerivAt ℝ (p i τ) (s i τ x) x (b i)
  hvx : ∀ i τ x, HasLineDerivAt ℝ (v τ) (q i τ x) x (b i)
  cu : Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => u z.1 z.2
  cv : Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => v z.1 z.2
  cp : ∀ i, Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => p i z.1 z.2
  cq : ∀ i, Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => q i z.1 z.2
  cs : ∀ i, Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => s i z.1 z.2

declarations.doc: The energy density of the fields.
declarations.statement: def e (τ : ℝ) (x : E) : ℝ

declarations.doc: The time derivative of the energy density.
declarations.statement: def e' (τ : ℝ) (x : E) : ℝ

declarations.statement: lemma hasDerivAt_e (τ : ℝ) (x : E) : HasDerivAt (fun r => D.e r x) (D.e' τ x) τ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.energy_integrand_nonneg
declarations.doc: The pointwise inequality behind the monotonicity of the weighted energy.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_integrand_nonneg {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (m V : ℝ) (hm : 0 ≤ m)
    (wg P G : ι → ℝ) (hP : ∀ i, 0 ≤ P i) (hG : ∀ i, |G i| ≤ V * P i)
    (hgrad : ∑ i, wg i ^ 2 ≤ m ^ 2) :
    0 ≤ m * (V ^ 2 + ∑ i, P i ^ 2) + 2 * ∑ i, wg i * G i

declarations.name: KleinGordon.WeightFields
declarations.doc:
A weight for the energy: smooth, compactly supported in space uniformly in time, decreasing in
time, with a spatial gradient bounded by its time derivative.
declarations.statement:
structure WeightFields {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (b : ι → E) where
  /-- The weight. -/
  w : ℝ → E → ℝ
  /-- Its time derivative. -/
  wτ : ℝ → E → ℝ
  /-- Its derivative along `b i`. -/
  wg : ι → ℝ → E → ℝ
  hw : ∀ τ x, HasDerivAt (fun r => w r x) (wτ τ x) τ
  hwx : ∀ i τ x, HasLineDerivAt ℝ (w τ) (wg i τ x) x (b i)
  cw : Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => w z.1 z.2
  cwτ : Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => wτ z.1 z.2
  cwg : ∀ i, Continuous fun z : ℝ × E => wg i z.1 z.2
  /-- The radius of the common spatial support. -/
  R : ℝ
  hR : ∀ τ x, -1 ≤ τ → R < ‖x‖ → w τ x = 0 ∧ wτ τ x = 0 ∧ ∀ i, wg i τ x = 0
  sign : ∀ τ x, wτ τ x ≤ 0
  grad : ∀ τ x, ∑ i, wg i τ x ^ 2 ≤ wτ τ x ^ 2

modules.title: The spatial Fourier transform of the retarded solution
modules.doc:
The retarded solution at time `t` has the spatial Fourier transform given by the Duhamel integral
of the sine multiplier.

## i. Overview

For a source `f` of compact support the slice of the retarded solution at time `t` is a Schwartz
function in space. Its spatial Fourier transform at the frequency `ξ` is the integral over
earlier times `s` of the sine multiplier `sin(ω (t - s)) / ω` times the Fourier transform of the
source slice at time `s`. Outside the time support of the source the transform obeys the free
oscillator evolution of its value and velocity at the last time of the support.

## ii. Key results

- `fourier_solutionSlice` : the Fourier transform of the retarded slice.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Fourier transform of the retarded slice

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Fourier transform of the retarded slice

- `fourier_solutionSlice` : the Fourier transform of the retarded slice.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourier_solutionSlice_of_le
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform of the retarded slice, when the source vanishes before the time `a`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourier_solutionSlice
declarations.doc:
The Fourier transform of the retarded slice at time `t` is the integral over earlier times of
the sine multiplier times the Fourier transform of the source slice.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_solutionSlice {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    𝓕 (solutionSlice F f hμ t) ξ =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, multiplier (t - s) μ ξ • 𝓕 (slice F f s) ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqSolution_cauchy
declarations.doc:
After the last time of the source the Fourier mode of the retarded solution is the free
oscillator evolution of its value and velocity at that time.
declarations.statement:
lemma freqSolution_cauchy {μ : ℝ} {a T t : ℝ} (hT : ∀ s ≥ T, s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f)
    (hTt : T ≤ t) (ξ : E) :
    freqSolution F f μ a ξ t =
      (Real.cos (dispersion μ ξ * (t - T)) : ℂ) • freqSolution F f μ a ξ T +
        (Real.sincPropagator (t - T) (dispersion μ ξ) : ℂ) • freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ T

modules.title: The free evolution
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The sine and cosine evolution of Schwartz data and its time and space derivatives.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution` : The propagation over the time `t` on Schwartz functions.
- `sineEvolutionTempered` : The propagation over the time `t` on tempered distributions.
- `cosEvolution` : The cosine evolution on Schwartz functions.
- `frequencySqOperator` : The Fourier multiplier `ω²`, i.e.
- `evolveU` : The field `u τ = C τ a + S τ b` evolved from the Cauchy data `(a, b)`.
- `evolveV` : The velocity `v τ = C τ b - ω² S τ a` of the evolved field.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier
- B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law
- C. The free evolution
- D. The free Klein–Gordon evolution as a one-parameter group
- E. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier

- `sineEvolution` : The propagation over the time `t` on Schwartz functions.
- `sineEvolutionTempered` : The propagation over the time `t` on tempered distributions.

Lemmas: `sineEvolutionTempered_coe`.

## B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law

- `cosEvolution` : The cosine evolution on Schwartz functions.
- `frequencySqOperator` : The Fourier multiplier `ω²`, i.e.

## C. The free evolution

Lemmas: `sineEvolution_apply_eq`.

## D. The free Klein–Gordon evolution as a one-parameter group

Lemmas: `sineEvolution_zero`, `cosEvolution_zero`.

## E. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data

- `evolveU` : The field `u τ = C τ a + S τ b` evolved from the Cauchy data `(a, b)`.
- `evolveV` : The velocity `v τ = C τ b - ω² S τ a` of the evolved field.

Lemmas: `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_apply`, `hasDerivAt_cosEvolution_apply`, `hasDerivAt_evolveU`,
`frequencySqOperator_sineEvolution`, `frequencySqOperator_cosEvolution`, `hasDerivAt_evolveV`,
`lineDeriv_evolveU`, `lineDeriv_evolveV`, `frequencySqOperator_eq`,
`continuous_sineEvolution_apply'` and more.

modules.title: Green operators on spacetime
modules.doc:
Retarded and advanced Green operators of the Klein–Gordon equation on `SpaceTime d` for every mass.

## i. Overview

Retarded and advanced Green operators of the Klein–Gordon equation on `SpaceTime d` for every mass.
Uniqueness and the exact sequence follow.

## ii. Key results

- `retardedResponse` : The retarded spatial Fourier response of a compact source on Minkowski
  spacetime.
- `advancedResponse` : The advanced spatial Fourier response of a compact source on Minkowski
  spacetime.
- `testFieldEquiv` : The neighbour's compact smooth fields and Mathlib's bundled test functions have
  the same data.
- `retardedMap` : The retarded Fourier response as a real linear map into the existing smooth-field
  space.
- `advancedMap` : The advanced Fourier response as a real linear map into the existing smooth-field
  space.
- `retardedGreenOperator` : The retarded Fourier Green inverse for the existing Minkowski equation
  in every dimension.
- `advancedGreenOperator` : The advanced Fourier Green inverse for the existing Minkowski equation
  in every dimension.
- `greenOperators` : The spatial Fourier Green pair for Klein–Gordon fields in arbitrary spatial
  dimension.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The spatial Fourier Green construction on Minkowski spacetime
- B. Fourier Klein–Gordon Green operators in every dimension
- C. Real scalar Fourier Green operators
- D. Continuous evaluation of the spacetime Fourier response
- E. Uniqueness for the Fourier Klein–Gordon Green operators

## iv. References

None.

## A. The spatial Fourier Green construction on Minkowski spacetime

- `retardedResponse` : The retarded spatial Fourier response of a compact source on Minkowski
  spacetime.
- `advancedResponse` : The advanced spatial Fourier response of a compact source on Minkowski
  spacetime.

Lemmas: `contDiff_retardedResponse`, `contDiff_advancedResponse`,
`tsupport_retardedResponse_subset`, `tsupport_advancedResponse_subset`,
`retardedResponse_sourceOperator`, `advancedResponse_sourceOperator`.

## B. Fourier Klein–Gordon Green operators in every dimension

- `testFieldEquiv` : The neighbour's compact smooth fields and Mathlib's bundled test functions have
  the same data.
- `retardedMap` : The retarded Fourier response as a real linear map into the existing smooth-field
  space.
- `advancedMap` : The advanced Fourier response as a real linear map into the existing smooth-field
  space.
- `retardedGreenOperator` : The retarded Fourier Green inverse for the existing Minkowski equation
  in every dimension.
- `advancedGreenOperator` : The advanced Fourier Green inverse for the existing Minkowski equation
  in every dimension.
- `greenOperators` : The spatial Fourier Green pair for Klein–Gordon fields in arbitrary spatial
  dimension.

Lemmas: `testFieldEquiv_compactOperator`, `retardedMap_solves`, `advancedMap_solves`.

## C. Real scalar Fourier Green operators

- `fiberIntertwiner` : A constant fibre transformation intertwines the equal-mass Klein–Gordon
  equations.
- `realRetardedGreenOperator` : The real part of the complex retarded response is a real scalar
  Green inverse.
- `realAdvancedGreenOperator` : The real part of the complex advanced response is a real scalar
  Green inverse.
- `realGreenOperators` : The real scalar Klein–Gordon Green pair for transposition in arbitrary
  spatial dimension.

Lemmas: `fiberIntertwiner_compactOperator`.

## D. Continuous evaluation of the spacetime Fourier response

- `retardedEvaluation` : Continuous evaluation of the complex Banach-valued retarded Fourier
  response.
- `advancedEvaluation` : Continuous evaluation of the complex Banach-valued advanced Fourier
  response.
- `realRetardedEvaluation` : Continuous evaluation of the real scalar retarded Green response.
- `realAdvancedEvaluation` : Continuous evaluation of the real scalar advanced Green response.

Lemmas: `retardedEvaluation_apply`, `advancedEvaluation_apply`, `realRetardedEvaluation_apply`,
`realAdvancedEvaluation_apply`.

## E. Uniqueness for the Fourier Klein–Gordon Green operators

- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient` : Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions of the Klein–Gordon
  equation are the compact source classes modulo the equation of motion, in every spatial dimension.

Lemmas: `existsUnique_retardedSolution`, `causalGreen_exactSequence`.

      causalPast (coordinates d '' tsupport f)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.existsUnique_retardedSolution
declarations.doc:
A compact smooth source has exactly one sharply retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon
equation, in every spatial dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_retardedSolution (m : ℝ)
    (f : (equation (d := d) (V := F) m).compactSources) :
    ∃! u : smoothFields d F,
      (equation (V := F) m).operator u = f.val ∧
      tsupport (u : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
        (causalRelation d).causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.causalGreen_exactSequence
declarations.doc:
The causal Green sequence for the Klein–Gordon equation in every spatial dimension:
the equation of motion is injective on compact fields, the causal propagator is exact in the
middle and the equation of motion is surjective on spacelike-compact fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalGreen_exactSequence (m : ℝ) :
    let P := equation (d := d) (V := F) m
    Function.Injective P.compactOperator ∧
      Function.Exact P.compactOperator (greenOperators F m).toSpacelikeCompact ∧
      Function.Exact (greenOperators F m).toSpacelikeCompact
        (P.spacelikeCompactOperator (causalRelation d)) ∧
      Function.Surjective (P.spacelikeCompactOperator (causalRelation d))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.smoothFieldsAddGroup
declarations.doc: Fix the inherited field addition for quotient inference.
declarations.statement: local instance smoothFieldsAddGroup : AddCommGroup (smoothFields d F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.solutionSpaceEquivQuotient
declarations.doc:
Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions of the Klein–Gordon equation are the compact source
classes modulo the equation of motion, in every spatial dimension.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def solutionSpaceEquivQuotient (m : ℝ) :
    let P := equation (d := d) (V := F) m
    P.spacelikeCompactSolution (causalRelation d) ≃ₗ[ℝ]
      (P.compactSources ⧸ LinearMap.range P.compactOperator)

modules.title: The propagation multiplier
modules.doc:
The dispersion relation and the sine and cosine multipliers of the Klein–Gordon evolution.

## i. Overview

The dispersion relation and the sine and cosine multipliers of the Klein–Gordon evolution. They are
smooth and have temperate growth.

## ii. Key results

- `dispersion` : The dispersion `√((2π)² ‖ξ‖² + μ)` of the Klein–Gordon equation with mass parameter
  `μ`.
- `multiplier` : The Fourier multiplier of the propagation over the time `t`.
- `cosMultiplier` : The Fourier multiplier `cos (ω t)`.
- `frequencySq` : The Fourier multiplier `ω² = (2π)² ‖ξ‖² + μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier
- B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law
- C. The propagation multiplier
- D. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data
- E. The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a test-function source
- F. Smoothness of the retarded solution
- G. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Klein–Gordon propagation multiplier

- `dispersion` : The dispersion `√((2π)² ‖ξ‖² + μ)` of the Klein–Gordon equation with mass parameter
  `μ`.
- `multiplier` : The Fourier multiplier of the propagation over the time `t`.

Lemmas: `dispersion_zero`, `norm_multiplier_le`, `multiplier_eq`,
`hasTemperateGrowth_comp_sincSqrt`, `hasTemperateGrowth_comp_cosSqrt`,
`hasTemperateGrowth_multiplier`.

## B. The free Klein–Gordon evolution and its group law

- `cosMultiplier` : The Fourier multiplier `cos (ω t)`.
- `frequencySq` : The Fourier multiplier `ω² = (2π)² ‖ξ‖² + μ`.

Lemmas: `cosMultiplier_eq`, `hasTemperateGrowth_cosMultiplier`, `hasTemperateGrowth_frequencySq`.

## C. The propagation multiplier

Lemmas: `continuous_dispersion`, `continuous_multiplier_uncurry`.

## D. The homogeneous Klein–Gordon evolution of Schwartz data

Lemmas: `continuous_cosMultiplier_uncurry`, `continuous_frequencySq`.

## E. The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a test-function source

Lemmas: `dispersion_sq_le`.

## F. Smoothness of the retarded solution

Lemmas: `contDiff_multiplier_joint`.

## G. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

Lemmas: `multiplier_neg`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.dispersion_zero
declarations.doc: The massless dispersion is the norm of the frequency.
declarations.statement: lemma dispersion_zero (ξ : E) : dispersion 0 ξ = 2 * Real.pi * ‖ξ‖

declarations.doc: The Fourier multiplier of the propagation over the time `t`.
declarations.statement: def multiplier (t μ : ℝ) (ξ : E) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_multiplier_le
declarations.statement: lemma norm_multiplier_le (t μ : ℝ) (ξ : E) : ‖multiplier t μ ξ‖ ≤ |t|

declarations.name: KleinGordon.multiplier_eq
declarations.doc: For `μ ≥ 0` the multiplier is the entire function `t * sincSqrt` of `t² ω²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma multiplier_eq (t : ℝ) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ξ : E) :
    multiplier t μ ξ = ((t * sincSqrt (t ^ 2 * ((2 * π) ^ 2 * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 + μ)) : ℝ) : ℂ)

lemma cosMultiplier_eq (t : ℝ) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ξ : E) :

modules.title: The retarded kernel as a boundary value in the spacetime Fourier variables
modules.doc:
The retarded kernel tested against a test function is the limit of an integral of the spacetime
Fourier transform against `1 / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²)`.

## i. Overview

Time and space are Fourier transformed in this order. The spatial transform of a slice is a
smooth compactly supported function of the time. Fourier inversion in the time writes it as an
integral over the frequency `w` (see `TimeSlice.spaceFourier_eq_integral`). The Laplace transform
of the sine propagation function turns the damped time integral into
`1 / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²)`. The damping is removed by dominated convergence. The result is
the boundary value `ε → 0+` of the resolvent, as a statement about the pairing of the retarded
kernel with a test function.

## ii. Key results

- `dampedKernel_eq` : the damped kernel in the spacetime Fourier variables.
- `tendsto_dampedKernel` : the damping can be removed.
- `tendsto_retardedPointSource` : the retarded kernel is the boundary value of the resolvent.
- `solution_zero_eq_advancedSolution_zero` : off the mass shell the retarded and the advanced
  solution agree at the origin.
- `retardedGreen_eq_advancedGreen_of_avoidsShell` : the causal propagator `E = R - A` vanishes at
  the origin for sources whose transform avoids the mass shell.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The damped kernel
- B. The boundary value
- C. The mass shell

## iv. References

None.

## A. The damped kernel

- `dampedKernel_eq` : the damped kernel in the spacetime Fourier variables.

## B. The boundary value

- `tendsto_dampedKernel` : the damping can be removed.
- `tendsto_retardedPointSource` : the retarded kernel is the boundary value of the resolvent.

## C. The mass shell

- `dampedKernel_zero_eq_of_avoidsShell` : the kernel off the mass shell.
- `solution_zero_eq_advancedSolution_zero` : off the mass shell the retarded and the advanced
  solution agree at the origin.
- `retardedGreen_eq_advancedGreen_of_avoidsShell` : the causal propagator vanishes at the origin
  for sources whose transform avoids the mass shell.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.dampedKernel
declarations.doc: The damped time integral of the sine evolution at the origin.
declarations.statement: def dampedKernel (μ ε : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The sine evolution at the origin is the integral of the multiplier against the transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_zero_eq {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ s μ (slice ℂ ψ s) 0 = ∫ ξ : E, multiplier s μ ξ * spaceFourier ψ ξ s

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrable_dampedIntegrand
declarations.doc: The integrand of the damped kernel is integrable in time and frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_dampedIntegrand {μ : ℝ} (ε : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × E => (Real.exp (-(ε * p.1)) : ℂ) *
      (multiplier p.1 μ p.2 * spaceFourier ψ p.2 p.1))
      ((volume.restrict (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))).prod volume)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.dampedKernel_eq
declarations.doc:
**The damped kernel in the spacetime Fourier variables.** The damped time integral of the
sine evolution at the origin is the integral of the transform against
`1 / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dampedKernel_eq {μ ε : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    dampedKernel μ ε ψ = ∫ ξ : E, ∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier ψ w ξ *
      (1 / ((dispersion μ ξ : ℂ) ^ 2 - (2 * Real.pi * w + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tendsto_dampedKernel
declarations.doc: **The damping can be removed.** The damped kernel converges to the undamped one.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_dampedKernel {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε => dampedKernel μ ε ψ) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (dampedKernel μ 0 ψ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.dampedKernel_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The damped kernel without damping is the advanced solution at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma dampedKernel_zero_eq {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    dampedKernel μ 0 ψ = advancedSolution ℂ ψ μ 0 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The retarded solution at the origin is the undamped kernel of the reflected source.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_zero_eq {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) :
    solution ℂ ψ μ 0 0 = dampedKernel μ 0 (reflect ℂ ψ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.resolvent
declarations.doc: The resolvent of the Klein–Gordon operator at the complexified frequency `2π w + i ε`.
declarations.statement: def resolvent (μ ε w : ℝ) (ξ : E) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.AvoidsShell
declarations.doc: The test function has no Fourier support within `δ` of the mass shell.
declarations.statement: def AvoidsShell (μ δ : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) : Prop

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_mul_resolvent_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_mul_resolvent_le {μ δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)}
    (hχ : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) (hεδ : ε ≤ δ / 2)
    (w : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    ‖timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ ε w ξ‖ ≤ ‖timeFourier χ w ξ‖ * (2 / δ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.measurable_resolvent
declarations.statement: lemma measurable_resolvent (μ ε : ℝ) : Measurable fun p : ℝ × E => resolvent μ ε p.1 p.2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.aestronglyMeasurable_timeFourier_mul_resolvent
declarations.statement:
lemma aestronglyMeasurable_timeFourier_mul_resolvent (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ))
    (μ ε : ℝ) (ξ : E) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun w : ℝ => timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ ε w ξ) volume

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tendsto_integral_resolvent
declarations.doc: Inner dominated convergence: the resolvent integral converges off the mass shell.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_integral_resolvent {μ δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)}
    (hχ : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) (ξ : E) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ ε w ξ)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ 0 w ξ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.aestronglyMeasurable_integral_timeFourier_mul_resolvent
declarations.statement:
lemma aestronglyMeasurable_integral_timeFourier_mul_resolvent
    (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (μ ε : ℝ) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ξ : E => ∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ ε w ξ)
      volume

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_integral_timeFourier_mul_resolvent_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_integral_timeFourier_mul_resolvent_le {μ δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)} (hχ : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) {ε : ℝ} (h1 : 0 ≤ ε) (h2 : ε ≤ 1)
    (h3 : ε ≤ δ / 2) (C : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ ξ : E, ∫ w : ℝ, ‖timeFourier χ w ξ‖ ≤ C * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(n : ℝ))) (ξ : E) :
    ‖∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ ε w ξ‖ ≤
      (2 / δ) * (C * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(n : ℝ)))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.dampedKernel_zero_eq_of_avoidsShell
declarations.doc:
**The kernel off the mass shell.** If the transform of the source vanishes near the mass shell
then the undamped kernel is the integral of the transform against the unregularised resolvent.
declarations.statement:
lemma dampedKernel_zero_eq_of_avoidsShell {μ δ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)} (hχ : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) :
    dampedKernel μ 0 χ = ∫ ξ : E, ∫ w : ℝ, timeFourier χ w ξ * resolvent μ 0 w ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.avoidsShell_reflect
declarations.statement:
lemma avoidsShell_reflect {μ δ : ℝ} {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)} (h : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) :
    AvoidsShell μ δ (reflect ℂ χ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_zero_eq_advancedSolution_zero
declarations.doc:
**The retarded and the advanced solution agree off the mass shell.** If the transform of the
source vanishes within `δ` of the mass shell then the retarded and the advanced solution have the
same value at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_zero_eq_advancedSolution_zero {μ δ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    {χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)} (hχ : AvoidsShell μ δ χ) :
    solution ℂ χ μ 0 0 = advancedSolution ℂ χ μ 0 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedPointSource_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The retarded kernel is the real part of the undamped kernel of the transported source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_zero_eq (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ =
      (dampedKernel (m ^ 2) 0
        (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ))).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.advancedPointSource_zero_eq
declarations.doc: The advanced kernel is the real part of the retarded solution of the transported source.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedPointSource_zero_eq (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    advancedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ =
      (solution ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) (m ^ 2) 0
        0).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.advancedPointSource_eq_retardedPointSource_of_avoidsShell
declarations.doc:
**On the mass shell.** If the spacetime Fourier transform of a test function vanishes within
`δ` of the mass shell then the retarded and the advanced kernel give the same value. So the
Fourier transform of the causal propagator `E = R - A` is supported on the mass shell.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedPointSource_eq_retardedPointSource_of_avoidsShell (m δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (h : AvoidsShell (m ^ 2) δ (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ))) :
    advancedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ = retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.tendsto_retardedPointSource
declarations.doc:
**The retarded kernel is the boundary value of the resolvent.** The retarded kernel tested
against a real test function `φ` is the limit for `ε → 0+` of the integral of the spacetime Fourier
transform of `φ` against `1 / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_retardedPointSource (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => (∫ ξ : Space d, ∫ w : ℝ,
      timeFourier (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) w ξ *
        (1 / ((dispersion (m ^ 2) ξ : ℂ) ^ 2 - (2 * Real.pi * w + ε * Complex.I) ^ 2))).re)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedGreen_eq_advancedGreen_of_avoidsShell
declarations.doc:
**The causal propagator vanishes off the mass shell.** If the Fourier transform of a real
test source vanishes within `δ` of the mass shell then the retarded and the advanced solution
agree at the origin. So `E f = R f - A f` vanishes at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedGreen_eq_advancedGreen_of_avoidsShell (m δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (f : TestField d ℝ)
    (h : AvoidsShell (m ^ 2) δ
      (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM (testFieldEquiv ℝ f)))) :
    ((realRetardedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val 0 =
      ((realAdvancedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val 0

modules.title: The retarded solution as a convolution with the retarded kernel
modules.doc:
The retarded solution at `p` is the retarded kernel tested against the reflected and shifted
source.

## i. Overview

The retarded kernel `K` is the retarded point source at the origin. The point reflection
`x ↦ p - x` reverses time. It is therefore a Poincaré transformation that is not orthochronous.
It maps the retarded point source at the origin to the advanced point source at `p`. The
advanced point source at `p` is the retarded response evaluated at `p`. This gives
`(G_R f)(p) = K (x ↦ f (p - x))`.

## ii. Key results

- `retarded_eq_kernel` : the retarded solution at `p` is the kernel tested against
  `x ↦ f (p - x)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The point reflection
- B. The convolution form

## iv. References

None.

## A. The point reflection


## B. The convolution form

- `retarded_eq_kernel` : the retarded solution at `p` is the kernel tested against
  `x ↦ f (p - x)`.
- `retardedDistribution_apply` : the retarded solution of a compactly supported distribution is
  the distribution tested against the cut off advanced solution.
- `retardedDistribution_delta_apply` : the point source gives the advanced solution at `p`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_eq_kernel
declarations.doc:
**The retarded solution as a convolution.** The retarded solution of a real test source at
`p` is the retarded kernel tested against the source reflected through `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_eq_kernel (p : SpaceTime d) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    ((realRetardedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val p =
      retardedPointSource m 0
        (actTestFunction (pointReflection p)⁻¹ (testFieldEquiv ℝ f))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.actTestFunction_pointReflection_apply
declarations.doc: The reflected source takes the value `f (p - x)` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma actTestFunction_pointReflection_apply (p x : SpaceTime d) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    actTestFunction (pointReflection p)⁻¹ (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) x =
      testFieldEquiv ℝ f (p - x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_apply
declarations.doc:
**Convolution with a compactly supported distribution by transposition.** The retarded
solution of `T` tested against `f` is `T` tested against the advanced solution of `f` cut off by
a function that equals one near the support of `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_apply (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) ℝ) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    retardedDistribution m T (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) =
      T.val (realAdvancedCutoff m (compactCutoff (compactDistributionBound T))
        (testFieldEquiv ℝ f))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.realAdvancedCutoff_compactCutoff_apply
declarations.doc: The cut off advanced solution has the value `χ p * (A f) p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma realAdvancedCutoff_compactCutoff_apply (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) ℝ)
    (f : TestField d ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    realAdvancedCutoff m (compactCutoff (compactDistributionBound T)) (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) p =
      compactCutoff (compactDistributionBound T) p *
        ((realAdvancedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_delta_apply
declarations.doc: For the point source the transposed convolution is the advanced solution at `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_delta_apply (p : SpaceTime d) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    retardedDistribution m (deltaCompact p) (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) =
      ((realAdvancedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f).val p

modules.title: The boundary value formula for compactly supported distributional sources
modules.doc:
The retarded response of a compactly supported distribution is the limit of the responses to its
damped advanced solutions.

## i. Overview

By transposition the retarded response of a compactly supported distribution `T` against a test
function `φ` is `T` applied to the cut off advanced solution of `φ`
(`retardedDistribution_apply`). For `ε > 0` the cut off advanced solution is replaced by
`x ↦ χ x * Re ⟨φ̂ translated by x, resolvent at 2π w + i ε⟩`. This is the cut off damped kernel
centred at `x`, the boundary value pairing of the kernel for the translate of `φ`. It equals the
conjugate `M_ε C M_{-ε} φ` of the cut off advanced solution `C` by the multiplication with
`exp (ε t)`. Finite order of `T` and the estimates for the twist give that the pairings converge
to the response for every compactly supported distribution.

## ii. Key results

- `timeCLM` : the time coordinate.
- `kernel_twist` : the kernel applied to a twisted test function is the damped kernel.
- `twisted_apply_fourier` : the twisted cut off advanced solution is the cut off resolvent
  pairing of the translate.
- `tendsto_distribution_boundary_value` : the boundary value formula for compactly supported
  distributions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The twist in time
- B. The damped kernel centred at a point
- C. Compactly supported distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The twist in time

- `timeCLM` : the time coordinate.
- `slice_twist` : the slices of a twisted test function.
- `kernel_twist` : the kernel applied to a twisted test function is the damped kernel.

## B. The damped kernel centred at a point

- `realAdvancedCutoff_eq` : the cut off advanced solution through the point source.
- `twisted_apply` : the twisted cut off advanced solution is the damped kernel at the translate.
- `twisted_apply_fourier` : the same as a resolvent pairing.

## C. Compactly supported distributions

- `tendsto_distribution_boundary_value` : the boundary value formula.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.timeCLM
declarations.doc: The time coordinate as a continuous linear functional.
declarations.statement: def timeCLM (d : ℕ) : SpaceTime d →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.timeCLM_symm
