declarations.statement: lemma timeCLM_symm (s : ℝ) (x : Space d) : timeCLM d ((coordinates d).symm (s, x)) = s

declarations.name: KleinGordon.slice_twist
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_twist (ε : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) (s : ℝ) :
    slice ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM
      (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) ψ))) s =
      (Real.exp (-(ε * s)) : ℂ) • slice ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ
        (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM ψ)) s

declarations.name: KleinGordon.kernel_twist
declarations.doc: The kernel at the origin applied to a twisted test function is the damped kernel.
declarations.statement:
lemma kernel_twist (m ε : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) ψ) =
      (dampedKernel (m ^ 2) ε
        (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM ψ))).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.realAdvancedCutoff_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma realAdvancedCutoff_eq (m : ℝ) (χ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    realAdvancedCutoff m χ g p = χ p * retardedPointSource m p g

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tsupport_realAdvancedCutoff_subset
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_realAdvancedCutoff_subset (m : ℝ) (χ g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    tsupport ⇑(realAdvancedCutoff m χ g) ⊆ tsupport χ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.precompTranslationCLM_twistCLM
declarations.statement:
lemma precompTranslationCLM_twistCLM (a : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d)
    (g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    precompTranslationCLM p (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) a g) =
      Real.exp (a * timeCLM d p) • ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) a (precompTranslationCLM p g)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.twisted_apply
declarations.doc: **The twisted advanced response is the damped kernel centred at `p`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma twisted_apply (m ε : ℝ) (χ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) ε (realAdvancedCutoff m χ
        (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) φ)) p =
      χ p * (dampedKernel (m ^ 2) ε
        (sourceEquiv ℂ
          (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM (precompTranslationCLM p φ)))).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.twisted_apply_fourier
declarations.doc: For `ε > 0` the twisted advanced response is the cut off resolvent pairing of the translate.
declarations.statement:
lemma twisted_apply_fourier (m : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (χ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) ε (realAdvancedCutoff m χ
        (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) φ)) p =
      χ p * (fourierPairing (m ^ 2) ε (ofTestFunction (precompTranslationCLM p φ))).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.splitSource_translate
declarations.statement:
lemma splitSource_translate (p : SpaceTime d) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    ⇑(splitSource d (ofTestFunction (precompTranslationCLM p φ))) =
      fun v => splitSource d (ofTestFunction φ) (v + (splitEquiv d).symm p)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierPairing_translate
declarations.doc:
**The pairing of a translate in Fourier variables.** The resolvent pairing of the translate of
`φ` by `p` is the integral of the phase `𝐞 ⟨p, ζ⟩` times the transform of `φ` times the
resolvent.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierPairing_translate (μ ε : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    fourierPairing μ ε (ofTestFunction (precompTranslationCLM p φ)) =
      ∫ ζ : SplitSpace d, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ((splitEquiv d).symm p) ζ) : ℂ) *
        (𝓕 (splitSource d (ofTestFunction φ)) ζ * splitResolvent μ ε ζ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.twisted_apply_phase
declarations.doc:
**The twisted advanced response in Fourier variables.** For `ε > 0` it is
`x ↦ χ x * Re ∫ 𝐞 ⟨x, ζ⟩ φ̂ (ζ) / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²) dζ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma twisted_apply_phase (m : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (χ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
    (p : SpaceTime d) :
    ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) ε (realAdvancedCutoff m χ
        (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) φ)) p =
      χ p * (∫ ζ : SplitSpace d, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ((splitEquiv d).symm p) ζ) : ℂ) *
        (𝓕 (splitSource d (ofTestFunction φ)) ζ * splitResolvent (m ^ 2) ε ζ)).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tendsto_distribution_boundary_value
declarations.doc: **The boundary value formula for compactly supported distributional sources.**
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_distribution_boundary_value (m : ℝ) (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) ℝ)
    (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => T.val (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) ε
      (realAdvancedCutoff m (compactCutoff (compactDistributionBound T))
        (ExpTwist.twistCLM (timeCLM d) (-ε) (testFieldEquiv ℝ f)))))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (retardedDistribution m T (testFieldEquiv ℝ f)))

modules.title: The Fourier form of the tempered retarded kernel
modules.doc:
The retarded kernel on Schwartz functions is the boundary value of the resolvent integrated
against the spacetime Fourier transform.

## i. Overview

The pairing of the spacetime Fourier transform with the resolvent at the complexified frequency
`2π w + i ε` is continuous on Schwartz space for each `ε > 0`. The bound is `2 / ε²` times the
`L¹` norm of the transform. For test functions the pairing is the damped kernel. The damped kernel
is bounded by a Schwartz seminorm that does not depend on `ε`. So the pairings converge on all
Schwartz functions to the tempered kernel. No principal value analysis near the mass shell is
needed.

## ii. Key results

- `fourierPairing` : the pairing of the spacetime Fourier transform with the resolvent.
- `norm_fourierPairing_le` : the pairing is bounded by `2 / ε²` times the `L¹` norm of the
  transform.
- `fourierPairing_eq_integral_integral` : the pairing as an iterated integral over `ξ` and `w`.
- `fourierPairing_ofTestFunction` : on test functions the pairing is the damped kernel.
- `exists_abs_dampedKernel_le` : the damped kernel is bounded by a Schwartz seminorm uniformly in
  `ε`.
- `exists_abs_fourierPairing_le` : the same bound on all Schwartz functions.
- `tendsto_fourierPairing` : the tempered kernel is the boundary value `ε → 0+` of the pairing
  for every real Schwartz function.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The split space and the resolvent
- B. The pairing
- C. Test functions
- D. The boundary value on Schwartz space

## iv. References

None.

## A. The split space and the resolvent

- `SplitSpace` : time and space with the Euclidean product norm.

## B. The pairing

- `splitSource` : a real Schwartz function of spacetime as a complex one of the split space.
- `spacetimeFourier` : the spacetime Fourier transform.
- `fourierPairing` : the pairing with the resolvent.
- `continuous_pairingRe` : the pairing is continuous on Schwartz space for each `ε > 0`.

## C. Test functions

- `fourierPairing_ofTestFunction` : on test functions the pairing is the damped kernel.
- `exists_abs_dampedKernel_le` : the uniform bound.

## D. The boundary value on Schwartz space

- `exists_abs_fourierPairing_le` : the uniform bound on Schwartz space by closure.
- `tendsto_fourierPairing` : the boundary value.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.SplitSpace
declarations.doc: Time and space with the Euclidean product norm.
declarations.statement: abbrev SplitSpace (d : ℕ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.splitResolvent
declarations.doc: The resolvent as a function on the split space.
declarations.statement: def splitResolvent (μ ε : ℝ) (p : SplitSpace d) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_splitResolvent_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_splitResolvent_le {μ : ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (p : SplitSpace d) :
    ‖splitResolvent μ ε p‖ ≤ 2 / ε ^ 2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_splitResolvent
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_splitResolvent {μ : ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    Continuous (splitResolvent (d := d) μ ε)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.splitEquiv
declarations.doc: Split space and spacetime are the same vector space.
declarations.statement: def splitEquiv (d : ℕ) : SplitSpace d ≃L[ℝ] SpaceTime d

declarations.name: KleinGordon.splitSource
declarations.doc: A real Schwartz function of spacetime as a complex Schwartz function of the split space.
declarations.statement: def splitSource (d : ℕ) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.splitSource_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma splitSource_apply (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) (p : SplitSpace d) :
    splitSource d φ p = (φ (splitEquiv d p) : ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.spacetimeFourier
declarations.doc: The spacetime Fourier transform of a real Schwartz function.
declarations.statement: def spacetimeFourier (d : ℕ) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.spacetimeFourier_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma spacetimeFourier_apply (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) (p : SplitSpace d) :
    spacetimeFourier d φ p = 𝓕 (splitSource d φ) p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierPairing
declarations.doc: **The pairing of the transform with the resolvent.**
declarations.statement: def fourierPairing (μ ε : ℝ) (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrable_mul_splitResolvent
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_mul_splitResolvent {μ ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (g : 𝓢(SplitSpace d, ℂ)) :
    Integrable fun p : SplitSpace d => g p * splitResolvent μ ε p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.pairingRe
declarations.doc: The real part of the pairing as a real linear functional.
declarations.statement: def pairingRe (μ : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.pairingRe_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma pairingRe_apply (μ : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    pairingRe μ hε φ = (fourierPairing μ ε φ).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_fourierPairing_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_fourierPairing_le {μ ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    ‖fourierPairing μ ε φ‖ ≤ (2 / ε ^ 2) * ∫ p : SplitSpace d, ‖𝓕 (splitSource d φ) p‖

declarations.name: KleinGordon.timeFourier_eq_fourier
declarations.doc: The transform of the transported test function is the transform on split space.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeFourier_eq_fourier (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) (w : ℝ) (ξ : Space d) :
    timeFourier (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) w ξ =
      𝓕 (splitSource d (ofTestFunction φ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (w, ξ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierPairing_eq_integral_integral
declarations.doc: **The pairing as an iterated integral.**
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierPairing_eq_integral_integral {μ ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    fourierPairing μ ε φ = ∫ ξ : Space d, ∫ w : ℝ,
      spacetimeFourier d φ (WithLp.toLp 2 (w, ξ)) * resolvent μ ε w ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourierPairing_ofTestFunction
declarations.doc: **For test functions the pairing is the damped kernel.**
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierPairing_ofTestFunction {m ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    fourierPairing (m ^ 2) ε (ofTestFunction φ) =
      dampedKernel (m ^ 2) ε (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_abs_dampedKernel_le
declarations.doc: **The damped kernel is bounded uniformly in the damping.**
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_abs_dampedKernel_le (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) :
    ∃ (q : Seminorm ℝ 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) (C : ℝ), Continuous q ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → ∀ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ),
        |(dampedKernel (m ^ 2) ε
          (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ))).re| ≤
          C * q (ofTestFunction φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_pairingRe
declarations.doc: The test functions are dense in Schwartz space.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_pairingRe (μ : ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    Continuous fun φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) => (fourierPairing μ ε φ).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_abs_fourierPairing_le
declarations.doc: **The pairing is bounded on all Schwartz functions uniformly in `ε`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_abs_fourierPairing_le (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) :
    ∃ (q : Seminorm ℝ 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) (C : ℝ), Continuous q ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ),
        |(fourierPairing (m ^ 2) ε φ).re| ≤ C * q φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tendsto_fourierPairing
declarations.doc:
**Fourier form of the tempered retarded kernel.** For every real Schwartz function `φ` the
tempered kernel is the limit for `ε → 0+` of the integral of the spacetime Fourier transform of
`φ` against `1 / (ω_ξ² - (2π w + i ε)²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_fourierPairing (m : ℝ) (φ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => (fourierPairing (m ^ 2) ε φ).re) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (temperedKernel d m φ))

modules.title: The boundary value formula for point sources
modules.doc:
The retarded response of a point source at `p` is the boundary value of the resolvent pairing of
the translated test function.

## i. Overview

By transposition the retarded response of a compactly supported distribution `T` tested against `f`
is `T` applied to the advanced solution of `f` (`retardedDistribution_apply`). For a point source
at `p` the advanced solution of `f` at `p` is the retarded kernel applied to the translate of `f`.
The boundary value formula for the kernel (`tendsto_fourierPairing`) then holds for the translate.
This gives the formula for every finite combination of point sources.

## ii. Key results

- `retardedPointSource_eq_kernel_translate` : the point source at `p` is the kernel at the origin
  applied to the translate.
- `tendsto_fourierPairing_translate` : the retarded response of a point source at `p` is the
  boundary value of the resolvent pairing of the translate.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Translation
- B. The boundary value

## iv. References

None.

## A. Translation

- `retardedPointSource_eq_kernel_translate` : the point source at `p` as a translate.

## B. The boundary value

- `tendsto_fourierPairing_translate` : the boundary value for a point source at `p`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.retardedPointSource_eq_kernel_translate
declarations.doc:
The retarded point source at `p` is the retarded kernel at the origin applied to the
translate.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedPointSource_eq_kernel_translate (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    retardedPointSource m p φ =
      retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) (precompTranslationCLM p φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tendsto_fourierPairing_translate
declarations.doc:
**The boundary value formula for a point source.** The retarded response of the point source
at `p` tested against `φ` is the limit for `ε → 0+` of the resolvent pairing of the translate of
`φ`. By transposition this is the response of the distribution `δ_p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_fourierPairing_translate (m : ℝ) (p : SpaceTime d)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ =>
      (fourierPairing (m ^ 2) ε (ofTestFunction (precompTranslationCLM p φ))).re)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (retardedDistribution m (deltaCompact p) φ))

modules.title: A Schwartz bound for the retarded kernel
modules.doc:
The retarded kernel tested against a test function is bounded by a finite number of weighted
derivative bounds of the test function. The bound does not depend on the test function.

## i. Overview

The retarded kernel at the origin applied to `ψ` is the integral over the positive times of the
sine evolution of the slice `ψ(s, ·)` evaluated at the origin. The multiplier of the sine
evolution is bounded by the time. The `L¹` norm of the Fourier transform of the slice is bounded
by Schwartz seminorms of the slice. The seminorms of the slice are bounded by weighted derivative
bounds of `ψ`. The weight in the time makes the time integral converge.

## ii. Key results

- `norm_sineEvolution_zero_le` : the sine evolution at the origin is bounded by the time and the
  `L¹` norm of the Fourier transform.
- `weighted_seminorm_slice_le` : weighted bounds of `ψ` bound the seminorms of its slices.
- `exists_norm_integral_sineEvolution_le` : the bound of the time integral.
- `exists_abs_retardedPointSource_le` : the retarded kernel applied to a test function is bounded
  by weighted derivative bounds of the test function.
- `exists_tempered_extension` : the retarded kernel extends to a continuous linear functional on
  the Schwartz space of spacetime, so it is a tempered distribution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sine evolution at the origin
- B. The slices
- C. The time integral
- D. The retarded kernel
- E. The tempered extension

## iv. References

None.

## A. The sine evolution at the origin

- `norm_sineEvolution_zero_le` : the sine evolution at the origin is bounded by the time and the
  `L¹` norm of the Fourier transform.

## B. The slices

- `weighted_seminorm_slice_le` : weighted bounds of `ψ` bound the seminorms of its slices.

## C. The time integral

- `exists_norm_integral_sineEvolution_le` : the bound of the time integral.

## D. The retarded kernel

- `exists_abs_retardedPointSource_le` : the bound for the retarded kernel.

## E. The tempered extension

- `exists_tempered_extension` : the retarded kernel is a tempered distribution.
- `temperedKernel` : the retarded kernel as a tempered distribution.
- `temperedKernel_unique` : the tempered extension is unique.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_sineEvolution_zero_le
declarations.doc: The sine evolution at the origin is bounded by the time and the `L¹` norm of the transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sineEvolution_zero_le [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (r : ℝ) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (g : 𝓢(E, F)) :
    ‖sineEvolution F r μ g 0‖ ≤ |r| * ∫ ξ : E, ‖𝓕 g ξ‖

declarations.name: KleinGordon.weighted_seminorm_slice_le
declarations.doc:
**Weighted bounds of `ψ` bound the seminorms of its slices.** If `(1 + ‖y‖)^N` times the
derivatives of `ψ` up to the order `N` are bounded by `M`, then the seminorm `(k, p)` of the slice
at the time `s` is at most `M / (1 + |s|)^3` for `k + 3 ≤ N` and `p ≤ N`.
declarations.statement:
lemma weighted_seminorm_slice_le (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) {N k p : ℕ}
    {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : ℝ × E, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ψ y‖ ≤ M)
    (hk : k + 3 ≤ N) (hp : p ≤ N) (s : ℝ) :
    SchwartzMap.seminorm ℂ k p (TimeSlice.slice F ψ s) ≤ M / (1 + |s|) ^ 3

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_norm_integral_sineEvolution_le
declarations.doc:
**The time integral is bounded.** There are an order `N` and a constant `C` such that weighted
bounds of the derivatives of `ψ` by `M` bound the damped time integral of the sine evolution of
the slices at the origin by `C * M`. The bound does not depend on the damping `ε ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_norm_integral_sineEvolution_le {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (C : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ψ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × E)), ℂ)) (M ε : ℝ),
      0 ≤ ε → (∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : ℝ × E, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ψ y‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖∫ s in Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), (Real.exp (-(ε * s)) : ℂ) *
        sineEvolution ℂ s μ (TimeSlice.slice ℂ ψ s) 0‖ ≤ C * M

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_weighted_bound_sourceEquiv
declarations.doc:
Transporting a complexified spacetime test function to time-space coordinates keeps the
weighted derivative bounds up to a constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_weighted_bound_sourceEquiv (d N : ℕ) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) (M : ℝ),
      (∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : SpaceTime d, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n φ y‖ ≤ M) →
      ∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : ℝ × Space d, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N *
        ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (sourceEquiv ℂ (TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) y‖ ≤
          A * M

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_abs_retardedPointSource_le
declarations.doc:
**The retarded kernel is bounded by Schwartz-type seminorms.** There are an order `N` and a
constant `C` such that weighted derivative bounds of a test function by `M` bound the retarded
kernel applied to it by `C * M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_abs_retardedPointSource_le (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (C : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ))
      (M : ℝ), (∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : SpaceTime d, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n φ y‖ ≤ M) →
      |retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ| ≤ C * M

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_seminorm_weighted_le
declarations.doc:
**Weighted bounds from Schwartz seminorms.** There is a continuous seminorm `q` on Schwartz
space such that `q` of a test function bounds its weighted derivatives of order up to `N`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_seminorm_weighted_le (d N : ℕ) :
    ∃ q : Seminorm ℝ 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ), Continuous q ∧
      ∀ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ), ∀ n ≤ N, ∀ y : SpaceTime d,
        (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n φ y‖ ≤ 2 ^ (N + 1) * q (ofTestFunction φ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_tempered_extension
declarations.doc:
**The retarded kernel is a tempered distribution.** The retarded kernel extends to a
continuous linear functional on the Schwartz space of spacetime.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_tempered_extension (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) :
    ∃ T : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ, ∀ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ),
      T (ofTestFunction φ) = retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.tempered_ext
declarations.doc: Two tempered distributions that agree on test functions are equal.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedKernel
declarations.doc: The retarded kernel as a tempered distribution on spacetime.
declarations.statement: def temperedKernel (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedKernel_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma temperedKernel_apply (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ)
    (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    temperedKernel d m (ofTestFunction φ) = retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.temperedKernel_unique
declarations.doc: **The tempered extension is unique.**
declarations.statement:
lemma temperedKernel_unique (d : ℕ) (m : ℝ) {T : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ}
    (h : ∀ φ : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ),
      T (ofTestFunction φ) = retardedPointSource m (0 : SpaceTime d) φ) :
    T = temperedKernel d m

modules.title: The retarded and advanced solution
modules.doc:
The retarded solution of a test function source is the Duhamel integral of the sine evolution.

## i. Overview

The retarded solution of a test function source is the Duhamel integral of the sine evolution. It
solves the equation and is linear in the source.

## ii. Key results

- `sourceHat` : The Fourier transform of the source at the frequency `ξ`, as a function of the time.
- `freqSolution` : The retarded solution at the spatial frequency `ξ`, with zero data at the time
  `a`.
- `freqSolution1` : The time derivative of the per-frequency solution.
- `solution` : The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation with the source `f`.
- `advancedSolution` : The advanced solution: the retarded solution of the time-reflected source,
  reflected back.
- `testOperator` : The Klein–Gordon operator `∂ₜ² - Δ + μ` on compact spacetime test fields.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a test-function source
- B. Causal support of the retarded solution
- C. The two-sided Klein–Gordon inverse on compact test fields

## iv. References

None.

## A. The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a test-function source

- `sourceHat` : The Fourier transform of the source at the frequency `ξ`, as a function of the time.
- `freqSolution` : The retarded solution at the spatial frequency `ξ`, with zero data at the time
  `a`.
- `freqSolution1` : The time derivative of the per-frequency solution.
- `solution` : The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation with the source `f`.

Lemmas: `continuous_sourceHat`, `freqSolution_eq`, `hasDerivAt_freqSolution`,
`hasDerivAt_freqSolution1`, `norm_freqSolution1_le`, `norm_freqSolution_le`,
`continuous_freqSolution_xi`, `continuous_freqSolution1_xi`, `hasDerivAt_solution_time`,
`hasDerivAt_solution_time1` and more.

## B. Causal support of the retarded solution

- `advancedSolution` : The advanced solution: the retarded solution of the time-reflected source,
  reflected back.

Lemmas: `propagatedSlice_eq_sineEvolution`, `advancedSolution_equation`,
`integrableOn_sineEvolution_slice`, `solution_eq_integral`, `solution_add`, `solution_smul`.

## C. The two-sided Klein–Gordon inverse on compact test fields

- `testOperator` : The Klein–Gordon operator `∂ₜ² - Δ + μ` on compact spacetime test fields.

Lemmas: `slice_testOperator`, `testOperator_apply`, `fourier_frequencySqOperator`,
`sourceHat_testOperator`, `freqSolution_testOperator`, `solution_testOperator`,
`solution_equation_at`, `testOperator_reflect`, `advancedSolution_testOperator`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sourceHat
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform of the source at the frequency `ξ`, as a function of the time.
declarations.statement: def sourceHat (ξ : E) (s : ℝ) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_sourceHat
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_sourceHat (ξ : E) : Continuous (sourceHat F f ξ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqSolution
declarations.doc: The retarded solution at the spatial frequency `ξ`, with zero data at the time `a`.
declarations.statement: def freqSolution (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqSolution_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma freqSolution_eq (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) :
    freqSolution F f μ a ξ t = duhamelOsc (dispersion μ ξ) a (sourceHat F f ξ) t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqSolution1
declarations.doc: The time derivative of the per-frequency solution.
declarations.statement: def freqSolution1 (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_freqSolution
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_freqSolution (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (freqSolution F f μ a ξ) (freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ t) t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_freqSolution1
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_freqSolution1 (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ)
      (sourceHat F f ξ t - (dispersion μ ξ ^ 2) • freqSolution F f μ a ξ t) t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_freqSolution1_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_freqSolution1_le {K N : ℝ} (hK : ∀ (ξ : E) s, ‖sourceHat F f ξ s‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-N))
    (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ t‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-N) * |t - a|

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_freqSolution_le
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_freqSolution_le {K N : ℝ} (hK : ∀ (ξ : E) s, ‖sourceHat F f ξ s‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-N))
    (μ a : ℝ) (ξ : E) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖freqSolution F f μ a ξ t‖ ≤ K * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-N) * |t - a| * |t - a|

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_freqSolution_xi
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_freqSolution_xi (μ a t : ℝ) : Continuous fun ξ : E => freqSolution F f μ a ξ
    t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_freqSolution1_xi
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_freqSolution1_xi (μ a t : ℝ) : Continuous fun ξ : E => freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ
    t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_solution_time
declarations.doc: The first time derivative of the Fourier integral of the retarded solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_solution_time {μ : ℝ} (a t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t' => ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • freqSolution F f μ a ξ t')
      (∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ t) t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_solution_time1
declarations.doc: The second time derivative of the Fourier integral: the source minus `ω²` times the solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_solution_time1 {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (a t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t' => ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • freqSolution1 F f μ a ξ t')
      (∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) •
        (sourceHat F f ξ t - (dispersion μ ξ ^ 2) • freqSolution F f μ a ξ t)) t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integral_sourceHat
declarations.doc:
Fourier inversion for the source: the inverse Fourier integral of the Fourier transformed
slice is the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_sourceHat (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    ∫ ξ : E, (𝐞 (inner ℝ ξ x) : ℂ) • sourceHat F f ξ t = f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrable_norm_pow_mul_freqSolution
declarations.doc: The weighted per-frequency solution is integrable in the frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_norm_pow_mul_freqSolution (μ a t : ℝ) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 2) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ξ : E => ‖ξ‖ ^ n * ‖freqSolution F f μ a ξ t‖)
      MeasureTheory.volume

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution
declarations.doc: The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation with the source `f`.
declarations.statement: def solution (μ : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_eq
KleinGordon.solution_equation
declarations.doc: The retarded solution solves the Klein–Gordon equation `(∂ₜ² - Δ + μ) u = f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_equation {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) {a : ℝ}
    (ha : ∀ s ≤ a, s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) {t : ℝ} (hat : a < t) (x : E) :
    deriv (deriv fun τ => solution F f μ τ x) t - Δ (fun y => solution F f μ t y) x +
        μ • solution F f μ t x = f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.propagatedSlice_eq_sineEvolution
declarations.statement:
lemma propagatedSlice_eq_sineEvolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r s : ℝ) (x : E) :
    propagatedSlice F f (fun r ξ => multiplier r μ ξ) r s x =
      sineEvolution F r μ (slice F f s) x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolution
declarations.doc: The advanced solution: the retarded solution of the time-reflected source, reflected back.
declarations.statement: def advancedSolution (μ : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolution_equation
declarations.doc: The advanced solution solves the Klein–Gordon equation `(∂ₜ² - Δ + μ) u = f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedSolution_equation {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    deriv (deriv fun τ => advancedSolution F f μ τ x) t -
      Δ (fun y => advancedSolution F f μ t y) x + μ • advancedSolution F f μ t x = f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrableOn_sineEvolution_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma integrableOn_sineEvolution_slice {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn (fun s => sineEvolution F (t - s) μ (slice F f s) x)
      (Set.Iic t)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_eq_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_eq_integral {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    solution F f μ t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, sineEvolution F (t - s) μ (slice F f s) x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_add
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_add {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (g : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    solution F (f + g) μ t x = solution F f μ t x + solution F g μ t x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_smul {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (c : ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    solution F (c • f) μ t x = c • solution F f μ t x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.testOperator
declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator `∂ₜ² - Δ + μ` on compact spacetime test fields.
declarations.statement: def testOperator (μ : ℝ) : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × E)), F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.slice_testOperator
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_testOperator (μ s : ℝ) :
    slice F (testOperator F f μ) s = slice F (dt F (dt F f)) s +
      frequencySqOperator F μ (slice F f s)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.testOperator_apply
declarations.doc: The compact source operator agrees pointwise with the Klein–Gordon differential expression.
declarations.statement:
lemma testOperator_apply (μ t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    testOperator F f μ (t, x) = deriv (deriv (fun s => f (s, x))) t -
      (Δ (fun y => f (t, y))) x + μ • f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.fourier_frequencySqOperator
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_frequencySqOperator (μ : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, F)) (ξ : E) :
    𝓕 (frequencySqOperator F μ g) ξ = frequencySq μ ξ • 𝓕 g ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sourceHat_testOperator
declarations.doc: The compact test-field operator becomes the forced oscillator operator at each frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma sourceHat_testOperator {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ξ : E) (s : ℝ) :
    sourceHat F (testOperator F f μ) ξ s =
      sourceHat F (dt F (dt F f)) ξ s + dispersion μ ξ ^ 2 • sourceHat F f ξ s

declarations.name: KleinGordon.freqSolution_testOperator
declarations.doc: The retarded Fourier mode recovers a test field with vanishing initial Cauchy data.
declarations.statement:
lemma freqSolution_testOperator {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (ξ : E) (a t : ℝ)
    (ha : a ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) (ha' : a ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport (dt F f)) :
    freqSolution F (testOperator F f μ) μ a ξ t = sourceHat F f ξ t

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_testOperator
declarations.doc:
Applying the retarded Green operator to the Klein–Gordon source of a compact test field
recovers that field.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_testOperator {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    solution F (testOperator F f μ) μ t x = f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_equation_at
declarations.doc: The retarded field solves the sourced equation at every spacetime point.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_equation_at {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    deriv (deriv (fun s => solution F f μ s x)) t -
      (Δ (fun y => solution F f μ t y)) x + μ • solution F f μ t x = f (t, x)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.testOperator_reflect
declarations.doc: Time reflection commutes with the compact Klein–Gordon operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma testOperator_reflect (μ : ℝ) :
    testOperator F (reflect F f) μ = reflect F (testOperator F f μ)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolution_testOperator
declarations.doc:
Applying the advanced Green operator to the Klein–Gordon source of a compact test field
recovers that field.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedSolution_testOperator {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    advancedSolution F (testOperator F f μ) μ t x = f (t, x)

modules.title: Smoothness of the retarded solution
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The retarded solution is jointly smooth in time and space.

## ii. Key results

- `solutionIntegrand` : The integrand of the retarded solution in the variables `(r, ξ)`, at the
  point `p = (t, x)`.
- `solution_eq_integral_solutionIntegrand` : A fixed propagation interval represents the solution
  when its lower source time precedes the support.
- `contDiff_solution` : The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a smooth compactly supported source is
  smooth on spacetime.
- `integrable_solutionIntegrand` : The Fourier integrand is integrable over a bounded propagation
  interval and all frequencies.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smoothness of the retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. Smoothness of the retarded solution

- `solutionIntegrand` : The integrand of the retarded solution in the variables `(r, ξ)`, at the
  point `p = (t, x)`.

Lemmas: `contDiff_solutionIntegrand_joint`, `contDiff_solutionIntegrand_p`,
`norm_iteratedFDeriv_solutionIntegrand_le`, `exists_char_mul_timeDeriv_bound`,
`exists_solutionIntegrand_bound`, `integrable_solutionIntegrand`,
`solution_eq_integral_solutionIntegrand`, `contDiff_integral_solutionIntegrand`,
`contDiff_solution`, `contDiff_advancedSolution`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionIntegrand
declarations.doc: The integrand of the retarded solution in the variables `(r, ξ)`, at the point `p = (t, x)`.
declarations.statement: def solutionIntegrand (μ : ℝ) (p : ℝ × E) (z : ℝ × E) : F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.contDiff_solutionIntegrand_joint
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_solutionIntegrand_joint {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun w : (ℝ × E) × (ℝ × E) => solutionIntegrand F f μ w.1 w.2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.contDiff_solutionIntegrand_p
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_solutionIntegrand_p {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (z : ℝ × E) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ fun p : ℝ × E => solutionIntegrand F f μ p z

declarations.name: KleinGordon.norm_iteratedFDeriv_solutionIntegrand_le
declarations.doc: The Leibniz bound separates the spatial character from the time derivatives of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_solutionIntegrand_le (μ : ℝ) (k : ℕ) (p z : ℝ × E) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun q => solutionIntegrand F f μ q z) p‖ ≤
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (k.choose i : ℝ) * (2 * π * ‖z.2‖) ^ i *
        (|z.1| * ‖iteratedDeriv (k - i) (fun s => 𝓕 (slice F f s) z.2) (p.1 - z.1)‖)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_char_mul_timeDeriv_bound
declarations.doc: Each Leibniz term has arbitrarily rapid frequency decay, uniformly in time.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_char_mul_timeDeriv_bound (i j N : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ξ : E) (s : ℝ),
      (2 * π * ‖ξ‖) ^ i * ‖iteratedDeriv j (fun r => 𝓕 (slice F f r) ξ) s‖ ≤
        C * (1 + ‖ξ‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.exists_solutionIntegrand_bound
declarations.doc: All parameter derivatives have rapid frequency decay on bounded propagation intervals.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_solutionIntegrand_bound (μ : ℝ) (k N : ℕ) (R : ℝ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (p z : ℝ × E), |z.1| ≤ R →
      ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ k (fun q => solutionIntegrand F f μ q z) p‖ ≤
        C * (1 + ‖z.2‖) ^ (-(N : ℝ))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrable_solutionIntegrand
declarations.doc: The Fourier integrand is integrable over a bounded propagation interval and all frequencies.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_solutionIntegrand {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (R : ℝ) (p : ℝ × E) :
    Integrable (solutionIntegrand F f μ p)
      ((volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 R)).prod volume)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_eq_integral_solutionIntegrand
declarations.doc:
A fixed propagation interval represents the solution when its lower source time precedes
the support.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_eq_integral_solutionIntegrand {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R)
    {a : ℝ} (ha : ∀ s ≤ a, s ∉ Prod.fst '' tsupport f) (p : ℝ × E) (hp : p.1 - R ≤ a) :
    solution F f μ p.1 p.2 = ∫ z : ℝ × E, solutionIntegrand F f μ p z
      ∂((volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 R)).prod volume)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.contDiff_integral_solutionIntegrand
declarations.doc: Integrating over a fixed bounded propagation interval gives a smooth spacetime field.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_integral_solutionIntegrand {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (R : ℝ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × E => ∫ z : ℝ × E, solutionIntegrand F f μ p z
      ∂((volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 R)).prod volume))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.contDiff_solution
declarations.doc:
The retarded Klein–Gordon solution of a smooth compactly supported source is smooth on
spacetime.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_solution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × E => solution F f μ p.1 p.2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.contDiff_advancedSolution
declarations.doc: The advanced Klein–Gordon solution is smooth on spacetime.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_advancedSolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun p : ℝ × E => advancedSolution F f μ p.1 p.2)

modules.title: Smooth sources as distributions
modules.doc:
The retarded solution of a smooth source and the distributional retarded solution agree.

## i. Overview

A smooth function is a distribution by integration against test functions. The weak derivative of
the induced distribution is the induced distribution of the derivative. The Klein–Gordon operator
on the induced distribution is the induced distribution of the smooth operator. So the retarded
solution of the distribution induced by a test field is the distribution induced by the smooth
retarded solution.

## ii. Key results

- `lineDerivCLM_lineDerivCLM_ofFun` : the second weak derivative.
- `distributionOperator_ofFun` : the Klein–Gordon operator on the distribution of a smooth field.
- `ofFun_mem_compactDistributions` : the distribution of a test field has compact support.
- `retardedDistribution_ofFun` : the retarded solution of the distribution of a test field is the
  distribution of the smooth retarded solution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Weak derivatives
- B. The Klein–Gordon operator
- C. Compact support
- D. The retarded solution

## iv. References

None.

## A. Weak derivatives

- `lineDerivCLM_lineDerivCLM_ofFun` : the second weak derivative of a smooth function.

## B. The Klein–Gordon operator

- `distributionOperator_ofFun` : the Klein–Gordon operator on the distribution of a smooth field.

## C. Compact support

- `ofFun_mem_compactDistributions` : the distribution of a test field has compact support.

## D. The retarded solution

- `retardedDistribution_ofFun` : the retarded solution of the distribution of a test field is the
  distribution of the smooth retarded solution.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.lineDerivCLM_lineDerivCLM_ofFun
declarations.doc: The weak derivative of the second order of a smooth function.
declarations.statement:
lemma lineDerivCLM_lineDerivCLM_ofFun {u : SpaceTime d → V} (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    Distribution.lineDerivCLM (n := ⊤) (k := ⊤) (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)
        (Distribution.lineDerivCLM (n := ⊤) (k := ⊤) (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)
          (Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)) u volume ⊤)) =
      Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d))
        (SpaceTime.deriv μ (SpaceTime.deriv μ u)) volume ⊤

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.distributionOperator_ofFun
declarations.doc:
**The Klein–Gordon operator on a smooth field.** The operator on the distribution induced by a
smooth field is the distribution induced by the smooth operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma distributionOperator_ofFun (m : ℝ) (u : smoothFields d V) :
    distributionOperator m (Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)) u.val volume ⊤) =
      Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)) (operator m u).val volume ⊤

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.ofFun_mem_compactDistributions
declarations.doc: The distribution induced by a test field has compact support.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFun_mem_compactDistributions (f : TestField d V) :
    Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)) (f.val : SpaceTime d → V) volume ⊤ ∈
      compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.retardedDistribution_ofFun
declarations.doc:
**Smooth sources.** The retarded solution of the distribution induced by a test field is the
distribution induced by the smooth retarded solution. This is the one Green operator realised on
test fields, on compactly supported distributions and on smooth fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_ofFun {F : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F]
    [CompleteSpace F] (m : ℝ) (f : TestField d F) :
    Solution.retardedDistribution m ⟨Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d))
        (f.val : SpaceTime d → F) volume ⊤, ofFun_mem_compactDistributions f⟩ =
      Distribution.ofFun (⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d))
        ((Solution.retarded F m f).val : SpaceTime d → F) volume ⊤

modules.title: Klein–Gordon fields and causal propagation
modules.doc:
A disturbance of a relativistic field spreads inside the light cone. This file states how the
Klein–Gordon equation describes this, for massless and massive fields in every spatial dimension.

## i. Overview

Time and space are measured in units with the speed of light equal to one. For a source `f` of
compact support the file solves `(∂ₜ² - Δ + m²) u = f` on `SpaceTime d`. The mass parameter `m`
is any real number. The source and the solution are smooth fields with values in a normed space.
Sources may also be distributions of compact support.

The retarded solution is supported in the causal future of the source. The advanced solution is
supported in the causal past. Their difference is the causal propagator. It solves the equation
without source. Every homogeneous solution with spacelike compact support arises this way.

## ii. Key results

- `existsUnique_retarded` : a compact source has exactly one solution with support in the causal
  future of the source.
- `exact_sequence` : compact sources, the equation of motion and the causal propagator form an
  exact sequence.
- `solutionsEquivQuotient` : spacelike compact solutions are the compact sources modulo the
  equation of motion.
- `retardedDistribution_unique` : the same uniqueness for distributional sources.
- `pointSource_solves` and `pointSource_reciprocity` : the point source solves the equation with a
  delta source, and the retarded kernel seen from `p` is the advanced solution at `p`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The problem
- B. The Fourier picture
- C. Smooth sources
- D. Distributional sources
- E. Tempered slices
- F. Not proved here

## iv. References

None.

## A. The problem

Given a source `f` of compact support, find a field `u` with `(∂ₜ² - Δ + m²) u = f`. The operator
is `operator m`. A source is a smooth field of compact support, `TestField d F`. A distributional
source is a compactly supported distribution, `compactDistributions`. A solution is a smooth
field, `smoothFields d F`, or a distribution, `DistributionField d V`.

## B. The Fourier picture

Transform in space. Put `f̂(s, ξ) = ∫ e^(-2πi x·ξ) f(s, x) dx` and `ω(ξ) = √(4π²‖ξ‖² + m²)`.
Each Fourier mode obeys the forced oscillator equation `û'' + ω² û = f̂`. Its solutions use the
kernel `sin(ω r) / ω`. This is `sincPropagator ω`. It equals `r` at `ω = 0`.

* The retarded solution is `û(t, ξ) = ∫_{s ≤ t} sin(ω (t - s)) / ω · f̂(s, ξ) ds`.
  Every cause comes before its effect.
* The advanced solution is `û(t, ξ) = ∫_{s ≥ t} sin(ω (s - t)) / ω · f̂(s, ξ) ds`.
  Every effect comes before its cause.
* The difference is the causal propagator `E`. It is
  `û(t, ξ) = ∫ sin(ω (t - s)) / ω · f̂(s, ξ) ds` over all times.

## C. Smooth sources

The results `retarded_solves`, `retarded_support` and `retarded_formula` describe the retarded
solution. The same results hold for the advanced solution. The causal propagator `E` solves the
equation without source and is supported in the causal future and past of the source. The sequence
`0 → D → D → Sol → 0` is exact. `D` is the space of compact sources. The first map is the
operator. The second map is `E`. `Sol` is the space of homogeneous solutions with spacelike
compact support.

## D. Distributional sources

Compactly supported distributions have retarded and advanced solutions with the same properties.
The point source at `p` is the retarded solution of a delta distribution. Reciprocity holds. The
retarded kernel seen from `p` and tested on `φ` is the advanced solution of `φ` at `p`.

## E. Tempered slices

At each time the solution is a tempered distribution in space. `fourier_sineEvolution` gives its
Fourier transform. `retarded_slice_pairing` gives its pairing with Schwartz functions.

## F. Not proved here

The Fourier transform in time and space, the convolution form `u = K * f` and closed expressions
for the kernel `K` in a given dimension are not proved here.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded
declarations.doc: The retarded solution of `operator m u = f`.
declarations.statement: abbrev retarded : TestField d F →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced
declarations.doc: The advanced solution of `operator m u = f`.
declarations.statement: abbrev advanced : TestField d F →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d F

declarations.doc: Smooth fields form an additive group, needed to form the quotient.
declarations.statement: local instance : AddCommGroup (smoothFields d F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_solves
declarations.doc: The retarded solution solves the equation.
declarations.statement: lemma retarded_solves (f : TestField d F) : operator m (retarded F m f) = f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced_solves
declarations.doc: The advanced solution solves the equation.
declarations.statement: lemma advanced_solves (f : TestField d F) : operator m (advanced F m f) = f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_support
declarations.doc: The retarded solution vanishes outside the causal future of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_support (f : TestField d F) :
    tsupport (retarded F m f : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
      (causalRelation d).causalFuture (tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced_support
declarations.doc: The advanced solution vanishes outside the causal past of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma advanced_support (f : TestField d F) :
    tsupport (advanced F m f : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
      (causalRelation d).causalPast (tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_formula
declarations.doc:
The retarded solution in time and space coordinates. At time `t` and position `x` it adds
the sine evolution of the source slice at every earlier time `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_formula (f : TestField d F) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    (retarded F m f : SpaceTime d → F) p = ∫ s in Set.Iic (coordinates d p).1,
      sineEvolution F ((coordinates d p).1 - s) (m ^ 2)
        (slice F (sourceEquiv F (testFieldEquiv F f)) s) (coordinates d p).2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advanced_formula
declarations.doc:
The advanced solution in time and space coordinates. It adds the sine evolution of the
source slice at every later time.
declarations.statement:
lemma advanced_formula (f : TestField d F) (p : SpaceTime d) :
    (advanced F m f : SpaceTime d → F) p = ∫ s in Set.Ioi (coordinates d p).1,
      sineEvolution F (s - (coordinates d p).1) (m ^ 2)
        (slice F (sourceEquiv F (testFieldEquiv F f)) s) (coordinates d p).2

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator
declarations.doc: The causal propagator `E`: the retarded minus the advanced solution.
declarations.statement: abbrev propagator : TestField d F →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d F

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_eq
declarations.doc: The causal propagator is the retarded minus the advanced solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagator_eq (f : TestField d F) :
    propagator F m f = retarded F m f - advanced F m f

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_solves
declarations.doc: The causal propagator solves the equation without source.
declarations.statement: lemma propagator_solves (f : TestField d F) : operator m (propagator F m f) = 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_support
declarations.doc: The causal propagator is supported in the causal future and past of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagator_support (f : TestField d F) :
    tsupport (propagator F m f : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
      (causalRelation d).causalHull (tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.propagator_operator
declarations.doc: The causal propagator kills every source that is an equation of motion.
declarations.statement:
lemma propagator_operator (f : TestField d F) :
    propagator F m (compactOperator (equation m) f) = 0

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.existsUnique_retarded
declarations.doc: A source has exactly one solution with support in the causal future of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_retarded (f : TestField d F) :
    ∃! u : smoothFields d F, operator m u = f ∧
      tsupport (u : SpaceTime d → F) ⊆
        (causalRelation d).causalFuture (tsupport (f : SpaceTime d → F))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.exact_sequence
declarations.doc:
Compact sources, the equation of motion and the retarded minus advanced solution form an
exact sequence ending in the spacelike compact fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma exact_sequence :
    let P := equation (d := d) (V := F) m
    Function.Injective P.compactOperator ∧
      Function.Exact P.compactOperator (greenOperators F m).toSpacelikeCompact ∧
      Function.Exact (greenOperators F m).toSpacelikeCompact
        (P.spacelikeCompactOperator (causalRelation d)) ∧
      Function.Surjective (P.spacelikeCompactOperator (causalRelation d))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.solutionsEquivQuotient
declarations.doc: Spacelike compact solutions are the compact sources modulo the equation of motion.
declarations.statement:
def solutionsEquivQuotient :
    let P := equation (d := d) (V := F) m
    P.spacelikeCompactSolution (causalRelation d) ≃ₗ[ℝ]
      (P.compactSources ⧸ LinearMap.range P.compactOperator)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution
declarations.doc: The retarded solution for a compactly supported distribution.
declarations.statement: abbrev retardedDistribution (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) : DistributionField d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedDistribution
declarations.doc: The advanced solution for a compactly supported distribution.
declarations.statement: abbrev advancedDistribution (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) : DistributionField d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_solves
declarations.doc: The retarded solution of a distribution solves the equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_solves (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    distributionOperator m (retardedDistribution m T) = T

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedDistribution_solves
declarations.doc: The advanced solution of a distribution solves the equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedDistribution_solves (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    distributionOperator m (advancedDistribution m T) = T

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_support
declarations.doc: The retarded solution vanishes outside the causal future of the support of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_support (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    IsVanishingOn (retardedDistribution m T)
      ((causalRelation d).causalFuture (compactDistributionBound T))ᶜ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.advancedDistribution_support
declarations.doc: The advanced solution vanishes outside the causal past of the support of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedDistribution_support (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    IsVanishingOn (advancedDistribution m T)
      ((causalRelation d).causalPast (compactDistributionBound T))ᶜ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_unique
declarations.doc:
A distribution solution supported in the causal future of a compact set is the retarded
solution.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_unique (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V)
    (u : DistributionField d V) {K : Set (SpaceTime d)} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hu : IsVanishingOn u ((causalRelation d).causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hT : distributionOperator m u = T) : u = retardedDistribution m T

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retardedDistribution_inverse
declarations.doc: Solving and then applying the operator returns the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedDistribution_inverse (T : compactDistributions (SpaceTime d) V) :
    retardedDistribution m (compactDistributionOperator m T) = T

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.pointSource
declarations.doc: The point source at `p`: the retarded solution of a delta distribution.
declarations.statement: abbrev pointSource (p : SpaceTime d)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.pointSource_solves
declarations.doc: The point source solves the equation with the delta distribution at `p` as source.
declarations.statement:
lemma pointSource_solves (p : SpaceTime d) :
    distributionOperator m (pointSource (m := m) p) = Distribution.delta p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.pointSource_support
declarations.doc: The point source vanishes outside the causal future of `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pointSource_support (p : SpaceTime d) :
    IsVanishingOn (pointSource (m := m) p) ((causalRelation d).causalFuture {p})ᶜ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.pointSource_reciprocity
declarations.doc:
Reciprocity. The retarded kernel seen from `p` and tested on `f` is the advanced solution for
`f`, evaluated at `p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pointSource_reciprocity (p : SpaceTime d) (f : TestField d ℝ) :
    pointSource (m := m) p (testFieldEquiv ℝ f) =
      ((realAdvancedGreenOperator m).toLinearMap f : SpaceTime d → ℝ) p

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.pointSource_apply
declarations.doc:
The point source at `p` applied to a test function `φ`. It integrates the sine evolution of
the delta distribution at the position of `p` against the slices of `φ` over later times.
declarations.statement:
lemma pointSource_apply (p : SpaceTime d) (φ : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (SpaceTime d)), ℝ)) :
    pointSource (m := m) p φ =
      (∫ s in Set.Ioi (coordinates d p).1,
        KleinGordon.sineEvolutionTempered ℂ (s - (coordinates d p).1) (m ^ 2)
          (TemperedDistribution.delta (coordinates d p).2)
          (slice ℂ (sourceEquiv ℂ (_root_.TestFunction.postcompCLM Complex.ofRealCLM φ)) s)).re

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.fourier_sineEvolution
declarations.doc: In Fourier space the sine evolution multiplies by `sin(ω r) / ω`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_sineEvolution {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, F)) (ξ : E) :
    𝓕 (sineEvolution F r μ g) ξ = (Real.sincPropagator r (dispersion μ ξ) : ℂ) • 𝓕 g ξ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Solution.retarded_slice_pairing
declarations.doc:
At time `t` the retarded solution is a tempered distribution in space. Tested against a
Schwartz function it is the integral over earlier times `s` of the sine evolution of the source
slice at time `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma retarded_slice_pairing {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    (solutionSlice F f hμ t : 𝓢'(E, F)) g =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, sineEvolutionTempered F (t - s) μ (slice F f s : 𝓢'(E, F)) g

modules.title: The solution as a tempered distribution in space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

At each time the retarded solution pairs with Schwartz functions through the sine evolution of the
source slices.

## ii. Key results

- `solutionSlice` : The spatial slice of the retarded solution as a Schwartz function.
- `solutionSlice_pairing` : **The retarded solution as a tempered distribution.** Tested against a
  Schwartz function `g` the spatial slice of the retarded solution at the time `t` is the integral
  over the source time `s ≤ t` of the Fourier multiplier `sincPropagator (t - s)` applied to the
  tempered slice of the source.
- `advancedSolution_eq_dirac` : **Advanced response at a point.** The advanced solution at the point
  `(t, y)` is the integral over the later source times of the pairing of the propagated Dirac
  distribution at `y` with the slice of the source.
- `sineEvolution_apply_eq_delta` : The propagation of a Schwartz function at a point is the pairing
  of the propagated Dirac distribution with it.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

## iv. References

None.

## A. The retarded solution as a tempered distribution in space

- `solutionSlice` : The spatial slice of the retarded solution as a Schwartz function.

Lemmas: `hasCompactSupport_solution_slice`, `solutionSlice_apply`, `integrable_pairing_integrand`,
`solutionSlice_pairing`, `sineEvolution_apply_eq_delta`, `advancedSolution_eq_integral`,
`advancedSolution_eq_dirac`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasCompactSupport_solution_slice
declarations.doc: The spatial slice of the retarded solution has compact support.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasCompactSupport_solution_slice {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) :
    HasCompactSupport fun x : E => solution F f μ t x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionSlice
declarations.doc: The spatial slice of the retarded solution as a Schwartz function.
declarations.statement: def solutionSlice {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) : 𝓢(E, F)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionSlice_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma solutionSlice_apply {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
    solutionSlice F f hμ t x = solution F f μ t x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.integrable_pairing_integrand
declarations.doc: The integrand of the Duhamel pairing is integrable on the product of space and past times.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_pairing_integrand {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    Integrable (fun q : E × ℝ => g q.1 • sineEvolution F (t - q.2) μ (slice F f q.2) q.1)
      ((volume : Measure E).prod (volume.restrict (Set.Iic t)))

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solutionSlice_pairing
declarations.doc:
**The retarded solution as a tempered distribution.** Tested against a Schwartz function `g`
the spatial slice of the retarded solution at the time `t` is the integral over the source time
`s ≤ t` of the Fourier multiplier `sincPropagator (t - s)` applied to the tempered slice of the
source.
declarations.statement:
lemma solutionSlice_pairing {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    (solutionSlice F f hμ t : 𝓢'(E, F)) g =
      ∫ s in Set.Iic t, sineEvolutionTempered F (t - s) μ (slice F f s : 𝓢'(E, F)) g

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_apply_eq_delta
declarations.doc:
The propagation of a Schwartz function at a point is the pairing of the propagated Dirac
distribution with it.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_apply_eq_delta {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (r : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (y : E) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r μ g y =
      sineEvolutionTempered ℂ r μ (TemperedDistribution.delta y) g

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolution_eq_integral
declarations.doc: The advanced solution is the integral over the later source times.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedSolution_eq_integral {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (t : ℝ) (y : E) :
    advancedSolution F f μ t y =
      ∫ s in Set.Ioi t, sineEvolution F (s - t) μ (slice F f s) y

declarations.name: KleinGordon.advancedSolution_eq_dirac
declarations.doc:
**Advanced response at a point.** The advanced solution at the point `(t, y)` is the integral
over the later source times of the pairing of the propagated Dirac distribution at `y` with the
slice of the source. By transposition this is the retarded response of a point source.
declarations.statement:
lemma advancedSolution_eq_dirac {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (f : 𝓓((⊤ : Opens (ℝ × D)), ℂ))
    (t : ℝ) (y : D) :
    advancedSolution ℂ f μ t y =
      ∫ s in Set.Ioi t, sineEvolutionTempered ℂ (s - t) μ (TemperedDistribution.delta y)
        (slice ℂ f s)

modules.title: Local action functionals
modules.doc:
The local action of a field, its value under admissible variations, and critical fields.

## i. Overview

This module defines the local action functional associated with a local Lagrangian, together with
the first notions needed to talk about variational criticality.

For the first implementation pass, the action is defined directly as the integral of a local
Lagrangian evaluated along jets of a field. The integrability conditions needed for this action and
for its variations are kept explicit in the API.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionDensity` : the density associated with a field.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.action` : the action of a field.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasFiniteAction` : finiteness of the action integral.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsAdmissibleForAction` : symmetric admissibility of a lagrangian and
  field pair for the action functional.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionVariation` : the action under an admissible variation.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsCritical` : vanishing first derivative of the varied action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Action densities and action
- B. Action under variation
- C. Critical fields

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics, Chapter 5.
  [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

sections.text: ## A. Action densities and action
## B. Action under variation
## C. Critical fields

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionDensity
declarations.doc: The action density determined by a local Lagrangian and a field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionDensity (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasFiniteAction
declarations.doc: The integrability condition for the action density of a field.
declarations.statement: def HasFiniteAction (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsAdmissibleForAction
declarations.doc:
Symmetric admissibility predicate for the action functional: the pair `(L, f)` is admissible
when the field is smooth and the corresponding action density is integrable.
declarations.statement:
def IsAdmissibleForAction (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.action
declarations.doc: The action associated with a local Lagrangian.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def action (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionDensity_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma actionDensity_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    actionDensity L f x = L (jetAt k f x)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.action_eq_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma action_eq_integral (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    action L f = ∫ x, actionDensity L f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.variedField
declarations.doc: The field obtained by varying `f` in the direction `η` with parameter `s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def variedField (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (s : ℝ) :
    Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.variedField_contDiff
declarations.doc: Smoothness of the varied field for smooth `f` and admissible `η`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variedField_contDiff (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (s : ℝ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (variedField f η s)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionVariation
declarations.doc: The action of a field under an admissible variation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionVariation (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) : ℝ → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasFiniteActionVariation
declarations.doc: Explicit integrability condition for the family of varied action densities.
declarations.statement:
def HasFiniteActionVariation (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference
declarations.doc:
Locality package for the action density under compactly supported variations: for every
variation parameter `s`, the change in the action density is a continuous compactly supported
function. Combined with finiteness of the base action, this implies finiteness of the varied
action.

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.hasFiniteActionVariation_of_hasFiniteAction_of_compactlySupportedDifference
declarations.doc:
If the base action is finite and every varied action density differs from the base density by
a continuous compactly supported function, then the whole varied family has finite action.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFiniteActionVariation_of_hasFiniteAction_of_compactlySupportedDifference
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (hbase : HasFiniteAction L f)
    (hdiff : HasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference L f η) :
    HasFiniteActionVariation L f η

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.variedField_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma variedField_apply (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) (s : ℝ)
    (x : Space d) :
    variedField f η s x = f x + s • η x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionVariation_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma actionVariation_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) (s : ℝ) :
    actionVariation L f η s = action L (variedField f η s)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_variedField_eq_of_notMem_tsupport
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_variedField_eq_of_notMem_tsupport
    (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) (s : ℝ)
    {x : Space d}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hx : x ∉ tsupport η.toFun) :
    jetAt k (variedField f η s) x = jetAt k f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.actionDensity_variedField_eq_of_notMem_tsupport
declarations.statement:
lemma actionDensity_variedField_eq_of_notMem_tsupport
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)))
    (s : ℝ)
    {x : Space d} (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hx : x ∉ tsupport η.toFun) :
    actionDensity L (variedField f η s) x = actionDensity L f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.hasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference_of_continuousInCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma hasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference_of_continuousInCoordinates
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (hcontL : Lagrangian.ContinuousInCoordinates L)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f)
    (η : AdmissibleVariation d (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))) :
    HasCompactlySupportedActionVariationDifference L f η

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsCritical
declarations.doc:
A field is critical for a local action if every admissible compactly supported variation has
vanishing first derivative at `s = 0`, under the explicit finite-action hypothesis for the varied
family.
declarations.statement: def IsCritical (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

modules.title: Local Euler-Lagrange operators
modules.doc:
The local Euler-Lagrange operator of a local Lagrangian, built componentwise.

## i. Overview

This module defines the local Euler-Lagrange operator associated with a local Lagrangian.

In the first implementation pass, the derivatives of the Lagrangian with respect to the jet
coordinates are packaged explicitly as part of the local Lagrangian data. This keeps the formula
close to the one in the book while avoiding a premature smooth structure on `JetPoint`.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeTerm` : a single summand in the local
  Euler-Lagrange formula.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeComponent` : one component `E_a(L)` of the operator.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeOp` : the full local Euler-Lagrange operator.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Euler-Lagrange summands
- B. Components of the Euler-Lagrange operator
- C. The full operator

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics, Chapter 5.
  [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

sections.text: ## A. Euler-Lagrange summands
## B. Components of the Euler-Lagrange operator
## C. The full operator

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeTerm
declarations.doc: The summand `(-1)^|I| D_I (∂L/∂u^a_I)` in the local Euler-Lagrange formula.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eulerLagrangeTerm (L : Lagrangian d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeTerm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeTerm_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    eulerLagrangeTerm L I a f x =
      (-1 : ℝ) ^ I.1.order * iteratedTotalDerivative k I.1 (L.coordDeriv I a) f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeComponent
declarations.doc: The `a`-th component of the local Euler-Lagrange operator.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eulerLagrangeComponent (L : Lagrangian d m k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeComponent_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeComponent_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (a : Fin m)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    eulerLagrangeComponent L a f x = ∑ I : DerivativeIndex d k, eulerLagrangeTerm L I a f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeOp
declarations.doc: The local Euler-Lagrange operator attached to a local Lagrangian.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def eulerLagrangeOp (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeOp_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) (a : Fin m) :
    eulerLagrangeOp L f x a = eulerLagrangeComponent L a f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.eulerLagrangeOp_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp L f = fun x => WithLp.toLp 2 fun a => eulerLagrangeComponent L a f x

modules.title: Local Euler-Lagrange equations
modules.doc:
A named predicate for the local Euler-Lagrange equations and the criticality criteria using it.

## i. Overview

This module gives a named predicate for fields satisfying the local Euler-Lagrange equations.

The equation itself is still the existing local coordinate equation

`eulerLagrangeOp L f = 0`.

The purpose of this file is only to expose that condition as a reusable API point and to restate
the already-proved criticality criteria using this named predicate. It does not introduce a new
Euler-Lagrange operator or any new analytic hypotheses.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.SatisfiesEulerLagrange`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.
  isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_contDiff_and_smoothInCoordinates`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.
  isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_admissibleForAction_and_smoothInCoordinates`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Euler-Lagrange equation predicate
- B. Criticality criteria

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics,
  arXiv:1612.03100v2, Chapter 5, Theorem 5.2. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

sections.text: ## A. Euler-Lagrange equation predicate
## B. Criticality criteria

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.SatisfiesEulerLagrange
declarations.doc:
A field satisfies the local Euler-Lagrange equations for a local lagrangian when the
Euler-Lagrange operator vanishes along that field.
declarations.statement:
def SatisfiesEulerLagrange (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.satisfiesEulerLagrange_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma satisfiesEulerLagrange_iff (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    SatisfiesEulerLagrange L f ↔ eulerLagrangeOp L f = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.SatisfiesEulerLagrange.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma SatisfiesEulerLagrange.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero
    {L : Lagrangian d m k} {f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)}
    (h : SatisfiesEulerLagrange L f) :
    eulerLagrangeOp L f = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.SatisfiesEulerLagrange.of_eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma SatisfiesEulerLagrange.of_eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero
    {L : Lagrangian d m k} {f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)}
    (h : eulerLagrangeOp L f = 0) :
    SatisfiesEulerLagrange L f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_contDiff_and_smoothInCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_contDiff_and_smoothInCoordinates
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f)
    (hL : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates L)
    (hbase : HasFiniteAction L f) :
    IsCritical L f ↔ SatisfiesEulerLagrange L f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_admissibleForAction_and_smoothInCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_iff_satisfiesEulerLagrange_of_admissibleForAction_and_smoothInCoordinates
    (L : Lagrangian d m k) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hLf : IsAdmissibleForAction L f)
    (hL : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates L) :
    IsCritical L f ↔ SatisfiesEulerLagrange L f

modules.title: First-order local field theory
modules.doc:
Aliases and projections specializing the local field theory API to first-order jets.

## i. Overview

This module provides a thin usability layer for first-order local field theory, i.e. the
specialization of the local CFT stack to `k = 1`.

The definitions here do not introduce a new theory. They are aliases and projections for the
existing coordinate-readout stack:

- first-order jet points are `JetPoint d m 1`,
- first-order lagrangians are `Lagrangian d m 1`,
- field values are still the zero-order jet coordinates,
- first derivatives are the coordinates indexed by `MultiIndex.increment 0 i`.

This keeps the general finite-order API as the source of truth while making the common first-order
case easier to state in examples and later mechanics bridges.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.FirstOrderJetPoint`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.FirstOrderLagrangian`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.firstDerivativeIndex`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.firstDerivCoord`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.firstOrderJetAt`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. First-order aliases
- B. First derivative indices
- C. First-order jet projections
- D. First-order evaluation and variational API

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics,
  arXiv:1612.03100v2, Chapter 5. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]
