modules.title: First variation and the Euler-Lagrange criterion
modules.doc:
Public entry point: a field is critical iff its local Euler-Lagrange operator vanishes.

## i. Overview

This module is the public entry point for the local first-variation theory. The core linearized
density objects live in `FirstVariation.Basic`, the analytic derivation tools and packaged
hypotheses live in `FirstVariation.Density`, `FirstVariation.IntegrationByParts`,
`FirstVariation.Regularity`, and `FirstVariation.Criterion`, and this file exposes the cleanest
surface-level statements of the local Euler-Lagrange criterion.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.hasSmoothEulerLagrangeRegularity_of_smoothInCoordinates`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.isCritical_iff_eulerLagrange_zero_of_contDiff_and_smoothInCoordinates`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.
  isCritical_iff_eulerLagrange_zero_of_admissibleForAction_and_smoothInCoordinates`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smooth-coordinate regularity
- B. Final Euler-Lagrange criteria

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics, Chapter 5,
  Theorem 5.2. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.hasSmoothEulerLagrangeRegularity_of_smoothInCoordinates

## i. Overview

This module introduces the coordinate-level point of the locally trivialized `k`-jet bundle for
fields on `Space d` with values in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.

This module only formalizes the local coordinate model `Jet^k(Ω, ℝ^m) ≃ Ω × V`; it does not
attempt to define global jet bundles.

At this core stage, a jet point is represented by:

- its base point in `Space d`,
- and its jet coordinates indexed by derivative indices of order at most `k`.

In particular, the zero-th order field value is not stored separately: it is the zero derivative
coordinate.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetCoordinates`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Jet coordinates
- B. Jet points
- C. Jet points of fields

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics,
  arXiv:1612.03100v2, Chapter 5, Section 5.1. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetCoordinates
declarations.doc:
Coordinate data `u^a_I` for `k`-th order jet points.

For each derivative index `I`, these are the scalar components of the corresponding
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)` fiber coordinate. We keep this componentwise form because the
local Euler-Lagrange formulas are indexed by both `I` and `a`.
declarations.statement: abbrev JetCoordinates (d m k : ℕ)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint
declarations.doc:
The coordinate-level points of the locally trivialized `k`-jet bundle for fields
`Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.
declarations.statement:
structure JetPoint (d m k : ℕ) where
  /-- The base point of the jet point. -/
  base : Space d
  /-- The jet coordinates indexed by all derivative indices of order at most `k`. -/
  fiber : JetCoordinates d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.coord
declarations.doc: The coordinate `u^a_I` of a jet point.
declarations.statement: def coord (J : JetPoint d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.value
declarations.doc: The zero-th order value encoded by a jet point.
declarations.statement: def value (J : JetPoint d m k) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.value_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma value_apply (J : JetPoint d m k) (a : Fin m) :
    J.value a = J.coord 0 a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma ext (J K : JetPoint d m k) (hbase : J.base = K.base)
    (hcoord : ∀ I a, J.coord I a = K.coord I a) :
    J = K

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates
declarations.doc: Build a jet point from a base point and its jet coordinates.
declarations.statement: def ofBaseCoordinates (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) : JetPoint d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.toBaseCoordinates
declarations.doc: The base point and jet coordinates of a jet point.
declarations.statement: def toBaseCoordinates (J : JetPoint d m k) : Space d × JetCoordinates d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_base
declarations.statement:
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_base (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :
    (ofBaseCoordinates x u).base = x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_fiber
declarations.statement:
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_fiber (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :
    (ofBaseCoordinates x u).fiber = u

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_coord (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (ofBaseCoordinates x u).coord I a = u I a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates_base_fiber
declarations.statement:
lemma ofBaseCoordinates_base_fiber (J : JetPoint d m k) :
    ofBaseCoordinates J.base J.fiber = J

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.toBaseCoordinates_ofBaseCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma toBaseCoordinates_ofBaseCoordinates (x : Space d) (u : JetCoordinates d m k) :
    (ofBaseCoordinates x u).toBaseCoordinates = (x, u)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt
declarations.doc: The jet-coordinate function determined by a field `g`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetCoordinatesAt (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) :
    JetCoordinates d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt
declarations.doc: The coordinate-level `k`-jet point of a field `f` at the point `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetAt (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    JetPoint d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_base
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_base (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    (jetAt k f x).base = x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_value
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_value (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    (jetAt k f x).value = f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_coord (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (jetAt k f x).coord I a = ∂^[I.1] (fun y => (f y) a) x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_coord_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_coord_zero (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d)
    (a : Fin m) :
    (jetAt k f x).coord 0 a = (f x) a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoordinatesAt_eq (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    jetCoordinatesAt k g x I a = ∂^[I.1] (fun y => (g y) a) x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoordinatesAt_zero (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) (a : Fin m) :
    jetCoordinatesAt k g x 0 a = (g x) a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_eq_ofBaseCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_eq_ofBaseCoordinates (k : ℕ) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) :
    jetAt k f x = JetPoint.ofBaseCoordinates x (jetCoordinatesAt k f x)

modules.title: Fiber directions on jet points
modules.doc:
Affine fiber-direction structure on coordinate-level jet points.

## i. Overview

This module adds the affine fiber-direction structure on coordinate-level jet points.

At this stage, it introduces:

- fiber-coordinate data on jet points,
- affine translation and line maps in the jet fiber,
- and the jet-fiber direction determined by a field.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.addFiber`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.lineMap`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fiber-coordinate data
- B. Affine fiber structure on jet points
- C. Fiber directions determined by fields

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Fiber-coordinate data
## B. Affine fiber structure on jet points
## C. Fiber directions determined by fields

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData
declarations.doc:
Fiber-coordinate data for jet points of order `k`. This records only the coordinates `u^a_I`,
not the base point in `Space d`.
declarations.statement:
structure JetFiberData (d m k : ℕ) where
  /-- The fiber coordinates indexed by all derivative indices of order at most `k`. -/
  coord : JetCoordinates d m k
instance : CoeFun (JetFiberData d m k) (fun _ => DerivativeIndex d k → Fin m → ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext (V W : JetFiberData d m k) (hcoord : ∀ I a, V.coord I a = W.coord I a) : V = W

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.value
declarations.doc: The zero-th order component of a jet-fiber direction, corresponding to the field value.
declarations.statement: def value (V : JetFiberData d m k) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.value_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma value_apply (V : JetFiberData d m k) (a : Fin m) :
    V.value a = V.coord 0 a
instance : Zero (JetFiberData d m k)
instance : Add (JetFiberData d m k)
instance : SMul ℝ (JetFiberData d m k)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.zero_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma zero_coord (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (0 : JetFiberData d m k).coord I a = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.add_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma add_coord (V W : JetFiberData d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (V + W).coord I a = V.coord I a + W.coord I a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetFiberData.smul_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_coord (c : ℝ) (V : JetFiberData d m k) (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (c • V).coord I a = c * V.coord I a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.addFiber
declarations.doc: Translate a jet point by a fiber-direction increment.
declarations.statement: def addFiber (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) : JetPoint d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.lineMap
declarations.doc: The affine line in jet space through `J` in the fiber direction `V`.
declarations.statement: def lineMap (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) (s : ℝ) : JetPoint d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.addFiber_base
declarations.statement:
lemma addFiber_base (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) :
    (J.addFiber V).base = J.base

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.addFiber_value
declarations.statement:
lemma addFiber_value (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) :
    (J.addFiber V).value = J.value + V.value

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.addFiber_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma addFiber_coord (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (J.addFiber V).coord I a = J.coord I a + V.coord I a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.lineMap_base
declarations.statement:
lemma lineMap_base (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) (s : ℝ) :
    (J.lineMap V s).base = J.base

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.JetPoint.lineMap_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma lineMap_coord (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) (s : ℝ)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (J.lineMap V s).coord I a = J.coord I a + s * V.coord I a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt
declarations.doc: The jet-fiber direction determined by a field `g` at a point `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDirectionAt (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) :
    JetFiberData d m k

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDirectionAt_coord (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d)
    (I : DerivativeIndex d k) (a : Fin m) :
    (jetDirectionAt k g x).coord I a = ∂^[I.1] (fun y => (g y) a) x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt_coord_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDirectionAt_coord_zero (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) (a : Fin m) :
    (jetDirectionAt k g x).coord 0 a = (g x) a

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_add_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoordinatesAt_add_smul (k : ℕ) (f g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) (s : ℝ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    jetCoordinatesAt k (fun y => f y + s • g y) x =
      jetCoordinatesAt k f x + s • jetCoordinatesAt k g x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetAt_add_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAt_add_smul (k : ℕ) (f g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (x : Space d) (s : ℝ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    jetAt k (fun y => f y + s • g y) x = (jetAt k f x).lineMap (jetDirectionAt k g x) s

modules.title: Regularity and support for jet-coordinate maps
modules.doc:
Smoothness of jet-coordinate maps of smooth fields and their vanishing outside the support.

## i. Overview

This module collects the analytic facts about coordinate-level jet maps that are needed later in
the local variational argument.

At this stage, it provides:

- smoothness of jet-coordinate maps of smooth fields,
- smoothness of the base-plus-coordinate jet map,
- and vanishing of jet coordinates outside topological support.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_contDiff`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetBaseCoordinates_contDiff`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smoothness of jet-coordinate maps
- B. Support and vanishing lemmas

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_contDiff
declarations.doc: Smoothness of the jet-coordinate map of a smooth field.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoordinatesAt_contDiff (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (jetCoordinatesAt k g)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetBaseCoordinates_contDiff
declarations.doc: Smoothness of the base-plus-coordinate jet map of a smooth field.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetBaseCoordinates_contDiff (k : ℕ) (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun x : Space d => (x, jetCoordinatesAt k g x))

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetCoordinatesAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
declarations.doc: Outside the topological support of a field, all of its jet coordinates vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoordinatesAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport (k : ℕ)
    (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) {x : Space d}
    (hx : x ∉ tsupport g) :
    jetCoordinatesAt k g x = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.jetDirectionAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
declarations.doc: Outside the topological support of a field, the corresponding jet-fiber direction vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDirectionAt_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport (k : ℕ)
    (g : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) {x : Space d}
    (hx : x ∉ tsupport g) :
    jetDirectionAt k g x = 0

modules.title: Local Lagrangians
modules.doc:
Local finite-order Lagrangians on jet points, their regularity, and evaluation along fields.

## i. Overview

This module defines local Lagrangians of finite order for fields on `Space d` with values in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.

In the first local stage of the Classical Field Theory development, a local `k`-th order
Lagrangian is treated as a function on `JetPoint d m k`. This matches the local book-level picture
`L : Jet^k(Ω, R^m) → R` while postponing any stronger smoothness packaging until the ambient
structure on local jet-point data has been made explicit enough to support it naturally.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian` : local `k`-th order Lagrangians.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.coordDeriv` : coordinate derivatives with respect to the
  jet coordinates `u^a_I`.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates` : the combined public regularity
  package for smooth local lagrangians in explicit jet coordinates.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.alongField` : evaluate a local Lagrangian along the jets
  of a field.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Local Lagrangians
- B. Regularity packages
- C. Evaluation along a field

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics, Chapter 5.
  [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

sections.text: ## A. Local Lagrangians
## B. Regularity packages
## C. Evaluation along a field

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian
declarations.doc: A local `k`-th order Lagrangian for fields `Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.
declarations.statement:
structure Lagrangian (d m k : ℕ) where
  /-- The underlying jet-dependent function. -/
  toFun : JetPoint d m k → ℝ
  /-- The derivatives of the Lagrangian with respect to the jet coordinates `u^a_I`. -/
  coordDeriv : DerivativeIndex d k → Fin m → JetPoint d m k → ℝ
  /-- The first derivative of the Lagrangian along affine lines in the jet-fiber coordinates is
  given by the pairing with the coordinate derivatives. -/
  hasDerivAlongFiber :
    ∀ J : JetPoint d m k, ∀ V : JetFiberData d m k,
      HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => toFun (J.lineMap V s))
        (∑ I : DerivativeIndex d k, ∑ a : Fin m, coordDeriv I a J * V.coord I a) 0
instance : CoeFun (Lagrangian d m k) (fun _ => JetPoint d m k → ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.fiberDerivative
declarations.doc: The derivative of `L` along the fiber-jet direction `V` based at `J`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fiberDerivative (L : Lagrangian d m k) (J : JetPoint d m k)
    (V : JetFiberData d m k) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.hasDerivAt_lineMap
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_lineMap (L : Lagrangian d m k) (J : JetPoint d m k) (V : JetFiberData d m k) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => L (J.lineMap V s)) (L.fiberDerivative J V) 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.ContinuousInCoordinates
declarations.doc: Continuity of a local lagrangian in the explicit local jet coordinates `(x, u^a_I)`.
declarations.statement: def ContinuousInCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.ContDiffCoordDerivInCoordinates
declarations.doc:
Intrinsic smoothness of the jet-coordinate derivatives of a local Lagrangian in the explicit
local jet coordinates `(x, u^a_I)`.
declarations.statement: def ContDiffCoordDerivInCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates
declarations.doc:
Public regularity package for a smooth local lagrangian in explicit local jet coordinates:
continuity of the lagrangian itself together with smoothness of all jet-coordinate derivatives.
declarations.statement: def SmoothInCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.ContDiffCoordDerivAlongField
declarations.doc: Smoothness of all coefficient functions `x ↦ ∂L/∂u_I^a (j^k f(x))` along a field `f`.
declarations.statement:
def ContDiffCoordDerivAlongField (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.ContinuousCoordDerivAlongFamily
declarations.doc:
Continuity of the coefficient family `(s, x) ↦ ∂L/∂u_I^a (j^k(F s)(x))` along a
one-parameter family of fields `F : ℝ → Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`.
declarations.statement:
def ContinuousCoordDerivAlongFamily (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (F : ℝ → Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.continuousAlongField_of_inCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma continuousAlongField_of_inCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (hcont : ContinuousInCoordinates L) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) :
    Continuous (fun x : Space d => L (jetAt k f x))

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.contDiffCoordDerivAlongField_of_inCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiffCoordDerivAlongField_of_inCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (hcoord : ContDiffCoordDerivInCoordinates L) (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) :
    ContDiffCoordDerivAlongField L f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.continuousCoordDerivAlongFamily_of_inCoordinates
declarations.statement:
lemma continuousCoordDerivAlongFamily_of_inCoordinates (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (hcoord : ContDiffCoordDerivInCoordinates L)
    (F : ℝ → Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hjet : Continuous (fun p : ℝ × Space d => (p.2, jetCoordinatesAt k (F p.1) p.2))) :
    ContinuousCoordDerivAlongFamily L F

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.alongField
declarations.doc: Evaluate a local Lagrangian along the `k`-jets of a field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def alongField (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.Lagrangian.alongField_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma alongField_apply (L : Lagrangian d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    L.alongField f x = L (jetAt k f x)

modules.title: Total derivatives on local jet-dependent functions
modules.doc:
Total derivatives of jet-dependent functions, defined via evaluation along fields.

## i. Overview

This module defines total derivatives of local jet-dependent functions by differentiating their
evaluation along jets of fields.

For the first local stage, this keeps the operator close to the use made in the Euler-Lagrange
formula, without yet introducing a separate coordinate-level derivative calculus on `JetPoint`.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.evalOnJet` : evaluate a jet-dependent function along a field.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.totalDerivative` : total derivative in one coordinate direction.
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.iteratedTotalDerivative` : iterated total derivative indexed by a
  multi-index.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Evaluation on jets
- B. Total derivatives

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Total derivatives

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.evalOnJet
declarations.doc: Evaluate a local jet-dependent function along the `k`-jet of a field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evalOnJet (k : ℕ) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.totalDerivative
declarations.doc: The total derivative of a jet-dependent function in the coordinate direction `i`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def totalDerivative (k : ℕ) (i : Fin d) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.iteratedTotalDerivative
declarations.doc: The iterated total derivative indexed by a multi-index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedTotalDerivative (k : ℕ) (I : MultiIndex d) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.evalOnJet_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma evalOnJet_apply (k : ℕ) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (x : Space d) :
    evalOnJet k F f x = F (jetAt k f x)

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.totalDerivative_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDerivative_eq (k : ℕ) (i : Fin d) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    totalDerivative k i F f = ∂[i] (fun x => F (jetAt k f x))

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.iteratedTotalDerivative_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedTotalDerivative_eq (k : ℕ) (I : MultiIndex d) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    iteratedTotalDerivative k I F f = ∂^[I] (fun x => F (jetAt k f x))

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.iteratedTotalDerivative_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedTotalDerivative_zero (k : ℕ) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    iteratedTotalDerivative k (0 : MultiIndex d) F f = evalOnJet k F f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.iteratedTotalDerivative_single
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedTotalDerivative_single (k : ℕ) (i : Fin d) (F : JetPoint d m k → ℝ)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    iteratedTotalDerivative k (Physlib.MultiIndex.increment 0 i) F f =
      totalDerivative k i F f

modules.title: Total divergences in local classical field theory
modules.doc:
Packaged total-divergence Lagrangians and the Euler-Lagrange-triviality property.

## i. Overview

This module introduces the local coordinate API for total-divergence lagrangians.

If `Bᵢ` is a jet-dependent current of order `k`, its total divergence

`∑ i, Dᵢ Bᵢ`

is naturally a lagrangian density of order `k + 1`. In the current Alpha stack, local lagrangians
carry their jet-coordinate derivatives as explicit data, so this module does not try to construct
that lagrangian automatically from the current. Instead, it packages the data needed by later
equivalence results:

- a local lagrangian of order `k + 1`,
- a current whose total divergence agrees with the lagrangian density along every field,
- and the Euler-Lagrange-triviality property of that lagrangian.

This keeps the API faithful to the standard total-divergence principle while avoiding premature
symbolic calculus for coordinate derivatives of total derivatives.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasTotalDivergenceDensity`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeTrivial`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergence`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Total-divergence predicates
- B. Packaged total-divergence lagrangians

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics,
  arXiv:1612.03100v2, Chapter 5. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

sections.text: ## A. Total-divergence predicates
## B. Packaged total-divergence lagrangians

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasTotalDivergenceDensity
declarations.doc:
A lagrangian density has total-divergence form if, along every field, it is the sum of the
total derivatives of a jet-dependent current. A current of order `k` gives a density of order
`k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
def HasTotalDivergenceDensity (L : Lagrangian d m (k + 1))
    (current : Fin d → JetPoint d m k → ℝ) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeTrivial
declarations.doc:
A local lagrangian is Euler-Lagrange-trivial if its Euler-Lagrange operator vanishes along
every field.
declarations.statement: def IsEulerLagrangeTrivial (L : Lagrangian d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergence
declarations.doc:
A packaged local total divergence.

The current has order `k`, while the associated lagrangian has order `k + 1`, matching the
coordinate expression `L = ∑ i, Dᵢ Bᵢ`. The Euler-Lagrange-triviality field records the
variationally trivial direction needed by later equivalence results.
declarations.statement:
structure TotalDivergence (d m k : ℕ) where
  /-- The lagrangian represented by the total divergence of the current. -/
  lagrangian : Lagrangian d m (k + 1)
  /-- The current whose total divergence gives the lagrangian density. -/
  current : Fin d → JetPoint d m k → ℝ
  /-- The density agrees with the total divergence of the current along every field. -/
  hasTotalDivergenceDensity : HasTotalDivergenceDensity lagrangian current
  /-- The associated lagrangian is recorded as Euler-Lagrange-trivial. -/
  isEulerLagrangeTrivial : IsEulerLagrangeTrivial lagrangian
instance : CoeFun (TotalDivergence d m k) (fun _ => Lagrangian d m (k + 1))

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergence.actionDensity_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma actionDensity_eq (T : TotalDivergence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    actionDensity T.lagrangian f =
      fun x => ∑ i : Fin d, totalDerivative k i (T.current i) f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergence.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero (T : TotalDivergence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp T.lagrangian f = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergence.isCritical
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical (T : TotalDivergence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hTf : IsAdmissibleForAction T.lagrangian f)
    (hT : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates T.lagrangian) :
    IsCritical T.lagrangian f

modules.title: Lagrangian equivalence up to total divergences
modules.doc:
Lagrangians differing by a total divergence have the same Euler-Lagrange equations.

## i. Overview

This module adds the local coordinate API for lagrangians that differ by a total divergence.

In the current Alpha stack, local lagrangians carry their jet-coordinate derivatives explicitly.
Consequently, this module does not construct the modified lagrangian by adding a current
divergence syntactically. Instead, it packages the data needed by later equivalence results:

- two local lagrangians of the same order,
- a total-divergence lagrangian witnessing the density difference,
- and equality of the corresponding Euler-Lagrange operators.

This is the field-theory analogue of the classical fact that adding a total derivative or total
divergence does not change the variational equations, while keeping the current API honest about
which facts are data and which facts are proved.

## ii. Key results

- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasTotalDivergenceDifference`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero_iff`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.isCritical_iff`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence`
- `ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.isCritical_iff`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Equivalence predicates
- B. Euler-Lagrange equivalence API
- C. Packaged total-divergence equivalences

## iv. References

* J. Cortés and A. Haupt, Lecture Notes on Mathematical Methods of Classical Physics,
  arXiv:1612.03100v2, Chapter 5. [ref: cortes_haupt_2016]

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.HasTotalDivergenceDifference
declarations.doc:
A lagrangian `target` differs from `source` by the density of a packaged total divergence.

The total divergence has current order `k`, hence its associated lagrangian and both compared
lagrangians have order `k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
def HasTotalDivergenceDifference (source target : Lagrangian d m (k + 1))
    (T : TotalDivergence d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent
declarations.doc:
Two local lagrangians are Euler-Lagrange equivalent when they determine the same local
Euler-Lagrange operator along every field.
declarations.statement: def IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent (source target : Lagrangian d m k) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.refl
declarations.statement: lemma refl (L : Lagrangian d m k) : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent L L

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.symm
declarations.statement:
lemma symm {L1 L2 : Lagrangian d m k} (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent L1 L2) :
    IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent L2 L1

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.trans
ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.eulerLagrangeOp_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq {source target : Lagrangian d m k}
    (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp target f = eulerLagrangeOp source f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero_iff {source target : Lagrangian d m k}
    (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp target f = 0 ↔ eulerLagrangeOp source f = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.isCritical_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_iff {source target : Lagrangian d m k}
    (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates target) :
    IsCritical target f ↔ IsCritical source f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.isCritical_target_of_source
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_target_of_source {source target : Lagrangian d m k}
    (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates target)
    (hcrit : IsCritical source f) :
    IsCritical target f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent.isCritical_source_of_target
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_source_of_target {source target : Lagrangian d m k}
    (h : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates target)
    (hcrit : IsCritical target f) :
    IsCritical source f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence
declarations.doc:
A packaged equivalence between two local lagrangians whose densities differ by a total
divergence.

The field `sameEulerLagrangeOp` records the variational consequence in the current Alpha API. It
will become a theorem once the stack has enough symbolic calculus for coordinate derivatives of
total divergences.
declarations.statement:
structure TotalDivergenceEquivalence (d m k : ℕ) where
  /-- The original local lagrangian. -/
  source : Lagrangian d m (k + 1)
  /-- The modified local lagrangian. -/
  target : Lagrangian d m (k + 1)
  /-- The total divergence giving the density difference. -/
  divergence : TotalDivergence d m k
  /-- The target density is the source density plus the total-divergence density. -/
  hasTotalDivergenceDifference :
    HasTotalDivergenceDifference source target divergence
  /-- The two lagrangians have the same Euler-Lagrange operator. -/
  sameEulerLagrangeOp : IsEulerLagrangeEquivalent source target

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.actionDensity_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma actionDensity_eq (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    actionDensity E.target f =
      fun x => actionDensity E.source f x + actionDensity E.divergence.lagrangian f x

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.eulerLagrangeOp_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp E.target f = eulerLagrangeOp E.source f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma eulerLagrangeOp_eq_zero_iff (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) :
    eulerLagrangeOp E.target f = 0 ↔ eulerLagrangeOp E.source f = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.isCritical_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_iff (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction E.source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction E.target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.target) :
    IsCritical E.target f ↔ IsCritical E.source f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.isCritical_target_of_source
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_target_of_source (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction E.source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction E.target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.target)
    (hcrit : IsCritical E.source f) :
    IsCritical E.target f

declarations.name: ClassicalFieldTheory.Local.TotalDivergenceEquivalence.isCritical_source_of_target
declarations.statement:
lemma isCritical_source_of_target (E : TotalDivergenceEquivalence d m k)
    (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m))
    (hsourcef : IsAdmissibleForAction E.source f)
    (htargetf : IsAdmissibleForAction E.target f)
    (hsource : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.source)
    (htarget : Lagrangian.SmoothInCoordinates E.target)
    (hcrit : IsCritical E.target f) :
    IsCritical E.source f

modules.title: The wave operator
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The wave operator on smooth fields and on distributions on spacetime.

## ii. Key results

- `smoothWaveOperator` : The smooth wave operator as the Minkowski metric trace of the second
  derivative.
- `distributionWaveOperator` : The wave operator on all distributions is the metric trace of weak
  second derivatives.
- `testWaveOperator` : The transpose wave operator on native smooth compact test functions.
- `smoothFiberMap_waveOperator` : Constant fibre transformations commute with the metric-trace wave
  operator.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Minkowski wave equation
- B. The distributional wave operator

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Minkowski wave equation

- `smoothWaveOperator` : The smooth wave operator as the Minkowski metric trace of the second
  derivative.

Lemmas: `smoothWaveOperator_coe`, `smoothWaveOperator_support`, `smoothFiberMap_waveOperator`.

## B. The distributional wave operator

- `distributionWaveOperator` : The wave operator on all distributions is the metric trace of weak
  second derivatives.
- `testWaveOperator` : The transpose wave operator on native smooth compact test functions.

Lemmas: `distributionWaveOperator_apply`.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.smoothWaveOperator
declarations.doc: The smooth wave operator as the Minkowski metric trace of the second derivative.
declarations.statement: def smoothWaveOperator : smoothFields d V →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d V

declarations.name: WaveEquation.smoothWaveOperator_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma smoothWaveOperator_coe (u : smoothFields d V) :
    (smoothWaveOperator u : SpaceTime d → V) =
      ∑ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d, (η μ μ : ℝ) •
        (SpaceTime.deriv μ (SpaceTime.deriv μ u.val))

declarations.name: WaveEquation.smoothWaveOperator_support
declarations.doc: Taking the metric trace does not enlarge field support.
declarations.statement:
lemma smoothWaveOperator_support (u : smoothFields d V) :
    tsupport (smoothWaveOperator u : SpaceTime d → V) ⊆ tsupport (u : SpaceTime d → V)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.smoothFiberMap_waveOperator
declarations.doc: Constant fibre transformations commute with the metric-trace wave operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma smoothFiberMap_waveOperator {W : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W]
    (L : V →L[ℝ] W) (u : smoothFields d V) :
    smoothWaveOperator (smoothFiberMap L u) = smoothFiberMap L (smoothWaveOperator u)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.distributionWaveOperator
declarations.doc: The wave operator on all distributions is the metric trace of weak second derivatives.
declarations.statement: def distributionWaveOperator : DistributionField d V →L[ℝ] DistributionField d V

declarations.name: WaveEquation.testWaveOperator
declarations.doc: The transpose wave operator on native smooth compact test functions.

declarations.doc: Two weak derivatives give the positive transpose wave operator on tests.
declarations.statement:
lemma distributionWaveOperator_apply (T : DistributionField d V)
    (φ : _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)) ℝ ⊤) :
    distributionWaveOperator T φ = T (testWaveOperator φ)

modules.title: Fourier properties of wave propagation
modules.doc:
The spectral description uses the Fourier phase and the sine multiplier of the wave propagator.

## i. Overview

The spectral description uses the Fourier phase and the sine multiplier of the wave propagator.

## ii. Key results

* `phase`: The Fourier phase as a complex exponential.
* `phase_add`.
* `norm_phase`.
* `phase_eq_fourierChar` : the phase is the Fourier character.
* `IsWavePropagator`: Fourier multiplier, finite propagation speed and Huygens' principle.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fourier properties of wave propagation

## iv. References

* Bär, [Green-hyperbolic operators on globally hyperbolic
  spacetimes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.0738).

## A. Fourier properties of wave propagation

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.phase
declarations.doc: The Fourier phase as a complex exponential.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def phase (t : ℝ) : ℂ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.phase_add
declarations.statement: lemma phase_add (s t : ℝ) : phase (s + t) = phase s * phase t

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.norm_phase
declarations.statement: lemma norm_phase (t : ℝ) : ‖phase t‖ = 1

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.continuous_phase
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_phase : Continuous phase

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.phase_eq_fourierChar
declarations.doc: The phase is the Fourier character at `-u`.
declarations.statement: lemma phase_eq_fourierChar (u : ℝ) : phase u = (𝐞 (-u) : ℂ)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.WaveOperator
declarations.doc: An operator on scalar fields on `ℝ³`.
declarations.statement: abbrev WaveOperator

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.HasWaveFourierMultiplier
declarations.doc:
The operator acts on Schwartz functions as the Fourier multiplier `sin(ω t) / ω` with
`ω = 2π c |ξ|`. Frequencies `ξ = 0` are excluded. There the multiplier has the limit `t`.
declarations.statement: def HasWaveFourierMultiplier (c t : ℝ) (T : WaveOperator) : Prop

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.HasFinitePropagationSpeed
declarations.doc:
Finite propagation speed for `c > 0`: if `f` vanishes outside the ball of radius `ρ` about `x₀`,
then `T f` vanishes outside the ball of radius `ρ + c |t|`.
declarations.statement: def HasFinitePropagationSpeed (c t : ℝ) (T : WaveOperator) : Prop

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.SatisfiesHuygensPrinciple
declarations.doc:
Huygens' principle for `c > 0`: if `f` vanishes outside the ball of radius `ρ` about `x₀`, then
`T f` vanishes inside the ball of radius `c |t| - ρ`. The wavefront is a shell of width `2ρ`
with no wave behind it.
declarations.statement: def SatisfiesHuygensPrinciple (c t : ℝ) (T : WaveOperator) : Prop

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.IsWavePropagator
declarations.doc:
The three properties of the free wave propagator in three dimensions: the Fourier multiplier,
finite propagation speed and Huygens' principle. This is a bundle of properties of one operator and
not a characterisation of wave propagators.
declarations.statement:
structure IsWavePropagator (c t : ℝ) (T : WaveOperator) : Prop where
  /-- The Fourier multiplier is `sin(ω t) / ω`. -/
  multiplier : HasWaveFourierMultiplier c t T
  /-- Signals travel at most at speed `c`. -/
  finiteSpeed : HasFinitePropagationSpeed c t T
  /-- The wave vanishes behind the wavefront. -/
  huygens : SatisfiesHuygensPrinciple c t T

modules.title: Properties of the wave propagator
modules.doc:
The wave propagator has the Fourier multiplier `sin(ω t) / ω`, finite propagation speed and the
Huygens property.

## i. Overview

The multiplier is `sin(ω t) / ω` with `ω = 2π c |ξ|`. A function supported in a ball is carried by
the
propagator to the shell around the ball. Points inside the light cone of the support see nothing.
The propagator is odd in time. The statements are first proved for positive time. The oddness of the
spherical integral extends them to negative time.

## ii. Key results

* `wavePropagator_fourier`: the Fourier multiplier.
* `wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_far`: finite propagation speed.
* `wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_near`: Huygens' principle.
* `wavePropagator_neg`: oddness in time.
* `wavePropagator_eq_of_eq_on_sphere`: the field depends on the data only on a sphere.
* `wavePropagator_isWavePropagator`: the three properties together.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Fourier multiplier for positive time
- B. Light-cone support for positive time
- C. Two-sided time
- D. The free three-dimensional propagator

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Fourier multiplier for positive time
## B. Light-cone support for positive time
## C. Two-sided time
## D. The free three-dimensional propagator

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_fourier_of_pos
declarations.doc:
**Kirchhoff's formula in Fourier space.** For `c > 0`, `t > 0` and `ξ ≠ 0` the mean has the
Fourier multiplier `sin(ω t) / ω` with `ω = 2π c |ξ|`, the wave propagator multiplier.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_fourier_of_pos (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) {c t : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (ht : 0 < t)
    {ξ : Space 3} (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
    ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * wavePropagator c t f x =
      ((Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * c * ‖ξ‖ * t) / (2 * Real.pi * c * ‖ξ‖) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall
declarations.statement:
lemma sphericalIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall {r : ℝ} {f : Space 3 → ℂ} {x : Space 3}
    (h : ∀ n : Sph, f (x + r • n.1) = 0) : sphericalIntegral r f x = 0

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_far_of_pos
declarations.doc:
**Finite propagation speed.** If `f` vanishes outside the ball of radius `ρ` about `x₀`, then
`S_t f` vanishes at every point farther than `ρ + c t` from `x₀`.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_near_of_pos
declarations.doc:
**Strong Huygens principle.** If `f` vanishes outside the ball of radius `ρ` about `x₀`, then
`S_t f` vanishes at every point `x` with `‖x - x₀‖ + ρ < c t`.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral_neg
declarations.doc: The spherical integral over the sphere of radius `-r` equals the one over radius `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sphericalIntegral_neg (r : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) :
    sphericalIntegral (-r) f x = sphericalIntegral r f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_zero
declarations.doc: The wave propagator vanishes at time zero.
declarations.statement: lemma wavePropagator_zero (c : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) : wavePropagator c 0 f x = 0

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_neg
declarations.doc: The wave propagator is odd in time.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_neg (c t : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) :
    wavePropagator c (-t) f x = -wavePropagator c t f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_of_eq_on_sphere
declarations.doc:
The wave propagator at `(t, x)` reads the data only on the sphere `‖y - x‖ = c |t|`, where the
light cone of `(t, x)` meets the initial time. Data that agree there give the same field.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_far
declarations.doc: **Finite propagation speed** for both signs of time.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_zero_of_near
declarations.doc: **Strong Huygens principle** for both signs of time.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_fourier
declarations.doc: The Fourier multiplier of the wave propagator for both signs of time.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_fourier (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) {c t : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {ξ : Space 3}
    (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
    ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * wavePropagator c t f x =
      ((Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * c * ‖ξ‖ * t) / (2 * Real.pi * c * ‖ξ‖) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_isWavePropagator
declarations.doc:
**Kirchhoff's formula.** For `c > 0` and every real `t` the wave propagator has the Fourier
multiplier `sin(ω t) / ω`, propagates at speed at most `c` and satisfies the strong Huygens
principle.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_isWavePropagator {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (t : ℝ) :
    IsWavePropagator c t (wavePropagator c t)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator_eq_time_sphericalMean
declarations.doc: The wave propagator is `t M_{ct}` with the normalized sphere mean.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavePropagator_eq_time_sphericalMean (c t : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) :
    wavePropagator c t f x = (t : ℂ) * sphericalMean (c * t) f x

modules.title: Waves propagating along spheres
modules.doc:
In three spatial dimensions, solutions of the scalar wave equation `∂ₜ²u - c² Δu = f` propagate
along expanding spheres.

## i. Overview

Kirchhoff's formula expresses this through integration over spheres. The wave propagator `S_c(t)`
maps an initial velocity to the wave it generates. In Fourier space it is the multiplier
`sin(c|k|t) / (c|k|)`. It is odd in time and equals zero at `t = 0`.

The complete homogeneous evolution also contains the initial displacement `a`. With initial velocity
`b` the solution is `u(t) = ∂ₜ S_c(t) a + S_c(t) b`. This is `waveEvolution`.

A source acting over time contributes through Duhamel's principle. The source emitted at time `s`
propagates for the time `t - s`. This is `retardedPotential`. The full solution of the inhomogeneous
equation is the sum of `waveEvolution` and `retardedPotential`.

Two geometric properties characterise the free three-dimensional propagator. Finite propagation
speed
confines the wave to the expanding ball around the support of the data. Huygens' principle removes
the wave inside this ball once the shell has passed. The properties are different statements.
Finite speed holds in every dimension. Huygens' principle fails in two space dimensions.

All functions are scalar and complex-valued. The file only introduces the constructions and the
predicates. Their properties are proved in `Proofs.Kirchhoff`.

## ii. Key results

* `sphericalIntegral`, `sphericalMean`: sphere integrals and their normalized means `M_r`.
* `wavePropagator`: the sine propagator `t M_{ct}`.
* `retardedPotential`, `waveEvolution`: the source term and the evolution of initial data.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Spherical integrals and the wave propagator
- B. Sources and initial data

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral
declarations.doc:
The integral of `f` over the sphere of radius `r` about `x` with respect to the surface measure.
The total mass of the unit sphere is `4π`, so the average is `1 / (4π)` times this integral. For
`r < 0` the sphere is the one of radius `|r|`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sphericalIntegral (r : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalMean
declarations.doc:
The normalized spherical mean `M_r f(x) = (1/(4π)) ∫_{S²} f(x + r n) dσ(n)`.
It reads only the sphere of radius `|r|` about `x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sphericalMean (r : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.wavePropagator
declarations.doc:
The wave propagator `S_c(t) f (x) = (t / 4π) ∫_{S²} f (x + c t n) dσ(n)`: Kirchhoff's sine
propagator `sin(c t √(-Δ)) / (c √(-Δ))` of `∂ₜ²u = c² Δu`. It maps an initial velocity `f` to the
wave with zero initial displacement. It is odd in `t`. It is not the full evolution, which is
`waveEvolution`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wavePropagator (c t : ℝ) (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (x : Space 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.retardedPotential
declarations.doc:
The retarded potential of a source `f(s, y)`: the source emitted at time `s ∈ [0, t]` propagates
for the time `t - s`. This is Duhamel's integral `∫₀ᵗ S_c(t - s) f(s) ds`. It is the part of the
solution of `∂ₜ²u - c² Δu = f` generated by the source, with zero initial displacement and velocity.
It is not the complete solution. For `c > 0` and `t ≥ 0` it is the integral of the source over the
points reached by emission after time zero, see `causalSourcePropagation`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def retardedPotential (c : ℝ) (f : ℝ → Space 3 → ℂ) (t : ℝ) (x : Space 3) : ℂ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.waveEvolution
declarations.doc:
The solution `u(t) = ∂ₜ S_c(t) a + S_c(t) b` of the homogeneous wave equation with initial
displacement `a` and initial velocity `b`, so that `u(0) = a` and `∂ₜu(0) = b`. The derivative is
Lean's `deriv`, which is defined everywhere. It is the classical derivative only where `a` is
regular enough.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def waveEvolution (c : ℝ) (a b : Space 3 → ℂ) (t : ℝ) (x : Space 3) : ℂ

modules.title: Fourier transform and integrability of spherical means
modules.doc:
The spherical mean of a Schwartz function has the transform of the sphere measure times that of
the function.

## i. Overview

The Fourier integral of a spherical mean is the transform of the sphere measure times that of
the function. Spherical means are integrable and square integrable.

## ii. Key results

* `sphericalIntegral_fourier`: the Fourier integral of a spherical mean.
* `integrable_sphericalIntegral`, `memLp_two_sphericalIntegral`: integrability of spherical means.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Fourier transform of a spherical mean
- B. Integrability of the spherical mean

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Fourier transform of a spherical mean
## B. Integrability of the spherical mean

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.translate_complex
declarations.statement:
lemma translate_complex (f : Space 3 → ℂ) (v ξ : Space 3) :
    ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f (x + v) =
      (phase (inner ℝ v ξ))⁻¹ * ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral_fourier_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma sphericalIntegral_fourier_integral (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (r : ℝ) (ξ : Space 3) :
    ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * sphericalIntegral r f x =
      (∫ n : Sph, (phase (inner ℝ (r • n.1) ξ))⁻¹ ∂sphereMeasure) *
        ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral_fourier
declarations.doc:
**Fourier multiplier of the spherical mean.** For `ξ ≠ 0` and `r > 0`, the Fourier integral of
the unnormalized spherical mean is `4π sin(2π r |ξ|) / (2π r |ξ|)` times that of `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sphericalIntegral_fourier (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    {ξ : Space 3} (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
    ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * sphericalIntegral r f x =
      ((4 * Real.pi * Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * r * ‖ξ‖) / (2 * Real.pi * r * ‖ξ‖) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ x : Space 3, phase (inner ℝ x ξ) * f x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.integrable_translate_prod
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_translate_prod (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (r : ℝ) :
    Integrable (Function.uncurry fun (x : Space 3) (n : Sph) => f (x + r • n.1))
      (volume.prod sphereMeasure)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.integrable_sphericalIntegral
declarations.doc: The spherical mean of a Schwartz function is integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_sphericalIntegral (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (r : ℝ) :
    Integrable (sphericalIntegral r f) volume

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.sphericalIntegral_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma sphericalIntegral_bound (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (r : ℝ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ x, ‖sphericalIntegral r f x‖ ≤ C

declarations.name: WaveEquation.Kirchhoff.memLp_two_sphericalIntegral
declarations.doc: The spherical mean of a Schwartz function is square integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma memLp_two_sphericalIntegral (f : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)) (r : ℝ) :
    MemLp (sphericalIntegral r f) 2 volume

modules.title: The wave operator is Poincaré invariant
modules.doc:
The wave operator commutes with the action of the Poincaré group on fields.

## i. Overview

The wave operator is the Minkowski metric trace of the second derivative. A Lorentz
transformation changes the second derivative by the matrix of the transformation. The metric
trace is unchanged because the matrix preserves the metric. A translation commutes with every
derivative. Together these show that the wave operator commutes with the action of the Poincaré
group on smooth fields.

## ii. Key results

- `sum_eta_lorentz` : the matrix of a Lorentz transformation preserves the metric.
- `waveTrace_comp_lorentz` : the metric trace of the second derivative of `u ∘ Λ`.
- `smoothWaveOperator_actSmooth` : the wave operator commutes with the action of the Poincaré group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The metric is preserved
- B. Derivatives of Lorentz transformed functions
- C. Derivatives of translated functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The metric is preserved

- `sum_eta_lorentz` : the matrix of a Lorentz transformation preserves the metric.

## B. Derivatives of Lorentz transformed functions

- `waveTrace_comp_lorentz` : the metric trace of the second derivative of `u ∘ Λ`.

## C. Derivatives of translated functions

- `deriv_comp_add_right` : a translation commutes with the spacetime derivative.

declarations.name: WaveEquation.sum_eta_lorentz
declarations.doc: The matrix of a Lorentz transformation preserves the metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_eta_lorentz (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (ν ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ∑ μ, η μ μ * Λ.1 ν μ * Λ.1 ρ μ = η ν ρ

declarations.name: WaveEquation.deriv_finset_sum
declarations.doc: The spacetime derivative of a finite sum is the sum of the derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_finset_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → SpaceTime d → V)
    (hf : ∀ i ∈ s, Differentiable ℝ (f i)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ μ (fun y => ∑ i ∈ s, f i y) x = ∑ i ∈ s, ∂_ μ (f i) x

declarations.name: WaveEquation.deriv_deriv_comp_lorentz
declarations.doc: The second derivative of a Lorentz transformed function.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_comp_lorentz (u : SpaceTime d → V) (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u) (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ μ (∂_ μ (fun y => u (Λ • y))) x =
      ∑ ν, ∑ ρ, (Λ.1 ν μ * Λ.1 ρ μ) • ∂_ ρ (∂_ ν u) (Λ • x)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.waveTrace_comp_lorentz
declarations.doc: The metric trace of the second derivative of a Lorentz transformed function.
declarations.statement:
lemma waveTrace_comp_lorentz (u : SpaceTime d → V) (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u) (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∑ μ, (η μ μ : ℝ) • ∂_ μ (∂_ μ (fun y => u (Λ • y))) x =
      ∑ ν, (η ν ν : ℝ) • ∂_ ν (∂_ ν u) (Λ • x)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.deriv_comp_add_right
declarations.doc: A translation commutes with the spacetime derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comp_add_right (u : SpaceTime d → V) (b : SpaceTime d) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ∂_ μ (fun y => u (y + b)) = fun y => ∂_ μ u (y + b)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.waveTrace_act
declarations.doc: The metric trace of the second derivative of a transformed function.
declarations.statement:
lemma waveTrace_act (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : SpaceTime d → V) (hu : ContDiff ℝ ∞ u)
    (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∑ μ, (η μ μ : ℝ) • ∂_ μ (∂_ μ (PoincareGroup.act g u)) x =
      ∑ μ, (η μ μ : ℝ) • ∂_ μ (∂_ μ u) (g⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: WaveEquation.smoothWaveOperator_actSmooth
declarations.doc: The wave operator commutes with the action of the Poincaré group.
declarations.statement:
lemma smoothWaveOperator_actSmooth (g : PoincareGroup d) (u : smoothFields d V) :
    smoothWaveOperator (PoincareGroup.actSmooth g u) =
      PoincareGroup.actSmooth g (smoothWaveOperator u)
